title: Joe Burrow Ranked Outside Top-Five NFL Quarterbacks as Bye Week Rolls on
full_text:
Sports Illustrated's Matt Verdarame dropped the site's latest 1-32 NFL quarterback rankings, and Bengals passer Joe Burrow fell outside the top five names in the update.
He started the season ranked fifth overall and is down to sixth on the board with Cincinnati sitting at 3-2 overall entering its bye week.
"When Burrow has been healthy, he’s been an elite quarterback throughout his seven-year NFL career," Verdarame wrote . "In 2026, Burrow has started all five games for the Bengals and looked like a superstar, ranking sixth with 1,361 passing yards while tossing 11 touchdowns against three interceptions.  Analytically, Burrow also ranks fourth in CPOE (6.0) and 13th in EPA per play (0.179) while checking in eighth in success rate (51.2%). With Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins on the outside, Cincinnati remains one of the more dangerous offenses in football, led by a quarterback whose only true challenge is remaining on the field for 17 games."
Names like Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen, Brock Purdy, Lamar Jackson and Jared Goff got slotted above Burrow in that order from 1-5.
Once you get to the top-eight quarterbacks this season, it's hard to really slice one apart from the other. The QB play at the top has been fantastic. If Burrow had 1-2 turnovers instead of four, he'd likely be in that top five, and Cincinnati could be 4-1 or 5-0.
Alas, he faces the easiest remaining strength of schedule on ESPN's NFL FPI. The veteran passer can light things up the rest of the way and cement himself as a top-five hurler by the end of the season.
"We got to be smarter. We got to be smarter. Two fumbles in the red zone. A couple of personal fouls that hurt us, hurt our field position, gave them points on the board. We got to be smarter," Burrow said about the offensive operation on Sunday before touching on his bye week plans. "We'll see. I don't know. It's so early. I want to maintain my conditioning, my strength and conditioning, and certainly want to keep throwing. I'll try to find a plan. This is uncharted territory for me, having a bye this early, so we'll see."

title: Bengals Could Reshape Backfield With Star SEC Running Back in 2027 NFL Draft
full_text:
The bye week is here for Cincinnati, prompting a little looking ahead to the 2027 NFL Draft. Pro Football Focus released a fresh mock draft projecting the first round this week, and Cincinnati added an offensive playmaker in the exercise.
The Bengals rolled with Florida running back Jadan Baugh with the 15th pick in the draft.
"The Bengals have fixed their offensive line and have a passing attack that opposing defenses are forced to respect," Gordon McGuinness wrote . "That's the ideal offensive environment in which to add a dynamic running back, and they would be well justified in using a first-round pick on Baugh. The Florida standout has averaged 3.72 yards after contact per attempt and forced 36 missed tackles this season."
Baugh could be a dynamic way to replace Chae Brown as he works his way through the final season on his Bengals contract.
The Florida bruiser has a nation-leading 12 touchdowns this season and is averaging 6.1 yards per attempt.
McGuinness framed his pick slotting to open the article. Cincinnati is right in the middle of the pack even with a winning record at 3-2. There are 11 teams at either 3-1-1 or 3-2 as of this writing.
"With the 2026 NFL season now past the quarter mark, it’s time to take a far-too-early look at how the NFL draft could shake out if the current draft order holds," McGuinness wrote. "This draft class has generated plenty of excitement over the past two offseasons, and it still looks very strong on paper as we approach the halfway point of the college football season.
"The Tennessee Titans currently hold the No. 1 overall pick, giving them the option to select a new quarterback or add an elite receiving prospect to support their current starter, Cam Ward. One note for this mock draft: Arch Manning does not appear in the first round. Given reports that several scouts don't view him as a first-round pick, I'm taking the approach that he is more likely to return to Texas than enter the draft if that remains the case."
Cincinnati has a long way to go before thinking about picking Baugh, and the team is hoping to be picking way closer to No. 32 than 15th.

title: Erick All Opens Up On Discipline from Zac Taylor During Bengals Recent Win
full_text:
Many eyes turned to Erick All last Sunday after he committed an egregious penalty and fumbled his second catch. Fortunately, the Bengals tight end avoided losing the fumble when the Dolphins recovered it out of bounds. He still, however, received an earful from Zac Taylor on the sideline after his costly penalty where he headbutted a Dolphins defender after the play.
All revealed the experience on First Word , saying it was the first mental error he had made regarding a penalty and that no coach had ever yelled at him as Taylor did on Sunday. He said that he did not intend for the headbutt to be egregious.
"I've never been yelled at by the coach like that besides like missing a block," All revealed. "It was my first stupid penalty like that, I didn't intend for it to be egregious, but it was just one of those little quick walk by things that you didn't think nobody was looking at you and it looked bad and it was stupid."
All then explained that Taylor's discipline after the play is something he respects, given how badly he messed up. He also said that, in that moment, he hoped the coaching staff still trusted him and that, if he got back on the field, they knew he wouldn't make that mistake again.
"Whatever he has to say you just respect it because you just messed up," All said. "You wear it on the chin and hope that they still trust you and can put you out there on the field and know that you won't do anything like that again."
Taylor showed what some may see as another side of himself as a coach, one they hadn't seen before, that being his increased aggressiveness toward players on Sunday.
"I look at Zac as that type of coach that's very transparent, he'll tell you how he feels and it just kind of surprised me hearing 'I'm surprised he hasn't done that with people in the past,'" All said. "Zac's a great coach, if he sees something that he doesn't like or that he wants you to fix, he'll voice it to you whether in practice, game, cameras on, it doesn't matter, and that's what I love about him."
With Tanner Hudson's recent injury, All should see an expanded role in the Bengals' offense. He finished Week 5 with three catches for 25 yards, including a 14-yard catch-and-run that extended a drive in which the offense scored and increased its lead by two scores.
He should continue to ramp up on offense and build more chemistry with Joe Burrow as the season progresses.

title: Bengals' Prized Offseason Acquisitions Already Paying Major Dividends
full_text:
Bye weeks can move rather slowly. However, there's plenty to discuss when it comes to the 2026 edition of the Cincinnati Bengals.
First off, the pass game is looking exactly like everyone had hoped. It's early, but Joe Burrow and Tee Higgins are one of the top quarterback/wide receiver duos in the league. Then, you have the major upgrades to the defensive line.
It's only been five weeks, but Dexter Lawrence has already proven that he is still one of the strongest anchors on a defensive line in the league. One stat from Pro Football Focus even backs that up.
PFF has revealed that the Bengals have the highest defensive stuff rate in the NFL, at 30%. Rounding out the top five is the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Miami Dolphins, Seattle Seahawks, and the Green Bay Packers.
The Bengals are getting everything they wanted and more with the addition of Lawrence. PFF has Lawrence graded as the third best defensive tackle in the NFL. That overall grade includes the fourth best grade in pass rush at 82.4 and the 10th-best rush grade at 72.8.
Lawrence has given opposing offenses fits all season long, but it's not just him who is reaping the benefits of being a part of this defensive line.
The Bengals' strong interior defensive line is opening doors for the pass rusher. Boye Mafe, who was another offseason acquisition, is having a strong start to his 2026 campaign.
Mafe has recorded three sacks and one forced fumble in five games. Mafe currently ranks as the 12th-best edge rusher in the league, according to PFF .
With a lot of the talk regarding the defense being about the weakness at linebacker and some struggles in the secondary, so far this season, the defensive line has been elite.
The pass game is rolling, the defensive line is playing some of the best football in the NFL, and even the offensive line has elevated its game. The Bengals are so close to getting it all together.
Having an early bye week can be a rough draw for a lot of teams. However, this season, it may have just come at the right time for the Bengals. This team is potentially on the cusp of finding greatness. Now, they will have a full week to dissect the issues in the running game and some areas on the defensive side before they play in an all important matchup with the Baltimore Ravens.
When the Bengals do take the field against the Ravens in two weeks, you'd best believe their AFC North rivals already have some concerns about the defensive line they will be seeing.

title: Bengals' Offensive Duo Off to an Explosive Start in 2026
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals didn't get a good draw as it pertains to where the bye week landed on the schedule. A bye in Week 6 is brutal for any team.
With so much season left after the bye week, there's no doubt that health is going to play a major role down the stretch. The win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday was a nice way to enter a bye week, but it still felt like the players and coaches knew they left a lot on the table.
There's no time to sulk in the negative, any win is hard to come by in this league and should be celebrated. It's time to highlight the positives, and the Bengals have a dynamic offensive duo that has been one of the best connections in the young season.
On paper and on the field, the Bengals have one of the most dangerous offenses in the league. Quarterback Joe Burrow is basically playing with two number one options at wide receiver. While Ja'Marr Chase gets most of the attention, and rightfully so, Tee Higgins is having a monster 2026.
According to Pro Football Focus , Burrow to Higgins has the fifth most receiving yards of a quarter/wide receiver duo in the league.
The only duos ahead of the Bengals stars is Matthew Stafford and Devante Adams, Jordan Love and Christian Watson, Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb, and the dup everyone expected to be at number one, Tyler Shough and Chris Olave.
Higgins had a quiet outing against the Dolphins this past Sunday, but he had a good reason, given that he was dealing with an adductor injury. But before Week 5, Higgins was having the strongest season of any receiver on the team.
With Chase having a monster game in Miami that led to arguably the greatest touchdown reception of his career, it seems this offense is finding its rhythm right before they play a very vital game against the Baltimore Ravens in two weeks.
The offense has a lot of things going its way. Burrow's connection with Chase and Higgins is as strong as ever, and the offensive line is playing some of the best football they've played under head coach Zac Taylor.
If we're nitpicking, the run game is going to be the focus as the team goes through the bye week. For now, letting Burrow throw nearly 60 times a game doesn't sound so bad.

title: Browns Get Much-Needed Injury Boost Ahead of Ravens Showdown
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have a chance to top the AFC North again. Luckily for them, they just received big injury news.
The Browns lost to the New York Jets in Week 5 of the NFL season in a sloppy, rainy game. Cleveland emerged from the loss with additional injury concerns and opened Week 6 with 17 players on its injury report. Important players on that list included Carson Schewsinger, Mason Graham, Quinshon Judkins, and Derek Barnett.
The Browns got some big names back at practice today: Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham, Quinshon Judkins and Derek Barnett. Not practicing: Mike Hall, Teven Jenkins, Kalia Davis. pic.twitter.com/FMTfDWDLkW
All four players returned to practice Friday, according to ESPN’s Daniel Oyefusi. Their return raises the possibility that all four could play in the pivotal division matchup vs. the Baltimore Ravens.
The Browns' run game has been less than desirable early in the NFL season. However, those struggles could worsen Sunday if the Browns are without their lead back, Quinshon Judkins.
Without Judkins, Cleveland would likely lean on Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime, who joined the team from Minnesota’s practice squad this week. Dylan Sampson’s potential return could also affect the backfield. Judkins’ return to practice offers encouragement for a Browns rushing attack still searching for consistency.
Arguably, the three most important players to return to practice are Mason Graham, Carson Schwesinger, and Derek Barnett. Graham got hurt during the Browns' Thursday Night Football game vs. the Pittsburgh Steelers in a scary injury many thought would take him out for multiple weeks. Now, just two weeks later, the star defensive tackle has returned to practice.
Having Graham, Schwesinger, and Barnett available matters because the Browns need to stop the run against one of the league's best backs, Derrick Henry . The Ravens' starting quarterback, Lamar Jackson, hasn't practiced all week leading up to the Browns matchup.
Ravens QB Lamar Jackson is not present during media viewing portion of Friday’s practice, which indicates Tyler Huntley will likely start for the second straight week. Jackson missed every practice this week and hasn’t suited up since spraining his left ankle in a win over the…
Considering the Browns allowed 134 rushing yards just a week ago to a less talented Jets team, Henry will get his fair share of carries. Graham missed that matchup, and having him available alongside Schwesinger and Barnett would give Cleveland a better chance to contain Baltimore’s ground game.
The Browns now have several key players back at practice ahead of Sunday’s matchup with the Ravens. With Lamar Jackson, the Ravens' MVP quarterback, potentially unavailable Sunday, the Browns have a real chance to reclaim the AFC North.
The question now is whether the team will rise to the occasion as it did in Weeks 2 through 4 or fumble an opportunity as it did in Weeks 1 and 5.

title: 4 Burning Questions Facing the Browns This Week
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are set to host the Baltimore Ravens at home in week six.
After last week's loss to the New York Jets , the Browns have a couple of questions they need to answer.
So far this season, Quinshon Judkins has yet to get back to his rookie-season form.
Through 73 rushing attempts, Judkins has only 221 yards and one touchdown. That averages out to just over three yards per carry.
Last week against the Jets, Cleveland had their chance to finally find out who they were on the ground. New York ranked 25th in rushing defense, yet the Browns still couldn't run the ball.
Now, Cleveland faces a Baltimore defense that ranks 11th in run defense and always brings an extra juice against AFC North rivals.
WOW: #Browns defense guilty of THREE penalties on ONE play and lose Mason Graham #NFL #TNF pic.twitter.com/PzHiPklMOk
Last week, the Browns did a better job of not hurting themselves with penalties. Still, they committed six penatlies for 30 yards.
On the season, Cleveland has the most penalties in the NFL with 49.
It has even been so bad at times that somehow the Browns managed to draw three penalties on one play.
A big key to getting the win on Sunday is playing clean football.
Through the first four games, Todd Monken called easy plays where Deshaun Watson just had to get the ball out to his playmakers.
This allowed the Watson to find confidence, the Browns to score points, and ultimately was the recipe for that 3-1 start.
Then the Jets game happened. It seemed as if Todd Monken was not play-calling as usual. While the rain may have played a factor, Cleveland still has to stay true to what they can do well.
Time after time, Deshaun Watson has proved that he is not the best at pushing the ball downfield. Even if he had a good throw, receivers like Isaiah Bond weren't able to make the plays happen.
It is incredibly important that the Browns call simpler plays for Watson and the Offense, especially when navigating the Ravens' defense.
Again, once the Browns called bad plays, dropped passes, and got themselves in a hole they weren't able to bounce back.
Coach Monken needs to rally his troops and get their heads back in the game in times of poor performance. Let's be honest, there is almost guaranteed to be at least one of those moments every game.
Overall, they will need to have their heads in the full 60 minute game.
No matter what happens, neither team will give up. That's AFC North football.

title: Browns Rookie Receives Highest PFF Grade among 2026 Draft Class
full_text:
After five weeks of the 2026 NFL season, PFF put out their rookie rankings by overall grade.
While many believe Cleveland won the 2026 NFL Draft , the rookie who ranks atop all the others may not be the one you're thinking of from the Brown and Orange.
Emmanuel McNeil-Warren is looking special pic.twitter.com/zcF1Nj0Bsb
Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has the highest PFF grade of any rookie this season through the first few games.
Somehow, the prospect fell all the way to pick 58 overall in April.
McNeil-Warren currently has a PFF grade of 89.9.
This number not only ranks him as the best of all rookies, but also the best of all 96 NFL safeties.
As for the stat line, EMW has 22 total tackles with only 4 targets allowed over 109 total snaps. Additionally, his average passer rating allowed per game is only 27.6.
But it's not necessarily the numbers that are the reason why the rookie is so great.
If you showed a regular fan highlights of the Browns defense, they could never tell McNeil-Warren is only five games in to his pro career.
The reason? His instincts.
Emmanuel McNeil-Warren is ready for primetime Watch how he closes QUICK on both of these balls intended for DK Metcalf to make two high quality pass breakups 👀 pic.twitter.com/brnADB0XoX
Just watching the young stud is incredible. He is already out there jumping passes, making reads, and ultimately playing like a seasoned veteran. The Browns truly have found a playmaker for their secondary
At this point, he is just having to split snaps with Ronnie Hickman. Ultimately, the Browns may decide at some point in the future to move on from Hickman as well, which would free up more snaps for EMW.
Something else we can't just overlook is the other rookie on this PFF top-graded list, who you may have thought sat at the top. Denzel Boston has simply been a beast for the Browns this season.
In five games, the second-round pick out of Washington has 16 catches, with three of those being touchdowns.
Not only does he lead all rookies in receiver yards with 330, but here are some elite NFL names who Boston has out gained:
Clearly, the Cleveland Browns knew what they were doing in the 2026 NFL Draft, especially in the second round.
Outside of Emmanuel McNeil-Warren and Denzel Boston, the Browns have had great success from KC Concepcion, Austin Barber, and Spencer Fano.

title: How Audric Estime Could Work His Way Into Legitimate Playing Time With Browns
full_text:
The running back room has been depleted with injuries and ineffectiveness . Backup Dylan Sampson landed on the injured reserve list during the first game of the season and his replacement Reheim Sanders joined him this week. The Browns signed Jaleel McLaughlin to replace Sampson. The next man up for Sanders is now Audric Estime.
Estime comes from the Minnesota Vikings practice squad and he will look to contribute to the Browns’ offense right away. Quinshon Judkins has struggled so far this season and the running attack has stalled as a whole. The running game could use a new look after five games to allow the offense to thrive.
The 5’11 227 pound back runs hard and never stops moving his legs. Estime has been in the NFL for two seasons and has amassed over 500 yards with a 4.2 average per carry. That average is greater than Judkins’ average per carry by over a whole yard. McLaughlin only has two carries all season and the Browns will have to give carries to all the backs to try and find any improvement.
When he played for the New Orleans Saints in 2025, he had rushing attempts out of the shotgun formation. The Browns’ offense mainly plays out of that formation, which has led to them struggling to run the ball. The running back needs terrific vision as he does not start with momentum before getting the ball and has to find cracks in the line. For the Saints, Estime showed that he has the patience to find an opening and a large frame that does not allow him to get tackled by the first defender.
Deshaun Watson got sacked eight times last week with pressure coming from everywhere. The running backs did not do a good job of stepping up to chip or block defenders. Estime has taken interior defensive linemen one on one to help protect the quarterback. The offense was exposed last week with all the blitzing and Estime can gain serious playing time if he can help buy Watson additional seconds to throw the ball.
Estime’s ability out of the shotgun formation will help him earn legitimate playing time for the Browns this season. Todd Monken insists that Watson and the offense operates best out of shotgun and Estime will bring experience and production to the position group.
He will be in on obvious passing downs to block an extra defender and with the injuries to the other running backs, he should get carries as well. While he will not be an every-down back, he can use his abilities to get legitimate playing time for an offense that needs any type of positive change running the football.

title: Is Shedeur Sanders’ Time in Cleveland in Jeopardy?
full_text:
So far in the 2026 season, Deshaun Watson has surprised pretty much everyone.
After being named the starter right before the season, many thought Watson would only last two games before being removed for Shedeur Sanders .
However, Watson continues to be the guy for the Browns. So far this season, Watson has led the Browns on three game-winning drives in just five games.
While the Browns organization has expressed that they do not want to move on from the second year quarterback, there may be a new development from Sanders' side of things.
Last week, Sanders signed with a new agent for representation.
While it may be a bit of a stretch, former Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. did the same thing and was traded just a week later.
Marvin Harrison Jr signed with an agent & was traded the same wk.. Shedeur Sanders now has an agent.. https://t.co/A2JGviWe6V
While there is still an unlikely chance the Browns deal Shedeur Sanders, getting an agent may sway his mind.
At the moment, Sanders has been content being the Browns backup. According to the media, he is taking the time to watch and learn from Deshaun Watson.
However, if the new agent comes in and pursuades him to push for a trade due to a starting job potentially somewhere else, you never know what may happen.
Regardless, Sanders has a ton of young and raw talent. It is most likely better for him to get this time to watch and develop, knowing he may take over the starting job for Cleveland soon.
Cleveland simply can't afford to lose Sanders.
The Browns finally have a somewhat stable quarterback room. For the past few seasons, its been the story of the starter going down or playing bad, and having to be replaced multiple times per season.
Now, with Deshaun Watson winning games and the young Shedeur Sanders developing on the bench, the Browns are actually looking alright for the future.
There have been many talks about when Sanders could see the field. It may be this season, it may not even be next year.
But let's look at the facts. If the Browns go on a slide and start losing games, let's say they fall out of playoff contention.
The moment that happens they should put Shedeur in to at least let him get in game starting reps when you know when your season will end.
Now let's say Deshaun Watson takes the Browns to the playoffs, and even gets resigned next year.
No matter how much they pay him and for how long, Deshaun Watson is still currently 31 years old and will be 32 by this time next year.
Clearly, the Browns will need another option in the near future. If Sanders can be patient and take more time to develop and learn, he can be ready to go the second the Browns call on number two.

title: Browns Receiver Criticized by Former Star After Disappointing Jets Defeat
full_text:
After the Cleveland Browns lost their week five matchup against the New York Jets, former Browns receiver Jarvis Landry had comments for Isaiah Bond .
In the game, Bond had to step in for the injured KC Concepcion.
By the end, Bond had been targeted seven times. Out of those targets, he had three catches for 74 yards.
However, the second-year man also had numerous plays where he had bad drops, including one that was late in the close game.
Jarvis Landry calls out Isaiah Bond for his costly dropped pass against the Jets, insisting the Browns receiver needs to adjust after the mistake and live up to Cleveland’s high standards for its wideouts. "Isaiah Bond, my dog, if you can't catch that s**t without gloves, you… pic.twitter.com/wZXYKe9Fem
Not only did Landry rip the young receiver for his mistakes, but he also continued to talk about how Bond wasn't "living up to Cleveland's high standards for its wideouts".
In the contest at MetLife Stadium, it did not stop raining throughout the entire contest.
With that being said, Bond was playing the game without gloves on. This was something Landry also made note on, even inserting himself in the situation.
"I'm catching that s**t. Period. Ain't no ifs, ands, or buts. If I drop one without gloves, best believe the next time I come on the field, I got gloves on or I got tape on my fingers or something." Landry said.
Coming into this offseason, Isaiah Bond was someone who flew under the radar for the Browns.
We knew he was going to have to come in and compete for a job on the team, especially after Cleveland drafted two receivers in the 2026 NFL Draft .
A lot of speculation the #Browns should trade Jerry Jeudy Im on board with anything that gets Isaiah Bond more targets Two weeks in: 1 target 1 catch- he’s way too talented to not get the ball pic.twitter.com/N0lwLzfKah
Throughout training camp, the former Texas Longhorn stood out. Day after day it seemed as if Isaiah Bond was the big name who was contantly making big plays and scoring touchdowns.
It almost seemed as if the Browns found another stud who was going to have a breakout season.
But then came game days. At the start of the season, Bond was barely being used. Through the first four games, he only had two catches on his only two targets for a total of 12 yards.
So how can the Browns use him more?
KC Concepcion's health is the main question at the moment for Bond's playing time. However, even when the rookie comes back, I think Bond deserves to get more reps over a guy like Jerry Jeudy.
Bond has showcased in both games and the offseason his breakaway speed. If the Browns utilize him as a deep threat, that will open up the field for KC Concepcion who had been getting great separation off the line of scirmmage.
Tough day for Isaiah Bond. I truly believe he’s better than what he put on tape, but man… Can’t help thinking about what could’ve been. Head up, 007. Still a long season ahead. #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/3iQtpwRgsg
Overall, if Bond wants to redeem himself, he will just have to do it on the field. Going forward, he needs to be able to catch wide open passes. If he can't, adjustments need to be made.
Who knows, maybe Jarvis Landry himself will help out the young pup with some pass catching drills.

title: Browns Should Consider Flipping Jerry Jeudy For This Overshadowed Wideout
full_text:
The current situation of the Cleveland Browns ' wide receiver room is headlined by the excellent play of both rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, who have combined for 34 catches for 449 yards and three touchdowns through the first five games of the season. Cleveland’s next leading receiver is second-year guy Isaiah Bond with 86 receiving yards. Bond struggled with a couple of drops vs. New York, but has gotten just nine targets this season.
Past those three, the rest of the room seems to be up in the air, and the one guy who is the odd man out is popping up in more and more trade rumors. That would, of course, be Jerry Jeudy, who is currently sixth for Cleveland in receiving yards and receptions.
Jeudy’s cap hit of $10.3 million this season, as well as $13.4 million in 2027, does not seem worth the price at the moment or in the future. Cleveland will be looking to trade him ; that’s no secret, but could it be for another receiver who has also seemingly lost his place in the room?
That would be the Jags wideout Brian Thomas Jr.
Thomas is now in his third season with Jacksonville, and after an unbelievable rookie season that showed him producing 87 receptions for over 1,200 yards and 10 touchdowns, his play has slowed down. The Jaguars hired Liam Coen last season, and since then, it doesn’t seem like Thomas has been a focal point of the offense.
An ankle injury also caused Thomas to miss three games last year, but through five games this season, the Jags offense has pivoted towards Parker Washington, Brenton Strange, Jakobi Meyers, and even sixth-round pick Josh Cameron over Thomas.
Now, a trade involving Jeudy for Thomas would have to come with some sweetening on the end of Cleveland, as Thomas is three years younger than Jeudy, and Thomas is making just $4 million on the cap this year, and just $4.6 million next season.
The Browns would most likely have to give up at least a fourth- and fifth-rounder alone, but if the Jags don’t see much value in Jeudy, Cleveland would have to ramp it up to a third, possibly.
Cleveland and Jacksonville have a recent history of trading with each other, as we know from the Travis Hunter & Mason Graham trade, along with the trade that brought Tyson Campbell to Cleveland in exchange for Greg Newsome.
Hi, I’m Paul, I’m from Northeast Ohio, and a recent graduate of Kent State University. As an Ohio native, I’m a huge fan of the Browns, Guardians, and Cavaliers. Just don’t ask me about my favorite college team, though.

title: Why Denzel Boston’s Case For ROTY is Rock-Solid Through Five Weeks
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have two rookies of the year on the defensive side of the ball and now may have found one on the offense. Second-round pick Denzel Boston has broken tackles, ran past, and out jumped defensive backs on his way to leading all rookies in receiving yards. Through five weeks of the season, Boston finds himself the front runner for Offensive Rookie of the Year.
The 6’4 receiver has 330 yards and three touchdowns through five games. During key moments of drives Deshaun Watson looks for the big-framed target for crucial first downs. Boston has taken the top off of the secondary and has multiple touchdowns over 30 yards and is averaging over 20 yards per reception.
The Browns have a surprising 3-2 start, which is due to Boston’s play-making ability. In Tampa Bay he caught a post pass and broke multiple tackles, rumbling his way to a touchdown, bringing life to the offense. In the win against the Carolina Panthers, he used his strong hands and great route running to secure a crucial two-point conversion. He caught a would-be game-winning deep pass against the New York Jets, until the special teams and defense made it null .
No other rookie has meant more to his offense than Boston. He was the 39th pick in the 2026 draft, but he has looked like he should have been drafted much higher. Ohio State’s Carnell Tate was drafted fourth overall to the Tennessee Titans and he is behind Boston in rookie receiving yards with 274 and zero touchdowns. Tate has not helped a maligned Titans’ offense as they are 0-5.
Boston’s teammate and 24th overall pick, KC Concepcion is fourth in rookie receiving yards with 149. The Arizona Cardinal’s third-overall pick at running back, Jeremiah Love, leads rookies in rushing with 245 yards. However, that is only good for 23rd overall in the league and the Cardinals are 1-4.
Jalon Daniels has been the best rookie quarterback so far this season for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers; however, he will get benched when Baker Mayfield returns from injury. First-overall pick Fernando Mendoza has not made a start this season as the Las Vegas Raiders have been relevant under Kirk Cousins.
Boston is averaging 66 yards per game, which, played out in a full season, would be over 1,000 with 10 touchdowns. While those expectations may be too high, it is very realistic. Concepcion was injured in last week’s game and rumors are swirling that Jerry Jeudy will be moved at the trade deadline. Boston will get many opportunities to make plays for the offense as the running attack has been one of the league's worst.
Watson is gaining chemistry with him every week and his production will be greater as the season progresses. Todd Monken coached the similarly framed Mike Evans during his best statistical season, so he knows how to use the big target. Boston is just getting started in the NFL and by the end of the season he will be considered a legitimate threat, and not just for a rookie.
The race for Offensive Rookie of the Year may be over before the halfway point. Nobody is close to Boston’s importance on their offense and the stats back that up. The future looks bright in Cleveland as they will have three rookie of the year winners on their roster.

title: How the Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade Benefits the Cleveland Browns
full_text:
Marvin Harrison Jr. was just traded from the Arizona Cardinals to the Houston Texans.
Obviously, the deal does not directly involve the Browns, but it actually does impact the team more than it may seem.
With Cleveland shopping Jerry Jeudy , his value just increased if teams are looking at the numbers.
This season, both receivers have been in similar situations on their respective teams. Each guy was slated to be the team's number one receiver, yet did not see much action to begin the season.
For Harrison, he only had 13 targets through the first four games. Out of those targets, he had five catches for 85 yards and one touchdown.
For Jeudy, he has only been targeted 15 times. His stat line currently sits at eight catches for 81 yards and zero touchdowns.
While the stats are close, there are some other key factors to argue against the Browns getting a similar trade package.
Marvin Harrison Jr. was drafted number four overall just two years ago. We cannot forget that he was one of the best college prospects we've seen in a long time out of Ohio State.
Mike LaFleur on Marvin Harrison Jr.’s effort: "I think his running style is different than some other people's." ( @BoBrack ) pic.twitter.com/k8m26OtpKm
With that being said, there is still much to be seen from Harrison. At only 24 years old, he has a long NFL career ahead of him.
As for Jerry Jeudy, teams already know what they are going to get. A diva receiver who can step up given the right situation. Otherwise, he won't fit in and will constantly drop passes.
At 27 years old, there is still some time for Jeudy, but obviously not nearly as much as Harrison.
With the recent injury to KC Concepcion, Cleveland may wait longer to trade Jeudy.
In the case they still decide to move him, what could they get in return?
TRADE: Cardinals trading WR Marvin Harrison Jr. and a 2027 7th-round pick to the Texans in exchange for a 2027 2nd-round pick and 2027 6th-round pick. (via @rapsheet , @adamschefter ) pic.twitter.com/abCg6guHE0
For Harrison, the Cardinals got back a 2027 second and sixth. While the Browns are unlikely to get the exact same package for Jeudy with Harrison being the better player, they can still get close.
If the Browns just want draft capitol in return for their receiver, they will most likely be able to get a mid round pick and late round pick. Some say they could manage to get a third, but I think that depends on which team they trade with.
Another option could be a player swap. The Browns have some gaps in the running back, offensive line, and secondary rooms, and could look to use Jeudy as a way to level out their team.

title: Browns Injury Report Highlights Concerning Trend Following Team Ahead of Week 6
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are headed into Week 6 with a 3-2 overall record on the young 2026 regular season.
Losing in Week 5 to the New York Jets on the road, the Browns have some work to do to bounce back in a Week 6 meeting with the Baltimore Ravens at home. However, being at full strength may be an issue.
On Wednesday, Oct. 14, news broke that the Browns were expected to be without multiple players for practice due to injury.
Of the bunch, defensive tackles Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr. stand out as big misses, with running back Quinshon Judkins and linebacker Carson Schewsinger also pulling eyeballs.
Both Graham and Hall Jr. missed Sunday's game against the Jets, but both second-years, Judkins and Schewsinger, are new additions. They left MetLife Stadium in boots.
Wednesday Pre-practice injury report - expected DNPs due to injury: Barnett (ankle), Collins (foot), Graham (knee, ankle), Hall (ankle), Howard (knee), T. Jenkins (back), Judkins (ankle), Ryan (calf), Schwesinger (ankle). RB Dylan Sampson has been designated for return and is…
Schwesinger, Judkins, Hall Jr. and Graham will all be the talking points for the injury report, especially because of how important each have been to their respective side of the ball.
But it is impossible to ignore that other relied-upon role players that may not practice much this week.
Defensive end Derek Barnett is working through an ankle injury, while defensive tackle Maliek Collins also likely sits out because of a foot injury. On the offensive end, Tytus Howard is fighting to get healthy following a knee injury he suffered in Sunday's loss to the Jets, while Teven Jenkins remains out with a back injury that has kept him sidelined all season.
Tight end Carsen Ryan, one of the Browns' 2026 NFL Draft picks, is still hoping to return to the field after picking up a calf injury.
If he remains out, the Browns will have weak depth at the tight end position . A move may have to be made before the weekend hits.
While the Browns being without plenty of players on Wednesday casts a lot of doubt on their availability for Sunday, running back Dylan Sampson did return to the field.
He was seen walking around the practice field as his practice window finally opened, following a knee injury that landed him on the injured list after a Week 1 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. He wasn't doing much, as showcased by a video from ESPN's Danile Oyefusi.
However, seeing him at least back on the field is a good sign that he can return in due time.
The Browns not only need to get a bit more productivity from the running back room after the first five weeks of the season, but with Judkins and Rahiem Sanders out , the depth is running thin at the position.
Hopefully, Sampson can begin to ramp back up his workload and make a return to the offense.
Along with Sampson, wideout KC Concepcion returned to practice Wednesday. He was put in concussion protocol following a hit from Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick.
Somehow, someway, he may be ready to go by the time the Browns and Ravens meet.
They'll meet at 1:00 p.m. EST from Huntington Bank Field on Sunday, Oct. 18.

title: Cowboys Hoping to Make Change With Caleb Downs' Role in Week 6 vs. Packers
full_text:
With the Dallas Cowboys having been ravaged by injuries in the secondary this season, it has forced them to deploy rookie defensive back Caleb Downs in a less preferred spot.
Through five games, the Cowboys have seen safeties Malik Hooker, P.J. Locke and Jalen Thompson all get hurt, with Thompson and Locke landing on injured reserve .
As a result, Downs has played almost exclusively at safety the last two weeks, with just eight snaps in the slot in that span.
Head coach Brian Schottenheimer admitted that is not where the Cowboys prefer him to play, but they've had to deploy him there because of the aforementioned injuries.
However, Schottenheimer hinted that the team could look to get Downs back into the slot, where he played the majority of his snaps over the first three contests.
“That’s not the design for Caleb,” Schottenheimer said of Downs at safety, according to Joseph Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News . “We want Caleb down near the line of scrimmage.”
“We want him around the ball," he added. "We want him playing nickel, but because we’re so beat up at safety, he’s had to play back there and we want to try to get him more involved and he’s able to make a lot more plays when he’s up around the line of scrimmage."
As you would expect, Downs says he is, well, down for whatever the Cowboys want him to do, and for whatever gets him around the ball more.
“Either one,” Downs said. “Wherever the ball is at. So if I get to be around the ball more at nickel, then that’s what it is.”
With the Packers' ability to attack downfield , Downs might actually be near the ball more in Week 6 if he plays at safety, but otherwise having him at the line of scrimmage will typically get him more regularly involved.
Not only does that give Downs more coverage opportunities, but he can also be deployed to blitz more often.
Schottenheimer has promised change this week and we suspect one of those changes will be putting Downs back in the slot, where he can make a bigger impact.
How the Cowboys will cover for moving Downs back to the slot remains to be seen, though, as Locke and Thompson are still sidelined due to injury.
The Cowboys have some options when it comes to a running mate for Hooker, who will start at one safety spot. Markquese Bell and Alijah Clark are ready to go, and Dallas has Juanyeh Thomas as another option on the practice squad.
Downs will still see snaps at safety in base defense, but we'd expect to see more snaps in the slot on Sunday.

title: 4 Dallas Cowboys Facing Make-or-Break Game in Week 6 vs. Green Bay Packers
full_text:
Change is afoot for the Dallas Cowboys going into their Week 6 game against the Green Bay Packers.
During the week, head coach Brian Schottenheimer revealed there would be some "roster adjustments" following the embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last week.
"I’m not going to get to a bunch of them. Obviously, there’s a competitive advantage. But there’ll be some roster adjustments you guys will see. Some will be more noticeable than others, and some will be subtle as you look at it," Schottenheimer said, per Tommy Yarrish of DallasCowboys.com .
With the Cowboys looking for solutions to fix their issues on the defensive side of the ball, players who have been struggling this season are on the chopping block more now than ever.
On the flip side, changes might lead to increased opportunity for other players and they must make the most of it or else their opportunity may not last long.
Here's four Cowboys who land in either one of those categories.
Bland is a weekly staple on this list and that isn't changing after his horrific performance against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. We keep hoping Dallas will make a change with Bland struggling as badly as he is, yet that hasn't happened yet.
But with the Cowboys having strong desire for change this week after the Week 5 debacle, perhaps we see Bland's snaps decreased in Week 6.
If not, another poor performance may finally lead to Bland seeing his role reduced the following week, especially if Cobie Durant finally makes it back from injury.
Ameer Speed and Joey Porter Jr. are questionable , and Durant is out once again, so Revel could see a bigger workload against the Packers.
It's very clear the Cowboys are as open to change as ever and if Revel can play at a high level with whatever snaps he's given, a more robust role could be coming his way.
Lawrence played his best game as a pro in Week 5 and was one of the very few bright spots on the team. The rookie notched his first sack and had two pressures in total.
Schottenheimer stated Lawrence should see more playing time this week versus the Packers as a result of last week's showing.
"He's played very well. I think he's starting to show the flash and the acceleration and the ability to rush the passer that we knew we were getting when we drafted him. I think he had a very good game against Tampa Bay, and you'll see him get more opportunities," Schottenheimer said of Lawrence .
If he steps up to help Dallas' struggling pass-rush, Lawrence will remain in a bigger role. If he doesn't, it might be back to his old one, which was already fairly sizeable.
Miller has been a total disappointment, but at least he has taken accountability for that .
"It's time for me to get rolling, too," Miller said. "I would like to point the finger at myself. If I get two plays, I need to find a way to make an impact on those two plays. If I get 10 (plays), I definitely should be able to have an impact on 10 plays.
"And don't let me get 15 and 20 plays. I have to be able to do something. And this Sunday, I'm just pointing the finger at myself. I have to make an impact with the type of burn that I'm able to get."
Last season, Miller notched his first sack with the Washington Commanders at Lambeau Field. He'll be hoping for a repeat this week or else his already dwindling role might get even smaller or cease to exist entirely.

title: Former Dallas Cowboys Star Criticizes Pointless Players-Only Meeting
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are heading into Sunday night’s matchup with the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field in danger of falling to 2-4 after a woeful start to the season. As a result of these early shortcomings, which is due in large part to having one of the league’s worst defenses, Dallas held a defensive players-only meeting in the days following their embarrassing Week 5 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
There’s been some mixed reactions to the players-only meeting after it became public knowledge. Perhaps it would have been best just to keep the entire ordeal private amongst the team, but too late now.
To no surprise, the Cowboys players and coaches have voiced support for it. Dallas head coach Brian Schottenheimer and defensive coordinator Christian Parker are obviously backing the decision by the players.
However not the same can be said for some analysts or former players.
In an interview with NFL insider Jordan Schultz, former Cowboys wide receiver Keyshawn Johnson didn't hold back his honest thoughts when asked about the players-only meeting, as it clearly is a topic he has some strong feelings about.
“Oh God. You’re so dead," Johnson said. "Why would I show up to talk about, what? What are you gonna tell me that I don’t already know? I already know we’re not good. I already know there’s a number of players on the team that are not living up to their billing. Why do I wanna sit through an hour of that, having some captains try to tell me something?”
“Mike Tomlin is correct. You’re done! This is a Hall of Fame coach telling you, this ain’t me. It came from a Hall of Fame coach.”
Here's a look at Johnson's entire reaction:
I asked former #Cowboys WR Keyshawn Johnson about the players-only meeting and what it means for HC Brian Schottenheimer: “You’re so dead. … Mike Tomlin is correct. You’re done.” 👀 pic.twitter.com/vwexKQvXYF
Those are certainly some harsh words from a player like Johnson, but they could end up being proven right if the Cowboys don't fix things on defense. Based on what we've seen so far this season, that appears unlikely to happen.
Johnson played two seasons in Dallas, appearing in 32 games (30 starts) while posting 141 catches for 1,820 yards and 12 touchdowns.
As for the current Cowboys, they will have a chance to prove that something as silly as a players-only meeting can pay off when they visit the Packers on Sunday Night Football.

title: Stephen Jones Contradicts Dallas Cowboys Injury Report on Joey Porter Jr's Week 6 Status
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are back on the road for Week 6, as the team aims to get back in the win column against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field in primetime .
After last week's disaster against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , Dallas needs a strong effort to show signs of progress and improvement, especially on the defensive side of the ball. One thing that would help is the return of star cornerback Joey Porter Jr .
Porter impressed in his Dallas debut after the team landed him in a trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers, but he was a last-minute inactive last week after falling ill hours before what would have been his home debut with the Cowboys.
However, Porter is listed as "questionable" on the team's official injury report for Week 6 because of an ankle injury that popped up on the injury report this week.
While Porter is listed as questionable, Cowboys EVP Stephen Jones seems to believe there are no questions about whether Porter will take the field on Sunday Night Football.
Jones made his weekly appearance on 105.3 The Fan and made it clear that there are no concerns about Porter holding out like he did with the Steelers because of a lingering "back injury," and indicated the cornerback will be on the field against Green Bay.
“Oh, absolutely. I think he’s all in. He wants to be out there," Jones told 105.3 The Fan, according to Jon Machota of The Athletic. ",He was sick, he couldn’t play last week with the flu.
"But he obviously played in our first game, and I think he’s fired up about what he can do to help us win against the Packers .”
For the sake of the defense, which is ranked No. 30 overall entering Week 6, getting Porter on the field would be a major upgrade for the ailing secondary, which has ruled starting cornerback Cobie Durant out for the game. So, hopefully, Jones proves to be correct, and Porter will help the team leave Lambeau with a win.
Kickoff between the Cowboys and Packers at Lambeau Field is set for 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and streaming on Peacock, with Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth in the booth, while Melissa Stark and Kaylee Hartung will provide updates from the sideline.

title: Cowboys' Mike Pettine Officially Arrives, Details How He'll Help Christian Parker
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys made some shake-ups to the defensive staff ahead of the team's Week 6 primetime showdown against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field .
Dallas hired former Cleveland Browns head coach and Packers defensive coordinator Mike Pettine to serve as a senior defensive analyst under defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Pettine will be helping Parker formulate weekly game plans and will bring some much-needed experience to the defensive staff.
Pettine and the Cowboys have been in conversations about a potential role on Parker's staff since the spring, but he wanted some time away to relax and enjoy time with his family, even if some Cowboys beat writers want to use Pettine's arrival to drum up drama .
But when the Cowboys called a second time, Pettine couldn't say no.
Pettine and Parker previously worked together in Green Bay, so there is a sense of trust and familiarity. As Pettine said when speaking to the media on Friday for the first time: “When somebody you care about reaches out, I just felt like I needed to answer the call.”
New Cowboys senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine said he’s here to support Christian Parker and Brian Schottenheimer. On gameday he’ll be in the booth as “another set of eyes.” On Dallas’ defensive issues: “It’s a lot of little things.” pic.twitter.com/acrIAadXs5
While Parker will remain on the sidelines during game days, Pettine will be his eyes in the booth. Pettine knows that there is along way to go for the Cowboys' defense, but because of his experience he will be bringing a wealth of knowledge on what not to do.
" I think that’s key, is learning from others’ mistakes ," Pettine said. "As much as you think you’re prepared for it, you’re really not until you get into it. And I think that’s where I’ll be able to help.”
Because Pettine is joining the operation late, he knows that he has a lot to catch up, but he's confident he will be able to help the team along the way.
“It’s  been a busy week, but when somebody you care about reaches out — I just felt I needed to answer the call," Pettine added. “I'm just trying to hit the ground running here, and I feel like I'm trying to sip water from a fire hose, but trying to get caught up on all the film and make observations here and there.
“I'm just here to support [Parker], both him and Schotty, and the rest of the defensive staff, in any way I can.”
Hopefully, the addition of Pettine will help the Cowboys' as they look for a midseason turnaround. Dallas will also benefit from key several key players returning from injury, after a flurry of injuries plagued the roster throughout the first five weeks of the season.
There is still a long way to go, but luckily, the Cowboys are showing an effort to improve and they are bringing in a man who everyone is comfortable with. Their first opportunity to show improvement will come on Sunday Night Football against Pettine and Parker's former team.

title: Caleb Downs Responds to Cowboys Legend Saying Dallas is 'Hopeless'
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys legend Michael Irvin ripped into his former team after the dreadful loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 5 and Caleb Downs has shared his thoughts on one of Irvin's comments in particular.
While appearing on ESPN's "First Take" last week, Irvin went in on the Cowboys, saying things look "hopeless" in Dallas after the Cowboys fell victim to a classic trap game.
I was sitting there saying, this is, this is ugly. And it looks hopeless. They played poorly,” Irvin said.
Most, if not all Cowboys fans would agree with Irvin's sentiment about feeling hopeless after losing to an 0-4 team that was starting an undrafted rookie quarterback.
On the latest episode of his "Downs 2 Business" podcast, Downs was asked about Irvin's comments admitted he tries to ignore the negativity surrounding the team, whether it's from Irvin or anyone else on the outside.
"I try not to look at stuff like that as much as I can," Downs said. "It's not going to be very helpful."
That's probably a winning strategy. After all, soaking up a bunch of negativity isn't going to fix an NFL defense.
In regard to what the Cowboys need to do to improve on that side of the ball, Downs mentioned playing with more energy.
"We know we need to play with more energy, more passion about what we're doing and then go ahead and do what we need to do," Downs added. "You have to find ways to get yourself energized to do whatever it is, whether you're working at CVS or playing in the National Football League. Whatever it is, you gotta find a way to have energy and we gotta do that at a high level."
The Cowboys already have coaching and talent issues on defense. I guess we can include an energy problem, also.
Talk about a terrible trio of problems to have.
That wasn't all Irvin had to say about the Cowboys after last week's loss.
He ripped Dak Prescott for his reaction to the heckler who drew the ire of the Cowboys quarterback and said Dallas should have shown that much fight against the Bucs.
"When that guy yelled 'embarrassing,' he was talking about you got everybody hoping and waiting that this is going to be different and it came out the same damn way it has always been over the last 30 years," Irvin said. "I had no issues with that man yelling 'embarrassing' because it was embarrassing."
"And I always say, you can have fight in you, make sure you know who and when to fight," he added. "And fighting (the embarrassing guy) was not the damn fight. Fighting them boys on the football field was the fight. And you ran from that fight."
Head coach Brian Schottenheimer promised changes after last week's loss and we have already seen one: Dallas hired veteran defensive coach Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant.
Another change we're likely, Schottenheimer said, is more snaps for rookie Malachi Lawrence .
We'd also like to see Downs back in the slot, where we believe he'd make a bigger impact. Downs has been playing safety lately thanks to injuries at the position.
The most important change the Cowboys need to make is the benching of DaRon Bland , who has one of the very worst cornerbacks in the NFL this season.

title: 2 Dallas Cowboys Starters Tabbed 'Longshots' to Play in Week 6
full_text:
Injuries have once again been a problem for the Dallas Cowboys this season, especially on the defensive side of the ball. That's not set to change as they prepare to take on the Green Bay Packers on Sunday Night Football in Week 6.
While speaking with reporters on Friday, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer gave an update on cornerback Cobie Durant and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who are both dealing with hamstring injuries. According to Coach Schotty, both players are currently "longshots" to take the field this Sunday against Green Bay.
Overshown was injured during their Week 1 loss to the New York Giants and has yet to return to action. As for Durant, he was injured in Week 2, when accidentally stepped on by safety Markquese Bell .
There was a brief moment when the Cowboys seemed encouraged about the possibility of Overshown returning in Week 5 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. When he was unable to play on Thursday Night Football, the attention turned to Week 6. Again, there was some early optimism .
Overshown was limited in practice on Thursday, but just one day later, Schottenheimer is throwing cold water on his chances of playing. Overshown has been a game-changer since being selected out of Texas, but has had a hard time staying healthy.
Dallas has been abysmal in the secondary this season, and even with Joey Porter Jr. in line for a larger role this weekend, there are still major concerns.
DaRon Bland seems to have lost a step, as well as his confidence. He's become a liability in coverage, but there aren't many other options. Shavon Revel Jr. hasn't done enough to steal a starting spot.
One player who could take snaps away from Bland is Durant. Signed as a free agent this offseason, Durant played in 17 games with 15 starts for the Los Angeles Rams in 2025. He had three interceptions and seven pass deflections in the regular season, and added another three picks and seven pass breakups in their three playoff games.
In his limited experience with Dallas, Durant has a PFF grade of  55.6 , which is significantly better than Bland's 45.3 and Revel's 41.7. Getting him back in the fold could be quite the boost as they continue to look for answers with their struggling defense.

title: Who Experts Are Picking For Dallas Cowboys vs. Green Bay Packers in Week 6
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers enter their Week 6 contest at Lambeau Field on Sunday night coming off very different Week 5 showings.
The Cowboys fell victim to the trap game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Dallas was heavily favored, and rightly so, as Tampa Bay was 0-4 and starting an undrafted rookie quarterback. But Dallas failed to so much as show up and fell to 2-3 on the year.
The Packers, on the other hand, absolutely throttled the Chicago Bears in what was far and away Green Bay's best game on both sides of the ball. Now, all of the talk of the Packers' demise has been shelved.
These two teams squared off last season and battled to a 40-40 tie. Before that, Green Bay had beaten Dallas in eight of their last nine meetings.
Will the Packers continue their dominance over the Cowboys? Or will Dallas flip the script and pull out a win? Here's what experts from different media outlets think.
The biggest problem for the Cowboys in this game is Green Bay's ability to move the ball through the air .
The Packers had struggled offensively over the first four contests, but they found their rhythm in Week 5 by torching the Bears with the deep ball.
Defending the pass has been a major issue for the Cowboys this season, with Dallas ranking 21st. That doesn't even do justice for how bad it has really been. The Cowboys' ranking would be even worse if teams weren't abusing Christian Parker's unit on the ground.
The good news for the Cowboys is the Packers haven't been able to run the football with any semblance of success, although Dallas presents a perfect get-right opportunity with their league-worst showing against the run this season.
Green Bay has also struggled to stop the run, ranking 24th, but the Cowboys aren't running the ball like they did last season and it remains to be seen if they can capitalize on Green Bay's woes.
Another problem for the Cowboys is the Packers are giving up the fifth-fewest yards per game through the air and if that holds true this week and the run game doesn't get on track, it's going to be tough sledding for Dallas' offense.
Joey Porter Jr.'s return is going to make a dent in Dallas' passing game struggles, but the Cowboys still have the other side of the field to defend and DaRon Bland has proven incapable of doing that. The slot is a another concern if Caleb Downs is still playing most or all of his snaps at safety like he has amid the Cowboys' slew of injuries at safety.
The Cowboys will get their points to keep this game close, but we're highly skeptical Dallas' secondary and pass-rush will do enough to keep Green Bay's passing attack at bay enough to emerge victorious.
Final score prediction: Packers 30, Cowboys 27

title: Joe Milton Poached Off Dallas Cowboys' Practice Squad By Division Rival
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys no longer have a quarterback on their practice squad thanks to a division rival.
According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz , the Philadelphia Eagles are signing Joe Milton off the Cowboys' practice squad.
"Breaking: The Eagles are signing QB Joe Milton off the Cowboys practice squad and to their 53-man roster, per sources," Schultz reported on Friday.
The Eagles poaching Milton comes in the wake of the Eagles losing quarterback Jalen Hurts for at least one game.
Philadelphia announced on Thursday that Hurts has been ruled out for Week 6 due to a superficial blood clot in his calf.
"On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday's game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority," the Eagles said Thursday.
There is currently no timeline for Hurts' return, which means the Cowboys may not face him in Week 7 when the two teams meet in Philly. That also means the Cowboys could face Milton in that contest if backup Tanner McKee struggles in Week 6.
Milton competed for the Cowboys' backup quarterback job with Sam Howell during the offseason in what was nothing short of a back-and-forth battle.
Howell was more consistent during training camp, but Milton shined over the first two preseason games and clearly outperformed Howell while showing improvement.
However, Howell had the stronger showing in preseason Week 3 and that might have made the difference. Milton was initially kept on the 53-man roster along with Howell, but the Cowboys ended up cutting the Tennessee product with the need to add a third running back.
“We felt like carrying two quarterbacks was the best way for us to strengthen our roster," head coach Brian Schottenheimer said .
After Milton cleared waivers, the Cowboys brought him back on the practice squad, where he had been ever since. Milton admitted he was shocked with the Cowboys' decision to cut him.
“It was shocking. But it’s life. You got to be able to live with it and deliver blows back when it’s time," Milton said .
“Somewhat, but not really," Milton added when asked if it was a hard decision to return to Dallas. "I have a lot of relationships here and guys I trust with my development.”
Now, Milton may have an opportunity to get some revenge on his old team, and that opportunity could come as soon as Week 7.

title: Cowboys Confirm Controversial Reporting Structure With Mike Pettine, Christian Parker
full_text:
With the Dallas Cowboys having major issues on the defensive side of the ball this season, the team has brought in veteran defensive coach Mike Pettine to try and help fix things.
Pettine was hired as a senior defensive assistant and head coach Brian Schottenheimer initially made it clear that his purpose is to help defensive coordinator Christian Parker.
"Had a chance to work with Pettine for a number of years, along with the Jets, and he's gonna be here in a role to support everything that [Christian Parker] is leading and guiding, and we are really, really excited," Schottenheimer said.
However, how the Cowboys plan on structuring the dynamic with Pettine and Parker is interesting, to say the least.
On Friday, Schottenheimer told 105.3 The Fan that Pettine will be reporting directly to him and not to Parker, which makes it sound like Pettine is much more than just a consultant.
"Mike reports directly to me," Schottenheimer said. "Obviously, he works side-by-side with the entire staff, all three phases, but again, the most important thing for him right now is to be a sounding board for Christian."
This kind of structure effectively places Pettine above Parker in the pecking order and takes a lot of the power away from Parker. Now, one could argue that's deserved after the struggles on the defense, but it doesn't change the reality of the situation.
There's also the awkward dynamic that Pettine has to report what he is hearing and seeing from Parker, which could create trust issues between the two.
Maybe this isn't a big deal because Pettine and Parker have a prior relationship from their days together with the Green Bay Packers, but we definitely can't say that for sure.
The midseason addition of Pettine was already a bad look for the struggling defensive coordinator, but the reporting structure only makes things look worse for Parker.
Parker was even asked if the addition of Pettine was a "save the day" hire, but Parker declined to answer that question .
"I don't need to respond to that," Parker said on Thursday.
During the week, the Cowboys weren't on the same page when it comes to whether Parker would be on the sideline or in the booth for Week 6 against the Green Bay Packers.
Owner Jerry Jones said he would be in the latter spot, but Schotty initially said nothing had been decided yet and Parker himself said he would "most likely" be on the sideline .
But Schottenheimer confirmed on Friday that Parker is going to be on the field and Pettine will be up in the booth .
