title: Jensen's Judgment: Bench Bo Nix? Don't Make Me Laugh
full_text:
Hot on the heels of defeating the defending Super Bowl champions on primetime , questions are being asked around the Mile High City about whether the Denver Broncos should bench Bo Nix.
On the local airwaves, the blogs, the podwaves, or just about any social media comment section, people are seriously advocating — or at least contemplating — whether the Broncos would be better off with Nix on the bench , even if it's just for a game or two to give him a mental and emotional breather.
I can only sit back in amazement at such questions. How quickly people seem to forget what the Broncos were before Nix arrived in the 2024 NFL draft.
The Broncos went eight long years without making the playoffs after winning the Super Bowl, which was an NFL first. One quarterback after another — from first-round picks to high-dollar free agents to big-name trade acquisitions — went through the carousel in Denver over that time period.
This team couldn't get the quarterback or head coach right. Then the Broncos made the fateful decision to hire Sean Payton , acquiring his coaching rights from the New Orleans Saints after the 2022 season.
Payton began to put things in order, but even he couldn't much out of Russell Wilson. After Payton benched him, the Broncos released him in the spring of 2024 with a then-NFL-record $85 million dead-money hit to the salary cap.
From there, Payton scouted the 2024 draft class, and identified Nix as his guy. The Broncos drafted Nix with the No. 12 overall pick in the first round, and he would go on to vanquish Jarrett Stidham and Zach Wilson in a training competition to become the first rookie quarterback to be the day-one starter since John Elway in 1983 — a harbinger of things to come.
Nix's rookie year was ugly at times, especially early on, and while he bumped his head along the way, he soon had the Broncos on the winning track. He almost beat the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium, and later actually pulled it off at home, and would go on to win 10 games as a rookie starter.
The Broncos qualified for the playoffs, snapping their near decade-long drought. The upstart Broncos were quickly bounced in the wildcard round by the Buffalo Bills, but the floodgates had opened.
Nix ended his rookie season injured, playing with fractured vertebrae in his back for the entire stretch run. Finishing as a Pro Bowl alternate, he was actually invited to the Games, but declined, deciding instead to undergo a " minor " procedure on an undisclosed body part unrelated to the transverse process fractures in his back.
Nix was healthy and good to go in time to kick off OTAs, and the Broncos hit the 2025 season. If you recall, the Broncos won their season opener last year in ugly fashion, then lost two straight on the road.
Sitting at 1-2 for the second straight season, it wasn't looking good. But then Nix found his groove with a big win over the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 4, and the Broncos went on an 11-game winning streak.
Along the way, the Broncos knocked off the defending World Champion Philadelphia Eagles on the road, vanquished the Houston Texans and their fearsome defense on the road, beat a desparate Patrick Mahomes-led Chiefs team at Mile High, and steamrolled the Green Bay Packers at home as underdogs.
Nix won 14 games in Year 2, dethroned the Chiefs in the AFC West, and helped the Broncos secure the No. 1 playoff seed. But he wasn't done.
That was supposed to be Josh Allen's year when the playoffs rolled around. With no Mahomes, Lamar Jackson, or Joe Burrow, Allen and the Buffalo Bills were supposed to romp all over the Broncos in the divisional round, and cruise to a Super Bowl berth — but that's not how it shook out.
Nix turned in a terrific performance against the Bills in the high-stakes environment of single elimination, passing for 279 yards and three touchdowns, with an interception, and rushing for 29 yards. The Broncos took the ball away from Allen five times, and ultimately won in overtime, 33-30.
That massive win over Buffalo came with a heavy price, as Nix suffered a fractured ankle on the third-to-last play of the game, ending his season. Hosting the AFC championship game, thanks to Nix's magical season, the Broncos tried to get past the New England Patriots with Jarrett Stidham under center, but he was overwhelmed by the moment, the opponent, and the weather.
In six games this season, we haven't seen the 2025 version of Nix since January 17 — or at least, not the full version. He's shown flashes, but he's looked... different.
Nix seems hesitant and anxious — like a deer caught in the headlights, at times. But he's also had signature moments, like his comeback against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 2 and Los Angeles Rams in Week 3.
Against the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night, Nix passed for just 107 yards on 27 attempts, with his longest completion being a 16-yard check-down to RJ Harvey. But without the two touchdown drives he led in the first half, the Broncos' suffocating defense wouldn't have been able to pin its ears back and get after Sam Darnold all night.
Amid all the talk of benching Nix, few people mention how the Seahawks' defense is yet to allow a single opponent to eclipse 200 yards passing this season, or how they entered Week 6 as the NFL leader in takeaways. For that matter, I don't hear too many people pointing to the exceedingly tough schedule the Broncos have faced through the first six weeks.
The Broncos have faced the NFL's toughest schedule thus far, but they're 4-2. Every opponent the Broncos have beaten won at least 12 games and were in the playoffs last year. And each of those opponents fielded a ferocious defense.
The Chiefs are the only non-playoff team the Broncos have played this year, and a quarter of the way into the season, they've clearly reestablished themselves as one of the NFL's elite.
Perhaps Nix's ankle isn't as fully recovered as the Broncos have led us to believe. Maybe he's still feeling the psychological effects of the injury.
If so, Nix has sure done a heck of a job to overcome it and do just enough — and sometimes more than enough — to keep the Broncos on a winning track.
Bench Bo Nix? Don't make me laugh.
If you think for a second that Denver would have been able to beat the Jaguars, Rams, Chargers, or Seahawks with Stidham under center, think again. Against the NFL's cream-of-the-crop defenses, he would have folded like a lawn chair, especially after the first 15-20 scripted plays.
And that Mile High Magic that Nix is able to conjure so often? Stidham has no such wand. There would be no iconic comebacks. The Broncos would be 0-6 — maybe 1-5 — but I don't think they beat the Chargers in L.A. with Stidham at quarterback.
Meanwhile, despite his imperfections and ongoing slump, Nix has the Broncos at 4-2 and through the worst of their schedule. There's a tough game in two weeks at home against the Chiefs, but making a change at quarterback right now would only torpedo the Broncos' 2026 ambitions, and squander the benefits of what their hard-fought 4-2 start has gifted them.
The Broncos are about to go on a run. I'm not predicting an 11-game winning streak, but the schedule is about to open up in a big way.
This team may have faced the NFL's toughest schedule so far, but from here on out, the Broncos get the fourth-easiest slate of opponents, per Pro Football Focus .
Hardest Strength of Schedule this season to date    remaining Broncos       1st             29th Pats               2nd           27th Rams            3rd            13th Bills               4th… pic.twitter.com/4D9CxPovnS
Nix will get the opportunity to find his footing and break out of this slump, especially if Payton can get to the bottom of the Broncos' run-game inefficiencies . If the Broncos made a change at quarterback, they'd quickly find themselves back at .500, and then what? Go crawling back to the quarterback who won you 28 games in 40 starts over two-and-a-quarter seasons?
No. Nix is the Broncos' guy,…

title: What Broncos’ Snap Counts Revealed in OT Win Over Seahawks
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have seemingly perfected the art of winning ugly. We saw it at times last season, but it's become a regular theme in 2026.
A win is a win, though. And in the NFL, nobody should apologize for victory.
The Broncos defeated the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night 17-14 in an overtime thriller. One of the most impressive aspects of Denver's fourth win of the season was the way its defense overcame the injuries to several key players to terrorize Sam Darnold all night long and pick him off twice.
Bo Nix and the Broncos' offensive line did not miss a snap, playing 60 snaps against the Seahawks. Beyond the starting five, depth lineman Alex Palczewski saw the field for just one snap.
As for everybody else, that's why we're here. Let's examine the Broncos' snap counts for what gleanings they can offer.
Dobbins carried the ball 17 times for 41 yards and a touchdown, but Seattle made him fight and scrape for every inch, as evidencd by his 2.2 yards-per-carry metric. He did have one really nice 16-yard run that helped set up the Broncos' second touchdown.
RJ Harvey had six carries for 25 yards and a touchdown, while also catching three passes on four targets for a team-high 31 receiving yards. Dobbins also caught three balls on three targets, but for just five yards.
Badie only received one touch before injurying his thumb, but it was a crucial six-yard gain on 4th-&-3 that extended the Broncos' first touchdown drive. Prentice saw a handful of snaps, but no touches.
The Broncos' receivers ran a lot of yards for very little production. Too many wasted routes as Nix's slump continues, but Sutton led the way in snap share, with Waddle right behind him.
Waddle led the team with seven targets, but he only caught four for 24 yards. He was open often, but Nix either didn't see him or was hesitant to push the ball. Probably both.
The Broncos may be 4-2 , but you have to wonder how Nix's slump is affecting the attitude of Waddle and Sutton. These are high-profile receivers who are barely touching the ball, despite running a high volume of routes.
Sutton only had two catches on three targets for 19 yards, but he drew a pass-interference penalty that set the Broncos up on the one-yard line. Franklin was only targeted once, catching it for two yards, while Mims earned four targets, including one deep pass that Nix put on the money.
It looked like Mims was interfered with but no flag was thrown. Humphrey did not touch the ball.
For the first time in a few weeks, Engram was not the Broncos' top snap-getter at tight end. Trautman beat him out by two, but Engram was targeted twice by nice, catching them both for 13 yards.
Trautman and Adkins were mostly blockers in their snaps, and neither did a good job against that tough Seahawks front seven.
The Broncos' D-line was relentless on Thursday night. Allen led in snap share, but Roach finished with the most quarterback pressures (six).
Uwazurike had a good game, too, pressuring Darnold four times, while D.J. Jones notched three pressures. Sai'vion Jones had two pressures and a hit on Darnold, while also getting his big mits up to bat down a pass.
Allen finished with a half-sack on four pressures.
Although he only finished with a half-sack — split with Allen — this was one of Bonitto's best pass-rushing games as a pro. His spin move was devastating, and he was a constant thorn in Darnold's side.
Hats off to Robinson, Elliss, and Tillman, too, as they all made an impact against Seattle. Robinson led the way with six pressures and a sack, but Elliss was able to finally notch his first QB takedown of the season, finishing with six pressures himself before suffering an ankle injury near the end of regulation.
Jonathon Cooper is headed back from the commissioner's exempt list, but this rush linebacker room is in the zone right now. The Broncos will be in a quandary when it comes to deciding who to sit on game day.
Singleton turned in one of his best games as a Bronco . He was one of three Broncos defenders who played 100% of snaps, and he finished with 13 tackles and three pressures, while allowing only two completions for 11 yards in coverage.
Strnad played well, too, finishing with four tackles and a half-sack. He wasn't targeted in coverage.
Barron played 100% of snaps and while he gave up nine receptions for 121 yards in coverage, he was targeted 12 times and had to cover Jaxon Smith-Njigba on five of them. It was a tough assignment, but Barron played physical, sticky coverage, and on most of the completions he allowed, he was right there to either get a hand on the ball or make the immediate tackle, but he did give up a long of 42 yards. Again, though, his coverage was tight.
Abrams-Draine answered the bell, though he too was targeted in the double digits. On 14 targets, he allowed eight completions for 94 yards, but he made Darnold pay late in the fourth quarter, undercutting a route to pick him off. Abrams-Draine's tackling left much to be desired.
McMillian was magnificent. He gave up three completions on six targets for just 16 yards, but had five solo tackles and a sack. His interception in overtime helped Denver seal the win.
Moss started the game, but only played 20 snaps. He should be back for Week 7, though I doubt Patrick Surtain II joins him.
With Talanoa Hufanga out, the Broncos relied on Jones and he answered the bell, finishing with eight tackles. He was targeted once, a completion that went for just one yard.
Rapp was elevated from the practice squad into the starting lineup, just as I suspected with Hufanga out. Technically, Key got the start, but he quickly took a back seat to Rapp, who played well in coverage and against the run in his first game as a Bronco.
Rapp finished with six tackles and was only targeted once, allowing a completion for 11 yards. It was good to have his experience on the back end of the defense because it helped prevent and deter some big plays.
Key also played well as the third safety and big nickel, finishing with three tackles. He gave up completions on both of his targets (for just nine yards), but was good in coverage. The Broncos could get by with this safety trio for some time if they had to.

title: OLB Jonathon Cooper's Potential Return A Huge Boon for Broncos Defense
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have played arguably the best brand of defensive football in the NFL over the last two weeks. And they're about to get even better.
ESPN reported Friday that Broncos starting outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper was removed from the commisioner's exempt list, giving him a chance to return for the team's Week 7 road game against the Arizona Cardinals.
Cooper -- who was arrested twice on domestic violence-related charges over the summer -- is still subject to punishment from the league "at a later date" under the Personal Conduct Policy.
"The Broncos will get a one-week roster exemption for Cooper, who can now return to practice. He could then be added to the 53-man roster at any point over the next week and play Oct. 25 against the Cardinals," ESPN's Jeff Legwold reported.
"His time on the exempt list -- the first six weeks of the regular season -- would count toward any league-mandated suspension in the future. He would, however, if suspended, have to return the weekly game checks he has received because suspensions from the personal conduct policy are without pay."
Cooper has yet to play this season but previously was permitted to attend Broncos team meetings and use the strength-and-conditioning and workout facilities.
The Broncos have primarily split the pass-rushing duties in Cooper's stead, rotating Jonah Elliss and Que Robinson opposite top OLB Nik Bonitto. The three combined for 2.5 sacks amid Thursday night's 17-14 victory over the Seattle Seahawks .
Though not considered among the sport's elite edge rushers, Cooper has quietly accumulated 31.5 sacks and 63 quarterback hits across 81 career appearances for the Broncos. He's also regarded as the defense's best run-stopping OLB.
Denver did a marvelous job against the Seattle offense in Week 6, holding the reigning Super Bowl champions to 113 yards on the ground while sacking QB Sam Darnold six times and forcing three turnovers during the overtime win.
"Defensively, we were magnificent. I don’t know how many times we hit the quarterback, we got three takeaways. ... Takeaways were huge," head coach Sean Payton said after the game. "You get a takeaway in overtime like that, that was a difference. Field position, all of that. They were fantastic.”
Cooper's immediate availability would allow the Broncos to insert him back into the starting 11 while allowing Elliss, Robinson, and Dondrea Tillman to come off the bench in situational roles.
Basically, the rich are about to get richer.

title: Former Broncos QB Takes Shot at Bo Nix, Deletes Post Amid Backlash
full_text:
You know the Bo Nix pile-on is reaching epic proportions when former teammates are coming out of the woodwork to join in.
After NFL On Prime 's Ryan Fitzpatrick called Nix's performance against the Seattle Seahawks "almost disrespectful to the quarterback position," former Denver Broncos quarterback Ben DiNucci decided to weigh in with an X post that he deleted shortly after.
"About time someone said it," DiNucci wrote in response to Fitzpatrick's comments. "Bo looks disinterested, checked out, and like there are 500 places he would rather be than on a football field every week. I am a fan of the Broncos and wish them the best, but I would rather watch paint dry right now than their offense play football."
Not long after deleting this post, DiNucci took to X to offer an apology of sorts for doing "a disservice to Bo and guys in that locker room who were my teammates."
"QB is the most scrutinized position in all of sports and takes a certain type of individual to be able to go out there week in and week out and ignore the noise and play ball," DiNucci wrote. "Bo is a winner, competitor, and leader of that team. Sure, he isn’t playing up to his standards right now, and he will be the first one to tell you that, but he doesn’t need former teammates and people who played the position speculating on what he’s going through/seeing."
I put out a tweet this morning about Bo and the state of the Broncos offense I deleted that tweet.. call me whatever you want idc it doesn’t bother me I was speaking on things that I don’t know to be true and I get that’s part of my job now being in the media but it felt like…
There's more to DiNucci's apology, but that covers the bases. Someone must have gotten to the former journeyman because he changed his tune faster than a chameleon changes colors.
Nix strikes me as the forgiving type. But that doesn't mean he'll be forgetting DiNucci's shade any time soon.
DiNucci, 29, had two stints with the Broncos under head coach Sean Payton — one in 2023 and again this past January after Nix suffered a fractured ankle in the playoffs. DiNucci has since begun a media career after six years in the NFL — mostly as a backup or practice squad option.
DiNucci was originally a 2020 seventh round pick of the Dallas Cowboys out of James Madison. He has exactly three NFL games on his resume with one start.
Nix has suddenly become the most hated man in the NFL. The Broncos are 4-2, weathering the gauntlet of their initial six-game schedule about as well as anyone could have hoped.
It's an impressive achievement, especially given the level of opposing offenses and defenses the Broncos have faced. All four of Denver's wins have come against opponents who won 12 or more games last season and made the playoffs.
However, Nix has not looked like his pre-ankle injury self this season. Whether it's due to the level of competition, the change in play-caller initially (first four games), the supporting cast around him, and/or lingering effects of his ankle injury, his performance has been nowhere close to what we saw in 2025.
We've seen flashes of the 2025 Nix, including in the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars and Los Angeles Rams, but he's looked hesitant and anxious, like he's overwhelmed for some reason and pressing. Nobody knows exactly what's going on with him, but he's still done enough to weather the initial six-game storm, thanks, in part, to some heavy lifting by the Broncos' defense.
Nix is aware of his and the offense's struggles, and while he claims he's unsure exactly why the Broncos have failed to launch on his side of the ball, he believes the schedule they've faced is part of it. But he also expressed confidence that he and the Broncos have time to turn the ship around.
"I think as we go, as we continue to go throughout the season, we’ll just find ways to get better and better," Nix said after Thursday night's 17-14 overtime win over Seattle. "I do think you have to [attribute it to] the schedule, just the first six games we knew were going to be tough. To come out 4-2 with really a complete team effort in all six games, it’s a complete team effort to get four of those wins... we’ll figure out ways to continue to improve.”
Nix often says he doesn't pay any attention to social media or outside noise, but the din is becoming louder by the week. I believe Nix's conservatism and hesitancy this season stem from his coaches preaching ball security in the face of game-planning for one top-ranked defense after another, but there's more to the story, for sure.
Something is going on between the ears, and it could simply be the lingering effects of his ankle injury. When a player suffers a major injury, it takes time for the physical injury to heal and for the psyche to recover and trust the body.
Those two healing processes don't always happen at exactly the same time, so even though Nix's ankle was healed enough for him to start training camp on time and not miss a single snap so far this season, it's possible he's not yet healed mentally. Granted, that's me donning the tin-foil and Freudian hat in equal measure, but it's just my take.
Nix will eventually turn the corner on the ankle thing, and when he does, I expect to see him looking much sharper and more poised. For now, though, all the calls to bench him are absolutely not in the realm of the plausible — and I'm hearing them from fans and media alike.
Despite Nix's inconsistent and lackluster play so far, the Broncos are 4-2. Does anyone honestly believe that Jarrett Stidham or Sam Ehlinger would have stood a chance in any of these games?
Nix may look hesitant and the consistency still isn't there, but he's still got the clutch-gene. Not many quarterbacks could come back against Jacksonville and the Rams the way he did, and on the Broncos' two touchdowns drives against the Seahawks — which came in the first half and were the difference in that game — he made some great throws and converted some big third downs.
With Stidham, the Broncos would stand a decent chance with the scripted first 15-20 plays. After that, just as we saw in the AFC championship game, it would get sketchy real, real fast, and you wouldn't get the clutch-time production.
Let's face it: the Broncos view Nix as their franchise quarterback, and he's earned it. He won 24 games in his first two seasons, a division crown, and he had the Broncos on the doorstep of the Super Bowl before getting hurt.
The Broncos are trying to compete for a Super Bowl now and every year in the future. The last thing they're going to do is bench their young franchise quarterback whose confidence may be a bit shaken, only to risk exacerbating it to a point where he might not recover.
Nix remains the Broncos' best option at the moment. For that and many other reasons, Payton is not going to bench his quarterback.
The Broncos are 4-2. In each of Nix's three seasons in Denver, he has defeated the defending Super Bowl champions.
The Broncos now get the benefit of a 'mini-bye,' which gives them three extra days to rest and prepare for Week 7's road trip to face the Arizona Cardinals. It's Denver's first chance to breathe a little bit since the onslaught of this season started, and hopefully it'll do Nix some good and offer Payton the chance to figure out his offense's run-game issues.
DiNucci shot from the hip and slammed a former teammate, painting with such broad strokes that everyone at Broncos HQ felt the brush.

title: Broncos Player Grades vs. Seahawks: Game MVP, Bo Nix Verdict & More
full_text:
The Denver Broncos pulled off an upset at home, defeating the Seattle Seahawks 17-14 in overtime with great defensive play and a strong first-half offense.
The Broncos' second-half offense? Putrid. The Broncos turned in some great individual performances, especially on defense, which ultimately led to the big win.
The offense did enough, but the Broncos can once again thank their defense as they've jumped out to a 4-2 start . This week's player grades reflect how " magnificent " the Broncos' defense played and the tale of two halves from the offense.
Singleton had a great game, flying around the field to make plays against the run and keep the Seahawks' passing game from developing. Some of his coverage drops were right where Sam Darnold intended to go, forcing him to adjust and often giving the pass rush that extra moment to get there.
Harvey works well in space, and the Broncos got him going a few times with screens. What stood out most, though, was his improvement in the run game, particularly his vision, which helped him average 4.2 yards per carry. He still had a couple of bad runs, but on six carries, four were successful, including a one-yard touchdown run.
Nix had a great start, looking poised, confident, and tough, and while the offense struggled in the second half, that early-game production still rang true. However, he didn’t have an answer for the Seahawks' defensive adjustments and began to look frustrated and confused by what he was seeing.
Nix's EPA/Pass in the third and fourth quarters was two of his four lowest EPA/pass quarters of the season
Nik Bonitto | OLB | Grade: 81.7
Charles Cross and Abraham Lucas, the Seahawks' tackles, are still stuck in the spin cycle that Bonitto put them in. Bonitto's pass rush was great, and he made some big plays off his spin move. This was probably his best game when it came to setting up counters and then adjusting when his opponent started to slow him down.
Ja’Quan McMillian | CB | Grade: 78.9
The Seahawks have a tough receiving corps, and the Broncos switched up their defense to account for injuries. McMillian handled the switch and played near an elite level, filling the box score with a sack and an interception while also playing tough against the run.
Garett Bolles | LT | Grade: 74.7
This was Bolles' best game of the season as a run blocker and one of the best as a pass protector. He drew a bad holding penalty, which was an easy call because he had the defender's head wrapped in his arm, but it was one of few negatives on his grade.
Quinn Meinerz | RG | Grade: 73.5
Meinerz was good throughout the game, but he lacked the elite blocking moments we've seen from him in his career, including this season. He didn’t allow any pressures and did well with his run blocking, though he struggled at times against a deep Seahawks defensive line.
Jahdae Barorn | CB | Grade: 36.2
Unfortunately, Barron didn’t have as good a game as McMillian, though his grade drop is largely due to eight negative plays. In the grading system, each play is worth +/- three points, and Barron was minus three on all eight of those plays, for a 24-point drop. Five were coverage plays, and three were against the run.
Kris Abrams-Draine | CB | Grade: 39.8
Abrams-Draine had a similar issue to Barron, with about nine such plays. Without those nine plays, his grade would’ve been 64.2. Seattle picked on Abrams-Draine, though he made a few of his own. Overall, both Barron and Abrams-Draine showed some promise, and while they've definitely stepped up with injuries to Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss , their inexperience has been clear.
Adam Trautman | TE | Grade: 42.1
Trautman's run blocking is inconsistent at best, and he struggled against the Seahawks. His play as a receiver isn’t a redeeming quality, and if he doesn’t turn it around, Denver could quickly regret the extension they signed him to this past offseason.
Evan Engram | TE | Grade: 45.5
Engram isn’t a blocker, and never has been, but he usually makes up for it as a receiver. However, he didn’t make much of an impact against the Seahawks. Part of the reason was how they covered him, but he doesn’t look athletic, especially compared to his 2025 form.

title: Sean Payton Unfazed by Broncos' Offensive Slump After 4-2 Start
full_text:
Despite defeating the reigning World Champions for the third time in his three-year career, Bo Nix is under fire once again.
In the Denver Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks, Nix barely eclipsed the 100-yard passing mark , completing 17-of-27 passes and finishing with a QB rating of 71.1. He didn't push the ball downfield much, and he seemed hesitant again.
However, Nix did not turn the ball over. Amid the ongoing Nix pile-on, it sounds like the Broncos' plan may have been to put some early points on the board and then play it safe against the Seahawks, knowing how good Vance Joseph's defense is.
"Fortunately, we didn’t make any mistakes, and I know that sounds a little conservative, but we felt that was going to be the difference," Sean Payton said post-game.
The Seahawks turned the ball over three times. The Broncos? Zero — despite the Seahawks leading the league in takeaways going into this game.
Apparently, some folks have forgotten just how good that Seahawks defense is. Denver's pair of long drives that culminated in touchdowns were dearly bought, and they proved to be the difference in this game because of how well its defense played against Sam Darnold and the Seahawks.
Last week, Brock Purdy made some off-schedule plays against Seattle in San Francisco's Week 5 win, but Nix wasn't able to follow suit on Thursday night. The Seahawks played a smothering defense with a two-high shell against Denver, and after getting that early two-score lead, Nix wasn't about to push his luck.
"There’s a ton of snaps with that defense where when the quarterback sets, there’s nowhere to go and then there’s those off-schedule plays," Payton said of the Seahawks. "Purdy last week was tremendous with some of those plays, but that was our concern, just timing and rhythm, protection and running it. We’re going to see a lot that we want to clean up.”
The Broncos had some early success on the ground, but the Seahawks' halftime adjustments snuffed out everything Payton tried to do in the second half. The Broncos punted on every second-half possession, but they didn't turn it over. That second part, at least, was according to plan.
The Broncos have been slow starters offensively this season, but since Payton took back the play-calling, they've scored 24 points first-half points over two games. That's not exactly an explosion of production, but it's a clear step in the right direction. Without it, the Broncos don't beat Seattle.
“It’s a different type of game. I’ve said this before, I can’t think of a game where I didn’t want to start fast," Payton said. "In other words, keys to victory... You’re always wanting to start ready, and we were able to do that, but [I] thought we were physical when we needed to be in this game and our crowd was unbelievable.”
Payton knew this game was going to be a rock fight, and he game-planned accordingly. But the Broncos got the job done, thanks to, as Payton described it, the "magnificent" performance of his defense — which sacked Darnold five times and took the ball away thrice — and the offense's early-game efficiency.
Would that Denver's offense could have contributed more in the second half. But Payton is more focused on his team's achievement of getting out to a 4-2 start despite the first six-game gauntlet the NFL handed them.
“The record," Payton said when asked what makes him smile. "Meaning I say that the record, because those wins are hard to get. So we just played a real good team, and I feel like we can continue to improve."
Once again, the Broncos have walked the razor's edge in one-score games, but they're 4-0 this season in such contests. Each win so far will go down in the record books as a one-score victory, and as impressive as it is to see Denver's close-game resilience from last year stretch into 2026, Payton knows that blade could cut the other way just as easily.
"Being at 4-2 right at this little three-day stretch and then get ready next week, that’d be the honest [answer]," Payton said. "And again, I’m a little bit of a realist to know that 4-2 could easily be 2-4.”
The Broncos now get the benefit of a "mini-bye," which simply means that, after playing on a short week, they'll get three extra days of rest before turning all their attention to the Arizona Cardinals next week. The Broncos have played the NFL's toughest schedule through the first six weeks — there's no getting around that fact — but now Payton and company get the chance to exhale a bit.
There is plenty to clean up and fix on the offensive side of the ball, including Nix's ongoing slump , the Broncos' run-game inefficiency, and the lack of even a semblance of downfield passing. That'll be the focus during these three extra days — which is the only break in the action Denver will get until its Week 10 bye.
At 4-2, though, Payton is seeing the forest for the trees. The triumph of that feat, relative to the gauntlet of opponents the Broncos have faced thus far, isn't lost on him.
“There’s still obviously a lot of things that we can improve on, we have to," Payton said. "When you look at last season and then you project what teams are going to be like, it’s hard to do. We found a way to get four wins. We understand that certainly we have to become more effective, more efficient offensively and yet…"
And yet the Broncos keep winning. Go ahead and say it, Coach.
"So obviously it’s easier to make these corrections when you get a win, and I think you guys know me enough by now that you’re never... It was a good win, but there’s a lot of work to do," Payton said.
All the hand-wringing over Nix's slump notwithstanding, the Broncos deserve a ton of credit for getting out to this 4-2 start. They've vanquished four 12-win teams from last year; every opponent the Broncos have beaten was in the playoffs this past January, including the winless Los Angeles Chargers.
Clearly, Nix's conservatism and hesitancy is coming from the coaches, on some level. Obviously, that doesn't explain all of it, but reading between the lines of Payton's comments, he wanted that rock fight with Seattle to shape up the way that it did, and by jumping out to an early 14-3 lead, the game unfolded according to plan and played into the home team's hands.
All this talk about the Broncos benching Nix is delusional. It's not going to happen. Nix is Payton's guy, but the Broncos' veteran coach is also smart enough to know that this model of offensive impotence is not sustainable.
Now that the worst of the schedule is behind him, here's to hoping that Nix will relax a little bit and get back to playing the loose, poised brand of quarterbacking we saw in his first two years in the league. If the Broncos can field even a league-average offense, they'll be unstoppable with this elite defense and sound special teams.

title: 4 Perplexing Takeaways From Broncos' 17-14 OT Win Over Seahawks
full_text:
The Denver Broncos were the home underdog against the Seattle Seahawks , and Sean Payton and company seemed to take that personally.
Offensively, the Broncos put together their best first-half performance of the season against Seattle, scoring 14 points and showing signs of life in the run game, while their defense was outstanding and smothering. Denver walked away with the upset win to move to 4-2, though it wasn’t easy, as the Seahawks surged in the fourth quarter.
With that 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks, the Broncos have now defeated the reigning Super Bowl champions in each of the past three seasons. But as elating as it is for Denver to get through this first six-game gauntlet at 4-2, this win tastes sour for so many fans because of how Nix and the offense played in the second half.
What did we really learn from the Broncos' fourth win of the season? Here are four key takeaways.
The Broncos' best first-half showing of the season came against one of the NFL's best defenses. The Broncos put up 14 points on two touchdowns, with both scores capping extended drives that saw them move the chains and convert third downs.
The offensive line, the running game, and Bo Nix were the best they've been all season — in terms of first-half showings. Was it perfect from the offense?
No. There were still too many dead plays in the run game —16 runs for 52 yards — with J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey logging 15 carries for 46 yards combined. Both had rushing touchdowns, but their run-game consistency was still lacking. That said, it was a major step forward and a positive sign of life for this run game.
In the first half, the Broncos got Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle involved, with the latter catching two and the former catching one. Sutton had a key third-down play and also drew a pass-interference penalty that set up the Broncos' second touchdown on the one-yard line.
Payton has been working for faster starts and wants Nix to " let it rip ." Again, despite some issues, this was at least one step closer, and against a tough defense.
Unfortunately, it didn’t carry over to the second half, especially with the defensive adjustments the Seahawks made, so the offense was still unable to put together a full game.
It wasn’t all pretty from Nix, but it was better than what Denver's got out of him in the previous two weeks. Outside of two throws, he didn’t push the ball deep and took the underneath throws, which is what the Seahawks aim for defensively, but he wasn’t always looking for the checkdown.
On top of that, Nix played tougher in the pocket. He didn't constantly bail on clean pockets or panic at even the slightest pressure. He had multiple first-half throws where he stood tough and tall in the pocket, took some contact, and still delivered a catchable ball, especially on third down.
One-read throws and plenty of option plays made things easier for Nix, like Payton putting the training wheels back on. That isn’t necessarily a bad thing; with Nix's confidence so clearly shaken, he needed these types of plays to build it back up, which hopefully leads to Payton opening up the playbook again later in the season.
The Broncos can't give up on trying to massage Nix through this slump and help him regain his pre-2026 footing. At the same time, they can't become overly reliant on the training-wheels type plays, because it's likely to catch up with them.
The offense faltered a lot in the second half, and some of it was on Nix, though not all of it. Far from it.
Even amid the second-half offensive collapse, Nix showed modest signs of progress, compared to what we saw from him in the Broncos' two-week road trip to California.
The Seahawks' offense has its fair share of issues, with a run game that was almost as bad as the Broncos' for the first five weeks. The Seahawks have also dealt with bad protection issues and questionable quarterback play that led to ball-security issues.
With Patrick Surtain II and Talanoa Hufanga out and Riley Moss limited, there were concerns about how the Broncos would handle the Seahawks' explosive passing game.
Denver shut down the run for most of the game and largely stonewalled Seattle's passing game, outside of a handful of plays. It was an elite showing, especially with three starters out and Moss mostly watching from the sideline.
Kris Abrams-Draine came up with a clutch interception at the end of the fourth quarter, while Jahdae Barron played sticky, physical coverage that helped limit Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the first half. Throw in Ja'Quan McMillian's overtime interception, and I'm not sure anyone could have expected this beleaguered secondary to play any better than it did against the defending champs.
Ja'Quan McMillian read this PERFECTLY. SEAvsDEN on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1igvuDtROG
The Broncos sacked Sam Darnold five times and harrassed him all game long. He battled in the fourth quarter, but eventually, his bad decision-making under pressure came home to roost.
The Broncos have improved each week defensively and have shown they can generate takeaways, which was an issue last year. This is a great unit on the cusp of being elite.
The Broncos will get there if they can fix some of the explosives they've allowed, while improving their run game and tackling inconsistency.
With the Broncos sitting where they are in the standings, it's hard to justify trading a player away, let alone one as impactful as Mims has been. However, his lack of effort on offense is becoming a detriment, especially when the Broncos go max protect, and he doesn’t even look for the ball.
Mims isn’t getting as much run as a kick returner, and his play as a punt returner hasn't been good. Troy Franklin can make up for Mims on offense, and the Broncos have other options to return punts, including Kolbe Katsis on the practice squad.
If there's an opportunity to trade Mims, who's playing on an expiring contract, the Broncos should do it.

title: Several Broncos Could Make History vs. Seahawks on TNF
full_text:
The Denver Broncos will try to get to 4-2 on Thursday night with the Seattle Seahawks coming to town .
The Seahawks also stand at 3-2, and they won their last meeting with the Broncos, which happened to be the first start of Bo Nix's career back in Week 1 of 2024. Broncos-Seahawks will be fought at Mile High under the bright lights of Thursday Night Football .
The Broncos are focused on getting the win , and we all know it won't be easy against the reigning Super Bowl champions. But in each of the past two years, the Broncos have defeated the defending World Champions in the regular season.
Several Broncos have some individual milestones and records on the table in Week 6's matchup with the Seahawks. And the Broncos, as a team, has a head-to-head record against the Seahawks to defend.
Here's what to watch for on Thursday night.
The Broncos are 35-21 against the Seahawks all-time, with a 23-5 home record. Up until 2002, the Seahawks were an AFC West rival, dating back decades.
When the Seahawks left the AFC West, they didn't just leave the division, they left the conference, become an NFC West team. The Broncos have dominated the Seahawks historically, but Seattle has the ultimate bragging rights of having defeated Denver in Super Bowl XLVIII.
The Broncos need just two sacks to tie for the NFL's fourth-longest streak all-time with multiple sacks at home. The Broncos have had two-plus sacks in 19 straight home games.
Expect the Broncos to get to Sam Darnold a few times.
With a touchdown grab, Sutton would tie Riley Odoms for the seventh-most receivng scores in Broncos history. Sutton broke the touchdown ice on this season last week, finding pay-dirt at SoFi Stadium.
Sutton is due for a touchdown in front of the Mile High Faithful. Hopefully, it comes against the Seahawks.
If Waddle can get over the century mark as a receiver tonight, he'll become the fifth player in Broncos history to record multiple 100-yard games in his first season with the team. It hasn't happened since 2014, when Emmanuel Sanders pulled it off.
Waddle's first 100-yard game came in Week 2 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, finishing with 138 yards on the day. Like Sutton, Waddle is due for a big game, but the Seahawks' defense is formidable.
Allen just one sack to become the ninth player in Broncos history to reach five sacks in four consecutive years. Five sacks doesn't sound like a lot, but it is, and pulling it off in five straight years is tough to do in this league, especially as an interior pass rusher.
Allen sacked Justin Herbert last week. Here's to hoping he gets home against Darnold.
With 2.5 sacks, Bonitto would tie Pryce for the third-most sacks by a Bronco in his first five seasons in team history. It's a pretty cool stat, given that Bonitto didn't become a starter until 2024.
Bonitto was drafted in 2022, so while it took him a couple of years to find his NFL footing, he made up for lost time by posting 27.5 sacks the past two years. This season started slowly for Bonitto, but he's posted three sacks in the past three games.

title: Why ESPN Put Broncos QB Bo Nix On Hot Seat — And Why He's Not
full_text:
Considering the multitude of aggravating factors within the struggling Denver Broncos offense, the opinions on quarterback Bo Nix have varied wildly in recent days.
The discourse has turned to the long-term viability of Nix as Denver's franchise signal-caller, with ESPN's Bill Barnwell speculating that he could be on (some form of) the hot seat entering Week 6 .
"Let's frame this one appropriately and be clear," Barnwell wrote in part on Thursday. "I don't think the Broncos are about to bench Nix for backup Jarrett Stidham, who hasn't been particularly impressive as a pro and didn't play well in last season's AFC title game loss to the Patriots while filling in for the injured starter. The hot seat here is more in the big picture, with Nix becoming eligible for a contract extension after the season and a decision on his fifth-year option in 2028 (at a projected $29.9 million) coming due next spring."
"The Broncos were hoping Nix would take a step forward after his great performance in the postseason and the addition of Waddle. If Nix doesn't get there, will the Broncos want to commit to him as their quarterback of the future on a second contract?"
Barnwell went on to allow that Nix's slump might be attributed to the ankle injury (and subsequent surgeries) he suffered in last season's Divisional Round win over the Bills. Nix currently ranks 29th in yards per attempt and 22nd in yards per dropback through five games.
The Broncos offense collectively ranks 30th in total yards, 26th in scoring, and 25th in passing and rushing as Nix has completed only 59.9% of his attempts for 942 yards, six touchdowns, and three interceptions. He's also largely been a non-factor on the ground, managing 35 yards and one TD on 18 carries.
Nix is the first one to tell you that he isn't performing up to standard. He's touched on potential confidence issues relating to turnovers and taking deep shots downfield. In many respects, he's the farthest iteration from what the fans saw in 2025.
But some perspective is warranted, too. The Broncos are 3-2, surviving a brutal schedule that begins to ease up in a few weeks. They'll get back rookie RB Jonah Coleman in Week 7 and WR Pat Bryant a bit thereafter following both players' stints on injured reserve.
Head coach Sean Payton recently took over control of play-calling, and the core talent level — Jaylen Waddle, Evan Engram, RJ Harvey, JK Dobbins — is good enough to make hay with. After all, this is the same team just eight months removed from what should've been a Super Bowl appearance.
Most importantly, Nix still holds the trust of Payton, who hand-selected and developed him into his version of ideal. And that work isn't about to end now, abruptly, with the Broncos above .500 and very much in the early playoff picture.
“I think as coaches, like I said to him, ‘Man, you’re the guy we want here. Let’s go. You’ve done a ton of things well.' But I think there’s a lot that goes into that," Payton said after last Sunday's victory over the Chargers. "In that old TBS series 'The Bear', where they say 'just let it rip.' I want him to make sure that we can let it rip.”
Winning cures everything in this business. Beat the Seahawks on Thursday Night Football, and a lot of this talk — magically — will evaporate into the ether.

title: 5 Bold Predictions for Broncos-Seahawks That Might Surprise Fans
full_text:
The Denver Broncos face the unenviable challenge of hosting the Seattle Seahawks on a short week. On top of that, injuries continue to pile up , and the Broncos' offensive struggles appear to have no end in sight.
That's a tough prospect to face against a team like the Seahawks, whose defense is one of the NFL's best. The Broncos will have to turn in an inspired performance if they're going to overcome all the factors working against them this week.
As for my bold predictions for this game, not all of them are favorable toward the Broncos. I can only call it like I see it, so let's get to it.
The Seahawks' defense is tough, disciplined, and the players trust each other to do their job. It's also a style of defense the Broncos' offense has typically struggled against since 2023, almost like Sean Payton can't fully figure it out.
That doesn't mean the Broncos won't have some moments, but it'll be another ugly showing as they end the game with their second-lowest yards total, barely beating out their offensive showing from the season opener in Kansas City.
The Broncos fail to reach the red zone as an offense, except for at least one possession that starts inside Seattle's 20-yard line thanks to a takeaway on defense.
Outside of the defense turning the ball over, the Broncos' offense has too many issues to overcome and fix in such a short-week turnaround. A few days and one true practice aren't enough time to turn the ship around, especially against a quality defense like Seattle's.
Ball security has been a major issue for the Seahawks' offense, especially their running backs, and that opens the door for some takeaways. Denver is able to force two fumbles and falls on them both.
One of those fumble recoveries puts Bo Nix and the offense in their one-and-only red-zone possession.
Sam Darnold can be tough to get to, with nine sacks in four games, but five of them came against the San Francisco 49ers this past Sunday.
Denver has the horses up front and the different looks to generate pressure, which can result in multiple sacks on Darnold, but the Broncos will need their secondary to hold up long enough to allow Bonitto, Allen, and company to get home.
Darnold will look to counter Denver's pass rush with the quick-pass game, but the secondary has to hold up.
Everything points to a high-volume game for the kicker. The Seahawks are allowing an average of 21 points per game, which is the eighth-fewest in the NFL this season.
The Seahawks do well in the red zone and have allowed only 10 touchdowns this season. With the Broncos' offensive woes, they turn to Lutz often in this game, and while he's not perfect, he mostly comes through.

title: Former Lions Punter Kasey Redfern Dies at 35 After Long Cancer Battle
full_text:
After a long cancer battle, former Detroit Lions punter Kasey Redfern has died at the age of 35.
According to his wife, Lauryl Redfern, he battled central nervous system lymphoma since 2023. Redfern played in Motown for just one season, back in 2017.
"He fought an incredible fight," Lauryl explained recently to the California Post. "He smiled the whole way through, never questioned why and always knew God had a purpose for this, having great hope that his miracle would be healing on Earth.”
Redfern played collegiately at Wofford (2010-2013) before embarking on a six-year NFL journey. He went undrafted in 2014, but landed with the Jacksonville Jaguars.
Besides the Lions, he had stops with the Jaguars, Chargers, Panthers, Browns, Cowboys and Falcons before his career ended in 2019.
In late September, the 35-year-old entered hospice care. The impact of treatment had started to take its toll on his mind and body.
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: One Advanced Metric Showcases Importance of Safety Brian Branch to Kelvin Sheppard's Defense
“His poor brain has had all it can take treatment wise so we want to make sure that he can be as comfortable as possible. As our NP pointed out this will also help me be able to love on him more/better and not have to do all of the caretaking as well," his wife shared on social media. "It’s been a really hard few weeks with this extreme decline. He’s still home and able to be home and could still have a lot more time with us, but we just can’t give him anymore treatmen t and unfortunately this decline is irreversible except by another miracle from the Lord which we are still of course praying for.
“We know that healing will take place regardless of the outcome, but if he makes it to Heaven soon, he will have it better than the rest of us and for that all I can do is be thankful and joyful and filled with peace (and a lot of jealousy) that He will be WHOLE and in glory with our Savior, the best place we could ask to be.”

title: Two Lions Players Whose Stock Is Trending Down Entering Bye
full_text:
The Detroit Lions recorded their best all-around effort of the 2026 season in their Week 5 win against the Arizona Cardinals. Dan Campbell's team found success on both sides of the football, delivering a promising performance going into its bye week.
Yet, not every Lions player delivered a strong performance in the intraconference contest. With that said, here are two players who saw their stock take a hit following the Week 5 tilt.
In Detroit's matchup with Arizona, TeSlaa had his first reception-less outing of the season since Week 1 against New Orleans. This came after the second-year wideout recorded two consecutive solid showings: vs. the Jets in Week 3 and against the Panthers in Week 4. He amassed at least three receptions and north of 65 yards in both games, including a career-best 95 yards in the Lions’ Week 4 loss in Carolina.
Consequently, TeSlaa appeared to be turning the corner and gaining a bigger role in Drew Petzing's offense until his no-catch, two-target day in the desert.
The onus now is on Petzing & Co. to carve out a more significant role for TeSlaa in the passing game coming out of the bye week.
Perhaps no Lions player's stock is more down than Izien. The fourth-year defensive back recorded a dismal effort in Week 4 against the Panthers, allowing five catches, 57 yards and a touchdown on five targets, equating to a passer rating of 153.8.
And for his efforts, he earned a lowly Pro Football Focus overall mark of 45.6, by far his worst overall grade of the season. It was the definition of a forgettable performance from the safety.
And to add insult to injury, the former Buccaneers defensive back was not given a single snap on defense this past week against Arizona. It's a pretty telling sign of how far he has fallen down the depth chart in a matter of just two weeks.
While his outlook isn't promising at the present moment, I believe there will come a time this season when the Lions will once again call upon Izien's number.

title: Detroit Lions Place Three Players On Injured Reserve List
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have made a decision on three injured players, opening up multiple spots on the 53-man active roster.
According to the team, wideout Tom Kennedy, offensive lineman Ben Bartch and linebacker Devin White have all been placed on the injured reserve list.
Detroit recently added veteran returner DeAndre Carter to the practice squad , paving the way for the 33-year-old to possibly be elevated to be the teams punt returner against the Green Bay Packers next week.
While the team wanted left guard Christian Mahogany to compete for the starting job, Bartch was not able to stay healthy long enough to make it any sort of competition. It appears that when Cade Mays returns, Juice Scruggs will be the player to continuously push the third-year lineman.
Head coach Dan Campbell delivered the bad news about Kennedy, when he last spoke to local reporters prior to the teams Week 6 bye.
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: 2026 First Quarter Risers and Fallers
“No, Tom, bad news," said Campbell. "All right, Tom's going to need surgery. So, it was significant enough to where he'll be out for the season. That's the stinker there. We already talked about (Lions linebacker) Devin White. He'll require surgery, but we'll get him back at some point. It'll just be a while. As of right now, I don't have an answer for you on contingency. I would rather not have (Lions wideout Amon-Ra) St. Brown back there for a whole game taking punts.
"I see him, he'll probably have some depending on where we're at on the field, but I don't want him to be our full-time punt returner," Campbell commented further. "So, we've got a couple of in-house candidates. We're looking for some guys, Brad (Holmes), and then we're looking right now to see what's out there, what's available. So, luckily we're not crunched to have to do anything just yet, but we're already looking.”
With White out of the lineup, players like Malcolm Rodriguez, Trevor Nowaske and rookie Jimmy Rolder will have an opportunity to earn more playing time.
While the linebackers unit had a rebound game against the Cardinals, their play to start to the 2026 season has not lived up to expectations.

title: David Montgomery Having Disastrous Season Shows Lions Won Trade
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have quickly seen the benefits of trading away running back David Montgomery.
Offensive lineman Juice Scruggs is the highest PFF-graded center in the National Football League (75.6), through the first five weeks of the 2026 NFL season.
It is evident the Lions and general manager Brad Holmes won the trade that sent away a popular running back who became part of a top tandem with Jahmyr Gibbs.
Montgomery had a solid first game for the Houston Texans, but the last month has seen the veteran running back fall off the map.
The 29-year-old is currently dealing with a groin injury that was suffered against the Tennessee Titans last week.
Additional NFL Insider Analysis: How Marvin Harrison Harrison Jr. Trade Negatively Impacts Lions
ESPN NFL writer Bill Barnwell recently released his list of 15 NFL players, coaches on the hot seat entering Week 6 of the regular season and Montgomery was included.
As Barnwell explained, "The latest in a series of offseason additions to try to fix a moribund Texans running game, Montgomery hasn't been able to transfer his successful three-year stretch in Detroit to Houston. Though the 2019 third-round pick scored three touchdowns in the Week 1 loss to the Bills, Montgomery has averaged just 2.7 yards per carry and posted a league-worst 23.1% success rate. You can help compensate for those issues with explosive runs, but Montgomery has just one gain of 10-plus yards across 52 carries this season."
With Montgomery struggling, the Texans may be forced to utilize Woody Marks much more.
"The second-year pro had what qualifies as a great game on the ground for a Texans back, turning 15 carries into 62 yards while adding four catches for 23 yards as a receiver," Barnwell writes. "The Texans have been hesitant to turn the lead role over to Marks, but Montgomery's struggles and the groin injury might leave them no choice."
The Lions have an interesting decision to make with Scruggs, who filled in admirably in the absence of Cade Mays.
The former Carolina Panthers lineman is set to return from a wrist injury. It is likely Scruggs will be a reserve, taking a back seat to a player that inked a lucrative three-year free agent contract this offseason.
While it would be quite unpopular, Holmes could decide to turn an asset into an opportunity to address a clear weakness.
It is not expected Scruggs will be traded at the deadline, but the Lions still have the worst pass defense in the NFL and are in need of more than just a band-aid at the cornerback position.

title: Updated 2026 Lions Game-by-Game Predictions Following First Quarter
full_text:
The Detroit Lions sit with a record of 3-2 through the first five games of the 2026 NFL regular season.
Here is an updated look at the remaining schedule, with predictions for each of the remaining games on the schedule.

Running back Josh Jacobs is still on the Commissioner's Exempt List. Detroit will be seeking to avenge two losses to their division rival last season.

title: Detroit Lions Defensive Line Has Exceeded Expectations
full_text:
The Detroit Lions’ defense has been one of the league's worst units through the first five weeks of the season. Yet, not all has been bad for defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit.
The defensive line, for one, has been quite reliable. And EDGE Aidan Hutchinson and interior defensive lineman Alim McNeill have arguably been the defense's most consistent performers.
Hutchinson has continued his steady play from seasons past, and continues to wreak havoc against opposing quarterbacks on a weekly basis.
He's generated the second-most pressures of any defender in the NFL this season (32). Plus, he's recorded the second-best Pro Football Focus overall grade among 106 qualified EDGE defenders (91.4), along with the highest pass-rush mark at the position (91.1).
The fifth-year pro is the Lions’ best defensive player and one of the most prolific pass-rushers in the game today. And he doesn't appear to be on the verge of slowing down anytime soon.
While Hutchinson's production has become a given, it wasn't quite as big of a certainty with McNeill entering the 2026 campaign.
The interior defender spent the majority of the 2025 season on the sideline recovering from a torn ACL. And when he did return to play, he wasn't exactly effective. In fact, he proved to be much more of a liability than a reliable contributor to Sheppard's defense. He generated just 23 total pressures and a single sack in 10 games a season ago, earning a measly PFF overall grade of 52.2.
Luckily for Dan Campbell's squad , McNeill has bounced back in a major way this season. The 26-year-old has already amassed 3.5 sacks and the same number of pressures he did a season ago. Additionally, his 23 pressures rank first among 133 qualified interior defensive linemen, and his PFF overall grade of 79.4 ranks ninth at the position.
McNeill is back to his productive ways, and it's been a godsend for Detroit's defensive line through the season's first five games.
While Hutchinson and McNeill have carried the D-line, it has also received production from a couple of unsung heroes: rookie interior lineman Skyler Gill-Howard and veteran EDGE D.J. Wonnum.
Gill-Howard, a sixth-round pick of the Lions this past April, has been a pleasant surprise for Detroit thus far in 2026.
Quite notably, he's been fairly proficient at getting after the quarterback, with 13 pressures to his name (the most among all rookie interior defensive linemen). That figure also ranks third among all first-year players.
Then, there's Wonnum, who has compiled five sacks, tied for fourth-most in the NFL and two more than he produced all of last season. And for his performance, he's earned a pass-rush grade of 65.5, ranking 43rd among all qualified EDGEs.
Through the collective efforts of these aforementioned linemen, the Lions have secured the most sacks in the NFL through five weeks (20.0).
So, even in an overwhelmingly disappointing season so far for the defense, all has not been lost. Detroit's pass-rush department , spearheaded by the defensive line, has managed to be productive, and has undeniably exceeded preseason expectations.

title: Detroit Lions Add Veteran WR, Returner to Practice Squad
full_text:
The Detroit Lions did not wait too long to add a veteran returner to be in the mix to replace Tom Kennedy.
Former Bears and Browns receiver DeAndre Carter will reportedly be inked to the teams practice squad.
Following the unfortunate MCL injury to Kennedy that will keep him away for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season, head coach Dan Campbell indicated the team would be in search externally for a new returner.
According to the transaction wire, the team worked out two wideouts, including Steven Sims and Carter.
The 33-year-old played collegiately at Sacremento State (2011-2014). He went undrafted in 2015, but landed with the Baltimore Ravens as an undrafted free agent. He has bounced around the league with stints at Oakland, New England, San Francisco, Philadelphia, Chicago, Washington, Los Angeles Chargers, Las Vegas and Cleveland.
During the 2024 season with Chicago, he averaged 31.9 yards per kickoff return, including 67-yarder. He returned a total of 17 punts and averaged 9.3 yards per return.
In late September of 2025, Carter was placed on the injured reserve list due to a knee injury suffered against Detroit in Week 4 of the regular season.
Special teams coordinator Dave Fipp was recently asked if the team was aiming for a certain starting spot average during returns.
“We have a lot of individual goals I'm not going to get into because you start saying those to people and then they start holding you accountable to all that," said Fipp. "We have our own metrics that we use. I certainly have mine. We have our own standards. We compare ourself to our standard after every single game in all areas, not only on kickoff, kickoff return. And the drive start is a major one for that. Obviously, we look at all the penalty stuff. That's really important in the return game.
"And then punt and punt and punt return, as you guys know, I mean, I do like stats," Fipp added. "I just don't like the way that they're publicized, like punt is terrible. The statistic for punt right now, I mean, I don't even know. They say gross punt's a good thing. Well, if you punt from the plus 40-yard line, your gross punt's not going to be very good. If you say net punt, same thing. If you punt out on your own 10-yard line a whole game, you're going to have a good net versus if you punt from the 50."
Fipp said the Lions have extensive information regarding return stats and compare themselves to league averages.
"We break down the punt into a bunch of different areas of the field and compare ourself to the league's numbers over the years," said Fipp. "And so, we do that after every single game, so we know exactly where we are in all areas. We have a high standard. It's not average. Our goal is to be well above that in all phases.”

title: One Advanced Metric Showcases Just How Important Brian Branch Is
full_text:
Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch could be returning to action soon from a torn Achilles. After continuing his rehab throughout the bye week, the team is hoping the former second-round pick can suit up against the Green Bay Packers in Week 7.
One advanced metric showcased just how vastly different the Lions' defense operates with Branch in the lineup and when he has been out due to injury.
According to TrueMedia, the Detroit Lions rank 30th in the league in defensive success rate without Branch in the lineup (2023-2026). With him patrolling the back end, the defensive success rate ranks third.
Defensive success rate is an advanced football metric that tracks how regularly a defense keeps the opposing offense "on schedule" rather than just counting total yards, according to Sports Reference .
Detroit's defense should feel quite comfortable with Branch returning. The safeties unit has been plagued with coverage breakdowns and communication issues, through the first quarter of the 2026 NFL season.
Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard recently addressed if his defense was trying to overcome trust issues.
"I kind of just alluded to that. I just mentioned that when a guy feels like this guy isn't in his gap now, 'Okay, I'm going to play my gap, but then I'm going to go try to peek to his and see if I can kind of help over there too.’ And then the ball hits in your gap. And this is happening a little too much," said Sheppard. "So now we've got to do one or two things. I told the guys this, 'We've got to make sure the guys you don't trust aren't out there or you guys get it corrected and you get it corrected in a hurry.’ Because we don't want to start doing that and guys feeling like they have got to carry the weight for another guy out there."
The former NFL linebacker indicated players cannot overcompensate for players that are in the wrong position.
"We should have an 11-man, that's why it's an 11-man defense," said Sheppard. "Everybody doing their one-eleventh. We can't have a guy play 10-man defense, now we've got two guys playing a gap and a half trying to overcompensate for somebody. We're done doing that.
"But again,  it's all lip service. I can stand here and give you the right answer and tell you things. It has to show up on game day.”

title: 'His Career Just Got Launched': Jon Gruden Praises Lions Rookie Defender
full_text:
Detroit Lions rookie cornerback Keith Abney II has earned a reasonable amount of praise for his performance at safety against the Arizona Cardinals.
The struggling NFC West squad was the perfect team to give the 2026 fifth-round draft pick an opportunity to gain experience at a new spot.
The Cardinals struggle this season to throw it deep, and without wideout Marvin Harrison Jr., who was ruled inactive in Week 5, the Lions' defense had an easier time defending the other Cardinals' offensive weapons.
Former NFL head coach and current analysis Jon Gruden named Abney his "Gruden Grinder" this week, praising the first-year defender for his play in a Lions 45-21 win.
"A lot of people ask me, 'What a Gruden grinder is?' They're versatile. A bit tough. Mentally tough. They don't come unglued when things go wrong," Gruden explained to his nearly 437,000 followers on social media. "They're team oriented and they're clutch. They feel no pressure . They apply it. Guys like Keith Abney II of the Detroit Lions. You know, nobody's been criticized more than the Detroit Lions defense. Their defensive coordinator, Kelvin Sheppard, has held this group together.
"One of the best things he did was put in Keith Abney II. He wears No. 6. He's 21-years-old. He's a fifth-round rookie out of Arizona State. Why was he in the fifth round? Well, maybe he not big enough. 5'9, 187-pounds. He goes to Arizona State, has limited play time in 2023," Gruden explained further. "But in 2024, he bursts onto the scene. Three interceptions, Nine pass breakups, 52 tackles. Then in 2025, he's All Big-12. Two picks, two forced fumbles, lot of ball production, 12 passes broken up."
Abney was inserted at safety to replace veteran Christian Izien, who struggled significantly against the Carolina Panthers. Playing alongside veteran Chuck Clark helped to stabilize a back end that had given up far too many explosive plays to start the season.
"Against the Arizona Cardinals, Abney returns home to Arizona, where he built the foundation that got him to the NFL," Gruden said. "He gets his first start. He has six solo tackles. He has his first interception and a pass broken up. And the Detroit Lions, not nly got five sacks, they have five straight three-and-outs against the Arizona Cardinals. A lot of it has to do with Keith Abney II. Instincts, versatility and mentality. This guy is a true grinder, and his career just got launched. Keep it up Keith."
