title: Lions 2026 First Quarter Risers and Fallers
full_text:
Through five games, the Detroit Lions have managed to secure a winning record.
Though they've had bumps along the way, the Lions are 3-2 with a chance to make a statement within the division with two NFC North opponents awaiting them out of the bye week.
While they've had some success to start the year, upcoming games against the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings at home should be telling about where this team ultimately stands.
Here are risers and fallers for the Lions through the first quarter of the 2026 NFL season.
The Lions were hoping they could find an ideal running mate for star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson in Wonnum after signing him to a one-year contract. Through five games, he's out-performed those expectations and is looking at a possible career year.
He currently leads the team with five sacks , and has three straight games with at least one. His career-high in a season is eight, and working opposite of Hutchinson has proven to be ideal for him. Not known for being an overly dominant pass-rusher, Wonnum is currently wreaking havoc.
Wonnum has a pass-rush win rate of 11.6 percent, which ranks behind only Hutchinson and Alim McNeill amongst Lions. He has also held his own against the run, and is looking like one of the team's better offseason signings.
Gibbs was entrusted with being the team's bell-cow back after they traded David Montgomery, and to this point he's lived up to the hype and then some. He ranks fourth in the league in rushing and is on pace for a career-high in receptions as well.
While there are rightfully some concerns about the level of usage that Gibbs has had to endure up to this point, he's certainly one of the league's most dynamic talents . He's quelled any concerns about the workload he's dealt with, and as a result there are high expectations for him moving forward.
The Lions were open about the fact that Mahogany would have to earn his starting job back heading into the season. In fact, they brought in veteran Ben Bartch and had plans of recently acquired Juice Scruggs also competing for the job.
However, due to injuries, the competition never materialized quite the way the team envisioned. That hasn't been to the detriment of the franchise, though, as the Lions have stuck with Mahogany and he has played at a high level through his first four starts.
The Boston College product missed the team's Week 2 loss to Buffalo, but has been one of the top-performing players. He's helped stabilize the interior amidst some offseason changes, and is currently the team's third-highest Pro Football Focus graded player with an 86.4 overall offensive grade.
While there were some concerns about Mahogany, he has ultimately found a way to cement himself as a starter moving forward and has taken his performance up a notch.
The Lions have needed Reed to be a shutdown corner, and he simply hasn't delivered at that level since signing a three-year deal prior to last season. While he's had some good moments, he's also been a big part of the team's struggles in the secondary.
Up to this point in the season, Reed has allowed an opposing passer rating of 124.2 and has drawn four penalty flags. He's been solid in run defense with a miniscule missed tackle rate of 7.5 percent, but has been beat for two touchdowns and allowed 17 completions on 27 targets.
It will be interesting to see whether the Lions elect to add cornerback help before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Reed will need to continue improving to help the defense bounce back from its early season struggles.
It has been a quiet start to the season for Detroit's second-round pick. Moore got a spike in snaps with a career-high 20 snaps against Arizona last week, but had played just 17 combined the previous two.
He has four total pressures in his pass-rush opportunities, and the emergence from Wonnum has further cut into his chances. Moving forward, he may not get as many opportunities given the state of Detroit's EDGE rotation unless he's more productive.
Expected to be the team's backup behind Gibbs, Pacheco has yet to appear in a game. He suffered a pair of injuries in training camp, and after undergoing a procedure he's expected to be out until December.
For a running back who already had an injury history entering the season, this isn't the most positive development. Pair that with the consistent improvement of Sione Vaki in the second running back role, and Pacheco may not get the opportunity to make a big impact after signing a one-year deal.
Sports journalist who has covered the Detroit Lions the past three NFL seasons. Christian brings expert analysis, insights and an ability to fairly assess how the team is performing in a tough NFC North division.

title: Ten Most Important Packers for Primetime Shootout vs. Cowboys
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers are riding high with a two-game winning streak that includes a 31-7 dismantling of the Chicago Bears last week at Lambeau Field.
Of course, that winning streak can quickly be made obsolete with a deflating loss to the Dallas Cowboys at home on Sunday night.
The Packers are 3-2, but those three wins do come with accompanying questions. All three came against either a backup quarterback or someone who is on his last legs in the NFL.
Dak Prescott is neither of those things. He’s a top-tier starter, and the Packers saw that firsthand last year. Prescott led the Cowboys to 40 points against a Packers defense that had Micah Parsons rushing the passer.
Parsons won’t be there Sunday for the Packers, but Prescott will, so expect the Green Bay offense to need to put up some points as Prescott is plenty capable of doing the same against them.
The need to limit Prescott is featured prominently in this week’s list of the 10 most important Packers.
With this game being a potential shootout, one play could swing it in either direction.
Xavier McKinney made two game-changing plays last week with interceptions that turned into touchdowns. The first set up Marshawn Lloyd’s first touchdown of the game. The second interception set up Lloyd’s second touchdown.
McKinney received a ton of praise from his teammates last week for his playmaking ability and leadership.
This week, the Packers will need both of those things in a secondary that was reeling against the Cowboys last year. Dak Prescott threw for 319 yards and three touchdowns while the Cowboys were able to pile up 40 points against a Packers defense that looked like it was out of answers by the end of the night.
McKinney could help in that regard. Last year, McKinney had just two interceptions but is up to three this season.
“I think DB and Bobby have done a great job when we got here for all of our players, all of our coaches, because X is obviously a high-profile, high-performing player,” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said of assistant coaches Daniel Bullocks and Bobby Babich. “He’s been really good throughout his whole career since he’s been in the NFL, but the great ones still want to get challenged and they still want to improve, and I think that the DB coaches have done a good job with him of saying, ‘Hey, let’s do a couple of these things and work on it.’
“X and all of our players took it to heart as far as here’s some fundamentals or here’s some coaching points that you can work on to make yourself a better player. All players really want is, ‘How can you help me?’ and they set forth a good plan, and give credit to X. He’s taken that and he works on it. He works on that part of his game a lot and it’s good to see it show up.”
On the other side of McKinney is the Packers’ other playmaking safety, Evan Williams. With the talent the Cowboys have at receiver, it’s unlikely that Jonathan Gannon is ever going to want to leave his two cornerbacks on an island against CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens.
The Cowboys are going to throw the ball a lot. That’s their identity as an offense. With the ball in the air that often, that leads to more chances for big plays for Green Bay’s defense. Williams was excited about the opportunity.
“For sure. For sure. You got to attack these opportunities,” Williams said. “If you’re hesitant in any facet, that’s when you get exploited as a defense. When you’re unsure or questionable about what you’re going to do, that’s when explosives start to show up and things can go downhill in a hurry.
“As a back end, you’re licking your chops for opportunities like this when you know the ball’s going to be in the air, and it’s up to you to stop it. That’s what we look forward to on any Sunday. It’s our job to shut down receivers like this, and when you get those opportunities, can’t shy away from it.”
In the next-man-up world that the Packers seem to constantly be living in, rookie defensive tackle Chris McClellan is the next man up with Jonathan Ford, Javon Hargrave and Warren Brinson on the shelf with injuries.
The Packers have been hammered by injuries so have had to lean on a lot of next men up. Here they are, ranked (see link in replies). pic.twitter.com/aVDRAT7TNQ
McClellan flashed in the preseason but has had a quiet start to the year save for a quarterback hit that resulted in roughing-the-passer penalty against Minnesota in the NFL debut.
McClellan is going to get more snaps with Ford out at least this week and Hargrave out for the rest of the season. Will that affect the rest of the rotation?
“I feel like it’s the next-man-up mentality,” McClellan said. “We got good players in our room, so even though Hargrave is down, we got AC (Anthony Campbell) up now. So, I feel like it doesn’t. They have a lot of faith in me, KB (Karl Brooks), D-Wy (Devonte Wyatt), obviously AC, all those guys.
“So, we’ll go out there and play our brand of football how we been doing, and we’ll see in the game. I’m sure it might change in the game but, for now, I know we’re just going to keep the same kind of rotation that we’ve been doing. At least in practice that’s what we’ve been doing.”
Whether or not McClellan starts, he’ll play plenty of snaps when Wyatt or Brooks need a break.
When Zach Bako-Bewele went down for the season in Week 2, it felt like a death sentence for the offense. Part of Green Bay’s resurgence on the offensive line, however, has been the play of his replacement.
Former second-round pick Anthony Belton has bounced around early in his career. He finished last season at right guard and looked like he was going to start there when training camp began.
Shortly into camp, however, the Packers moved Belton back to tackle as an insurance policy for Bako-Bewele, a decision that looks like a stroke of genius.
According to PFF, Belton has gone 78 consecutive snaps without allowing a pressure and 473 consecutive snaps without allowing a sack. In terms of pressures, the only offensive tackles he’s behind are Tristan Wirfs and Trent Williams. Those are two of the best tackles in all of football, with Williams ticketed for Canton as soon as his playing days are over.
“He’s done a nice job. He’s firmed the pocket up,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said. “I think that was the biggest thing the first couple weeks was just the push that we were feeling in the pocket. There were a couple reps in the game that, obviously, we got to clean up with him but, for the most part, he’s out there competing and doing a nice job.”
Belton is not going to the Hall of Fame yet. There’s still a lot to prove as to whether he can even play tackle at a winning level over a long period. This week, he’ll be facing former Packers edge Rashan Gary, who will be plenty motivated. Gary has not gotten off to the start he’d hoped for in Dallas, but you know he’d love to stick it to his former team that made him a bit of a forgotten man after they acquired Micah Parsons.
Dallas’ defense is not good at much. It’s at the bottom of the league in almost every statistical category that matters. The Packers should have plenty of opportunities in the passing game, but after last week’s aerial assault on the Bears, it’s likely the Cowboys will be looking to limit Green Bay’s big-play passing attack. That means it could see a lot of shell defenses with two safeties protecting the back end.
That means, at some point, the Packers will have to run the ball with some effectiveness. MarShawn Lloyd was the team’s leading rusher last week with 31 yards on 10 carries, but he did look good on his first touchdown run, when he ran over Jaylon Johnson to get into the end zone.
“Definitely confidence,” Lloyd said. “Each week I feel like there’s something I’ve worked on that I’m getting better at. Now it’s just learning the game more, being around it, being out there more. The more opportunities I get, the more opportunities I’m able to get better and learn from my mistakes. Now, I just need to keep growing.”

title: Here’s Why GOAT Jordan Love Will Be Waiting All Day for Sunday Night
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The theme song for NBC’s Sunday Night Football is Carrie Underwood’s Waiting All Day for Sunday Night.
Nobody will be more eager for Sunday night than Jordan Love, who will lead the Green Bay Packers into a primetime showdown against the Dallas Cowboys.
Love has been the brightest star under the primetime light. He is 4-0-1 in five career starts, and has been sensational in each.
Week 13 of 2023, 27-19 win over the Chiefs: Love was 25-of-36 for 267 yards with three touchdowns, zero interceptions and a 118.6 passer rating.
Week 17 of 2023, 33-10 win at the Vikings: Love was 24-of-33 for 256 yards with three touchdowns, zero interceptions and a 125.3 passer rating.
Week 15 of 2024, 30-13 win at the Seahawks: Love was 20-of-27 for 229 yards with two touchdowns, zero interceptions and a 124.8 passer rating.
Week 4 of 2025, 40-40 tie at the Cowboys: Love was 31-of-43 for 337 yards with three touchdowns, zero interceptions and a 118.1 passer rating.
Week 8 of 2025, 35-25 win at the Steelers: Love was 29-of-37 for 360 yards with three touchdowns, zero interceptions and a 134.2 passer rating.
The five-start total is rather absurd, with Love completing 73.3 percent of his passes for 1,449 yards with 14 touchdowns, zero interceptions and a 124.0 passer rating.
Love has thrown 176 passes during his Sunday night starts. That’s the highest passer rating of all-time among quarterbacks who’ve thrown at least 175 passes as a starter, according to Stathead . Drew Brees was next with 121.7; they are the only quarterbacks with a Sunday night passer rating of 121.7.
That’s impressive considering four of those five starts came on the road.
Over the past three-plus seasons, 26 quarterbacks have thrown at least 50 passes in Sunday night starts. Love is first in passer rating (Brock Purdy is second at 119.6), first in completion percentage (Drake Maye is second at 71.6), first in touchdowns (Dak Prescott and Patrick Mahomes are second with 12 in eight games apiece), fourth in yards per attempt (8.2; Purdy is first with 9.0). Love and Joe Burrow are the only quarterbacks with zero interceptions; Love has thrown 176 passes compared to 122 for Burrow).
Love is one of four quarterbacks with double-digits touchdowns. The other three quarterbacks have thrown at least five interceptions.
He’ll have to be at his best considering the high-powered opponent.
“They’re a good offense,” Love said this week. “Dak Prescott is a very good quarterback. They’ve got a lot of good weapons over there, some great receivers, so you know what it is. They find ways to put up points week after week.
“Last year, it was a shootout game. Who’s going to score last was really the mindset. In that game, you’ve just got to keep your head down, keep putting up points as an offense, attack the field every time you get an opportunity and just have that mindset that you’re going to go score, as well.”
Love lit up the Cowboys on the road on Sunday night last year but settled for a 40-40 tie.
“Love was actually my scout-team quarterback my second year as a QC there,” Cowboys defensive coordinator Brandon Parker said. “To see the way he's grown, he's very talented. He can make every throw on the field. You see him taking command at the line of scrimmage.
“Anytime you have history with people, you kind of know some things in terms of how they think and what they want to do, how they see you, I think that's most important. I think they've done a great job evolving.”
The Packers are coming off their best game of the season. With the offensive line providing the protection, Love tore apart Chicago’s defense with one long completion after another in a blowout win.
Love threw for 367 yards and two touchdowns while completing 80.6 percent of his passing attempts against the Bears. With that, Love became the only quarterback in the NFL this season to hit 350 yards, two touchdowns and 80.0 percent accuracy, according to Stats Perform’s Opta data. He joined Aaron Rodgers (twice) as the only Packers quarterbacks to achieve that feat since 1950.
How can Love build on that success in order for the Packers to extend their winning streak to three games and score an important win over another team that expects to be in the playoff race until the end of the season?
“You’ve got to keep stacking,” Love said. “We talk about it in the locker room all the time and team meetings, you have a game like that, you’ve got to be able to follow it up with another great performance. That’s the mindset heading into this week. We’ve got to be able to stack wins and get rolling as an offense and as a team.
“Just comes back to it’s a new week. You’ve got to learn from the mistakes, learn from the good things that happened last week, and move on. Flush it, put all the focus on Dallas this week and understand that they’re going to be a hungry team coming in here – Sunday Night Football – so we’re excited about it. What a great opportunity to just continue to stack, keep improving as a team and take it one week at a time.”

title: Packers-Cowboys Final Injury Report: A New Problem And a Big Problem
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – First, the good news for the Green Bay Packers: Starting cornerback Keisean Nixon is not on the final injury report and will play on Sunday night against the Dallas Cowboys.
Now, the bad news: The other starting cornerback, Brandon Cisse, was limited participation at Friday’s practice and is questionable.
And, finally, the big news – the literal big news: The Packers will be shorthanded at defensive tackle with two players listed as out for the game.
Keisean Nixon did not practice on Wednesday due to a groin injury but practiced on Thursday and Friday. He has not missed a game in his four-plus seasons with the Packers, a fact he reminded coach Matt LaFleur of on Wednesday.
“I take my body serious. It’s my resume, it’s my life,” he said. “I take pride playing every Sunday. That’s just my goal, what I want to do. I definitely told him that.”
He will play in his 80th consecutive regular-season game. It’s so important to him that he started in Week 18 at Minnesota last year.
How has he stayed healthy in a sport in which players are injured routinely, either through big collisions or freak incidents?
“Pray to the Man Above,” he said. “Keep the process the same. I feel like you stay with your regimen and don’t go away from it, it helps. So, been working out for me, for sure.”
Nixon said he feels “a lot better right now” compared to the start of the week.
Now, will Cisse start? It’s possible his addition to the injury report was precautionary. In fact, he walked through the locker room without any issue. His availability will be key against the Cowboys’ high-powered passing attack.
Fellow cornerback Benjamin St-Juste is out with a hamstring.
The Packers took seven defensive tackles into the regular season. They’ll have only four of those players available for the game, though. Warren Brinson is on injured reserve, Javon Hargrave will wind up on injured reserve because of a torn Achilles and Jonathan Ford is out with a calf injury.
“We’ve got a plan but, certainly, it doesn’t help,” coach Matt LaFleur said before practice.
The four available players include starters Devonte Wyatt and Karl Brooks, rookie Chris McClellan, and young Anthony Campbell, who suffered an ankle injury in his NFL debut against the Jets and missed the last three games.
“He’s progressing good,” LaFleur said of Campbell. “He had two good days of practice. We’ll see how he does today.”
Brooks, Wyatt and McClellan have been playing between 30 and 40 snaps per week. They might have to play more to pick up the slack.
“Man, just honestly keep a 1-0 mindset,” McClellan said. “I feel like I don’t let stuff like that change my process. I’m going to come in and do the same thing I was doing last week that I do this week. I’m a big believer in that. If you’re consistent with your process, doing what you got to do, eventually it’ll come through for it.
“Obviously, having more opportunities to get more snaps is mentally I’ve been trying to watch a little extra tape. Other than that, I treat it like a normal week. Try not to change anything and just be myself. Do what I do.”
The team has only one player, undrafted free agent David Blay, on the practice squad. He signed three weeks ago .
With Javon Hargrave headed to injured reserve, the Packers could fill the void with receiver Savion Williams. Williams opened the season on injured reserve but just completed his second week of practice.
He is questionable for Sunday.
“I’m good. It’s been good. Getting out there and getting my legs back under me,” Williams said.
The Packers could use him because receiver Skyy Moore is out with a high-ankle sprain. He said he’s making “good progress” but didn’t rule out being placed on injured reserve.
“I feel good in where my progression’s at,” Moore said. “It probably looks bad, but the scooter and the boot is just to help, but I can walk and everything. So, I feel good in my progression, for sure.”
Out: DT Javon Hargrave (Achilles), DT Jonathan Ford (calf), WR Skyy Moore (ankle), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring).
Doubtful: DT Jordon Riley (Achilles).
Questionable: LG Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), CB Brandon Cisse (hip), C/G Jacob Monk (quad), WR Savion Williams (ankle).
Off the injury report: CB Keisean Nixon (groin), Edge Lukas Van Ness (shoulder), S Evan Williams (illness), DT Devonte Wyatt (ankle).
Riley and Savion Williams have been designated to return from injured reserve and are within their 21-day practice windows.
Out: CB Cobie Durant (hamstring), T Drew Shelton (hamstring).
Questionable: LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring), DT L.T. Overton (foot), CB Joey Porter (ankle), CB Ameer Speed (knee).
Off the injury report: S Alijah Clark (hamstring), LT Tyler Guyton (back), OLB James Houston (shoulder), WR CeeDee Lamb (thigh), CB Shavon Revel (knee), LG Tyler Smith (thumb).

title: NFL Removing Josh Jacobs From Exempt List, But What’s Next for Packers’ RB?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The NFL on Friday announced that Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs will be removed from the Commissioner’s Exempt List on Monday.
Jacobs spent the first five games of the season on the exempt list, where he was paid while the legal process ran its course and the league conducted its own investigation. Sunday’s home game against the Dallas Cowboys will mark the sixth and final game on the list.
“The National Football League today notified Josh Jacobs of the Green Bay Packers that he will be removed from the Commissioner Exempt List on Oct. 19. He will be eligible to play in the Packers’ Week 7 game on Oct. 25 after missing six games,” the league said in a statement.
“The NFL initiated an investigation under the Personal Conduct Policy following Jacobs’ arrest in May. The league’s review remains ongoing and is not affected by this change to Jacobs’ roster status.
With Jacobs coming off the exempt list on Monday, he could practice on Wednesday and be available for next Sunday’s game at the Detroit Lions.
Jacobs has been around the team and working out; he has not been allowed to practice. That means he presumably will be in good shape and would not need much of a ramp-up period, which would be the case for a player coming off an injury.
However, as noted by the NFL in the statement, the matter has not been settled.
In fact, it’s not impossible that Jacobs could play in a game or games with the Packers and then be suspended. That, however, would require new evidence – evidence the league would like to see.
That investigation is ongoing, it is important to note, meaning it’s possible that Jacobs could face a suspension. In fact, that is the expectation. The question is whether it will be a six-game suspension, meaning Jacobs’ time on the exempt list would serve as the punishment, or for additional games if additional evidence is uncovered if more information is revealed.
Jacobs was paid while on the exempt list; any suspension would be unpaid.
That new evidence would be video evidence of the incident. The NFL has been trying to see the video of the incident. Both Jacobs and the victim filed lawsuits against the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department to prevent the release of that video.
“Plaintiff joins ANM’s position and supports her request to protect her privacy, dignity, personal security, emotional well-being, and ability to participate safely in the criminal justice process,” reads the suit by Jacobs’ legal team, with ANM being the initial of the victim.
“ANM is a crime victim who seeks closure, not public attention. ANM is not publicly known by her identity and has deliberately avoided public discourse concerning the underlying incident. Public release of records that identify, depict, locate, or disclose sensitive information concerning ANM would force unwanted exposure upon her and risk revictimizing her through renewed public scrutiny.
“Plaintiff requests that Defendant be prohibited from publicly releasing information that directly or indirectly identifies, locates, depicts, or reveals private or sensitive information concerning ANM.”
In a statement, Jacobs’ attorneys, Clarence F. Duchac III, David Z. Chesnoff and Richard A. Schonfeld, said: “Josh has dedicated the last several months to bettering himself, and he accepts responsibility for his actions. He is excited to get back to work and on the field with his teammates. Josh is grateful for the support he is receiving from his teammates, coaches, the Packers organization, and the greatest fans in the world. Since there are ongoing legal matters, he will not have any further comment.”
Jacobs was booked on Tuesday, May 26 , due to an incident that occurred on Saturday, March 23. On Sept. 10, he pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property. He had to pay a $1,000 fine plus court costs for the battery charge.
Asked before the season-opening game against Minnesota whether that court ruling changed how he felt about his former Pro Bowl running back and team captain, coach Matt LaFleur said no.
“Well, because I know the guy and I know the character of the guy,” he said. “I’ve said that many times. And, unfortunately, situations occur in life and it’s just an unfortunate situation.”
The locker room voiced its support, as well.
“It’s my brother. It’s my brother. No matter what, that’s my brother forever,” fellow running back MarShawn Lloyd said. “I don’t know what’s going on, but that’s my brother, so I just got to stay on that, forever. Like I said, he’s helped me when I was in the worst part of my life, really, those last two years, coming in early as a rookie. I don’t know everything but, at the end of the day, he’s my brother.”
Without Jacobs, Green Bay’s running game has been terrible. The Packers enter Sunday night’s game against the Dallas Cowboys ranked last in the NFL with 60.4 rushing yards per game – worst in the league by almost 20 yards – and 31st with 3.05 yards per carry.
Lloyd leads the team with 112 rushing yards but on a woeful 2.8-yard average. Jacobs had two games with more yards during his debut season with the team in 2024.
The run game has at least had a handful of open-field runs in back-to-back wins over the Bucs and Bears.
“What’s improved, I think, is the consistency,” LaFleur said before Friday’s practice. “I think our backs are doing a better job of pressing and cutting. I think they’re running with better pad level. I just think from an efficiency standpoint, that’s where we need to see the best jump. It’s cool to have explosive runs. We’re all for that, but can you stay ahead of the sticks, can you stay out of get-back-on-track situations and third-and-long situations.”
Publicly, the Packers have remained in Jacobs’ corner due to what he’s meant on and off the field.
“I fully anticipate him being a member of our team,” LaFleur said after the final preseason game. “I think you've got to let everything play out [in the courts], but I anticipate him being a member of our football team.”

title: Packers Friday Update From Practice: He Always Plays, And He Will Again
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – When Green Bay Packers cornerback Keisean Nixon missed practice due to a groin injury on Wednesday, it was worthy of concern.
After all, the Packers aren’t facing rookie Jalon Daniels or backup Tyson Bagent this week. Instead, the opposing quarterback on Sunday night will be Dallas Cowboys star Dak Prescott and the opposing receivers will be CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.
Well, there is no concern anymore. Nixon practiced on Thursday, practiced again on Friday and will play on Sunday night, barring a setback.
“I asked him on Wednesday,” coach Matt LaFleur said before practice. “I’m like – because he doesn’t miss too many practices – and he looked at me and said, ‘How many games have I missed since I’ve been here?’”
The answer is zero. He played in all 17 games from 2022 through 2025 and is now a perfect 73-of-73 after starting the first five games of this season.
Assuming he gets through practice without a problem and plays on Sunday, it will be his 80th consecutive game.
“He’s wired the right way and he loves to compete,” LaFleur said.
Keisean Nixon is practicing again and will play on Sunday. pic.twitter.com/ETdKFQmBKM
Reporters only get to watch the pre-practice warm-ups on Fridays. Based on that, four players did not practice: cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), receiver Skyy Moore (ankle) and defensive tackles Jonathan Ford (calf) and Javon Hargrave (Achilles).
LaFleur was hopeful that Ford would be able to practice on Thursday. That did not happen, though, and LaFleur said he would not play.
That means the Packers will be thin at defensive tackle, with Ford banged up, Warren Brinson (groin) on injured reserve and Hargrave destined for injured reserve. So, the Packers are down to Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks, rookie Chris McClellan and first-year player Anthony Campbell, who missed the last three games.
“We’ve got a plan for that,” LaFleur said. “We’ve got a plan. But, yeah, certainly, it doesn’t help.”
If the plan means a call to the practice squad, undrafted rookie David Blay would be making his NFL debut.
Starting linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and backup cornerback Cobey Durant are “long shots” to play against Green Bay due to hamstring injuries, Dallas coach Brian Schottenheimer said before practice.
“[He's] doing OK,” Schottenheimer told reporters about Overshown's rehab work. “I still think it's probably a long shot for this game, but it was good to see him out there moving around a little bit better.”
Overshown was supposed to miss only a game or two; instead, this would be his fifth consecutive game on the sideline.
“These are tricky,” he said earlier in the week . “You can have six good days in a row and then out of nowhere, something happens. Right now, I'm feeling great. I'm feeling like I can run around and do everything I could before the injury. At this point, it's just how practice goes throughout the week, how the [hamstring] handles all the stresses of a full 60 minutes of football.”
LaFleur came to the podium wearing a Brewers hat in recognition of their sweep of the Dodgers on Thursday night to clinch their first trip to the World Series since 1982.
“I want to support the Brewers,” he said. “That was pretty cool to watch last night. Got a lot of respect for their organization, Coach (Pat) Murphy. I saw something Christian Yelich said after the game that certainly resonated with me in terms of what it takes to be successful. I think they’re a first-class organization and really happy for them.”
LaFleur was a little busy on Thursday so wasn’t able to “watch a whole lot” of the game.
“But it is pretty cool when you have an in-state team to reach a World Series for the first time in 44 years,” he said. “That’s a pretty big deal. Just really happy for those guys.”
While it’s been nothing but rain in Green Bay, the forecast will clear up for the weekend. It’s supposed to be sunny and not quite as breezy, with temperatures in the 50s for the game, according to WBAY .
The Packers are 1.5-point favorites at FanDuel Sportsbook , though most of the money is on Dallas.
“Any time we can get a primetime matchup in Lambeau Field, we'll take it. Love the atmosphere,” tight end Tucker Kraft said.
The teams will reveal their final injury reports of the week after they get done practicing on Friday. For now, here are the injury reports from Thursday.
Packers Thursday Injury Report
Did not participate: DT Javon Hargrave (Achilles), DT Jonathan Ford (calf), WR Skyy Moore (ankle), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring).
Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), C/G Jacob Monk (quad), CB Keisean Nixon (groin), DT Jordon Riley (Achilles), WR Savion Williams (ankle), DT Devonte Wyatt (ankle).
Full participation: Edge Lukas Van Ness (shoulder), S Evan Williams (illness).
Riley and Savion Williams have been designated to return from injured reserve and are within their 21-day practice windows.
Cowboys Thursday Injury Report
Did not participate: CB Cobie Durant (hamstring), T Drew Shelton (hamstring).
Limited participation: LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring), CB Joey Porter (ankle), CB Ameer Speed (knee).
Full participation: S Alijah Clark (hamstring), LT Tyler Guyton (back), WR CeeDee Lamb (thigh), OLB James Houston (shoulder), OLB Von Miller (rest), CB Shavon Revel (knee), LG Tyler Smith (thumb).

title: Packers Next-Man-Up Rankings, From Duds to Season-Changing Studs
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – It’s been a painful start to the season for the Green Bay Packers.
According to Rotowire , they are the fourth-most-injured team in the NFL through five games. While the 49ers might tell the Packers to hold their chardonnay when it comes to injuries, the Packers in some instances will have backups on the field for backups when they host the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night.
While the star players have been instrumental in the Packers surviving with a 3-2 record, the backups have played key roles. From worst to first, here are our next-man-up rankings.
With Aaron Banks inactive for Week 1 at Minnesota, Donovan Jennings made his first career start. It didn’t go well. When Banks was unable to get through Week 2 against the Jets, Jennings replaced him again. When Jennings was injured, he was replaced by rookie Jager Burton. For Week 3 against Atlanta, it was Burton’s turn to start.
If Jennings was bad, Burton was worse with a ghastly 10 pressures allowed against the Falcons. Due to a combination of Banks’ injuries and the play of the backups, general manager Brian Gutekunst signed 34-year-old Laken Tomlinson off Dallas’ practice squad. More on him later.
The Packers carried seven defensive tackles into the regular season, with Campbell earning the final spot after a surprisingly strong training camp.
Campbell, however, suffered an ankle injury in his NFL debut against the Jets and missed the last three games. He is going to need to step up in big-time fashion with the Packers reeling without Brinson and Javon Hargrave and potentially Jonathan Ford.
Jayden Reed is one of the top slot receivers in the NFL. There simply is no replacing him from an impact perspective.
Skyy Moore was the player who took over the slot role. Moore was a second-round pick in 2022 who the Packers signed this offseason to solve their kickoff- and punt-return woes. He’s been excellent in that role.
On offense, though, it’s been a different story. After catching a total of 43 passes in 30 games for the Chiefs in 2022 and 2023, he’s caught a combined 12 passes in 28 games for the Chiefs in 2024, 49ers in 2025 and Packers in 2026. That includes 7-of-14 targets this year for just 35 yards.
According to PFF, he’s one of 54 players who’ve been targeted at least seven times in the slot. He’s caught 2-of-7 passes for 8 yards and is last with 0.21 yards per route.
Moore suffered an ankle injury against Chicago and isn’t expected to play against Dallas.
With Savion Williams starting the season on injured reserve with an ankle injury, Bo Melton saw a bump in playing time. In five games, he has caught 4-of-8 targets for 30 yards. His one opportunity to make a play was at Tampa Bay, which he dropped. Of 113 receivers who’ve been targeted at least eight times, Melton is 109th with 0.58 yards per route.
At the end of training camp, the Packers opted to trade for Kaleb Johnson rather than hand the No. 3 job to Pierre Strong.
Strong got his chance last week. After spending all of last season on the practice squad without getting into a game, he carried the ball five times for 7 yards and caught three passes for 11 yards against Chicago. The numbers are pretty bad, but he converted on fourth-and-1 and broke a tackle on an 8-yard catch.
“He has nice vision, good balance, he can cut, and then he’s reliable in pass protection,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said this week. “He made some nice plays on the edge catching the ball, broke a couple tackles. So, he’s just a good overall back that you can trust in any situation to go out there and do his job.”
Jonathan Ford earned his spot on the roster with an excellent training camp and preseason. So, he was a natural to replace Jordon Riley, who missed training camp and the start of the season following last year’s torn Achilles, in a run-stopping role.
He has five tackles in five games, including a half-sack against Minnesota, while averaging 23 snaps per game. Ford’s not on the roster to rush the passer, though he has only one less than Devonte Wyatt.
Ford hasn’t practiced this week due to a calf injury and Riley returned to practice this week .
Barryn Sorrell has started all five games as Micah Parsons comes back from last year’s torn ACL. He has a half-sack, zero tackles for losses and 13 tackles. PFF has credited him with six pressures. Six pressures was a decent game for Parsons.
According to PFF, Sorrell is one of 83 edge players who’ve had at least 66 pass-rushing opportunities. He ranks 68th in pass-rush win rate and 65th in pass-rush productivity, a formula that includes sacks, hits and hurries per pass-rushing snap.
Sorrell is a solid player who’s going to have a long career. Asking him to play 33 snaps a game, which has been the case this season, might be too much.
The Packers’ excellent right tackle, Zach Bako-Bewele, suffered a season-ending knee injury during the opening series of Week 2 against the Jets. The next man up was Belton, who seems to have settled in after a rough start.
He is one of 64 offensive tackles to play at least 150 snaps. He ranks an excellent 18th in PFF’s pass-blocking efficiency, which measures sacks, hits and hurries allowed per pass-protecting snap. He’s on a two-game streak without allowing a pressure. He’s a big guy but must play bigger in the run game.
“He’s done a nice job,” Stenavich said. “He’s firmed the pocket up. I think that was the biggest thing the first couple weeks was just the push that we were feeling in the pocket. So, I think him and Laken (Tomlinson) have done a really nice job just firming that up, allowing Jordan to see and not have that pocket pushed in his face. There were a couple reps in the game that, obviously, we got to clean up with him but, for the most part, he’s out there competing and doing a nice job.”
Edgerrin Cooper was one of the Packers’ most irreplaceable players. But, to their credit, they held off the Buccaneers following his torn Achilles and trounced the Bears in their first full game without him.
The Packers are fortunate to have Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper waiting in the wings. They aren’t Cooper – who is? – but you could do much, much worse in terms of depth.
They essentially shared the snaps against the Bears, with McDuffie recording five tackles and Hopper two tackles and a goal-line interception. By splitting the snaps on defense, both players also can be factors on special teams.
Asked about Hopper, defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said: “Consistency of doing what you’re coached to do with the way that you want to do it with technique, fundamentals, playmaking. But I thought he played well. You guys saw what we did to fill Coop’s spot and I thought him and Duff played well.”
With Luke Musgrave out with a neck injury, the Packers at the end of training camp signed veteran Jonnu Smith and traded for Mark Redman. Smith has played 101 snaps and Redman 98.
The 24-year-old Redman has been excellent in providing the best blocking tight end the Packers have had in years.
“Literally, I was just thinking about that a minute ago, you’re paid to play a sport where sometimes it takes running full speed at another grown man who’s 250 pounds, and yeah, I think logically you would say, ‘Don’t do that,’” Redman said . “But that’s part of the job description, and honestly, it’s fun for me.”
Smith’s calling card for most of his career has been catching the football. He’s caught only five passes for 85 yards but has been an asset alongside Redman in the team’s packages of two and three tight ends.
The most incredible of the next-men-up stories has been Travis Glover. A sixth-round pick in 2024, he barely played as a rookie until being thrown in the fire in the playoff game against the Eagles. He wound up getting benched at one point. He spent last year on injured reserve with a shoulder injury.
So, he entered training camp as a total afterthought. He was treated as such, too. When the team took the starting job at right guard away from Anthony Belton,…

title: (Bell-Ringing) Endorsement Speaks Volumes for Packers TE Mark Redman
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich delivered a ringing endorsement for tight end Mark Redman.
Or, perhaps it was a bell-ringing endorsement.
“He’s kind of messed up in the head,” Stenavich said on Tuesday.
Redman smiled when relayed the quote after Wednesday’s practice.
“My wife sent me a picture of that tweet from somebody the other day,” he said. “Isn’t everyone a little messed up in the head? Aren’t we all a little weird in our own sense?”
Football is played by big, tough, athletic men who seek and embrace the contact that almost everyone else in society would prefer to duck. Redman, who was acquired in a trade at the end of training camp, has found his niche as the team’s tough-guy blocker.
Most of the team’s big running plays have featured the 258-pound Redman sprinting across the formation and delivering a jarring blow against a defender with similar size and strength.
“Literally, I was just thinking about that a minute ago, you’re paid to play a sport where sometimes it takes running full speed at another grown man who’s 250 pounds, and yeah, I think logically you would say, ‘Don’t do that,’” Redman said.
“But that’s part of the job description, and honestly, it’s fun for me. It’s the challenges that not everyone can do in this game, in this league. So, when your number’s called and you’re asked to do that – absolutely, whatever it takes. Maybe that’s the one that bounces MarShawn (Lloyd) or Kaleb (Johnson) or any of the guys for a 20-yard gain. So, if that’s how I can play and help support the team, then I’ll do whatever they ask me.”
Among Redman’s greatest hits were the two biggest runs of the season against Tampa Bay, the first by Chris Brooks …
Here is Mark Redman with a big block against Tampa Bay. The Packers' run game has been poor overall but he's been really good and sprung some big runs with these in-motion blocks. pic.twitter.com/9vD5uR9qnH
And the second by Kaleb Johnson …
When the season is over, it will be interesting to see the percentage of explosive running plays by the Packers in which TE Mark Redman is a factor. Here he is leading the charge for Kaleb Johnson. pic.twitter.com/kXfmziZrmL
As well as Pierre Strong’s fourth-and-1 pickup against Chicago …
Mark Redman motions right and has the point-of-attack block on Pierre Strong's fourth-and-1 conversion. pic.twitter.com/UBJkisHmzM
And MarShawn Lloyd’s walk-in touchdown against Chicago.
Mark Redman motions left and serves up a pancake on MarShawn Lloyd's walk-in touchdown. pic.twitter.com/jrEhONocJX
On all four runs, Redman sprinted across the formation and inserted himself as the point-of-attack blocker.
“Yeah, he definitely is” giving the Packers a different look than their past tight ends, Stenavich said on Tuesday. “You definitely need guys like him to run our offense. He’s a versatile player, he’s intelligent. You can move him around. He’s physical. He’s kind of messed up in the head. So, it’s good.
“He’s a physical player, and he loves that part of the game, which is awesome. So, he’s one of my favorite guys I see every day. He’s got a smile on his face. He’s excited. He’s ready to go. So, it’s been really fun to have him. Picking him up was a good pickup, for sure.”
The Packers never addressed the role of a blocking tight end during the offseason. So, with the Packers having an obvious need and the Rams having an obvious surplus, general manager Brian Gutekunst sent a 2028 seventh-round pick to Los Angeles at the end of the preseason.
“Yeah, I love it. We can’t have enough of those guys,” coach Matt LaFleur said of Redman’s mentality. “Physicality is part of our game and in order to be physical, you better have the right mindset. He’s a fearless guy that will throw his body in there, and he’s been doing a great job for us, and I’m really glad we have him.”
And Redman is glad to be here. He went undrafted in 2025 and spent his rookie season on the Rams’ practice squad. With the Rams, there was no pathway to playing time. With the Packers, he’s been a staple of the offense. In five games, he’s played more than 20 snaps in four.
“It’s just a mentality/mindset type thing of someone’s got to do this, so why not it be me?” he said. “Pop the big ones, and it’s really fun. Kaleb popped that one against Tampa Bay. I think you can see me on film, kind of hooting and hollering and pointing. It’s really fun to see that hard work and doing some of the dirty stuff, see it pay off, and spring a big one for 20 or 30.
Redman has two receptions for 29, with both passing-game targets coming in the win at Tampa Bay.
The 25-yard catch against Tampa Bay was exciting, but he knows his role is to make big blocks more than it is to make big catches.
“Everyone wants the big spotlight and shine,” he said. “If I could go for 1,000 yards, I would do that — absolutely. But you’ve got to play to the best of your ability, and everyone wants to get paid at the end of the day and be the greatest player of themselves.
“But, at the end of the day, it comes down to winning, too. If you’re on a winning team and you keep winning and keep winning, go to the playoffs, make it to the championship, make it to the Super Bowl, you’re going to get noticed that way. So, whether it’s 100 yards that you catch for or none, and you spring 10 runs with great blocks. As long as you win at the end of the day, I think that’s kind of the main thing here, and then everyone will see that on tape, too.”
It’s been a rewarding start to Redman’s career in Green Bay. The Packers believed in him, obviously. So did his wife, Jenna. After not playing in a game since his final season of college at Louisville in 2024, he’s become a vital part of a team that looks like a playoff contender heading into Sunday night’s home game against the Dallas Cowboys.
“It’s awesome being on the other side of things,” he said. “I was on the practice squad last year, and just being able to play and kind of showcase your talents [has been great]. My wife’s my biggest sporter. She’s like, ‘I knew you could do it. I knew you could make it.’ So just doing that, and putting your head down and grinding and, like I said before, it’s whether you catch five balls for 100 yards or you just spring a couple big blocks, or you’re on special teams if you’re winning, you’re going to get noticed.
“So, that’s kind of what it is to me. The Tampa game was fun, obviously, but the Chicago game, (I) didn’t get passed to at all, and who cares? I mean, we blew them out. That was really fun too. So, as long as you’re winning and putting out more points on the other team, that’s all I really care about.”

title: Packers-Cowboys Thursday Injury Report: (Really) Big Help on the Way
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers needed to beef up their run defense last season. So, they grabbed 6-foot-5, 338-pound Jordon Riley off the Giants’ practice squad.
Riley impressed in four games with Green Bay but suffered a torn Achilles during the Week 17 game against Baltimore. Now, with veteran Javon Hargrave having suffered a torn Achilles last week, the timing of Riley’s comeback could hardly be better.
Riley was designated for return from the PUP list on Wednesday and went through his second practice on Thursday. While he probably will need more than one week of practice, he will be a huge asset – literally and figuratively – whenever he’s cleared for game action.
“Definitely rusty,” he said after being limited participation at practice. “Just trying to knock the rust off. We got a saying, ‘Got to vs. get to.’ I get to get coached. I get to get those reps in practice, which are very expensive, as I like to say, expensive reps. So, I take those very seriously and it's been good. I’m good physically. No sores or aches. I’m just in a good spot. Taking it day by day at a time.”
Riley was a seventh-round pick by the Giants in 2023. He played in eight games as a rookie and 13 games (with five starts) in 2024. He didn’t make their roster in 2025 but joined the Packers on Dec. 3.
It was a career-changing move. Imagine going from the practice squad of one of the worst teams in the NFL to the active roster of a Super Bowl contender.
And then, it was all taken away from him.
“Man, it sucks, but it’s part of the business,” he said. “It’s part of the game we play. We love to play. You can’t really be so stuck on the past. You just got to continue to look forward, so when it happened, I just knew I’m going to recover from an Achilles injury. Few seconds to get down a little bit, but after that’s over, the emotion’s over, I told myself I’m going to return from an Achilles injury.”
The Packers need help on the defensive line. It was one of their strongest positions coming out of training camp but Warren Brinson is on injured reserve and he’ll soon be joined by Hargrave. That leaves the Packers with only five players at a position group in which coordinator Jonathan Gannon prefers to rotate players in and out of the lineup.
“That is above me,” he said of his potential return. “I just stick on one day at a time. Today, we had padded practice, so that’s what my focus was on – padded practice today. No really looking forward; just taking it each day at a time.”
Cornerback Keisean Nixon and defensive tackle Jonathan Ford did not practice on Wednesday. Nixon returned on Thursday and was limited participation. Coach Matt LaFleur before practice said “I would expect (Ford) to be out there today,” but, while he went through the pre-practice warmup, he officially did not practice.
Their importance for Sunday night can’t be overstated .
Nixon, who is having a strong season, is a key part in a Packers secondary that must contend with Dak Prescott throwing passes to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Plus, veteran cornerback Benjamin St-Juste missed a second consecutive practice with a hamstring injury.
Ford, who has played in all five games with one start, could be in for a heavier workload following Javon Hargrave’s torn Achilles if healthy. He’s averaged 23 snaps per game. If he can’t play and Riley isn’t ready, the Packers would have only four defensive tackles available.
Nixon and safety Evan Williams (illness), who went from limited participation on Wednesday to full participation on Thursday, were the only changes.
St-Juste, Ford, Hargrave and receiver/returner Skyy Moore (ankle) did not practice.
For the Cowboys, only one starter did not practice on Wednesday due to injury. That was linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who missed the last four games with a hamstring injury. He progressed to limited participation on Thursday.
Ageless pass rusher Von Miller got a rest day on Wednesday and was full participation on Thursday.
Only cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) and offensive tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring) did not practice for Dallas, which is coming off a Thursday night game so is well-rested.

title: Packers Thursday Update From Practice: Two Texas-Sized Sighs of Relief
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers walked onto the practice field on Wednesday with two enormous question marks on defense.
Twenty-four hours later, their outlook has brightened at both.
At cornerback, starting cornerback Keisean Nixon returned to practice after, as coach Matt LaFleur put it, Nixon “was feeling a little something in his groin” on Wednesday so got the day off.
There’s no doubting Nixon’s toughness. This is his fifth season with the team and he hasn’t missed a game. He started all 17 games last season.
This season, he’s allowing only 8.7 yards per reception, 5.4 yards per target, and a 65.3 passer rating according to Stathead. Those are big improvements over 11.6 yards per catch, 7.5 yards per target and a 105.1 passer rating last season.
At defensive tackle, Jonathan Ford didn’t practice on Wednesday because of a calf injury but returned to the field on Thursday.
The availability of both players will be critical for the Packers against the high-powered Cowboys.
At cornerback, Benjamin St-Juste missed most of last week’s game with a hamstring injury and has not practiced this week. Dallas’ offense, of course, features quarterback Dak Prescott and the elite receiver duo of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. It would be huge for the Packers to have their starting corners, Nixon and Brandon Cisse, available.
At defensive tackle, Warren Brinson is on injured reserve and Javon Hargrave will land there following last week’s torn Achilles. Plus, first-year player Anthony Campbell is coming off an ankle injury that sidelined him the past three weeks.
Not practicing today: CB Benjamin St-Juste WR Skyy Moore DT Javon Hargrave Returning: CB Keisean Nixon DT Jonathan Ford Here is Savion Williams. pic.twitter.com/PnuV85FI3W
Five players didn’t practice on Wednesday. With the returns of Nixon and Ford, that was down to three on Thursday as the team practiced inside the Don Hutson Center because of the rain. Along with Hargrave and St-Juste, the only other player who didn’t practice was receiver/returner Skyy Moore.
Practicing again as their return-to-play windows have been opened were receiver Savion Williams, who’s in his second week of practice, and defensive tackle Jordon Riley, who returned this week.
Riley’s return will be important considering the absence of Hargrave and Brinson.
“I think he can do a lot of things,” coach Matt LaFleur said before practice. “I thought he played good football for us last year. Watching him and getting him back out on the practice field was great to see. This guy’s worked his tail off with our trainers, with our strength staff and really put himself in a pretty good position.”
At receiver, the Packers lost Jayden Reed early in the season and now Moore is out. That could mean more opportunities for J. Michael Sturdivant, the undrafted rookie whose first career touchdown last week was nullified by pass interference.
“We talk about it all the time – next-man-up mentality,” quarterback Jordan Love said. “I think for J-Mike, and we always say this, but for rookies it’s just how fast can you continue to evolve and learn from mistakes and learn from everything that happens in the game and learn from other people’s reps. There’s just so much put on you as a rookie.
“Another guy that hasn’t got too many reps with the 1s and now injuries, things like that happen, now he’s put in that role. I think he’s done a great job so far.
Cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who was acquired by the Cowboys in a trade with Pittsburgh a couple weeks ago, didn’t play in last week’s loss to Tampa Bay due to illness.
“On my way to the game, I was throwing up outside of my Uber,” he told DallasCowboys.com . “It was brutal. I'm not going to lie. … You go into the week thinking you're going to get more of a workload, and you're ready to go, and then that's ultimately what doesn't happen.
“It was very frustrating. I was prepared to play all week. My mindset was on playing, the mindset was to get the dub and, obviously, I didn't get to do that and we didn't get the dub. I was pretty pissed.”
Porter is past his illness and expects to be in the starting lineup on Sunday night.
The teams will file new injury reports after their Thursday practices. For now, here are the reports from Wednesday.

Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), C/G Jacob Monk (quad), DT Jordon Riley (Achilles), S Evan Williams (illness), WR Savion Williams (ankle), DT Devonte Wyatt (ankle).
Full participation: Edge Lukas Van Ness (shoulder).
Riley and Savion Williams have been designated to return from injured reserve and are within their 21-day practice windows.
Cowboys Wednesday Injury Report

Limited participation: CB Joey Porter (ankle).

title: Packers’ Christian Watson Blazing Pace That’s Second to None in NFL History
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – In five games, Green Bay Packers receiver Christian Watson has 474 receiving yards and six touchdowns.
It’s a small sample size, but not so small as to render the statistical projections completely useless. If Watson were to keep up that production over 17 games, he’d finish with 1,612 receiving yards and 20 touchdown catches.
That season has never been accomplished in NFL history.
In fact, even if you dial it back a bit, no player has ever reached 1,500 receiving yards and 18 touchdown catches in a season. Only five players have had 18-plus touchdown receptions in a season, with Davante Adams the most recent in 2020. From that quintet, Randy Moss’s 1,493 yards and NFL-record 23 touchdowns is the best season.
After practice on Wednesday, with the Packers getting ready for Sunday’s game against the Dallas Cowboys, Watson was asked about being mentioned in the same breath as Moss and Jerry Rice.
“It definitely motivates me to keep going, but I’m trying to continue to be the best version of myself,” he said. “I want to look back at the end of the season and be able to have those same comparisons rather than looking at it during the season.”
Watson is off to an incredible start to the season, bookended by six catches for 147 yards and two touchdowns in the opener at Minnesota and six catches for 143 yards and two touchdowns against Chicago on Sunday.
This is the fourth season together for Watson and Love. They’ve never connected for more than the six touchdowns that Watson has already.
“I think he’s just playing at a high level right now,” Love said on Wednesday. “He’s making plays. We know what type of speed Christian has – everybody knows what. He’s making plays when the ball is in his hands. Like that [second] touchdown catch he had [against Chicago], he’s making contested catches. That’s the area that everybody’s talked about, growth, and he’s been making huge strides in that area.”
Of the 56 receivers who have run at least 20 routes, Watson is fourth with a passer rating when targeted of 139.7 and sixth with 2.86 yards per route, according to Pro Football Focus. He’s caught 8-of-12 contested-catch opportunities, with the 66.7 percent success rate tied for 12th.
He’s third with 11.9 yards per target. The players ahead of him are Atlanta’s Drake London, who has zero touchdowns, and Baltimore’s Zay Flowers, who has two.
Obviously, Watson has elite physical tools. The growth has come through experience – he’s turned himself into a complete receiver and not just a deep threat – and the additional opportunities that have come through health and the evolving depth chart.
“I think he’s just a consistent player for us right now,” Love said. “He’s in the right spots, both the passing game, the run game. He knows what to do, he’s been in the system for a while and he’s a smart guy. So, now it’s just seeing how far we can take this thing with me and him and our connection.
“Really, for me, it’s just fun to watch. When you’ve got a guy that you can get on any route, you never know, he can take it to the crib at any time. For me, it’s finding ways to continue getting him the ball, putting him in great places and just keep letting him succeed and go do what he does.”
The interesting line there was Love saying “how far we can take this thing.” Does that mean they can be even more productive?
“Oh, yeah, for sure,” Love said.
“There’s more out there,” he said with a smile. “There’s more out there. There’s always more out there.”
“There's definitely more. Honestly, I could probably look back at the game and go back and say there's five plays. whether it be run game or pass play, that I wish I would have been better on or executed better,” he said.
“There’s always ways to still learn and grow from stuff. Even when you have success, there’s still things that we left out there that we want to have back. Obviously, perfection is almost impossible, but we’re still always trying to chase that. So, just finding ways to still clean things up and not leave anything out there.”
Green Bay’s single-season records are 1,553 yards by Davante Adams in 2021 and 18 touchdowns by Adams in 2020 and Sterling Sharpe in 1994. The only season of 1,400 yards and 14 touchdowns was Antonio Freeman’s 1,424 yards and 14 scores in 1998.
“I think he’s getting more opportunities,” coach Matt LaFleur said. “I think he’s done a great job of coming in – he’s always been in shape but he’s been able to stay on the field. Certainly, that’s something that we’ve challenged him. Like, ‘Hey, man, I know you run a lot of these deep routes but we need you in there as much as humanly possible,’ and he’s answered the bell. I think you’re seeing the growth of a player.
“For all these guys, the more they play, usually the better they get.”
While Seattle’s Jaxon Smith-Njigba is having an even better season than Watson – he’s fourth with 37 receptions and first with 583 yards and seven touchdowns – Watson among players with 20-plus catches is No. 1 with 18.2 yards per catch. Watson is the only player with more than 16.5 yards per catch and at least one touchdown.
“I think I’m right where I’m at but, obviously, I’ve got to keep on climbing,” he said after the game. “There’s a lot of individual goals I want to achieve, but I’ve got to keep on doing what I’m doing if we want to have success as a team. Obviously, they’re relying on me a lot, so I’ve got to keep on doing what I’m doing to obviously get the team the best chance to continue winning.”

title: Predicting Marvin Harrison Jr.’s Stat Line in Texans Debut vs. Jaguars
full_text:
The Houston Texans will be getting their first look at Marvin Harrison Jr. in their Week 6 trip to London against the Jacksonville Jaguars .
Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed earlier this week that Harrison Jr. would be making the trip overseas for this week's matchup, and would be due to play a certain number of snaps.
But how Harrison Jr.'s first game against the Jaguars could fare has the chance to go a few different directions. After all, it's a very quick turnaround for any player to make when being traded and dropped onto a new team in a week's span, and could lead to his performance in Week 6 being a bit more limited compared to how things might look a little later into the season.
So how might Harrison Jr.'s stat line look by the end of Week 6's matchup over the pond? Let's simply predict how the Texans' newest receiver could do in his official debut, and break down just how limited he could be in the offensive game plan.
DeMeco Ryans emphasized earlier this week that Harrison Jr. would be involved in the Texans' offense as soon as this weekend. However, he also made sure to note that he won't be expected to play a super high number of snaps .
"Don't expect him to come out and play all 60 snaps in the game," Ryans said on Wednesday. "But we'll make sure he gets what he needs, and make sure he's confident in what we're asking him to do."
So just how many snaps could Harrison Jr. play? One outcome that could make sense is simply putting him in the role that now-former Texans wideout Jared Wayne had been in for the first few weeks.
Jared Wayne and Marvin Harrison Jr. are vastly different talents, let's be clear. However, they are similarly big-bodied, outside receivers who can line up as a Z in several plays and situations, pairing pretty nicely next to the existing talent Houston has around the field at the position.
Last week, Wayne saw a little over 30% of the snaps on offense. He went without any offensive stats being recorded throughout, but he did see as high as seven targets back in Week 2 against the Cincinnati Bengals .
Imagine Harrison Jr. simply slotting into those same snaps; likely with a bit more involvement in terms of being targeted or being a first read, but maybe not on the field for an excessive amount until he's able to get a few more weeks of practice and overall reps under his belt.
A 30% snap share would likely be around the 15 to 20-snap mark. But in those limited looks, it feels likely that the Texans will involve him on a fair share of those plays––in this case, perhaps for four targets––to build up his confidence and rediscover some chemistry with his college quarterback, C.J. Stroud .
And in a best-case scenario for the Texans, maybe Harrison Jr. is able to haul in his second touchdown of the season so far. If Houston is within striking distance for a score, and there's an ideal situation for Harrison Jr. to fill into, why not start off the tenure with his new team on a good note?
So in all, a 3-43-1 stat line feels like a modest projection for Harrison Jr. in game one. It'd be a nice start for what hopes to be a long tenure in Houston, wouldn't overwhelm him with a ton of involvement, while also being paired with a ton of room to grow moving forward.

title: Texans Injury Report vs. Jaguars: 3 Players Ruled Out, 2 Questionable
full_text:
The Houston Texans have dropped their final injury report heading into their Week 6 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars over the pond in London .
And overall, it looks like the Texans will be down at least three players from their lineup, with two others remaining in question before Sunday's kickoff.
Let's break down the latest on the injury front for Houston:
WR Tank Dell: OUT (knee) S Jalen Pitre: OUT (shoulder) RB David Montgomery: OUT (groin) LB Henry To'oTo'o: QUESTIONABLE (shoulder) CB Jamarcus Ingram: QUESTIONABLE (elbow)
It was known from Thursday afternoon that the Texans would be without a couple of starters in defensive back Jalen Pitre and running back David Montgomery, who both suffered their respective injuries in last weekend's contest against the Tennessee Titans .
The good news is that neither have been placed on injured reserve in the days following. That means there's a pretty good chance that we'll see both of these guys back in the lineup within the next four weeks.

title: Texans' C.J. Stroud Defends Marvin Harrison Jr. Amid Outside Criticism
full_text:
Upon his arrival to the Houston Texans, wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. has seen no shortage of criticism from his first few years in the NFL.
Since being selected as the No. 4 pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, Harrison Jr.'s stock has largely been up and down in the league . His rookie season with the Arizona Cardinals was encouraging, but since then, things have been a bit turbulent.
It's almost a similar situation that Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud has faced himself over the past few seasons: he had a strong, Offensive Rookie of the Year campaign in 2023, but has seen many critics surface in the years since–– especially coming off of his latest postseason loss earlier this year.
So as Harrison Jr. takes the next step in his NFL career in Houston and looks to bounce back from his ups and downs, Stroud tends to have about as good a perspective as anyone on how to take on that outside noise.
Stroud addressed some of the criticism surrounding Harrison Jr. following the Texans' first practice with their new wide receiver earlier this week, ultimately giving some quality insight having been in a comparable position himself.
"I don't think anybody is ever a finished product. You're always learning ways to get better and improve at what you're already good at," Stroud said on Wednesday.
"I think there are two perspectives you can look at: the world's perspective, or what people think you are, and your own perspective of who you think you are and who you believe you can be. I think the latter is more important. I've learned that what people say doesn't really matter. They can't stop or start what you have going on."
"Marv knows that. He's a heck of a player. I don't agree with some of the things being said about him, but at the end of the day, those are outside opinions... I think he'll be fine. I'll try to be that resource for him if he needs me, but he's a confident dude. He'll be fine."
Even for Stroud himself, handling all of the critics that have surrounded him has still required an adjustment process on his part.
In his case, he's gone from being viewed as one of the brightest young quarterbacks in the NFL by many back during his rookie season, to now having an array of doubters questioning how good he really is in just a couple of years’ time.
In a world where just about everyone can voice their opinion, and in this type of profession, Stroud has come to learn that tuning out that noise–– whether it be good or bad–– is simply a part of the job.
"It's taken time, and I'm still working on it now," Stroud said of balancing praise and criticism.
"I remember my rookie year. I was playing really well, and everybody was praising me. I also remember a time in college when everybody was really hard on me and critical. Then I started playing really well, and everybody started loving me. I thought that was kind of weird because people were so up and down."
"At the end of the day, people are going to have opinions and critiques, and rightfully so. People get paid a lot of money to judge what we do, and we're in the entertainment business. We're not exempt from criticism. It's up to you whether you let it affect you."
Now with Harrison Jr. in the mix , Stroud can now go to battle with not only one of his former teammates from Columbus, but also alongside someone else that's faced their fair share of bashing from the court of public opinion. That's some pretty good motivation to be had for any player.

title: Why Texans Need RB Woody Marks to Deliver in Week 6 vs. Jaguars
full_text:
The Houston Texans are due to give their second-year running back Woody Marks a pretty notable workload in Week 6 against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
That's because his veteran counterpart in the backfield, running back David Montgomery, won't be making the trip to London because of the groin injury he suffered last weekend against the Tennessee Titans.
So for Marks, there's a good chance that he gets even more opportunities on the offensive side in Week 6 compared to what he saw against Tennessee. It was just last week when he recorded 19 touches for 85 all-purpose yards, setting up for his best day of this season by far, and showed that this run game might have a bit more life than once thought.
But with a matchup like the Jaguars , finding that same traction in the run game will be a task much easier said than done, and thus sets up for what could be Marks' biggest challenge of the year when combining his steep workload and the talent on the other end.
There's very few teams around the NFL right now playing better run defense than the Jaguars.
Through the first five games of the regular season, the Jaguars have allowed the lowest rushing yards per game in the NFL (63.8), the lowest rushing yards over expected (-0.84), have allowed just three rushing touchdowns, and are second in rushing yards allowed after contact (1.97).
On its own, those numbers are pretty daunting for the Texans to try and overcome. But the recent production of Houston's run game might tend to make that challenge even tougher.
The Texans come into this game with the second-lowest rushing yards per game (79.0) in the NFL, next to only the Green Bay Packers. They're one of four teams with a run-stuffed rate of over 20%, and have just 10 runs at 10-plus yards.
They're lacking explosiveness and overall production on the ground, which has led to C.J. Stroud and the passing game having to pick up some of that slack. In five games, Stroud has played about as well as you could hope considering the circumstances, but such a script against a team as talented as the Jaguars probably won't be cutting it .
Sure, the Texans certainly have shown improvement upfront and in their run game to offer some form of encouragement for this weekend. Yet there's little doubt that for that run game to be up to par, it all relies on Woody Marks to take care of his business.
The two aspects that Marks must key in on to ensure a successful day in London is to stay efficient in his opportunities on the ground, as well as provide a much-needed sense of explosiveness .
We've seen in the past how Marks can be a potent, home-run hitter in both the running and the passing game. But those highlights have also come with several moments where his efficiency wasn't exactly up to par, or the offensive line couldn't do him any favors, and led to many days averaging 3.0 yards per carry or less.
This season, he's had two games with that type of performance––coming in Week 2 against the Cincinnati Bengals (1.7 YPC) and Week 3 against the Indianapolis Colts (3.0 YPC).
If Marks can efficiently handle what is expected to be a heavy workload against a defense like this, as well as offer the Texans a few chunk plays in the process, there's little doubt that the day will be a successful one for the Texans' second-year runner.
Houston has had several games already this season where their running game proved to be underwhelming, and thus snowballed into an even bigger calamity for the offense entirely. Marks helping Houston avoid that type of outcome in London would be a huge step to get win number two in the books.
However, when looking at the track record of how this Jaguars run defense has handled opposing running backs this season, Marks certainly has some big hurdles to overcome to make that big day become a reality.

title: 3 Storylines I'm Watching Most in Texans' Week 6 Matchup vs. Jaguars
full_text:
The Houston Texans have their third AFC South matchup of the 2026 season on the horizon for Week 6, as they'll be making the trek overseas to London for a date against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
Last year, these two had split their season series 1-1. Jacksonville got the best of this group in Week 3, which sunk them to a brutal 0-3 through three games, while Week 10 back at home marked the Texans' first victory of an eventual eight-game win streak to finish the season at 12-5.
The Texans are certainly hoping that this game looks a little more like that second meeting from 2025 as opposed to the first. And in the process of their first matchup against Jacksonville for this season, there are a select few storylines worth keeping a close eye on from now until these two take the field at Wembley Stadium on Sunday morning.
Let's break down three of the bigger storylines surrounding the Texans' Week 6 matchup against the Jaguars that I'll be watching the closest:
The Texans will get their first look at Marvin Harrison Jr. within their offense in Week 6 as the team has confirmed that he will be making the trip to London to face the Jaguars, and he will be getting on the field.
The bigger question for Harrison Jr.'s Week 6 showing, though, is just how involved he'll be from the jump.
DeMeco Ryans has already emphasized that the Texans won't be rolling out their new wideout for a huge chunk of snaps for this game earlier in the week, and will likely only have a select few designed plays where he'll be able to get on the field.
So how much will Harrison Jr. be utilized? How does he look in his first game as a part of the Texans, catching passes from his college quarterback against a pretty stout Jaguars defense? All eyes will be on the 2024 No. 4 pick in this one, even if on the field for a limited amount of time.
Veteran running back David Montgomery won't be making the trip to London as he recovers from a groin injury suffered in Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans . That means Woody Marks is due to be the Texans' primary runner throughout the day against Jacksonville, as he was for virtually the entire second half last weekend.
And Marks had a solid game when given the opportunity against Tennessee. He had a season-high 15 carries to turn in 62 yards on the ground, and paired that with four receptions for 23 yards.
But this Jaguars run defense is a force to be reckoned with. Jacksonville has allowed the lowest yards per game (63.8 yds/gm) and the lowest rushing yards over expected (-0.84) through the first five weeks of this season, meaning there aren’t many better at stuffing the run in the NFL than this team.
If Marks is able to overcome the tough matchup, and be the explosive threat in the backfield that this Texans offense could really benefit from, it'll pay off some major dividends for this offense entirely.
The first four weeks of the season for the Texans' defense was a far cry from what they had been used to throughout all of their 2025 campaign.
After some electric performances from the likes of Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills in Week 1, along with CeeDee Lamb and the Dallas Cowboys in Week 4, the Texans decided to shift their defensive play-calling duties to head coach DeMeco Ryans, who had held onto the role for the first two seasons at the helm in Houston.
And that shift was able to work quite well against the Titans in Week 5 . Houston limited Cam Ward and their offense to just three points on the day, and looked a whole lot similar to the form Texans fans had gotten used to over the course of last season, and thus landed them win number one on the season.
Now though, the Texans have a much tougher date against another AFC South opponent in the Jaguars, who have been an above-average scoring attack en route to their own 4-1 start to the season, and can be a true test of whether or not this Houston defense really is back to where they left off last season.
