title: Potential Ben Bredeson Trade Makes Too Much Sense for Vikings to Ignore
full_text:
As the bye week continues, Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley is likely weighing the various avenues he can take to address his team's remaining roster problems. Specifically, the offensive ones. Whether it's more depth at wide receiver or help in the backfield, the Vikings clearly need help to unlock more firepower after averaging 21.8 points (T-21st) and 283 total yards (27th) per game through five weeks.
The left side of the offensive line is also a concern after the Vikings lost tackle Christian Darrisaw to concussion protocol, while guard Donovan Jackson's season is over due to a torn meniscus . Former undrafted blocker Joe Huber has been solid but nothing special filling in for Jackson so far; no one would blame Teasley & Co. for wanting more LG depth—if not someone who'd even improve the starting lineup.
That's why veteran guard Ben Bredeson could be on the Vikings' radar heading into the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline. With the Buccaneers heading towards seller's territory as they enter Week 6 with a 1-4 record, it makes sense for Teasley to give Tampa Bay GM Jason Licht a call.
If the last name sounds familiar, it's because the Buccaneers' blocker is the elder brother of Vikings rookie fullback Max Bredeson. Although a family reunion would certainly be heartwarming, a potential trade for the former 2020 fourth-rounder isn't just about reuniting the brothers or improving the locker room's already-good vibes.
After all, the elder Bredeson boasts the kind of experience Minnesota's O-line could use at the moment. The 28-year-old gap-opener has played 78 games (58 starts) across his time with the Buccaneers, Giants, and Ravens, as well as a trio of postseason appearances. Although he's played all three interior positions, most of Bredeson's snaps have come at left guard , where he's played 2,960 compared with 586 at center and 487 on the right side, per Pro Football Focus .
This is about adding LG depth, but that versatility could come in handy as injuries pile up later in the season.
Bredeson's individual stats won't blow anyone away, but he's still been a reliable asset on a struggling Bucs team this season. According to Pro Football Focus , his 61.2 run-block grade is tied for the second-best effort of his career , while his 62.9 pass-block grade is his third-best. For comparison, Huber owns grades of 60.5 and 46.5, respectively.
Jackson was arguably the Vikings' best offensive lineman before his injury, and while he's expected to make a full recovery, it isn't guaranteed that he'll pick up where he left off. He still needs to recover and go through rehab before proving himself all over again throughout the offseason, which is why having another capable LG around—even if you include Huber—would be a good idea.
Fortunately, Bredeson would be more than an average deadline rental that Minnesota would need to re-sign at season's end. The former Michigan Wolverine is under contract for the 2027 season with an affordable $8.2 million cap hit , according to Spotrac . And even if he proves to be a poor fit, the Vikings can designate him for a post-June 1 release, saving $7 million in cap space while leaving dead money in 2027 ($1.2 million) and 2028 ($2.5 million).
A trade also likely wouldn't cost Teasley too much draft capital. Bleacher Report' s Alex Kay projects the Vikings acquiring Bredeson and a 2027 seventh-rounder for a fifth-round pick in April's draft. While I don't think the Buccaneers would want to send any picks back if they're blowing it up, I could see the Vikings needing to give up a 2027 fourth- or fifth-rounder, along with one from the sixth or seventh round in 2028.
Assuming the Buccaneers keep losing, proven veterans like Bredeson will attract attention from playoff contenders. The Vikings should be in that conversation, especially since Jackson's year is done, giving them every reason to call the Bucs sooner rather than later.

title: Vikings Week 6: 3 Most Important Things to Watch for During Minnesota's Bye This Weekend
full_text:
The bye week is always a bittersweet event for any NFL fan.
While Vikings fans won’t be able to watch their team try to keep their unbeaten streak alive this weekend, the time off will let the team work through a growing list of offensive injuries. It also allows all of us to plop down on the couch with a bag of chips, a bowl of Top the Tater and a beverage of choice for a relatively stress-free Sunday of football.
Still, fans of the Purple and Gold have a few key storylines to keep an eye on this weekend. Here are three things to watch for in Week 6 with the Vikings on break.
The Vikings are one of two NFC North teams with an early Week 6 bye this season, as the Lions are also off for the week. That leaves the Bears and Packers as your two divisional rivals to rage-watch this weekend.
Luckily, they just played each other last week, so you won’t have to awkwardly root for one of them to win.
The Bears travel to Atlanta on Sunday to face a feisty Falcons squad . Atlanta should have Michael Penix Jr. back at quarterback barring any setbacks, after leaving last week’s game with a rib injury. The Packers will then host a desperate 2-3 Cowboys team at Lambeau for Sunday Night Football.
Needless to say, Vikings fans should have clear rooting interests in both games, as Minnesota can gain even more separation early in the divisional race. A loss would put both teams at an even 3-3 on the season.
After five weeks, only three undefeated teams remain in the NFL. The Vikings and 49ers are both 5-0, while the Chiefs come off a Week 5 bye at 4-0. No one gets a prize for being the last unbeaten team, but bragging rights and some playoff implications are on the line.
The Chiefs will host the winless Chargers at Arrowhead Sunday afternoon in a game they’ll be heavily favored to win. With this being an all-AFC matchup, the Vikings get no real benefit from the Chiefs taking their first loss of the season. Even so, Minnesota fans should root for an upset if they want to stand alone atop the mountain of unbeatens.
The 49ers' matchup against the Commanders, on the other hand, actually carries some weight.
It may seem ridiculous to discuss potential playoff tiebreakers before we’re even through October, but every game matters if Minnesota and San Francisco are battling for the NFC’s top seed throughout the season (h/t: ESPN's Adam Schefter).
Five weeks in: pic.twitter.com/KAhZ7tdjj3
The two NFC powerhouses will meet in Mexico City on Nov. 22, and any buffer Minnesota can build before then will be a major advantage. A Commanders victory at Levi’s Stadium would be a great first step.
With the Vikings pushing for a deep playoff run and the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaching quickly , it’s worth keeping an eye on teams that could be potential sellers. The Chargers, Titans and Dolphins are the obvious candidates, as none of them have even won a game so far in 2026. Miami is on their bye this week, but L.A.'s matchup against Kansas City and Tennessee’s trip to Indianapolis are worth monitoring for potential trade targets.
Chargers' pass rusher Khalil Mack is one name to watch as the Vikings' defense may look to add more weapons to its already aggressive arsenal (h/t: ESPN 's Adam Schefter).
After two trades last week, here are more names to monitor ahead of next month’s #NFL trade deadline. pic.twitter.com/i9XdEC0oPQ
The Eagles are also a fascinating team to watch as their season appears to be spiraling quickly. A fourth consecutive loss to the Panthers could prompt general manager Howie Roseman to make some dramatic roster decisions.

title: Just-Released WR Should Have Vikings' Attention as Depth Remains an Issue
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings remain undefeated as their bye week continues , but that doesn't mean they should be satisfied with their performance so far.
Although the Purple and Gold's special teams and defensive units are among the NFL's best, the Vikings' offense hasn't been firing on all cylinders this season. Sure, things were slowly improving heading into the bye, but there's still plenty of room for improvement—especially at wide receiver.
Outside of Justin Jefferson, who's been his usual dynamic self, Minnesota's wideout situation has been a bit of a mess over the past five games. Jordan Addison was picking up steam but hasn't played since Week 4 due to a hamstring injury. The Jauan Jennings signing has been a colossal bust so far ; Tai Felton has been invisible more often than not, and Myles Price has been too, who fumbled against the Saints last week.
Clearly, the Vikings need some WR help, and while general manager Nolan Teasley could look to the trade market, he should be interested in a newly available name that just hit the market.
The Vikings recently added Odell Beckham Jr. to their practice squad, and now they can sign another ex-Giant. On Friday morning, the Colts announced they've released veteran WR Darius Slayton , who signed with Indianapolis last month, two weeks after New York released him .
We have released WR Darius Slayton.
With their top wideout, Alec Pierce, dealing with a foot injury, the Colts brought Slayton in for help. The 29-year-old playmaker, however, didn't suit up for any games and was scratched in Week 5 due to a knee injury.
Assuming that the knee issue isn't severe, though, the Vikings should at least kick the tires to see if Slayton is open to joining Murray's arsenal.
Drafted 171st overall in 2019, Slayton was a reliable weapon throughout his seven years with the Giants. He was often available (missing 11 regular-season games) and productive, hitting the 700-yard mark four times while averaging 651.3 receiving yards over his last four seasons. A large part of that success stems from his blazing speed, with a 4.39-second 40-yard dash time .
For what it's worth, Jefferson and tight end T.J. Hockenson are the only Vikings on pace to surpass 700 receiving yards this season.
It's been a few years since Slayton achieved that feat, but that doesn't mean he can't help the Vikings.
He just recorded 37 catches for 538 receiving yards and a touchdown in 14 games, averaging 14.5 yards per catch, only slightly below his career average (15.0). Slayton's four penalties last season might raise some concerns, but hopefully it's something that head coach Kevin O'Connell can iron out of his game.
Slayton's reputation as a decent human being is another reason why the Vikings should want him in the locker room. He won the 2025 Alan Page Community Award for his community work in the New York area, and that's a big deal since the award is considered "the NFLPA’s highest honor." More leadership like that is never a bad thing.
It also wouldn't hurt to inject another veteran face into the practice squad after signing Beckham.
Dillon Bell and Michael Briscoe have potential, but they're both undrafted rookies whom the Vikings might not be ready to throw into the fire yet. Second-year WR Jeshaun Jones made his first-career catch (h/t Minnesota Vikings UK) against the Saints in Week 5, but even then, he played more special teams snaps (11) than offense (six).
First career catch for Jeshaun Jones 🙌 📺 Watch live on @nflondazn 🎧 Listen live on @talkSPORT pic.twitter.com/novGysE5yv
Slayton likely won't be a significant upgrade over the current taxi-squad options, but his experience stemming from 106 career games (78 starts) can't be understated. The Vikings would be better off throwing him into a high-stakes late-season game than an unproven undrafted rookie, who might not be ready for that kind of pressure.
Injuries around the NFL will keep piling up with each passing week, meaning teams will only get more desperate to sign a veteran WR like Slayton. If the Vikings are wise, they'll use their available time during the bye week to contact the just-released playmaker, potentially taking the first of several steps toward addressing their receiver-related depth concerns.

title: Aaron Jones' Role Must Change Significantly After Vikings' Bye
full_text:
Aaron Jones Sr. has been an absolute workhorse for the Minnesota Vikings this season. Through the first five weeks of the season, the veteran running back has played 73 percent of the team's offensive snaps despite being 31 years old and having an extensive injury history.
Jones was forced to carry the team on the ground when Jordan Mason needed surgery on his thumb and was placed on injured reserve. The Vikings' backup running back is eligible to return in Week 7, and having him back should make things a lot easier on Jones.
In Week 5 against the New Orleans Saints, Jones played 87% of Minnesota's offensive snaps. Although he turned that into 25 carries for 113 yards and a touchdown, plus three catches for four yards, the Purple and Gold cannot afford to continue working him to this extent.
Mason will be in line to handle a healthy amount of work, but the Vikings will not phase Jones out of the offense completely. Relying on a one-two punch of the running back duo will yield the best results in future weeks.
It is a shame that rookie running back Demond Claiborne and veteran backup DeeJay Dallas couldn't pitch in more while Mason was out, but Minnesota was fortunate that Jones was able to do so much while his backup got healthy.
To put things in perspective, Claiborne has participated in 7% of the Vikings' offensive snaps this season, while Dallas has been on the field for 12%. It is even worse when looking at only the Saints game, where Dallas played five offensive snaps and Claiborne played four.
Minnesota can't afford to have Mason miss any more time, and Jones has been too valuable to risk by playing the ridiculous number of snaps he's had recently. Although Claiborne and Dallas can't be trusted to give the running back duo some relief, Jones and Mason need to lean on each other to provide rest during the remaining weeks of the 2026 NFL season.
It wouldn't be entirely shocking if Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley explored free agency and the trade market to try to get a running back to help Jones and Mason. Unless head coach Kevin O'Connell feels comfortable with the current positional depth chart, there needs to be some change made to keep the top two contributors healthy and available.
Expect Minnesota to do what they can to cut Jones' offensive snaps starting in Week 7. Although he did an admirable job while Mason was out, the Vikings can't afford to continue working him the way they have over the last few weeks.

title: 3 Vikings Firmly on Thin Ice During the Week 6 Bye (Josh Metellus Is Becoming an Issue)
full_text:
The Week 6 bye couldn't have come sooner for a Vikings team dealing with a long list of injuries. Despite those ailments, the Purple and Gold are 5-0 and sitting atop the NFC North as they reach the second half of their bye week.
Although the Vikings are undefeated, there are still issues to be addressed . While some players are thriving this season, others are struggling to make a positive impact when on the field.
Some of the Vikings' players are on thin ice after multiple weeks of ineffectiveness. The clock is ticking on them to find their role on the team. If they can't, they may end up losing snaps or even their job on the team
Minnesota's big free-agent wide receiver signing this offseason has been a flop this season. In the team's first five games, Jauan Jennings has played 201 offensive snaps and has only caught two of the five passes thrown his way for nine yards. Not exactly worth the $8 million cash he's earning this season, per Spotrac.
There are already rumblings that Jennings could potentially be on the trade block since he has struggled to contribute to the Vikings' passing attack this year. Minnesota would be silly not to listen to offers to try to recoup an asset before the trade deadline. Needless to say, don't be surprised if he's traded, assuming that he remains on thin ice.
The Vikings prepared to limit the defensive snaps of veteran safety Harrison Smith by drafting Miami defensive back Jakobe Thomas in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft and signing undrafted free agent Jacob Thomas out of James Madison.
While both those rookies are growing and developing, Minnesota has played Josh Metellus on every defensive snap this season. In 295 defensive snaps and four special teams snaps, he has earned a putrid Pro Football Focus grade of 40.2 , ranking him 90th out of 96 qualifying safeties this year.
Metellus has played well in previous seasons, but hasn't found his footing in 2026. Minnesota will be patient with the versatile defender because they know he can rise above the recent struggles, but until one of the Thomas rookies is ready for a bigger role, he will need to be a workhorse .
Sometimes the hype around a player gets so out of hand that they can't possibly live up to the expectations. The Vikings brought back Aaron Jones Sr. on a reworked deal and have Jordan Mason returning to injured reserve after the bye
The Vikings drafted Demond Claiborne in the sixth round of the 2026 NFL Draft to hopefully become a contributor for Minnesota. Instead, Claiborne and DeeJay Dallas have been unable to share the burden of rushing the ball with Jones.
Claiborne isn't in danger of losing his job, but his ineffectiveness could lead the Vikings to look for a more reliable third option in the backfield . So far, he has run the ball six times for 13 yards and caught two passes for eight yards while only playing 18 offensive snaps.

title: 3 Vikings Overreactions After the First Quarter of 2026 Season (Is Kyler Murray the Future?)
full_text:
A quarter of the way through the 2026 NFL season , the Vikings are just one of three remaining undefeated teams. And while it hasn't always looked pretty, it's hard to complain about a 5-0 start.
Still, there are plenty of questions to be asked about this Jekyll and Hyde team, and we're here to judge some of them. Is Kyler Murray the guy for 2027? Should Brian Flores have Kevin O'Connell's job?
Let's get it those and more with some overreactions five games in.
After two impressive weeks, a picture of what Minnesota's offense could look like with Murray for the next few months (or years) is starting to take shape. Despite a rocky start, Murray has racked up 543 total yards over the past two games and has the Vikings' offense looking functional .
As he gets more comfortable (h/t Bring Me The Sports ' Will Ragatz), Murray should improve even more in this new iteration of O'Connell's offense. But what level of play—or wins—will have the Vikings shelling out $200 million to retain him?
Here's Kyler Murray converting nine third downs against the Saints with his arm and his legs. Good football player. pic.twitter.com/1e0zLkSs51
It's hard to say, and if Murray's play is good enough to warrant a new deal, he'll certainly have the attention of other teams as well. Baker Mayfield's recent three-year, $165 million deal is likely the starting point for Murray, assuming he continues his 2026 ascension, and as much as the Vikings may like keeping their current starter, they'll need to put their money where their mouth is after essentially getting him for pennies this season.
Despite Murray's shorter stature, an even shorter history of winning football, and debatable fit with O'Connell, it would certainly be hard to let yet another veteran walk and go on to do great things. If Murray delivers the Vikings' first playoff win in seven years, the decision will be an impossible one , especially with the possibility of Justin Herbert, Mac Jones or others becoming available.
This idea has come up often enough that it deserves addressing. Clearly, the Vikings have been propelled by Flores's elite defense, while O'Connell and the offense have lagged behind, tinkering and toiling to simply achieve mediocrity.
But would the Vikings actually move on from O'Connell in favor of  Flores?
O'Connell has yet to win a playoff game since becoming the head man in 2022, and just bailed on his 10th-overall pick quarterback after 10 starts. It's not the greatest resume, and for most franchises, moving on seems like the prudent thing to do, barring an epic playoff run in 2026.
And yet, the Vikings are not like most franchises, and their faith in O'Connell appears to be just as strong as it was the day they hired him. That's for good reason, too.
As the man himself has pointed out several times, when the Vikings stay healthy at quarterback, O'Connell's teams win. A lot. In the seasons that O'Connell had his starter all year, he's 27-7. In the years he hasn't, the Vikings are 17-18. Of course, any coach would be better off with their starting quarterback staying healthy, but O'Connell has proved with two, and now maybe three , different signal-callers that he can win double-digit games with at least average play behind center.
Flores is a genius in his own right, and he might very well get another opportunity elsewhere, but it's just too hard to see the Vikings moving away from O'Connell.
Speaking of Flores, the Vikings' defense is playing some of the best football in the NFL , and there are exactly zero offensive coordinators in the league looking forward to facing Minnesota right now. But despite ranking top-five in virtually every defensive metric, does trouble lie ahead?
The answer is no, unless injuries start to stack up. Eight of the Vikings' defensive starters have been on the field for at least 80% of the snaps (h/t ESPN ), highlighting both their injury luck and a possible lack of depth.
Are rookies Caleb Banks, Domonique Orange or Jake Golday ready to start 10 or more games if needed? Likely not, and the Vikings probably know that. If a key injury happened, general manager Nolan Teasley & Co. could add a free-agent veteran while ramping their rookies up to speed. Still, despite the overwhelming amount of snaps from the starters, there's little reason to think the defense would crater if one or even several were lost to injury.
Surely the injury bug will bite at some point, but the Vikings are too well-balanced and well-coached to see the wheels fall completely off. Moving on.

title: 3 Winners & 2 Losers From Vikings' Pre-Bye Week Performance
full_text:
While many fans, players, and coaches hate the idea of an early NFL bye, the 5-0 Vikings may be very thankful for theirs. The team has battled through its fair share of adversity on its undefeated start, including a mounting list of injuries and an offense that is only beginning to find its identity.
Still, several players have stood out for their consistency and performance, while others have disappointed early on.
Here are my three biggest winners and two glaring losers for the Vikings through five games.
A Vikings kicker getting this much hype means one thing: get ready for a nerve-racking NFC Championship Game. Kidding (hopefully).
If we’re being honest, every longtime Vikings observer is terrified of Reichard’s “inevitable” Minnesota moment of misery shared by so many kickers in franchise history. So far, there’s plenty of reason to believe he may just be the one to change the narrative.
His 34 straight successful field goals, dating back to last season, put him just ten shy of the 44-kick record held by the legendary Adam Vinatieri. We even have fans throwing his name out in MVP talks to start the season. Heck, even former Vikings linebacker Anthony Barr mentioned the idea of Reichard securing the honor on the Bent Outta Shape Podcast he hosts with former teammate Eric Kendricks (h/t: @BentOuttaShape_).
Could Vikings kicker Will Reichard win MVP?! 🤔 New episode of BOS is out now 💯 pic.twitter.com/ZBEJoXhtgj
Reichard’s 53 points currently place him third in the NFL behind Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (54) and Colts kicker Spencer Shrader (58).
The Jauan Jennings situation seems to be reaching a boiling point after he showed visible frustration on the sideline Sunday in New Orleans. His two receptions for only nine yards on five targets through four games played are frustrating enough, but the film is showing that he’s actually getting open fairly often (H/t: Janik Eckardt).
Kyler inexplicably turning down an open Jauan Jennings in the endzone two plays before the Myles Price fumble pic.twitter.com/zw9rjAMwzi
His slow start sparked trade speculation early on, with his former team, the 49ers, looking like a realistic partner. Hopefully, the Vikings and Jennings can work things out so he can build his connection with quarterback Kyler Murray. After all, the Vikings desperately need depth at wide receiver.
Despite missing almost two full games with a sprained ankle and catching only one touchdown from his starting QB, Jefferson’s three receiving TDs in five games have already surpassed his two-TD total from 2025. I know, not exactly a high bar to clear, but it's clear Jefferson is truly enjoying football again.
His touchdown against the Saints in his home state of Louisiana showed all the typical traits of a classic Jefferson highlight: a jaw-dropping catch, an endzone Griddy, and a sideline celebration with his teammates .
Whole sideline was hyped for the Kyler to Jettas TD. pic.twitter.com/rQfaBLPckT
The Vikings' offense still has room to grow, but it seems like the Justin Jefferson we all know and love is fully back in action.
Is it punching down to say a sixth-round rookie RB has been a disappointment? Maybe, but it’s hard to ignore how rough Demond Claiborne’s 2026 start has been , despite having more opportunities than many expected.
Training camp showed Claiborne’s explosive speed and potential, but it also gave a laundry list of reasons he’d be unlikely to see the field early. Ball security, pass blocking, catching, and vision were all concerns this summer.
The rookie was listed as inactive in Week 1, but Jordan Mason's injured reserve stint opened the door for him beginning in Week 2. Still, the team cycled through several RB additions and even placed recent signing DeeJay Dallas above Claiborne on the depth chart. When he did get opportunities, Claiborne often looked unprepared for the speed of the NFL game, missing a wide-open gap in Tampa that could have led to a TD with his blazing speed (h/t: Patrick Siepman).
Demond Claiborne struggled in the preseason and missed this massive hole yesterday. Should the Vikings try and trade for a RB? pic.twitter.com/mzurfKCTd2
Claiborne is physically gifted but still has a long way to go to process NFL defenses.
The third-year pass rusher did not register a sack in Week 5 and is still third in the league in sacks and first in the NFC with 5.5 through five games. Dallas Turner, who is still only 23, has been a key piece of the Vikings' dominant defensive start .
Some fans showed hesitation about Turner’s increased role this season after the team traded Jonathan Greenard to the Eagles during April’s draft. That was understandable, given Greenard’s impact over two seasons and Turner’s early-career inconsistencies. So far, Turner has put any of those concerns to rest in 2026.
The Vikings seem to have found their next in a long line of dominant pass rushers.

title: Revisiting 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Five Weeks Into the Season (Has Flores's Defense Exceeded Expectations?)
full_text:
Before the Vikings even took a snap, I wrote about three bold predictions that could make or break the 2026 season. Some still have life; another is already buried six feet under. It's easy to throw guesses at the wall and see what sticks, but it's another thing to confront those and even admit defeat.
The 5-0 Vikings have surprised many and shocked even more with a perfect start to the campaign, so let's see how close (or far) I sit with these preseason predictions as their Week 6 bye continues .
Get back up off the floor, cut the laughter, and hear me out on this one.
The Vikings really headed into the season looking folks straight in the eye and said, "We're starting a pair of Kwesi Adofo-Mensah Day 3 picks and a former UFL player up front, and we're going to win." So you may forgive me if I didn't have the utmost confidence in Levi Drake Rodriguez, Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins, Jalen Redmond and—oh yeah—a pair of rookies who didn't exactly dominate the preseason.
And yet, here we are six weeks into the season .
The Vikings currently have the NFL's fifth-best run defense, allowing just 86.6 yards per game, and clearly a far cry from a bottom-five unit. And while they almost certainly won't drop to that level, their toughest days still lie ahead. The defensive coordinator Brian Flores's unit still has yet to face Jahmyr Gibbs (twice), Bijan Robinson, Jonathan Taylor, Christian McCaffrey, and 2025's rushing champion James Cook this season.
I don't think this hot take will ring true come Week 18, but I also don't think they'll remain in the top 10 after this gauntlet either.
Hey, now we're talking. Despite featuring a line with Christian Darrisaw and Brian O'Neill, this prediction was shaping up to be mostly true until Jackson suffered a season-ending injury in Week 4. Up until that point, he had just two allowed pressures on the year, and zero quarterback hits or sacks. Not too shabby.
After an up-and-down rookie season plagued by a wrist injury, Jackson showed enough of what made him a first-round pick. But now, with two seasons cut short due to injury, he will also face an uphill battle to continue his impressive trajectory.
Meanwhile, Darrisaw remains as talented as they come, but now has a sixth straight season of missing at least a game due to injury . O'Neill is steady as usual and may take this year's crown as the Vikings' top protector.
This one still has some juice, and at 5-0, anything and everything is on the table. The division will stay tight all the way to the finish, and despite the perfect record, the Vikings have just a two-game lead over every other team in the NFC North. So their playoff seed, barring a repeat of 2016, could be anything from one to seven at this point.
Initially, my biggest worry about making the playoffs in 2026 was Kyler Murray getting off to a slow start, and sure enough, his start with the Vikings took off about as fast as Linval Joseph's 40-time. I recall wondering how he might mesh with head coach Kevin O'Connell.
But despite the rough start in Green Bay and another dud against Tampa Bay, Murray has strung together some really nice weeks as of late, completing 76% of his passes over the last two weeks. O'Connell has also adjusted and run more shotgun against Miami than he ever has before.
Is an NFC Championship Game in the cards? Absolutely, but the defense's health and Murray's ascension will be key.

title: 3 Free-Agent TEs for Vikings to Sign as T.J. Hockenson Injury Remains a Concern During Bye Week
full_text:
The Vikings were already hurting at tight end entering Week 5, but when T.J. Hockenson left the game with a suspected concussion against the Saints, that situation got even worse for head coach Kevin O'Connell. As of Thursday morning, there have been no updates on Hockenson's condition, and even though the Vikings have extra time due to their bye , the last thing they need is another offensive concern.
After all, Josh Oliver has been on injured reserve with a potentially season-ending biceps tear. He was typically used as a blocking specialist as well as a sneaky option in the passing attack. Not having him available is tough, and the TE-related struggles will compound if Hockenson misses extended time.
Against the Saints, the Vikings used a combination of Gavin Bartholomew and Ben Yurosek at tight end. Bartholomew took on the role of the receiving tight end , while Yurosek was more of a blocker in the offense.
If O'Connell isn't sure he can trust Bartholomew and Yurosek if Hockenson is sidelined indefinitely, the Vikings need to explore other options to provide depth and talent at the position.
Here are three potential reinforcement options for O'Conell & Co. to consider.
A Swiss Army knife of a player, Taysom Hill is a player who could do a lot of things for the Vikings. While with the Saints, he was known for being a tight end, quarterback, receiver, or special teams player when he was needed.
Hill is 36 years old, so he wouldn't be a long-term asset for Minnesota, but that's not what they need him to be. The Vikings would want him to run routes and be a receiver, which he has shown the ability to do over his nine previous NFL seasons.
Catching 110 passes for 1,034 yards and 11 touchdowns is great, but he also has 489 rushing attempts for 2,551 yards and 34 TDs. However, due to his age and with his complicated skill set, the Vikings may be looking for a more traditional and complete tight end. Still, it's worth considering.
Will Dissly is six years younger than Hill, but has eight years of NFL experience. Although he is better known for his time with the Seahawks, he spent the last two seasons with the Chargers, playing 24 games in which he caught 61 passes for 578 yards and two touchdowns.
Dissly fits more of the traditional TE role, like Hockenson. He catches about 80% of his targets and could be a reliable target for starting Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray if Hockenson can't suit up.
A six-foot-four, 265-pound tight end, Dissly has the size to be a blocker if needed as well. He posted run-block and pass-block grades of 64.1 and 74.3 , respectively, according to Pro Football Focus last season.
Even if Minnesota only wants a temporary player to fill in until Hockenson returns, it makes sense to take a look at the former NFC West standout.
Bringing a former Vikings tight end back to Minnesota can make a lot of sense. Drafted 157th overall in 2018, Tyler Conklin spent his first four seasons with the Purple and Gold before moving to the Jets, Chargers and Lions before becoming a free agent in 2026.
At one time, Conklin was a hot commodity. After leaving the Vikings, he signed a three-year deal with the Jets worth $21 million and played out his entire contract. Last season, his one-year deal with Detroit was worth $1.3 million, so it isn't unfathomable to imagine he'd be a relatively inexpensive player to sign six weeks into the season.
Conklin could be an interesting practice-squad stash who could be elevated if needed while Hockenson is out. He could help Bartholomew and Yurosek without taking away from their development and growth, providing security and depth in the meantime.

title: Patriots 'Likely' to Make Major A.J. Brown Move Ahead of Week 6
full_text:
It's not official yet, but the New England Patriots could be getting a major piece of their offense back this week.
According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Patriots "will likely" activate wide receiver A.J. Brown from injured reserve to play this week against the New York Jets. The star wideout, who suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 1, returned to practice and participated in a limited capacity.
The Patriots do have an open spot on the 53-man roster, allowing Brown to be added straight to the active roster. Should the team not activate him, they'll have a 21-day window for him to return. He was listed as questionable for this week's game .
As of Friday afternoon, it was up in the air if Brown would play or not.
"We won't make that decision until tomorrow, so we'll have to see how he responds from practice today and then go from there," head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters.
The Patriots traded two draft picks (including their first rounder in 2028) for Brown's services, but haven't been able to enjoy his talents. He caught just three passes against the Seattle Seahawks in the opener, but has missed the last four games on the sideline.
Still, he's been engaged with his teammates and coaches. Brown was spotted in the locker room the past two weeks, often in cleats and chatting with Drake Maye . He's also been active on social media, cheering on his fellow wide receivers during games.
Without Brown (and Mack Hollins, who was placed on IR following the Patriots' 29-26 win over the Buffalo Bills), the Patriots had just four wideouts active — Romeo Doubs, Kyle Williams, DeMario Douglas and Efton Chism III.
"I feel like the guys did a great job. You know, last week (against the Las Vegas Raiders) was phenomenal," Brown said. "Obviously, there were still things to improve on and they would tell you that, but I think they did really well. Whenever I do decide to come back, I just want to add and continue to keep putting it out on display."
Brown will be a big jolt for a Patriots offense that's started to find its footing in recent weeks. Struggles early in the year put the team in a rut, but now they've started to open up (and it helps that Maye is playing lights out again). Now that they can add their top-tier pass catcher to that unit, the Patriots should be firing on all cylinders this week.
Vrabel said that this week of practice was good for Brown to get back into the swing of things.
"I mean, I think he looks OK," Vrabel said. "Like everybody, some good plays, some bad plays. I try to see where his conditioning level is."
The Patriots will announce any other roster moves at 4 p.m. today.

title: Predicting How Patriots Look vs. Jets in Week 6: Is It a Trap Game?
full_text:
The New England Patriots swept the New York Jets a season ago. There's no reason to believe that it won't happen again in 2026.
Despite starting off slow, both teams have started to find a more balanced footing heading into Week 6. The Patriots are one game up on the Jets in the AFC East standings, and are a win away from making their winning streak three. But the Jets have gotten good play out of Geno Smith under center.
"He's done a fantastic job," Mike Vrabel said this week. "And so, if you want to try to create turnovers, you're going to have to actually go out and force them. He hasn't made many mistakes. He's been really good with the football. He’s been decisive, has been able to create some X plays."
Ahead of Week 6, Patriots On SI beat reporters Ethan Hurwitz and Zac Ventola break down how the game will unfold, which players will be x-factors and predict a final score. Who do you think is right?
The Jets have Breece Hall as their top back, but a quad injury is holding him out of the game. That means it will be Braelon Allen for a second-straight week for New York. He rushed for more than 100 yards a week ago against Cleveland, and the Patriots front seven will need to key into who Vrabel called "a smooth runner."
The Patriots' defense has helped carry the load this season, and it hasn't come because of the secondary. That unit has dealt with injury after injury to open up the year, and they'll be down Carlton Davis and Karon Prunty once again. Even though New England's offense is gaining momentum, it will be the other side of the ball that will need to shine.
One of the players who can truly break out for the Patriots is the second-round rookie in Jacas . He recorded a sack in his first game in Seattle, but has taken a backseat to Elijah Ponder in the pass rushing department since. That's not to say that he's been bad by any stretch of the imagination, but he's yet to have a true breakout game. This can be his shot.
Final Score Prediction: Patriots 34, Jets 10
The Patriots have rattled off wins against the Bills and Raiders, who both came into the matchup with winning records. Now yes, any given Sunday is a real thing, but it's hard to imagine the Patriots losing to a Jets team that's just been a doormat for most of the 21st century. If Brown plays — even in a limited capacity — the Patriots' offense can roll once again.
The Patriots have far fewer questions surrounding its team this week than it has in its past few games. New England went into its matchups against the Jacksonville Jaguars and Buffalo Bills unsure of the level quarterback Drake Maye would perform at. Then, against the Las Vegas Raiders, the Patriots had multiple of their best players ruled out due to injuries.
Against the Jets this weekend, the stars seem to have aligned. Maye has scored eight touchdowns in his past two games, while New England begins to get healthier. Star wide receiver A.J. Brown returned to practice this week from injured reserve, while cornerback Christian Gonzalez has no injury designation for Sunday.
Last time out against the Jets, Maye had a field day. The Patriots signal caller completed 19 of his 21 pass attempts, tossing for five touchdowns and more than 250 yards. He also tallied those numbers despite being taken out of the 42-10 win midway through the third quarter. Coming off of a performance against Las Vegas where Maye tallied nearly 400 total yards and five touchdowns, I expect Madden-esque numbers this Sunday.
Final Score Prediction: Patriots 38, Jets 13
Mark my words: I do not see a world where the Patriots lose this game. Yes, the Jets are a substantially better team than they were a year ago … but they are still the Jets. I expect Maye to throw four touchdowns before New England allows backup quarterback Tommy DeVito to take the reins late in the fourth quarter. With a Thursday Night Football matchup against the Chicago Bears on the horizon, the Patriots should on the board early and often to give their starters some much-needed rest late in the game.

title: Jets' Defensive Front Pose Biggest Threat to Drake Maye, Patriots
full_text:
Despite selling out of stars DL Quinnen Williams and CB Sauce Gardner, the New York Jets have put together a pair of scrappy wins in five games behind impressive defensive performances.
Currently, the Jets rank fourth in yards allowed per game (293) and are tied for fourth in total sacks (17). Last year's second-worst placed team (based off records) in the NFL is in the midst of a full on rebuild, behind defensive minded coach Aaron Glenn.
Leading the front seven of the defense is veteran DeMario Davis, currently in his 15th year and back with the team that drafted him. Other veteran presences include fourth-year player Will McDonald IV and veteran linebacker Kingsley Enagbare, who has two sacks already this season.
The real threat within this defense comes in the form of a rookie 251-pound edge rusher. David Bailey was the second overall pick in the 2026 draft, and has taken the league by storm as a front-runner for the Defensive Rookie of the Year award. The 23-year-old out of Texas Tech already has five sacks on the season, tied for fourth most among all NFL players.
Most of the success for this quarterback-hungry passing attack has come on the blitz. The Jets defense blitzes at a 47% rate, the third highest in the NFL and a signature play calling style of Glenn's.
However, Drake Maye has the fourth most passing yards against the blitz this season, and in 2025 was statistically the best performingquarterback against the blitz. This leaves a big question mark as to how effective and often New York's pass rush will be, and makes for entertaining chess match along the line of scrimmage.
It also leaves a big challenge for veteran offensive tackle Morgan Moses, who previously played for the Jets, and rookie offensive tackle Caleb Lomu, who is slated to make his first NFL start in place of an injured Will Campbell.
In addition to a heavy pass rush, the Patriots will be challenged to move the ball at extended distances downfield, with the Jets having one of the top safety groups in the league. The threat of the bltiz will also force Maye to get the ball out early, meaning there is a lesser chance of explosive plays happening on the Patriots offensive side of the ball.
Despite having an interior line that generates the fifth-fewest quarterback pressures (21) in the league and second to last in pass rush win rate (10.1%), the threat of outside pressure makes up for a lack of interior hurriedness.
Another strength of the Jets defense will test the Patriots' turnover troubles, which has been a challenge for this offensive group since last year's post season. New York has forced 10 fumbles this season, the second most of all defenses, while the Pats have put the ball on the ground four times, tied for the fourth most across the NFL.
Despite having positive points allowed statistics (the Jets average 19.2 points per game, tied for sixth in the NFL), their opposition has proven to be less challenging — meaning the Patriots offense has a chance to expose this statistically competent defense.
The only real test for the Jets was against the Lions, a game in which they led up 31 points. All other offenses the team has played rank bottom-five in the NFL (with the exception of the Chicago Bears, led by backup quarterback Tyson Bagent).
Stats aside, the real test this weekend happens upfront for the Patriots. Down two starting offensive linemen , New England will face one of the best pass rushes in the league on the outside, and one of the more trigger happy blitz play callers in the NFL.
If the Patriots want to improve to 4-2 on Sunday, their game plan will likely be geared towards protecting the edge and getting the ball out quickly.

title: Patriots, TreVeyon Henderson Remain Optimistic About Ankle Injury
full_text:
FOXBORO — Last week against the Las Vegas Raiders, TreVeyon Henderson suffered an ankle injury and would be ruled out before the game was over . Henderson, who dealt with an ankle ailment that held him out of Week 1 as well, was a limited participant in practice all week.
He looked good moving on the practice field, but how did the second-year running back feel?
"Honestly, yeah. I was surprised. I felt a little bit different than what they diagnosed it as and what the MRI showed," Henderson told reporters in the locker room Friday, acknowledging that it was in fact a high-ankle sprain. "I'm hoping that I'm able to be out there with the guys and try to help this team continue in games."
Henderson will be questionable heading into the Patriots' Week 6 matchup with the New York Jets, one of several players who'll likely have that designation slapped onto them. Head coach Mike Vrabel wouldn't go as far as to confirm if Henderson would play, but seeing him out on the field for their final practice of the week is a positive sign.
"There'll be some guys listed as questionable," Vrabel said. "(We'll) see how TreVeyon responds in the morning. Again, see how they come in and then we'll evaluate and go from there."
Henderson, who's run for 163 yards and one touchdown this season, got banged up in the first half of last week's game. He wasn't ruled out immediately and remained on the sideline for a little bit before heading into the Patriots locker room. It wasn't until halftime that he and offensive tackle Will Campbell ( who suffered a knee injury on the same drive ) were downgraded to out.
"Honestly, once that happened, I couldn't put any pressure on my right side," Henderson said. "And so I tried to get back out there, but it just wasn't where it needed to be."
The Patriots had three practices this week, and reporters saw Henderson moving around for two of them. He participated in all three of the sessions, but now the question will be if he's able to progress into a game situation. For now, all the 23-year-old can do is just see how he responds in the next few days.
"I feel pretty good," Henderson said. "I think I'm getting better. We'll see how things continue to go and the decision that we all end up making."
If Henderson isn't able to go on Sunday, the Patriots have three other options that could step up into that RB2 spot. The likely option is Corey Kiner, who is the third running back on the active roster . He did fumble in last week's game, but has chipped in on special teams.
Vrabel told reporters he feels comfortable in Kiner's abilities, even after the turnover, while mentioning that the fumble wasn't solely on the running back.
"We all have to take care of the ball, but Corey did a lot of really good things, so there's a high confidence (in him)," Vrabel said. "Nobody notices or really talks about the guy that comes back into the gap and hammers the ball out. You guys always fail to mention that. You guys always just put it on the guy who has the ball. So we all share in that, and we'll be better.
"But I like the way Corey runs, and yes, he does have to hang onto the ball. We got to do a better job  of protecting the guy, keeping people away from him."
The Patriots also have Lan Larison and Hassan Haskins on the practice squad, and could end up being elevated to the game day roster on Saturday. As it stands right now, considering how serious it sounded earlier in the week, the Patriots should be thrilled with how Henderson is moving and feeling less than 48 hours until kickoff.

title: Patriots Receive Bad Practice News, But It Certainly Wasn't Surprising
full_text:
FOXBORO — For the second-straight week, the New England Patriots might be down two members of their secondary.
Ahead of their Week 6 matchup with the New York Jets, cornerbacks Carlton Davis and Karon Prunty were both absent from the Patriots' third practice of the week on Friday. Davis, who's dealing with a neck injury that held him out of the team's Week 2 win earlier in the season, also missed last week's game.
Prunty is working through a hamstring injury. He's played in three games so far, primarily as a special teamer.
This news shouldn't come as a surprise, as they missed each of the last three practices last wee k as well. The Patriots have been banged up in the secondary, and succeeded a week ago against the Las Vegas Raiders — rolling out Marcus Jones, Charles Woods and Kindle Vildor at cornerback.
Now they'll get back Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) and Channing Canada (hamstring), who both missed Week 5 with injuries.
The Patriots secondary had a solid outing against the Raiders, and could now have a good showing against a Jets team that will be down Adonai Mitchell. Vildor, who was signed to the 53-man roster last weekend , stepped up in a larger role. With Davis potentially not on the field, he may need to do the same thing again.
"He gets a PBU, gets a big punch out there, changes the momentum, helps us get the drive stopped," Mike Vrabel said this week on Vildor. "I think one of the coaches was talking and said, 'Well, he had a mental error on the play, but he also had an extra effort.'
"And so, I think that's really defines what we want our identity to be, is that the ability to have an error or a mistake, but also the ability to go finish, still impact the play and know that a mental error doesn't have to necessarily mean that the play is over or a mistake. It certainly doesn't limit our ability to finish."
Safeties Mike Brown and Jaylen Reed will be the top replacements for Prunty on special teams, as they've done in recent weeks. Defensive tackle Cory Durden, who missed Thursday's session with an illness, returned one day later.
Last week, the Patriots were down Gonzalez and also lost running back TreVeyon Henderson and offensive tackle Will Campbell mid-game. They've all been present at practices this week in limited capacities, and Gonzalez was upgraded to a full participant on Thursday.
After Henderson and Campbell both went down against Las Vegas , their statuses for this week were in jeopardy. Now, they could end up suiting up.
"Guys are playing through stuff and that’s kind of the mentality," Drake Maye said this week on Campbell. "(Need) to be smart, but at the same time you wanna be out there with your guys. That’s an example of what Will is, and you go to battle with those guys."
The Patriots also designated wide receiver A.J. Brown to return from IR this week . He might not be activated for this game, but his return to practice is a good sign for this offense.
Vrabel will speak to the media after practice ends around 1 p.m. and will likely give updates on who'll be on the final injury report of the week.

title: How Patriots Are Preparing For A.J. Brown's Eventual Return
full_text:
FOXBORO — A.J. Brown has returned to practice this week, but the New England Patriots aren't 100% certain if the wide receiver will return to game action on Sunday. The team designated him to return off of injured reserve this week after missing the league-mandated four games with a high-ankle sprain.
Since then, B rown has been a constant on the practice field , leading the way in the receiver drills when reporters are present. However, there's still a lot to figure out about whether or not Brown will actually play.
Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels spoke to reporters Thursday afternoon, sharing that the team is preparing several game plans (like they do each week), with one of them including Brown — and another without Brown.
"Those kind of things are slashed with two different groups anyway in case we lose somebody," McDaniels said. "Guys are already studying both ends of the spectrum. ... They'll all be ready to go."
The Patriots got good production out of the wide receiver position these last few weeks, and adding Brown into that bunch will only help the team's output. But they don't want to rush anything. Brown's ankle — one that got hurt just three quarters into the season — could be the last piece of the Patriots' offensive output.
Right now, it's a wait-and-see type of situation.
"It's always good to bring some fresh juice to the guys and to the unit," McDaniels said. "We know what he can do when he's out there and he's healthy. We'll see how the rest of this week goes, and ultimately what ends up happening, (I'm) sure Mike (Vrabel) will make a great decision about exactly how we need to do that if that goes forward that way."
When you factor in the Patriots' trip to Chicago on Thursday Night Football one week later, that could end up throwing a wrench into some potential planning.
"The quick turnaround affects everybody obviously," McDaniels continued. "There'll be a lot of things that'll happen after this game that we'll have to figure out offshore in terms of bumps and bruises and all that stuff, so we'll play it as it goes."
The Patriots would love to get Brown back in the huddle. He caught three passes in the season opener against the Seahawks, and it looked like his connection with Drake Maye was forming. But that had to be cut short .
Brown , obviously, would love to play. His answers didn't stray away much from McDaniels'.
"It's still up in the air," Brown said. "Obviously, it's going to be coach Vrabel's decision to see where I'm at and make the better decision for the long haul and not just temporarily. But I'm just trying to stack each and every day right now. My focus is just on today and trying to get better, and see how I feel afterward."
For now, the Patriots aren't worried about Brown's availability for this week. Yes, it would be great to have him for Sunday, but they'll have 21 days to activate him to the 53-man roste r. For now, it's all about getting him up to speed with the reps he's missed.
"There's no way to make up for all of the time that has been missed," McDaniels said. "I think you do the best you can with I would say a very intelligent amount of work. I don't think you can bring somebody back and then overwork them to try to hurry up and catch up. I don't think that's really the right process."
"I'm one step at a time," Brown said. "Right now, I just want to practice."

title: History of the Patriots vs. Jets Matchup Ahead of Week 6 Battle
full_text:
Sunday will be the 135th meeting between the New York Jets and New England (or former Boston) Patriots. The Patriots lead the all-time series, dominating their division rival 77-56-1. The Patriots' 77 total wins over the Jets are the second most of any team over one opponent (second to themselves, with 81 wins over the Buffalo Bills).
Of course, a majority of these wins can be contributed to the Tom Brady-Bill Belichick era, where from 2001 (the year Brady became the starter) to 2024 (Belichick's final year coaching the Patriots) the Patriots went 38-10 over the Jets.
Speaking of the old dynasty, the Jets introduced the league to the legacy of TB12, when on September 23, 2001, New York linebacker Mo Lewis took out quarterback Drew Bledsoe as he ran to the sideline. Brady entered a game that the Patriots would end up losing 10-3, then go on to lead the Pats to their first Super Bowl win.
Brady and the Pats met the Jets in the playoff twice. Once in 2006, a wild-card round win for New England, then again four years later, where the Patriots were stunned by quarterback Mark Sanchez in the divisional Round. The two teams also met in 1985, during the Patriots run to their first Super Bowl appearance.
Prior to the dynasty, an infamous game defined this rivalry: The 1997 Week 3 match, which saw the return of Hall of Fame head coach Bill Parcells to New England. Just 9 months after leading the Patriots to an AFC Championship, Parcells was now on the opposite side of the field. In this 27-24 overtime victory for the Patriots, Curtis Martin ran the ball 40 times and notched 199 yards.  The following season, Martin would join Parcells' Jets.
Another meeting between these two teams made league history, but not for its score or anything that happened on the field. On September 9, 2007, the Patriots eased their way past the Jets 38-14 — however, the result of this match would create the term SpyGate . Belichick's Patriots, accused of stealing signals from the Jets sideline, made sports history with their record-setting fine punishments and removal of a first-round pick.
Both the Patriots and Jets are under new regimes with head coaches Mike Vrabel and Aaron Glenn beginning their tenures in the 2025 season. The Patriots swept the Jets in the season series a year ago, winning by a total margin of 69-24.
Each team has some linemen familiarity, as well. The Patriots currently roster or reserve four offensive linemen that formerly played for the New York Jets (Greg Van Roten, Morgan Moses, Alijah Vera-Tucker, and Xavier Newman-Johnson). Former Patriots offensive tackle Chukwuma Okorafor is currently a Jet.
Geno Smith, in his second stint with the team that originally drafted him, is very familiar with the Patriots. As a starting quarterback, Smith is 2-4 against the Pats, winning the last two in 2024 with the Seahawks and 2025 with the Raiders.
While each team has different goals for the season, both are relying on their young stars to push them into the conversation of great NFL teams.
The Jets are relying on their young talent, which is very recently acquired. After trading cornerback Sauce Gardner and defensive linemen Quinnen Williams, the Jets stacked six first-round picks in two straight drafts (2026-27). Former first-round picks WR Garrett Wilson and EDGE Will McDonald IV are already impact players.
In this past draft, they selected EDGE David Bailey fourth overall, whose already proven to be a hit, reaching top five in the NFL in sacks (five). They also selected WR Omar Cooper Jr. and TE Kenyon Sadiq with their remaining two first-round picks. Their second-round pick in CB D'Angelo Ponds has shown promise defensively.
The Patriots have seemingly hit on most of their first-round picks over the course of the past few drafts. CB Christian Gonzalez just became the highest paid cornerback in the league , and Drake Maye was runner-up for MVP last season. Offensive linemen Will Campbell and Caleb Lomu round out the remaining quarters of a four-season rebuild built through first-round talent.
The Patriots future also depends on home grown talent such as EDGE Gabe Jacas , S Craig Woodson, and RB TreVeyon Henderson.
Will the next best chapter of this rivalry start on Sunday? With each team currently placd second and third in the division, Sunday's battle could have major effects on how the AFC East shapes up.

title: Patriots Hall of Fame Center Jon Morris Dies at 84
full_text:
Jon Morris, one of the greatest offensive linemen in New England Patriots history, has died, the team announced Thursday. He was 84.
Morris was one of the stalwarts of the upstart Boston Patriots in the American Football League, anchoring the offensive line for 11 seasons. He was a fourth round draft pick (29th overall) by the club in 1964, and remained with the Patriots until 1974. He was named a team captain and was named an AFL All-Star six times from 1964 to 1969.
"Jon Morris was one of the great players who helped build the foundation of our franchise," Patriots Chairman and CEO Robert Kraft said in a statement released by the team. "For generations of Patriots fans, he represented the toughness, dedication and pride of those early teams.
"It meant so much to me to call Jon in 2011 and tell him he had been selected to our Hall of Fame, ensuring that his contributions would always be remembered. On behalf of our family and the entire Patriots organization, we extend our deepest condolences to Jon's family, friends and former teammates."
He was the first Patriots player to ever ben selected to the Pro Bowl following the 1970 merger with the NFL, and added that accolade onto his previous five All-AFL Team honors (one First Team, four Second Team). Morris was also named to the franchise's All-1960s Team, as well as their 35th and 50th Anniversary Teams.
Morris chose the Patriots over the NFL's Green Bay Packers, who had selected in the fourth round of the 1964 draft.
"I was 22, and Boston was a lively town, and I felt comfortable there," Morris said, via Holy Cross Magazine in 2010 . "Green Bay seemed dead outside football."
Morris played in 130 games with the franchise and helped lead the way for fullback Jim Nance in the running game. He'd close his pro career with stops on the Detroit Lions (1975-77) and the Chicago Bears (1978).
A Holy Cross alum, Morris would also become a radio broadcaster for the Patriots from 1979 to 1987. He became the third offensive lineman inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame (behind John Hannah and Bruce Armstrong) in 2011 — and the first to be inducted by the newly-formed senior committee.
Morris called the induction "the crowning achivement of my football life."
"I'm thrilled beyond words," Morris said at the time of his name being nominated for the Patriots Hall of Fame three years prior in 2008 . "It's really nice for an old-timer like me. I played with Nance, so I know how good he was. ... But this is almost like a once-in-a-lifetime situation for me, because there are so many great players in the organization."
Morris' name also appeared on the i nitial ballot for induction into Pro Football Hall of Fame Class of 2026 , but he did not move further into the voting process.

title: Patriots' Christian Gonzalez Full Participant in Practice for the First Time in 2 Weeks
full_text:
On Wednesday, cornerback Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) returned to New England Patriots practice after missing two straight weeks of practice. One day later, he was upgraded to a full participant in their fully-padded session.
The fourth-year star was sidelined after sustaining a shoulder injury in the Patriots' Week 3 game against Jacksonville. Following six-straight "did not participate" practice designations, Gonzalez was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday. A day later, he's back in full pads and participating in every drill.
Gonzalez told the media on Wednesday that he was feeling, "good, ready to go for Sunday." He also said, "I've been itching, kind of going a little crazy when I'm not getting to play."
The 24-year-old had his rookie season cut short with a labrum injury in 2023. His injury history extends to following two seasons where in 2024, he suffered a concussion and in 2025, he started the season with a hamstring injury.
Christian Gonzalez back at practice today 👏 #Patriots #NEPats pic.twitter.com/2epMq6XKjw
The 2024 second-team All-Pro cornerback made history in the offseason by signing a four-year, $135 million extension with $130 million guaranteed. The contract, announced a day before the start of the 2026 season, made Gonzalez the highest paid at his position in the NFL.
On Thursday, Patriots defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr told media members, "It's always great to have (No.) 0 out there. ... He's been flying around, good energy, good communication with the guys. Doesn't look like he missed a step, and we're excited to have him out there for sure."
Patriots defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr on CB Christian Gonzalez: Flying around out there, doesn’t look like he missed a step. pic.twitter.com/W4W54BuWpW
With the 2023 first-round pick returning to the lineup, the Patriots become larger favorites over the New York Jets (2-3).
With cornerback Carlton Davis (neck) still sidelined in practice , Gonzalez's lockdown coverage will be needed to contain the likes of Garrett Wilson, who's been the Jets' leading receiver through five games.
Additionally, New York could have rookie first-round wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. back from an ankle injury, and Adonai Mitchell back from a finger injury.
Last week, along with Gonzalez and Davis, the Patriots were without defensive backs Karon Prunty and Channing Canada — both rehabbing hamstring injuries. As a result, the team trotted out just three active cornerbacks to face the Las Vegas Raiders' passing attack.
While Canada was listed as limited participant in Thursday's practice, having the 24-year-old star back on the field to face a divisional opponent, in what some are calling a trap game , makes all the difference for this banged up Patriots secondary.
After receiving an historic extension, Gonzalez will almost certainly suit up for the Patriots on Sunday for his fourth game of the season.

title: Patriots Week 6 Injury Report: A.J. Brown Returns, OTs Banged Up Bad
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots have gone through a lot of injuries these last five weeks. They've been forced to put more players on injured reserve at this point in the season (19) than they did all of last season. They've been banged up , but have still won two-straight games to improve to 3-2.
But they're getting some players back this week ahead of their matchup with the New York Jets.
"I mean, I think that we'll just focus on this week and see if guys are ready to go," Mike Vrabel said Wednesday about handling injuries ahead of this week and next week's Thursday Night Football game. "We obviously know we have a shortened week next week. It can’t impact our decisions to try to do everything we can to win this week. Then we’ll figure out where we are after that."
Here's the initial injury report for the Patriots, including some returners off of injured reserve.
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (illness)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (neck)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (hamstring)
Here's the Jets' initial injury report for Week 6, including a few major pieces of their offense sidelined.
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (quad)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (finger)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (knee)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (ankle)
The biggest story for the Patriots? The return of A.J. Brown, who missed Weeks 2 through 5 with a high-ankle sprain . He was designated to return off of IR this week, and will work to try and play this week against a Jets team he should thrive against.
But the Patriots aren't sure yet how he'll impact the offense ... or if he'll even be activated by Saturday. The Patriots will have three weeks to officially decide if they'll remove him off of IR and stick him on the 53-man roster.
"He hasn't been out there, so I can't tell you until we actually see it," Vrabel said. "He hasn't been out there for four weeks, so we'll get him back out there practicing and see if he's ready to go in a couple days. And if not, then we have a 21-day window, and we'll go from there."
Brown participated in practice , going through drills with his receivers coach, Todd Downing. There didn't seem to be any limitations in how he looked (at least when reporters were present).
A.J. Brown goes through a catch possession drill with WRs coach Todd Downing: pic.twitter.com/ipUvbBZmUx
The Patriots also started the 21-day window for second-year offensive tackle Marcus Bryant, who was placed on IR ahead of the regular season with an ankle injury.
Last week against the Raiders, the Patriots lost both TreVeyon Henderson and Will Campbell in a matter of minutes. Both players would leave the game and wouldn't return, and after tests on Monday, could end up missing some time .
When reporters were present during Wednesday's practice, neither of them were spotted on the field with their teammates. Campbell did speak prior to going out to practice, but he only participated in a limited capacity.
When Campbell was ruled out, the Patriots turned to first round rookie Caleb Lomu . He would play pretty good football from the left side — allowing just one pressure in 47 snaps.
"I think all the times that they have to be able to get some game action, whether that's at the jumbo tight end or getting some snaps in there at different times in practice and being able to work on both sides is critical," Vrabel said Monday on Lomu's first month. "I think that's something that the swing tackle has to be able to do. He has to be ready to go in the game. I know he's working hard, and he's going to try to take advantage of whatever opportunity comes his way."
As for how the Patriots can replace Henderson's skills at running back , they'll have to rely a lot on third-string Corey Kiner, and practice squad players Lan Larison and Hassan Haskins. The team had Haskins in the building during the preseason and the first two weeks of the season, but just signed him back this week just in case.
After starting the week as a limited participant, Christian Gonzalez was upgraded to a full participant for Thursday. He's been on the field working as a starter after missing the past two weeks of practice, and is now in line to make his return to the game field.
Earlier this week, Gonzalez told reporters that he was "ready to go" for his battle with the Jets. Now that he's a full go in practice, the Patriots coaching staff is looking forward to seeing their top cornerback return to action.
"He's the same guy," cornerbacks coach Justin Hamilton said. "He came back out and prepares, going to work, playing the game in his head like what he always has done."

title: Saints Injury Report: Olave Questionable as Giants Face Offensive Line Concerns
full_text:
As pressure mounts around the organization , the New Orleans Saints look to end their losing skid and get back on track on the road against the New York Giants on Sunday, but concerns linger over their latest injury report.
The Saints' top receiving target, Chris Olave , who missed the last two practices with an illness, was a limited participant Friday. If Olave can play Sunday, starting quarterback Tyler Shough can breathe a sigh of relief.
Olave has recorded 39 catches for 537 yards with a touchdown. Olave is second in the league in receiving yards and is tied for third in receptions.
On defense, linebacker Kaden Elliss and edge rusher Anfernee Jennings are out again for Sunday.
Elliss, who is arguably the Saints’ best player at his position, has been greatly missed as the Saints have allowed 179 yards per game on the ground since his injury during their 35-27 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 3.
After Saints owner Gayle Benson said the Saints’ 1-4 start was “unacceptable” earlier in the week, head coach Kellen Moore said after practice he speaks with her regularly and communicated with her throughout the week.
"We're all just trying to reach the same goal," Moore said. "We all want to win football games, and so we're all working toward that."
As for the Giants, edge rusher Abdul Carter and starting offensive tackles Jermaine Eluemunor and Andrew Thomas have been listed as questionable.
The availability of both Eluemunor and Thomas could have major implications for Sunday's matchup, particularly against a solid edge rusher rotation of New Orleans’ Carl Granderson , Chase Young and Cameron Jordan .
The Saints will take on the Giants on Sunday at MetLife Stadium is set for noon CDT.

title: Saints vs. Giants: Jameis Winston's Return Headlines 3 Key Storylines
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints enter Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the New York Giants looking to avoid their fourth consecutive loss, but a familiar face stands in their way and remains a fan favorite in New Orleans.
Former Saints quarterback Jameis Winston will lead the Giants against his former team as New Orleans attempts to rebound from a disappointing 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings .
The Saints (1-4) have struggled to find consistency on both sides of the football, particularly offensively, where turnovers and an ineffective passing attack have contributed to their disappointing start.
Meanwhile, the Giants (3-1-1) have emerged as one of the NFC's early surprises under first-year coach John Harbaugh, overcoming injuries and inconsistent quarterback play to remain atop the NFC East.
Beyond Winston's reunion with New Orleans, the Saints must contend with two dangerous receiving threats in Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely while finding a way to exploit New York's ball-security problems.
Here are three major storylines to watch heading into Sunday's matchup.
Winston, a fan favorite among Who Dat Nation, will be the starter against his former team. The former No. 1 overall pick spent four seasons with the Saints from 2020-23, initially serving as Drew Brees ' backup before becoming New Orleans' starting quarterback in 2021.
Now, Winston has the chance to face his former team while trying to keep the Giants atop the NFC East.
Winston became the starter after Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending injury. Through three starts this season, Winston has thrown for 805 yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions while completing 57.6% of his passes.
In his latest outing against Washington, Winston helped engineer the comeback by completing 33 of his 54 passes for 326 yards and three touchdowns, connecting twice with Isaiah Likely and once with Malik Nabers .
Perhaps most importantly, Winston avoided throwing an interception despite attempting 54 passes.
While Winston commands attention, the Saints' biggest defensive challenge may be containing his top targets, wide receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely.
Nabers (29 catches for 329 yards and two touchdowns) and Likely (33 catches for 284 yards and four touchdowns) are responsible for 58% of the yardage production and number of targets thrown to.
Nabers, a former LSU star, has bounced back from a season-ending knee injury. He caught six passes for 112 yards and a touchdown against Arizona in Week 4, then recorded 11 catches for 121 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets against Washington.
Focusing solely on Nabers, opens opportunities for Likely, a former Baltimore Raven who has become Winston's primary red-zone threat. Against Washington, Likely had 11 receptions for 94 yards and two touchdowns, becoming the first tight end in Giants history with at least nine catches and two touchdowns in a game.
At 6 feet 4 inches, Likely presents matchup problems with his size and athleticism. Given New Orleans' recent struggles against Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers , defending Likely will test the Saints' coverage scheme.
For the Saints, the challenge becomes determining how to distribute coverage responsibilities without leaving either player in favorable one-on-one situations.
Despite their contrasting records, both the Saints and Giants have struggled with ball security this season.
New York has committed seven turnovers through five games, including three interceptions and four lost fumbles. Meanwhile, New Orleans enters Sunday's matchup with a minus-six turnover differential.
However, the Giants have compensated for their mistakes by intercepting six passes, tied for third-most in the NFL, while the Saints have recorded just one interception.
That discrepancy could prove decisive, particularly with quarterback Tyler Shough coming off a disappointing performance against Minnesota.
Shough completed 16 of 25 passes for just 96 yards and two interceptions, finishing with a 38.1 passer rating. Through five games, he has thrown for 1,299 yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions.
Meanwhile, New York's turnover problems nearly proved costly against Washington.
Jameis Winston lost a first-half fumble before running back Cam Skattebo fumbled at Washington's 24-yard line in overtime, squandering a potential game-winning scoring opportunity.
It marked Skattebo's fourth fumble of the season and his first lost fumble.
Despite his ball-security concerns, Skattebo leads the Giants with 294 rushing yards on 81 carries.
His production presents another challenge for New Orleans, which ranks 30th in rushing defense, allowing 148.8 yards per game.
For the Saints, protecting the football, forcing Winston into difficult throws and capitalizing on New York's mistakes could determine whether they snap their three-game losing streak.
