title: 3 Key Matchups Will Decide Jets’ Week 6 Outcome vs. Patriots (Gang Green Needs a Braelon Allen Encore)
full_text:
The Jets head into Week 6 trying to build on last week’s victory over the Browns. This will be a challenge, however, as they’ll be heading to Gillette Stadium to take on the Patriots.
Even with the Tom Brady-Bill Belichick era behind them, the Patriots continue to dominate this rivalry, with New York going 2-10 against New England since 2020. Although leaving with a win will be difficult, especially with the Patriots turning things around in the last two games, it’s not impossible.
If Gang Green can win these three matchups, they’ll give themselves a chance to pull off a road upset and earn back-to-back victories for the first time since 2023.
Unlike last year, the Jets have been ineffective at running the ball, ranking 22nd in rushing yards per game (94) and tied for 25th in yards per attempt (3.6). Despite their inefficiencies, their victories have relied heavily on pounding the ball.
In their three losses, the Jets ran the ball on 31.3%, 37.5%, and 43.8% of their plays, averaging 61.3 rushing yards per game. In their two victories, however, they ran the ball on 48.5% and 62% of their plays, averaging 143 rushing yards per game.
This trend makes establishing the run a priority against the Patriots, even without Breece Hall, who’s missed the team’s last three practices before officially being ruled out by the Jets on Friday, reported by ESPN 's Rich Cimini.
Out for Sunday: Breece Hall, Adonai Mitchell, Joseph Ossai and Dylan Parham. Kenyon Sadiq will be full practice today and is finishing his concussion protocol, per Glenn. #Jets
Braelon Allen will likely take on the bulk of the workload again . Allen played a key role in the Jets' Week 5 win over the Browns, setting career highs in rushing attempts (24) and rushing yards (116) and adding a touchdown.
Running the ball won’t be easy against the Patriots' defense, as they rank sixth in rushing yards allowed per game (90.8) and are tied for 13th in yards per carry allowed (4). Still, the Jets can’t afford to abandon the ground game if they struggle to find success early.
Pounding the football will be crucial to taking pressure off Geno Smith and giving the Patriots another dimension to keep New England’s defense guessing. With Garrett Wilson being the team’s only reliable receiving option, maintaining a balanced attack will be crucial.
The more the New York feeds Allen, the more opportunities he will have to break through for explosive runs. That’s exactly what happened last week against the Brown, as the bruising back from Wisconsin displayed his big-play potential, recording five runs of 10 or more yards.
If the Jets remain patient and continue feeding him the ball, Allen could eventually break through for a big gain. Although the Jets' offensive line hasn’t been great at creating running lanes, ranking 14th in run blocking , per Pro Football Focus, one play can spark the ground game.
At 6'1" and 250 lbs, Allen has the size that makes him hard to bring down and the speed to break away from defenders. If New York’s offensive line opens running lanes for him at the second level, Allen could replicate similar success on the ground and keep New England’s defense on its heels.
Two weeks ago, this matchup looked more attainable for the Jets, with Drake Maye struggling mightily through the first three weeks. The third-year quarterback from North Carolina threw for 585 yards, one touchdown, and six interceptions in New England’s first three games.
But in the last two games, Maye has started to look like the MVP runner-up he was last season, throwing for 643 yards, seven passing touchdowns, and just one interception. He’s also remained elite against the blitz, completing 71.7% of his passes, throwing four touchdowns and an interception.
To limit Maye success through the air, New York must make some adjustments to its scheme.
With head coach Aaron Glenn taking over as defensive play caller, the Jets have taken an aggressive approach, ranking fourth in blitz rate at 39%. They’ll have to switch things up against Maye and rely on their front four to generate pressure rather than consistently sending extra rushers.
Maye has been far less effective when defenses don’t blitz, completing 62.9% of his passes for one touchdown and six interceptions. When defenses sit back, he can hold the ball too long while searching for big plays, leading to costly mistakes and 14 sacks.
This puts added pressure on the Jets’ secondary to stay disciplined in coverage and limit downfield opportunities, where Maye is most dangerous. With A.J. Brown potentially making his return, Gang Green could face an even greater challenge downfield.
New York can match Brown’s physicality with Azareye’h Thomas, who’s impressed in coverage this year, earning a 74.4 coverage grade, per PFF , ranking 11th among 104 qualifying cornerbacks .
Ultimately, the Jets’ ability to contain Maye will depend on how their secondary plays in coverage. If New York can prevent the Patriots’ receivers from creating separation, it could force Maye to hold onto the ball long enough for the pass rush to get to him.
Staying with Brown and the Patriots’ other deep threats could also create interceptions, which they’ll need to stay in the game.
For the most part, Smith has been a good game-managing quarterback. The 14-year veteran impressed with his efficiency in the first three games, completing 75.5% of his passes for 783 yards, four touchdowns, and zero interceptions.
While Smith kept the ball out of harm’s way in the last two games, he hasn’t been as effective, completing 55.5% of his passes for 301 yards and two touchdowns. Although injuries to several key playmakers have played a role, Smith has been less aggressive in pushing the ball downfield, attempting just 12 passes of 20 yards or more this season.
However, Smith’s struggles aren’t entirely on him. Aside from Wilson, the rest of the Jets’ receiving corps has struggled to get open , forcing Smith to wait for throwing windows to develop. He’s tied 14th in time to throw at 2.93 seconds and has been sacked 16 times through five games, the third-most in the league.
This is where New England’s pass rush could make life miserable for Smith. The Patriots rank ninth in blitz percentage (36.1%) and are tied for 15th in quarterback pressure rate (36.7%), according to NFL Next Gen Stats.
Although their pass rush hasn’t been as effective, with New England tying for 12th in sacks with 11, defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr could test Smith early by dialing up some blitzes.
If the Jets want to improve their chances of winning, Smith must make quick decisions with the ball and avoid holding the ball too long. Screen and quick passes to Isaiah Williams and,if he plays,  Kenyon Sadiq could help counter the Patriots’ blitzes and give the offense opportunities to move the chains.
Smith must also continue to target Wilson early and often. Reich must build on last week’s game plan against the Browns and get Wilson more involved in the slot. The five-year veteran made plays with the ball in his hands last week, recording a season-high 55 yards after the catch.
Even if cornerback Christian Gonzalez plays and lines up against him, Smith shouldn’t shy away from targeting his best playmaker. Getting Wilson the ball in space rather than relying on him to make contested catches downfield could help New York move the ball downfield.

title: Jets' Ideal Approach for Omar Cooper Jr. Injury Return Becoming Clear in Week 6
full_text:
Football can be a numbers game sometimes. For fans, the best way to judge if a unit is playing well is cross-checking stats across the league.
If we judge the New York Jets based on stats alone offensively, then only one conclusion can be brought:
They haven't nearly been good enough.
New York ranks as the 23rd-best passing attack, 26th overall, and 27th in points. Part of the reason for that is the unit has been decimated with injuries to key players. Running back Breece Hall, left guard Dylan Parham, wide receiver AD Mitchell, and tight end Mason Taylor have all missed significant time to begin the year.
But the cavalry is close to arriving. In the case of New York's passing unit, the return of one of their top rookies could greatly impact how the group looks moving forward.
New York activated first-round rookie Omar Cooper Jr. off of the short-term IR list this week. Over the last two practices, the Indiana prospect has been "limited" on the field. New York has been clear for Cooper:
They won't force him onto the field unless he is ready, and he needs to pass through a series of rep tests in practice to do so.
"He's a really good player, but you never want any rookie to actually miss time because the reps are valuable for these guys," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said. "And I think all of our rookies that's been getting these reps have been valuable."
Cooper made a major impact in his lone appearance this season. Against the Tennessee Titans in Week 1, he caught a short pass and raced 30 yards downfield to set the team up for their first touchdown of the game. Unfortunately for him, he suffered an ankle injury that has cost him the last four weeks.
Now that he is healthy, though, the Jets should not be patient with him. They should not hesitate to give him a full load of plays going into Week 6 and beyond. There's no guarantee he plays against the New England Patriots on Sunday, of course, but if he does, he should get the full work of a WR2.
Why? Because he is easily New York's second-best receiving option when on the field. While the Jets have preached their desire to be patient with rookies, some like David Bailey, have proven to be ready for a large set of plays right away.
Based on Cooper's excellence at Indiana, and his strong training camp, the Jets should treat their first-round receiver the same way. Otherwise, the team will have to trust Tim Patrick or Isaiah Williams to take pressure off of Garrett Wilson.
That just isn't good enough.
And it's why there should be no hesitation to get their rocket rookie the ball as early and as often as possible when he gets back on the game field.

title: How Week 6 Could Alter Jets' Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
The New York Jets are in rare territory going into Sunday's contest. With the trade deadline less than a month away, Gang Green must decide whether to be buyers, sellers, or stand pat with the current roster they have.
At 2-3, it's hard to determine exactly which way the Jets will go. After all, while they have been competitive in some games, they have yet to show they can beat top competition in order to place themselves in playoff contention.
That all can change on Sunday.
A showdown against their archrival New England Patriots could very well determine which side of the coin the Jets will fall on: buyers or sellers.
New York knows how important Sunday's game is. It's not just a chance to get to .500 against the defending conference champions. It's the first chance the team has to show how far they have come as a roster and a coaching staff.
A win in Foxborough would be the signature win for head coach Aaron Glenn. It would quiet a lot of the animosity fans have for him. A victory would also be a sign for owner Woody Johnson to know that he ended up picking the right head coach.
"There's a premium on this one because it is our first one [in the division]," Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson said on Wednesday. "I don't know how to exactly put it, but it's a big-ass game."
If the team is blown out in any way, shape or form, then there will certainly be something of a letdown. It would show general manager Darren Mougey that the team is not ready for true title contention and they would need more time to actually develop as a roster. It would also show the coaching staff is unable to make up for a talent deficiency against tough competition.
In the sense of the trade deadline, though, a loss would put the team close to the sellers' market. Players who may not be seen as a value to the organization may be moved: performers like Dane Belton, Kingsley Enagbare, or Harrison Phillips could be moved for draft capital.
It may seem like a long shot now, but at this time last year no one thought Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams were both going to be moved. And then they were after a dismal 1-7 start to the year.
If the Jets want to avoid a similar deadline to the one they had last year, they will need to win more games. And the easiest way to get on that board is to beat their arch rival in New England.
Should that happen, New York won't just come away with a massive win, they could reset their entire culture going forward.

title: It's Crucial for Isaiah Davis to Be a Key Part of Jets' Week 6 Plans to Beat the Patriots
full_text:
Fresh off a hard-fought 17-12 win over the Browns last Sunday, the Jets turn their attention to a Week 6 clash with the Patriots after snapping a three-game losing streak and injecting a little optimism into an upcoming schedule that presents some opportunities.
While a pitiful trend of going 25-65 against AFC East opponents since 2011 and just 4-26 against the Patriots during that same stretch is not exactly encouraging, the Jets did some positive things in the Week 5 win over Cleveland and have a division opportunity in front of them to build off that and make some proper tweaks.
With Breece Hall sidelined due to a right quad injury, Braelon Allen brought his best with a career-high 116 yards on 24 carries and the game-winning 22-yard touchdown. Although his stock is certainly skyrocketing after a long-awaited breakout performance , there is no reason that fellow RB and 2024 draftee Isaiah Davis should not be more involved in the offense on Sunday.
Davis hasn't been used all that often this season, but that needs to change for the Jets' offense to be a problem for the Patriots' defense.
While Hall's return is of the utmost importance in terms of getting their versatile RB1 back on the field, ESPN Jets reporter Rich Cimini noted on Thursday that he "is working with trainers on the side field" and is "considered week-to-week."
Breece Hall (quad) is working with trainers on the side field. That’s progress. He’s considered week to week. #Jets
As Hall continues to make progress, that could obviously impact the amount of playing time that Davis receives.
The Patriots are coming off back-to-back wins, including a signature win over fellow AFC East rival Buffalo in Week 4. That said, their defense hasn't been perfect; tied for the 11th-most catches allowed (24) and tied for the fifth-most receiving yards allowed (200) to RBs this season. That is definitely an area to exploit for a Jets team that is still trying to get healthy.
If Hall can't play, it makes sense to use Davis as a receiving option out of the backfield since he averages an impressive 8.7 yards per catch in his career. He only had two carries for eight yards and one catch for nine yards last week, but the fact that he played a season-high 10 offensive snaps adds to the idea that the Jets are ready to put more on his plate.
As good as Allen has been, he is only averaging 2.7 yards per catch this season with a career-worst 63.6% catch rate. He averages 6.6 in that department for his career, and his lackluster pass-catching production could open the door for Davis to get an uptick in snaps as early as this weekend.
Davis has been productive in his young NFL career and has scored three total TDs without fumbling the ball until this past Sunday, although quarterback Geno Smith recovered it, and it did not result in a turnover. It made sense for New York to get Davis more involved in the game plan while Hall has been out of action and for him to take on a more important role .
Head coach Aaron Glenn shared a conflicting injury update that only raised more questions than answers , specifically regarding the availability of wide receiver Adonai Mitchell. For weeks, this wideout group has been without two of its top-three targets—Mitchell and rookie Omar Cooper Jr.—though Cooper is nearing his crucial return from an ankle injury that he suffered in the opener.
Those depth concerns, along with rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq entering concussion protocol after suffering a head injury in the Week 5 win over Cleveland, have left holes in the passing game behind WR1 Garrett Wilson. Is Davis ready to step up when Gang Green needs him most?
At the same time, Davis has primarily been used on special teams and could find himself on the trade block before the month is over , especially if the Jets continue to shy away from him when the opportunity is right in front of the 2024 fifth-rounder. That's why it's crucial for him to capitalize on every chance he gets, whether it leads to a bigger role with the Jets or elsewhere.
At the end of the day, the Patriots have clearly struggled to contain pass-catching backs so far this season. If the Jets want to put themselves in position to pull off the upset and earn a rare divisional win, Davis should be a key part of those plans, especially if Hall is out for another week.

title: Job's Not Over: David Bailey Still Has Plenty to Prove to Jets Despite Winning AFC Defensive Player of the Week
full_text:
It's good to be David Bailey right now.
The Jets' second-overall pick in the 2026 draft has been highly productive through his first five games, becoming just the third rookie since 2000 to accomplish that feat. He was aided by a three-sack effort in Gang Green's 17-12 win over the Browns last week, as well as a season-high nine pressures , according to Pro Football Focus .
Bailey was the best player on the field in that game, resulting in him being awarded major NFL honors : AFC Defensive Player of the Week.
AFC Players of the Week! (Week 5) @Nunless2 | @gregrousseau pic.twitter.com/wsavBPaARN
Not Defensive Rookie of the Week. Player. Bailey was that good on Sunday.
But as the Texas Tech product moves forward beyond his breakout game, the Jets know that one game does not make or break a prospect, meaning Bailey still has plenty more to prove.
Transcendent draft picks often get misassociated with great ones. Myles Garrett was a transcendent talent. Aidan Hutchinson was a great one. Bailey's moniker falls somewhere in the middle between what Garrett was and what Hutchinson became when they were both drafted.
But through sheer production, his motor, and willingness to improve, the Jets have known for a while now how special Bailey can be for their team.
"(Bailey is) everything you'd want in an edge," Jets cornerback AZ Thomas said on Monday. "We can go into stats and stuff like that, but I mean, like he's a rookie, and it's going to be a learning curve just like I had last year. … David Bailey is David Bailey, and he put that on display last night (h/t NFL). I just look forward to seeing more of that."
David Bailey was a man on a mission in Week 5 🔥 @Pepsi pic.twitter.com/DKOYWjlsLg
That's the ticket going forward. More. New York wants to see more from Bailey.
Fellow teammate Will McDonald IV is a good example of a player who can get to the quarterback in bunches. He has the talent of a first-round pick. Yet he is too inconsistent as a pass rusher to be trusted the way the Jets want to trust Bailey.
Already they are seeing that trust pays off.
Bailey's motor and pass-rushing skills are apparent. But another factor that has made him an everydown player is the one skill that was considered a detriment to him coming out of the draft: defending the run.
"The other things that really showed up in the game was (David's) ability to play the run," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said of Bailey's performance. "He just had an all-around game as far as affecting the quarterback and playing the run."
Before the draft, the big weakness to Bailey's game was his inconsistencies against the run. Teams were worried that he wouldn't be able to become the three down player that someone like Arvell Reese could be.
Through five games, though, Bailey's run defense has been the best part of his game. Pro Football Focus grades him as the 16th-best run defender of all edge rushers. His grade (76.1) is also two points higher than Reese's (74.0) so far in that category.
Winning defensive player of the week is certainly an achievement to celebrate, especially for a rookie making just his fifth start. His latest effort has made him DraftKings Sportsbook's current +200 favorite to be named the 2026 Defensive Rookie of the Year , but the mark of a special player is performing at a high level each and every week.
Garrett, Hutchinson, and T.J. Watt are all great examples of that. If Bailey wants his name to be thrown into the groups of the elite, he'll need to show that last week's performance against the Browns was not a mirage.
It was a sign of things to come.

title: Adonai Mitchell Injury Is Easily Jets’ Biggest Concern Heading Into Week 6 vs. Patriots
full_text:
Thanks to Braelon Allen’s career-high 116 rushing yards and a dominant pass-rush effort, the Jets ended their losing streak with a much-needed win over the Browns in Week 5. Star wide receiver Garrett Wilson once again provided the main spark through the air, recording 104 of the Jets’ 182 passing yards.
Despite finally returning to the win column, Gang Green’s passing attack continued to struggle in the sloppy conditions. Some of these struggles can be attributed to the absence of receiver Adonai Mitchell, who has missed the last three games with a finger injury .
The severity of the former 2024 second-round pick’s injury had been unknown, adding more frustrating to his absence.
When asked last week about Mitchell’s injury, head coach Aaron Glenn said he didn’t know whether his finger was sprained or fractured , but that he didn’t have surgery on it. Turns out things can change quickly, because on Wednesday, Glenn told reporters that Mitchell underwent a "small procedure" last week.
“ (Adonai) did have a small procedure on his hand ,” Glenn said. “But the good thing is, man, that he’s moving his hand really, really well.”
With the former Texas Longhorn not at practice Wednesday and Glenn keeping his status as week-to-week, Mitchell appears unlikely to suit up against AFC East rival the Patriots.
Naturally, that makes his looming absence a major concern in Week 6.
Mitchell quickly established himself as New York’s WR2 during the summer workouts, and the former Texas Longhorn has given the Jets another vertical threat alongside Wilson.
He’s been Smith’s favorite target downfield, receiving four targets on passes of 20-plus yards , according to NFL Next Gen Stats . He hauled in one catch for 40 yards against the Titans in Week 1.
Standing at 6'2" and 205 lbs with a blazing 4.34-second 40-yard dash time , this shouldn’t come as much of a surprise. His physical frame and athleticism, combined with his ability to win 50/50 balls, make him an enticing target.
After the first two games, Mitchell ranked second on the team in receptions (9), targets (15), and receiving yards (123).
Since his injury, the rest of the receiving corps hasn’t provided consistent production. While tight end Kenyon Sadiq exploded for seven catches and 105 yards against the Lions in Week 3, he posted two catches for three yards over the next two games. He's also currently battling through the NFL's concussion protocol , leaving his outlook uncertain.
Granted, the Jets were also without Breece Hall, Tim Patrick and Mason Taylor at various points during this stretch, further complicating their passing attack.
Still, New York has tried to fill Mitchell’s void on the outside by giving Isaiah Williams a larger role in Weeks 3 and 4 before turning to Patrick in Week 5. While both receivers have their own strengths, neither has been as intimidating downfield as Mitchell.
Williams showcased his big-play ability against the Bears, hauling in a 58-yard touchdown in the team’s 23-12 loss. However, much of his production has come at or near the line of scrimmage. Patrick, like Mitchell, is a big receiver, standing at 6'5" and 210 lbs, though he is more of a run-blocking, red-zone threat receiver.
Mitchell’s value isn’t limited to deep plays downfield. He’s also proven he can add value in the intermediate areas and win matchups with his route-running, logging three catches (four targets) for 47 yards at these levels.
With Mitchell out, the Jets are missing a receiver who can take pressure off Wilson and give their passing game another dimension. Through five games, the five-year veteran from Ohio State leads the team in receptions (31), receiving yards (373), and touchdowns (3).
Williams and Patrick can’t replicate Mitchell's production , as each brings a different skill set to the table. Until New York can consistently find ways to create plays at multiple levels, opposing defenses can afford to focus all their attention on Wilson.
That makes it abundantly clear why Mitchell’s continued absence a significant concern heading into Week 6 and beyond.

title: Future of Jets' Offense Hangs on Garrett Wilson-Geno Smith Duo's Next Steps
full_text:
In case it wasn't already clear, the central game plan for the Jets' offense each week should be five simple words.
"Get. Garrett. Wilson. The. Ball."
Five words. Every single week. That's the game plan.
Jokes aside, it is no coincidence the Jets defeated the Cleveland Browns thanks in large part to their top receiver. Wilson recorded seven catches for another 100-yard game and a touchdown catch (h/t NFL).
What a play by Garrett Wilson for the touchdown! @CLEvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6mepGsdHbd
New York may have only put up 17 points, but the game plan and operation made perfect sense for the group, according to head coach Aaron Glenn.
“When you’ve got players like Garrett, you try to do everything you can to try to make sure you feed him the ball,” Glenn said.
Of course, while Wilson remains a star in the league, the quarterback getting him the ball hasn't been too bad himself. It's that partnership that appears to be getting better and putting the Jets in rare territory as an offense.
On paper, the stats don't look too dominant. The Jets are 23rd in the league in passing, with some questions about protection and a lack of big plays.
But the partnership between Wilson and quarterback Geno Smith remains the most important for the Jets as the 2026 season rolls on. Gang Green needs their top quarterback and receiver on the same page at all times, even if Wilson isn't always going to get the ball, and Smith knows it.
Smith has played well in his return to New York. He has yet to throw an interception and is completing just under 70% of his passes. His 73.1 passing grade on Pro Football Focus is also the 15th-best among 51 qualified QBs.
Meanwhile, Wilson ranks seventh in receptions and 11th in the league in receiving yards. This has all come as the Jets have struggled with injuries at the receiver position behind him (Omar Cooper Jr., Adonai Mitchell, Arian Smith, etc.).
"(Garrett's) got great range in terms of you can put the ball anywhere, he goes and gets it, and it's hard for guys to cover him out there," Smith said. "We have to find ways to get him the ball as many times as we can."
The pile of injuries hasn't mattered. Wilson has still played well, and that's a credit Smith respects more than anything.
Still, it wasn't always pretty, of course.
In Week 4's loss to the Bears, Wilson was targeted just four times on 32 plays run by the Jets' offense. The fact that the Jets made a focused effort to change that early in Sunday's win over the Browns, though, shows the team understands the importance of getting the ball to their best offensive player.
As Gang Green prepares for their Week 6 showdown with the Patriots , that game plan will be put to the test. Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel is notorious for trying to take the opposing team's best player out of the game entirely.
It's something the receiver is geared for in the organization's first AFC East game of the season.
"If the looks look how they did during the week, all of a sudden you have an idea," Wilson said. "They can always do unscouted looks, throw wrenches at you, things like that. You’ve got to be ready for it all as a player.”
The Patriots may try to take him away, but the Jets should be well prepared for that by now. There won't be an excuse if New York struggles to get its No. 1 playmaker on Sunday.
Wilson is good enough to dominate any opponent. It seems his quarterback and team are ready to allow that to happen now.

title: Jonathan Greenard Has Opportunity to Prove Himself With Eagles Thin at Edge vs. Panthers
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — Eagles edge rusher Jonathan Greenard expressed clear frustration Friday over the injuries that have limited him early in his first season with the Eagles, while emphasizing his confidence and eagerness to show what he can do once he returns to the field.⁠
Greenard first dealt with a pectoral issue that sidelined him for the first two games of the season and then an ankle injury sustained against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4 that cost him last week’s loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London as a late scratch.
Greenard has played in just two of the Eagles’ five games so far, although he has been very effective in his limited snaps.
The Eagles (2-3) host the Carolina Panthers on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field, and Greenard does not have a formal game status designation, meaning he will play.
Speaking at his locker after practice Friday, but before his game status was revealed, Greenard intimated that it might come down to a pregame evaluation. But it turns out it will not come down to the wire this week and Greenard is anxious to show what he can do.
“I still feel like I’m one of the best at my position. I like myself against anybody,” Greenard said. “It’s a matter of me getting out there and actually showing it, putting it on tape, ’cause I know it’s there.”
Greenard acknowledged that neither Eagles fans nor many of his new teammates have seen him at full strength yet, noting that they primarily know him from his time with the Minnesota Vikings. ⁠
The inability to play has weighed on him. “When you’re still not able to be out there, just still that, that gets you, man. I mean, that’s just the most frustrating part out of everything is that I still can’t play ball,” Greenard said. “... I can’t be out on that field, that s--- hurts my soul and it eats me up. But I know that day is soon to come. I see the light at the end of the tunnel. We gonna turn this s#$% around.”
The veteran pass rusher described the ankle as the current focus while noting the pectoral has improved and is stronger.
"Like many in the league," Greenard said, “you get back healthy, something else gonna bother you.”
The Georgia native has leaned on the training staff, his faith and family—including his two-year-old and an eight-month-old at home—to try to stay patient.
Greenard stressed that availability is the best ability and that he will only play if he can be effective, not just present, for the team’s sake. The decision involves collaboration with the staff, though he ultimately has the final say.
Greenard also addressed the Eagles’ three-game losing streak and lengthy injury list, which he jokingly called “longer than a novel.” He said the team is using the adversity as fuel and looks forward to defending its home field against the Panthers.
“We’re not a losing team. We may be doing some losing things at times, but we’re not a losing team,” he said. “I’m excited to see what we do on Sunday.”
Greenard’s presence will be important for the Eagles’ edge rotation, which could be down two players on Sunday. Jalyx Hunt was ruled out on Friday with ankle and knee injuries suffered against the Jaguars, while A.J. Epenesa was listed as doubtful with a back injury.

title: Tanner McKee, Cole Payton Unfazed By Eagles QB Depth Chart Shuffling as Joe Milton Joins the Room
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – They started the season just five weeks ago, without much hope of getting on the field. But it’s been that kind of season for the Eagles, with injuries mounting at an incredible rate, so Tanner McKee will start at quarterback on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers and Cole Payton, a rookie fifth-round pick not quite six months ago, will be his backup, meaning he is one more injury away from making his pro debut.
Joe Milton was added to the 53-man roster after being signed off the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad. He will likely serve as the emergency quarterback on Sunday. The Eagles made room for the QB when they placed Will Shipley on injured reserve Friday evening.
“Very prepared,” Payton said when asked at his locker on Friday if he would be ready to go if something happens to McKee. “Whether the two or the four, I've been preparing every single week like I'm the starter. That's our expectation. That's been our expectation. I feel very confident for when my number's called.”
McKee didn’t look great during training camp as he adjusted to the new scheme being installed by first-year offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, but the sixth-round pick out of Stanford three years ago said his knowledge and grasp of the scheme has increased since August.
“I feel like it's been growing and it's at its highest point right now,” said McKee, who will make his third career start. “Every opportunity that you get to play is a huge opportunity, especially being a sixth-round pick. Every opportunity's a huge opportunity, so I'm obviously very excited and ready to make the most of it.”
The irony is that, because of all the injuries to the starters and a rebuilt offensive line, McKee will be playing with several reserve players that he lined up with on the second and third team during the summer, so familiarity is there.
“Tanner, he's a great guy, smart guy,” said running back Dameon Pierce, who will start on Sunday with the Eagles’ top three running backs out. “I had a chance to be around him pre-season. He's very clear in the huddle, a very vocal guy. When he sees something, he's not shying away from it. There's no secret on the field, and everybody’s gonna be on the same page.”
The Eagles ruled out five players for Sunday, listed one as doubtful, and five others as questionable. Given all that, would it be a surprise if Payton made his pro debut sooner rather than later? Actually, he got his feet wet last week in London when he played 10 special teams reps.
“Last week was a blast,” he said. “I'm willing to do whatever it takes. I'll do whatever. I love the game.”
“I think he's worked his butt off,” said head coach Nick Sirianni about Payton before Friday’s practice. “He gets plays in those developmental periods. He gets reps on the scout team as well. He works extremely hard with the coaches after practice. He gets even more reps there after practice with [Quarterbacks Coach] Parks [Frazier] and with Gummy [Offensive Assistant/Assistant Quarterbacks Coach Montgomery VanGorder], just continuing to go [through] different things that we have as tools.”
There has been some thought that perhaps Payton’s development was stunted after a summer in which he took very few reps, except during developmental periods, because the Eagles were busy running a competition to be Jalen Hurts’ backup.
Andy Dalton won the battle against McKee, but the Eagles released Dalton on Oct. 9 after he threw one pass – a goal-line interception against the Bears in Week, 3 so McKee was elevated to No. 2.

title: Jalen Hurts Headlines 5 Key Players the Eagles Will Be Without vs. the Panthers in Week 6
full_text:
As has become an unfortunate trend for the team early in the 2026 NFL season, the Eagles will likely be missing a plethora of key contributors for their critical Week 6 matchup with the Panthers .
The Eagles enter the matchup with the Panthers on a three-game losing streak, desperate not to allow that streak to extend to four. If they are going to get their first win since the second weekend of the season, the Eagles will have to overcome some major absences.
After three practices this week, we have a pretty good idea of who will be taking the field for Philadelphia on Sunday, and who won't be. That's especially true after the Eagles announced on Friday that several key players will be inactive against the Panthers in Week 6.
Here's a look at five key Eagles who won't be on the field this weekend.
Let's get the most impactful absence out of the way at the start. Eagles star quarterback Jalen Hurts was already ruled out against Carolina on Thursday due to a superficial blood clot in his calf. It's a scary situation for Hurts, and it remains to be seen how long he'll be sidelined as a result, but there's a good chance that his absence stretches beyond a single game.
In the meantime, Tanner McKee will step into the starting spot for Philadelphia and look to try to lead the team to a much-needed win over Carolina. McKee has some experience in that spot, but not much. He's started two previous games for the Eagles in his career, one last season and one the season before. He's appeared in six games total for Philly and compiled 54 completions, 597 yards, five touchdowns, and one interception.
In a contract year, McKee will have an opportunity to boost his own stock with solid play in Hurts' absence.
Saquon Barkley missed Philadelphia's Week 5 loss to the Jaguars in London due to a hamstring injury that he suffered the previous week against the Rams. Unfortunately, he was one of the players that the Eagles ruled out vs. the Panthers.
Barkley didn't participate in any of Philadelphia's practices this week, which made it clear that his availability was a long shot. Hamstring injuries are tricky, especially for an explosive back like Barkley.
The Eagles will want to be sure he's fully good to go before clearing him to return, so we shouldn't expect to see him out on the field on Sunday.
Unfortunately for Philly, Barkley isn't the only running back on the roster dealing with injury issues.
Backup back Tank Bigsby is already on the injured reserve list due to a core muscle injury that required surgery, and third-string back Will Shipley suffered a foot injury against Jacksonville in Week 5, landing him on the Eagles' injured reserve .
We have placed RB Will Shipley on the Injured Reserve List. pic.twitter.com/4UzsmEMyam
With Shipley officially on IR, practice squad call-ups Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele are the top two backs on Philadelphia's active roster.
Philadelphia's injury issues aren't just limited to the offensive side of the ball. Starting linebacker Jalyx Hunt left Philadelphia's loss to Jacksonville last weekend in the first half with an apparent leg injury, and he didn't return. He's missed all practices this week, so it isn't surprising that he won't be available against the Panthers on Sunday.
The good news for the Eagles is that Hunt's injury isn't as bad as initially expected, which means that his stay on the sideline might not be an extended one. “No timetable. ... It’s not as bad as they thought it was going to be, based on how it looked,” Hunt said of his return earlier this week (h/t SportsRadio 94WIP ).
Safety Michael Carter II suffered an abdominal injury against the Jaguars in Week 5 and didn't return to the game. He's been sidelined from practice this week due to the injury, so his unavailability isn't a surprise either.
Carter has played in all five games for the Eagles so far this season and started in two of them. In his absence, the team will have to rely heavily on the trio of Marcus Epps, Andrew Makuba and Kenny Moore II.

title: Eagles Have 3 Key Advantages Over Panthers Ahead of Week 6
full_text:
Sixteen of the Eagles' 22 opening-day starters are hurt, and it's only the middle of October . It's safe to say things don't look good in the slightest for the organization as Philadelphia heads into Week 6, looking to avoid a fourth consecutive loss.
Despite being 2-3, the Eagles still have a full season in front of them. A win over the Panthers on Sunday could build some momentum heading into the rest of the 2026 season . As long as they get healthier, the Eagles still have room to play better football.
The good news is that they are walking into a contest where the Eagles have some clear advantages over the Panthers. Let's look at the three biggest ones now.
Panthers wideout Tetairoa McMillan has blossomed into a star, and quarterback Bryce Young is playing the best football of his career. It's honestly nice to see, after so many analysts and fans had written him off after a struggling first few seasons.
All that said, the Panthers haven't gone up against a secondary quite like the Eagles.
Quinyon Mitchell is having another All-Pro-type season . Riq Woolen has been a very good boundary corner as well. Add in the exploits of Cooper DeJean, who is having a decent, albeit slow, start to the season, and defensive coordinator Vic Fangio's secondary is still a calling card for Philadelphia.
McMillan vs. Mitchell will be one of the most intriguing matchups to watch on Sunday. Until Philadelphia's top corner gets beat, I still think he has the edge.
The Eagles' defensive line, when healthy, is one of the best in football. The problem is that both Jonathan Greenard and Jalyx Hunt could both be out for Sunday's contest .
The good new is that the Eagles' interior defensive line is both healthy and dominant.
Jalen Carter is coming off a monster game, Moro Ojomo and Jordan Davis are starting to pick things up, and the rest of the line has followed suit. It's not always going to be pretty, but against Carolina's offensive interior, which is average at best, this is a matchup the Eagles should be able to find success with.
Before Thursday, it appeared that, despite the Eagles' rash of injuries across the offense , they still had the chance to find success against a Panthers secondary that ranks 22nd in yards allowed.
Then it got out that quarterback Jalen Hurts would miss Sunday's game after suffering a blood clot in the Eagles' Week 4 loss against the Rams. We won't get into too much of how much trouble the Eagles are in without Hurts, but it is worth noting that Tanner McKee, Philadelphia's QB1 for Week 6, struggled throughout training camp.
Perhaps he's able to salvage the season with a win on Sunday, with the potential of DeVonta Smith returning to the lineup.
Time will tell, but this is a matchup Philadelphia should still be able to exploit, even with a backup quarterback.

title: Examining the Eagles' QB Situation After Signing Joe Milton to the 53-Man Roster
full_text:
The Eagles head into a Week 6 showdown with the Panthers with less-than-ideal quarterback conditions . In an announcement that surprised most Philly fans on Thursday, the Eagles said star signal-caller Jalen Hurts is out indefinitely due to blood clots, forcing backup QB Tanner McKee into the starting spotlight at Lincoln Financial Field this weekend.
That said, McKee has two career starts under his belt, with rookie QB Cole Payton as the only other signal-caller on the 53-man roster or practice squad. The young duo doesn't exactly have much experience for the Eagles to lean on, which is likely why general manager Howie Roseman signed Cowboys practice-squad QB Joe Milton to the 53-man roster on Friday morning , according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz.
Breaking: The #Eagles are signing QB Joe Milton off the #Cowboys practice squad and to their 53-man roster, per sources. pic.twitter.com/e4LVVD4ove
Milton isn't exactly a stranger to the NFC East, having been with the rival Cowboys since the Patriots traded him to Dallas back in April 2025. The Michigan/Tennessee product made four relief appearances last season but couldn't hold on to the backup QB position behind Dak Prescott, ending up on the practice squad as Sam Howell took Milton's old job.
But now, with the Eagles, Milton has a new lease on life and an opportunity to perhaps win another QB2 job. Here's what his signing could mean for his and Philadelphia's outlook moving forward.
Some Eagles fans thought Hurts's injury could lead to Andy Dalton's return after being released last week . The Eagles clearly had other plans, and sometimes it's better to go with an unknown commodity rather than what's familiar but didn't work.
Drafted 193rd overall by the Patriots in 2024, Milton has the size (6-foot-5, 236 lbs) and talents ( world-class arm strength , h/t ESPN ) that most NFL coaches want in their quarterback room. He's still a work in progress, which was expected since he carried a "project" label heading into his draft year, but that means there's plenty of room to grow as a 26-year-old.
Given McKee's inexperience, it isn't unfathomable to believe that the Eagles want to challenge him—especially if Hurts is sidelined indefinitely. Milton might not have any starts under his belt, but he has played 112 offensive snaps across five backup appearances compared with McKee's 178 over six outings, which include the two aforementioned starts. That isn't a huge sample difference, making it easier to compare the two QBs.
McKee might have the edge in touchdown production and fewer INTs thrown. But Milton is clearly the more accurate arm and even averages slightly more yards per completion than his counterpart. That at least gives the Eagles some reason to consider starting the ex-Cowboy should McKee flounder in Hurts's absence.
Having Milton on the 53-man roster also means that the Eagles don't have to throw Payton into the fire. The 2026 fifth-rounder's preseason performance (5-for-12 passing with 47 yards and one touchdown) showed that he isn't ready for the limelight. The last thing Philadelphia needs is to be forced to play an unproven rookie in a must-win situation, and adding Milton to the mix helps avoid that situation.
Milton's presence could also add a new layer to the Eagles' offseason plans. McKee will be a restricted free agent in March, but a return isn't guaranteed unless he successfully proves he can be a reliable backup to Hurts. With Milton also a free agent then, Philly might have to choose between one or the other (or maybe neither, depending on how things go), which makes capitalizing on every opportunity even more crucial.
For now, Eagles fans should expect McKee to remain the de facto starter until Hurts is cleared. At the same time, each mistake will open the door for Milton to take over center, making it a storyline worth following into the next stretch of the 2026 campaign.

title: Landon Dickerson's Trade Deadline Value Becoming Clear as Eagles' Offensive Losses Mount
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - If this season has proven anything in Philadelphia, it's that the NFL is fluid with the latest bomb being the uncertainty of quarterback Jalen Hurts due to a superficial blood clot.
The Eagles’ offensive line, long the foundation of the organization, had already become unrecognizable. Lane Johnson, the future Hall of Fame right tackle and emotional anchor, retired. Cam Jurgens, the versatile Pro Bowl interior lineman, was traded to the Baltimore Ravens for draft capital. Now, as three-time Pro Bowl left guard Landon Dickerson works his way back from injured reserve and the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaches, the franchise faces a clear choice: stabilize what remains of the unit or accelerate its dismantling.
They cannot let Dickerson become the third departure.
Johnson’s retirement and the Jurgens trade were not identical situations. Johnson’s exit was driven by personal priorities after a long career. Jurgens’ move netted a valuable 2028 second-round pick for a player the Eagles viewed as a fit risk in their evolving scheme and someone who had not fully returned to peak form after injury.
Dickerson, still just 28, is somewhat different. He is under contract through at least 2027 after a revised deal this offseason, remains a proven high-level starter when healthy, and represents the last established Pro Bowl-level presence on the interior next to left tackle Jordan Mailata.
The results without him have been predictable and less than optimal.
After Dickerson went on IR with a bone bruise in his knee following a Week 1 performance he himself called a liability, the line has been in disarray as it has shuffled through multiple combinations. Young, developmental players like Willie Lampkin, Jake Majors and Markel Bell have been pressed into starting roles with limited experience. The offense, already struggling with first-year coordinator Sean Mannion’s new scheme , has ranked near the bottom of the league in yards, scoring, and efficiency.
Any further depletion would compound an already narrow margin for error, especially with Hurts sidelined, Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith still dealing with hamstring injuries, and the team trying to stay relevant in what's shaping up as a poor NFC East as a whole.
You can't necessarily just default to Dickerson’s resume: a second-round pick out of Alabama in 2021 who quickly became a foundational piece on a great team with three consecutive Pro Bowl berths (2022-24) and a key blocker for Barkley’s historic 2024 rushing season, and a Super Bowl LIX championship.
At his best, he pairs size, power, and enough athletic ability that fit both the old vertical schemes and the new zone concepts Mannion and the staff are trying to install. That said, the injury history is also real—Dickerson has dealt with multiple issues and even reportedly weighed retirement this offseason.
Opening his practice window this week signals the team still sees him as a viable option now, not merely a trade chip.
Trade rumors have surfaced, of course, as they often do around the deadline for any productive veteran on a reworked contract. Insiders have noted that rival teams could inquire, and Dickerson’s own recent comments—deflecting questions about whether he remains the long-term left guard by saying it is not his decision—reflect that uncertainty.
Yet a fire sale does not align with the Eagles’ stated posture of remaining competitive rather than selling off pieces, especially in a weak division. Draft capital from another trade would be useful long-term, but the immediate cost would be steep: an interior line relying almost entirely on young or unproven players while the offense tries to install a new identity and figure out what they have to do long-term at quarterback with a potential $60 million extension looming for Hurts.
Removing the last proven interior veteran outside Tyler Steen risks turning the remainder of the season into something even worse than the season from hell.
The Eagles have already accepted significant change on the line. Further erosion with Dickerson is not required by circumstance or contract. The one complication is health, but Dickerson is young enough to be part of the next competitive window, experienced enough to stabilize the present, and still capable of high-level play if the worm turns there. Letting him follow Johnson and Jurgens out the door would not be smart roster management by GM Howie Roseman right now. It would be self-inflicted damage to a unit that has already lost too much.

title: McMullen: Tanner McKee Could Provide Important Answers About Sean Mannion's Eagles Offense
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - The “week from hell,” as dubbed by star left tackle Jordan Mailata after a cascade of roster upheaval, a transatlantic trip, and a gut-wrenching loss in London, may have just been elevated to the “season from hell” for the Philadelphia Eagles.
As late as Sept. 28, Tanner McKee was the Eagles’ QB3 . On Sunday, the fourth-year pro will take over the struggling Eagles offense after Jalen Hurts was ruled out indefinitely Thursday with a superficial blood clot in his leg.
“I think I was a little early,” Mailata laughed when Eagles On SI asked about his team's bad luck this season. “I might have jumped the gun on that one. Holy cow! That's the NFL, man. It's the gift that keeps on giving."
The situation unfolded after Hurts asked the training staff to treat his calf late last week after taking a cleat to the leg during the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. The results of an ultrasound performed after the team flew to London in the subsequent days showed the superficial blood clot, but medical staff concluded the Super Bowl-winning quarterback could safely play.
From there, a follow-up ultrasound performed on Wednesday night revealed movement in the small clot. As a result, Hurts will sit out this weekend and possibly beyond that, depending on what needs to be done from a medical standpoint .
The Eagles’ medical staff say they are determining the appropriate course of treatment.
“Superficial blood clots form near the skin's surface and, while generally less dangerous than deep vein thrombosis (DVT), must be taken seriously. If a clot extends into deeper veins, it can cause severe complications, including traveling to the lungs," explains Dr. Alina Mitina, Emergency Medicine Physician at Hackensack University Medical Center (HUMC). "While many resolve with simple treatments like warm compresses and anti-inflammatories, the clot's size and location determine whether blood thinners are necessary.
“Recent trauma and prolonged inactivity are major risk factors. Although we can't definitively say the flight to London worsened his condition, combining long-distance air travel with a recent leg injury creates a higher-risk environment for a clot to progress."
With Hurts sidelined, the Eagles turn to McKee, a 6-foot-6 pocket passer drafted in the sixth round out of Stanford in 2023. He has just two career starts and limited regular-season snaps (54 of 88 for 597 yards, five touchdowns, and one interception), but he has impressed in spots, including a solid Week 18 performance in 2024.
The team recently released veteran Andy Dalton, solidifying McKee as the clear No. 2 before the injury elevated him further; rookie Cole Payton is now the primary backup.⁠
The change comes at a precarious moment for an offense that ranks near the bottom of the league in scoring, yards, and efficiency under first-year offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. Hired from the Packers (where he served as quarterbacks coach under Matt LaFleur) after playing under Sean McVay and in Kevin O’Connell’s system, Mannion has installed a scheme rooted in the McVay/Shanahan tree: the goals of more under-center work, heavy play-action, wide-zone running concepts, motion, and pure progression reads rather than the RPO-heavy, dual-threat-friendly attack that previously maximized Hurts.
That philosophical shift has been a work in progress and, by most accounts, an imperfect marriage for Hurts, whose strengths as a runner and off-schedule playmaker have been featured less amid the new structure.
Mannion, meanwhile, has repeatedly said the core tenets of the offense remain non-negotiable even as results lag, with the unit averaging under 15 points and struggling to sustain drives during a three-game skid. ⁠
McKee is perceived as a more traditional pocket passer, although his processing has been slow when given opportunities in training camp and the preseason.
That said, inserting the Stanford product could offer a clearer picture into whether the scheme’s issues stem primarily from execution, personnel, or a fundamental mismatch with Hurts’ skill set.
A better fit for McKee might allow Mannion’s preferred play-action and progression concepts to better shine, even if the Eagles lose Hurts’ unique dual-threat dimension.
How long Hurts remains out—and whether McKee’s stint reveals more about the long-term viability of Mannion’s offense—could shape Philadelphia’s path through the rest of the season and into the future.
For an offense still searching for identity, the next several games may serve as an unplanned but needed evaluation of both Hurts’ fit into Mannion’s vision and the system itself.

title: Everything Important Eagles Players Said About Jalen Hurts Injury After Today's Practice
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Markel Bell arrived at Thursday morning’s walkthrough, glanced about the field, and didn’t see the No. 1. Jalen Hurts wasn’t there.
Players then saw Tanner McKee in the huddle, and they began checking their phones. That was how the Eagles learned the news that their quarterback would not play on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers as the QB and the organization determine the best course of treatment for the superficial blood clot in his calf.
“I didn't hear about it until I got to my phone,” said the rookie right tackle. “I got to my phone after walk-through. I found out when you guys found out. I was sitting around and I'm like, ‘Dang,’ like, ‘Wow,’ this is crazy.”
Bell’s recollection of finding out about Hurts was echoed among others in the locker room on Thursday.
“I found out when you guys found out,” said left tackle Jordan Mailata. “It's insane.”
Added linebacker Zack Baun: “It was shocking, And then to find out that he had been dealing with it last game was very shocking. But it just shows his toughness, his grit, his attitude, his willingness to win. I hope he gets better soon. I really do.”
It’s been that kind of season so far for the Eagles, with one big injury, followed by another big injury, followed by Lane Johnson's retirement, the Cam Jurgens trade, and then another injury.
“It'll be a good story to tell once I get older and all that and in my career as well,” said Bell, “but right now, my vet retires, Cam gets traded, all the injuries, it’s just crazy.”
The Eagles don’t have time to dwell on crazy. They have a game on Sunday and are trying to find a way to snap a three-game losing streak. And they’ll have to do it without Hurts and several other players that could include DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley.
“Just gotta keep my brother up in prayers, and that's what we're doing,” said Darius Cooper, who has become a favorite target for Hurts, with four touchdown catches on just seven receptions. “We just have to continue to encourage him and continue to walk with him through it.”
The Eagles will turn to Tanner McKee, who began the season as the third-string quarterback but was elevated to No. 2 when they released Andy Dalton on Oct. 9. McKee said he found out before the team’s morning walkthrough that he would be the starter.
It was at his locker when Hurts turned to him and said, “It looks like you’re going to be the guy.”
“It was like, ‘OK, well I'm taking the one reps now, and let's move like I'm gonna be the guy," said McKee. “As a backup quarterback, that's the mindset you have to have. At any moment you can be ready to play. On Sunday, it could be the first play; it could be the last play; you have to be ready.”
The Eagles hope it will be every play for McKee against the Panthers because his backup is rookie Cole Payton.
“It's not like Tanner's a new guy,” said Mailata. “He's been here for four years. Love everything about him. His poise, his energy, too. High energy guy.
“It's not Jalen, where Jalen's like cool, calm, collected 24/7. Tanner provides great... there's a very calm nature about him, but there's also a lot of high energy in him, too, just the way he attacks the practice.”

title: 2 Winners & 4 Losers Following Jalen Hurts Blood Clot Health Scare
full_text:
Looking to end their growing losing streak in Week 6 , the Eagles were dealt a massive blow that will make defeating the Panthers even more difficult this weekend. On Thursday, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts will be sidelined for Sunday's clash due to a "superficial blood clot."
According to a statement released by the Eagles, Hurts has been dealing with the issue since he was "cleated" during the Week 4 clash with the Rams. Although he ultimately faced the Jaguars and even practiced to begin the new week, "a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement" on Wednesday, leading Philadelphia to opt to sit Hurts for at least one game.
Breaking: #Eagles QB Jalen Hurts is out for Sunday due to a superficial blood clot. Full statement from the #Eagles on QB Jalen Hurts: “On Thursday, October 8th, Jalen visited the training room after practice requesting treatment for his calf. He informed the medical staff he… pic.twitter.com/16hVutehsp
Hurts has been far from perfect this season (57.8% completion rate, 84.7 passer rating), but it isn't a secret that his absence in Week 6 will impact the Eagles—for better or worse. His upcoming absence will negatively impact at least four members of the Philadelphia organization this week, as well as a pair who could benefit from not having him around.
Anytime a starting QB misses a game, his head coach's job is usually tougher. That's about to be the case for Eagles HC Nick Sirianni, whose fate hinges on each passing game.
Sirianni's play-calling and leadership have come under question throughout the last two seasons, and that's been even more the case now that Philadelphia is on a three-game skid. The Eagles have averaged only 14.7 points during that stretch, all while being outscored by an average margin of 9.0 ppg. Now, it's going to be an even more uphill battle to put up points without Hurts in the mix, adding even more pressure to Sirianni's job.
Sirianni has been without Hurts seven times since the start of the 2021 season, and the results aren't promising. The Eagles own an uninspiring 3-4 record in those contests, which includes being held to 20 or fewer points in three of the last four. In other words, Sirianni needs to buck that trend to prove that he's still the right man for the job.
In terms of players, Darius Cooper might suffer the most from not having Hurts on the field this weekend.
After all, the former undrafted wideout out of Tarleton State is coming off the best performance of his young NFL career. Cooper recorded two catches for 71 receiving yards and a touchdown against the Jaguars in London, which included a beautiful 62-yard score late in the second quarter (h/t NFL).
DARIUS COOPER, 62-YARD TOUCHDOWN EAGLES TAKE THE LEAD. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/eKpCwhW8QZ
Cooper now has 104 receiving yards and three TDs in his last two games, which puts him on pace for a 43-884-25 stat line in 17 games. Obviously, scoring that many touchdowns would be nearly impossible, but the reception and yardage totals underscore what Cooper might be losing now that Hurts is out of commission for at least one week.
That said, Cooper has seen plenty of Eagles backup QB Tanner McKee in practice over the last two years, leaving time to tell whether that familiarity will produce in-game results.
When one door closes, another opens, and now all eyes are on McKee to see if he'll stroll through or stumble in the face of his new opportunity.
Barring any setbacks, McKee will be the Eagles' QB1 against the Panthers, marking his first start since a 24-17 loss to the Commanders in Week 18 of the 2025 season. The former 2023 sixth-rounder now has a decent amount of experience after making six appearances (two starts) for Philadelphia since being drafted, in which he completed 61.4% of passes for 597 yards, five touchdowns,  one interception and a 99.5 passer rating.
After a strong end to the preseason , all eyes will be on McKee to see what he can do against the Panthers, who might allow the 11th-most passing yards per game (230.8), but have also surrendered the fifth-worst completion rate (61.1%) and fourth-fewest passing TDs (4) so far.
Considering how he'll be an unrestricted free agent in March, capitalizing on any opportunities he sees during Hurts's time away could be huge for McKee's future, either in Philly or elsewhere.
Circling back to the coaching staff, offensive coordinator Sean Mannion is another Eagle impacted by Hurts's Week 6 absence.
The former Packers QBs coach hasn't had the expected impact after taking over the Eagles' OC role in the offseason. Philadelphia has entered the week ranked 29th in points, 31st in total yards, 28th in passing yards and T-10th in rushing yards, truly underscoring how disastrous the ball movement has been under Mannion's guidance.
Well, an already difficult job just became harder because now Mannion needs to prove to the Eagles that he's the right offensive coordinator without Hurts. His play-calling has already left little room for optimism, so it's hard to imagine that things will magically improve without the straw that stirs Philly's drink.
Having no Hurts on the field means that the Eagles' defense could see a lot more action this weekend.
The early offensive issues to begin the season mean that Philadelphia's defenders have already seen more action than the team would like. The Eagles' offense has only held the ball for an average of 27:50 per game, which ranks 27th in the NFL, making the defense one of the league's most-worked units.
For comparison, the offense controlled the ball for an average of 30:16 in 2025 (12th) and a league-leading 32:21 in 2024.
The Bears, Rams and Jaguars all beat the Eagles by controlling the ball, each finishing with 30 to 35 minutes of possession time, and that was with Hurts. Without their franchise signal-caller, the Eagles' defense will likely be on the field more often than not against the Panthers, who know how to tire teams out, as they average the third-most offensive plays per game this season (67.0).
Needless to say, expect the Eagles' defense to remain busy throughout Hurts's absence, no matter how long it lasts.
The Eagles raised some eyebrows when they traded a seventh-round pick to acquire Andy Dalton from the Panthers back in March. Although Dalton is an experienced backup QB, the fact that McKee was already around made the move somewhat redundant. Even Philadelphia seemingly admitted that it was a mistake by releasing Dalton last week after throwing an INT on his lone passing attempt of the year.
Fast-forward less than a week, and Hurts's injury may have paved the way for Dalton's return to the City of Brotherly Love. Even NFL insider Mark Garafolo thinks there's a chance for a reunion , despite the fact that Dalton has "had a few teams check in with him since the team released him."
Andy Dalton is an option to return for the #Eagles . He’s had a few teams check in with him since the team released him, per sources, though there’s familiarity and a clear role in Philly for him if he decides to return. https://t.co/bNeypdIjiO
That isn't to say Dalton should be the primary signal-caller without Hurts around (that should still be McKee). However, it certainly wouldn't hurt the Eagles to bring him back. Rookie QB Cole Payton is on the 53-man roster but lacks the experience to step in if something happens to McKee, and there aren't any other options on the practice squad.
Dalton's best days are behind him, but he'd at least provide a steady presence behind McKee, and his familiarity from being around Sirianni and company for the last nine-ish months is a bonus.

title: Medical Expert Weighs in on Jalen Hurts Blood Clot Situation as Questions Surround Eagles
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — There are several different angles to view the news that broke Thursday midafternoon about Eagles starting quarterback Jalen Hurts after it was announced that he has a superficial blood clot in his calf and will not play in Sunday’s game against the Panthers.
pic.twitter.com/9SeK1XzYRL
How did Hurts get cleared to play against the Jaguars on Sunday? More importantly, how was he able to fly such a great distance in such a short period of time, going from Philly to London?
He said he was cleated on the calf against the Rams, but didn't look for treatment until Friday, the day the Eagles flew to London.
Will he be OK in the long term? What about the short term? What is the prognosis for return to play? Could this be a one-week situation or multiple weeks?
There are more questions will emerge. Right now, the situation is still new, and there is a game to play in about three days.
Eagles on SI received an email from Dr. Alina Mitina, an emergency physician at Hackensack Medical Center, that helps make sense of Hurts's situation, reading:
“Superficial blood clots form near the skin’s surface and, while generally less dangerous than deep vein thrombosis (DVT), must be taken seriously. If a clot extends into deeper veins, it can cause severe complications, including traveling to the lungs. While many resolve with simple treatments like warm compresses and anti-inflammatories, the clot’s size and location determine whether blood thinners are necessary."
In the short term, the Eagles are down to just two quarterbacks: Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton. They released Andy Dalton last week , but may now look to bring him back to the practice squad to serve as the backup to McKee.
Dalton and McKee waged a summer-long battle to be the primary backup and by doing that, Payton probably didn’t get the development he needed to possibly be ready should something in-game happen to McKee.
Hurts’s injury is the latest in what has been a landslide of injuries this season. There were 17 players listed on Wednesday’s injury report : six of whom did not practice and 11 others who were limited.
Some key players weren’t at Thursday’s practice either, including wideout DeVonta Smith and running back Saquon Barkley.
So, it looks like the Eagles will take the field on Sunday with a backup quarterback, a fourth-string running back in Dameon Pierce and an offensive line that last week saw two undrafted free agents start, Willie Lampkin and Jake Majors, and a third-round rookie, Markel Bell, make just his second career start at right tackle.

title: Steelers WR Situation Might Be Worse Than Believed
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are down bad at the wide receiver position.
Roman Wilson (finger), Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Ben Skowronek (calf) are already out against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Pittman Jr. is already on Injured Reserve, and DK Metcalf is now questionable with an illness.
But it doesn't stop there.
The team and fanbase are optimistic that, when everything is back to normal, this group is exciting. Germie Bernard is breaking out as a rookie, Metcalf remains, well, Metcalf, and Wilson and Pittman Jr. are talented starters with steady contributions.
They may not get back to normal, though. According to Pat McAfee Show correspondent Mark Kaboly, there's a belief that Pittman Jr. isn't coming back anytime soon. And that the foot injury that has already shut him down for several weeks could last much longer, putting his return at risk this season.
Report: There are "bad feelings" about Michael Pitman Jr returning anytime soon. He will likely miss more time than the minimum 4 weeks he has to spend on injured reserve. Per Pat McAfee Steelers correspondent Mark Kaboly. Pittman Jr is looking like a bad trade/extension. pic.twitter.com/Oink0Ous92
If Pittman Jr. is to miss time, the Steelers are left with Bernard, Metcalf, Wilson, Skowronek and rookie returner Kaden Wetjen as their wide receiver room. Wilson is expected to miss several weeks, and could end up on Injured Reserve himself. It's unknown how long Skowronek is going to miss.
If the Steelers are truly down multiple wideouts for a large chunk of the season, they're going to rely on other options.
Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington are going to be heavily involved in the passing game. Running backs Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle will also be utilized.
At some point, the Steelers will likely sign Brandon Smith off of the practice squad. Smith was called up last week and is expected to be called up again in Week 6. He'll have one more game to be called up before needing to be signed to the active roster.
He'd be their top option to replace Wilson and Pittman Jr., but may not be enough if Wilson is also going to be out long-term.
Pittsburgh may need to get creative and look at outside options at some point. Right now, that's not on their agenda, but it could change if they believe Pittman Jr. is set to miss most of the season and Wilson is headed to Injured Reserve.
Expect the Steelers to activate two wideouts against the Buccaneers. After that, Smith will likely sign to the 53-man roster and they'll continue to rely on either Brandon Johnson or Isaiah Hodgins as their call-up. But if this situation keeps trending in the wrong direction, who knows what the Steelers do to vill the void.

title: Steelers WR Depth Gets Even Worse With DK Metcalf News
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers were delivered another potential blow at wide receiver.
On their final injury report ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , DK Metcalf was listed as questionable to play with an illness.
Though it's an illness rather than an injury, which is positive news long-term, it's yet another instance of a receiver dealing with some type of hinderance.
Metcalf was not listed on either of the first two injury reports of the week before registering as a non-participant on October 16.
On the season so far, he has recorded 225 yards and a touchdown across 19 receptions.
Pittsburgh is already down three receivers for its bout with Tampa Bay. Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) was placed on the reserve/injured list, meaning the earliest he can return after missing the minimum of four games while on IR is in Week 10 following the team's Week 9 bye.
Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have also been ruled out vs. the Buccaneers after suffering their respective injuries in the first half of the Steelers' Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
Now, Pittsburgh will take a wait-and-see approach with Metcalf before kicking off against Tampa Bay and hope that it doesn't lose another receiver for that contest.
Given that the Steelers' wide receiver depth was already going to be tested in a major way this week, Metcalf's status now being up in the air is quite the negative development.
There's clearly still a chance that he ends up suiting up and playing at Raymond James Stadium against Tampa Bay, but in a scenario where he doesn't, Pittsburgh is going to have to get creative.
Germie Bernard would temporarily take over as the No. 1 option at the position, and he showed that he's capable of handling those duties at least in the short-term following a six-catch, 80-yard outing vs. Indianapolis.
Kaden Wetjen is the only other receiver on the 53-man roster beyond Metcalf and Bernard, though there's not a ton to suggest that head coach Mike McCarthy is comfortable throwing the fourth-round rookie out on the field on offense yet.
“Well, he’s hasn’t gotten a lot of work as far as our primary game plan and things like that, but he’s developing. He’s out here every day working, so as far as how we use him so forth, we’ll let the games dictate that,” McCarthy said this week.
As such, the Steelers will likely run more 12 personnel than originally expected if Metcalf doesn't play while relying on a player or two coming up from the practice squad, which could include Brandon Smith, Brandon Johnson and/or Isaiah Hodgins, in addition to potentially making another roster move.

title: Concern Growing for Steelers' Nick Herbig
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- After an impressive first two weeks of the season, the Pittsburgh Steelers' defense is in a strange place. They haven't been a bad group, suggesting so would be a dishonest evaluation.
But over the past three weeks, the Steelers' defense has not been great. They allowed 22 points to the Indianapolis Colts and 27 points each to the Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals. Far from the group they want to be, multiple players on the defensive side are searching for more production.
The most important of this group is linebacker Nick Herbig. After signing a massive extension that made him the team's second-highest paid defensive player behind T.J. Watt, the pressure has been cranked up on the 24-year-old edge rusher.
In response, it's been a disappointing first third of the regular season for Herbig. Through five games, he has just 12 tackles and has yet to record a sack. Is it time to worry about the fourth-year edge rusher? The answer is more complicated than you think.
It's been a forgetful first five games for Nick Herbig, but we need to pump the brakes on any large concerns. Sure, Herbig hasn't gotten home, with just one quarterback hit, one pressure and 0.0 sacks to his credit.
But there has been flashes. For example, Herbig's athleticism remains a threat. In the pair of times he's been targeted in pass coverage, quarterbacks aren't finding success. Data from Pro Football Reference shows that he's been targeted just twice in coverage, but each time was an incompletion.
There have also been plenty of plays where Herbig's athleticism and speed are present. It hasn't resulted in those big plays we've come to expect yet, but there is still plenty of time to snap out of this funk.
The thing that remains worrisome for Herbig is where the Steelers are using him the most. For starters, he's not seeing the field nearly enough, which is just a continuation of the same issue he's faced the past few seasons. He's played 161 defensive snaps through five weeks, which adds up to around 52% of the total defensive snaps played by the Steelers. Still in a limited role, it's clear that he has fewer chances to make impact plays.
Secondly, one way the Steelers have gotten him on the field is as a part of three edge rusher sets. In those instances, he often plays in the box as an off-ball linebacker. He fills the role admirably, but again, it's not the ideal position for a playmaking edge rusher to be in.
The last concern is missed tackles. In Week 5, there was a noticeable play where Herbig knifed into the backfield from the weak side, but he was unable to bring Jonathan Taylor down and he turned it into a positive play for the Colts. That's happened a few times this season, and according to game data from PFF , he's missed on just over 35% of his tackle attempts in 2026.
If the current usage of Herbig is the plan moving forward, then he might be in trouble. Hopefully, defensive coordinator Patrick Graham has some tricks up his sleeve to get their $25 million linebacker back on track.
