title: Steelers Rookie Grades: Early Evaluations Bring Excitement and Worry
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are 3-2 as they prepare to take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. In many respects, the season is off to a good start.
After all, the Steelers are 3-0 at home. Their offense is clicking. There are plenty of reasons for optimism in Pittsburgh.
One of the biggest reasons is the impact of their rookie class. After drafting 10 players and keeping another undrafted free agent on their roster, the expectation was clear. The Steelers needed immediate production from their first-year players, and from many of them, that's exactly what is happening.
Entering their sixth game of the season, here's how each Steelers rookie grades out.
Max Iheanachor should have been the starting right tackle to begin the regular season, and it's not a coincidence that the right side of the line has improved greatly since he and Brock Hoffman were inserted for Spencer Anderson and Dylan Cook.
Iheanachor has had bad reps over his first few games, but overall he's been excellent. He has quick hands and feet, he's incredibly strong, and he isn't easily fooled. The Steelers might just have their starting right tackle for the next five to 10 years with Iheanachor in the organization.
Week 5 was a breakout for wide receiver Germie Bernard, but it was just a matter of time for the team's second-round draft pick. Bernard has quickly earned trust from quarterback Aaron Rodgers, and with injuries piling up, he was the team's top pass-catching weapon against the Indianapolis Colts. Bernard has made some mistakes, including some unforced drops that halted drives or led to turnovers, but he has also produced over the first five weeks. And he still has so much room to grow.
The Steelers didn't envision Daylen Everette playing a large portion of the snaps on the outside, but after trading Joey Porter Jr., the team had no choice. In response, Everette looks like a serviceable starter. If they had paid a premium on the free agency market to bring him in, he'd be subject to far more criticism. But for a rookie, third-round pick, he's giving the Steelers a huge boost at a depleted position.
A tough, tough blow was dealt to Gennings Dunker after a lower-body injury effectively ended his rookie campaign before it ever started. A bruising offensive lineman in college, the Steelers project him to be a starting right guard eventually. That plan will have to wait until 2027. Because of that, Mr. Dunker receives an incomplete grade for the time being.
Drew Allar was the darling of training camp and the preseason. With the regular season one-third of the way completed, however, Allar's preseason is in the rearview. He made the roster but won't sniff the field unless multiple injuries occur. Perhaps in 2027, this pick rewards the organization, but in 2026 it's just an average pick.
The Steelers used a fourth-round pick on Kaden Wetjen, the most regretful choice of the 2026 draft. So far, the return has been anything but positive. He can't create splash plays on the kick or punt return, and he can't get on the field when the offense is out there. It's a harsh but realistic grade for a player who feels like an absolute misfit in Pittsburgh.
As a special teams player, Riley Nowakowski is excelling. As a fullback, the primary reason he was drafted by the Steelers, there is nothing to evaluate. He barely plays outside of special teams situations, and that feels like the plan for the remainder of the 2026 season.
14 snaps on defense took Gabe Rubio from another non-contributing member of this class to an impressive depth find. Rubio got his first and only taste of NFL action in Week 5, but he was a stout presence along the line of scrimmage over that small sample size. The hulking defensive tackle is 6'5" and over 320 pounds, and he's already showing the traits of a tenacious run-stopper in the Steelers' front seven.
The most consistent player in this rookie class is undoubtedly Robert Spears-Jennings. Since arriving in Pittsburgh, the safety out of Oklahoma has been rock solid. Regardless of the role, he succeeds. And now he's finally getting his due with the starting defensive group.
The Steelers landed a gem in RSJ.
It's a bit unfair, like some of the other rookies on the roster, but the early returns are underwhelming for Eli Heidenreich. The seventh-round pick surprisingly made the 53-man roster out of training camp, but he's been hardly used in the regular season. In the past few weeks, he's been inactive on game days, and even with injuries mounting on offense, he still is unlikely to take on a larger role.
The Steelers like the talent and potential, but that's the end of the compliments for the athletic running back.
The undrafted free agent made the roster, but like so many others, is patiently waiting for his shot. He showed some impressive pass rush moves in the preseason, which kept him around in 2026. But we won't see that on the field any time soon.

title: No One Knows What Steelers Trade Deadline Plans Are
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have several needs across their roster. So, that means they will be aggressive buyers before this year's NFL trade deadline, right?
Well, that might be the case for the Steelers, depending on which beat writer you subscribe to. If you are an ardent believer in long-time insider Gerry Dulac, that feels like a stretch. In his recent mailbag article for the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette , he shot down the idea of a trade, barring more significant injuries.
But if you are a Mark Kaboly fan, you're now expecting the exact opposite. Via an update on his X account, he shared that sources indicated to him that the Steelers are very interested in upgrading with a trade.
Getting strong indications that the Steelers are going to be active heading into the NFL trade deadline set for Nov. 10
So, which is it? Are the Steelers on the prowl or are they standing pat? The answer is more complicated than you think.
The short answer is that the Steelers are constantly trying to upgrade; it's just that their approach is hardly what you would expect. The team has already been active in trying to improve their roster. They added two veteran defensive backs via other organizations' practice squads, bringing in Sean Murphy-Bunting and Terrell Smith recently to bolster their depth.
That's the likeliest route this team will take when addressing their biggest issue currently: wide receiver. Down three players from their active roster, the offense needs a boost. This is where the varying opinions diverge.
The reality, however, is that the Steelers are extremely unlikely to give up the draft capital they just acquired or previously stockpiled on immediate wide receiver help. Despite sources indicating to Kaboly that the Steelers are shopping, don't buy the rumors that they are shopping for big-time names.
Instead, the focus should be on veteran names on practice squads, just like they did at cornerback. Names like K.J. Osbsorn, Mecole Hardman, Lil'Jordan Humphrey, Jalin Hyatt, Scotty Miller, Trey Palmer and Xavier Gipson make much more sense and fit the profile of their previous acquisitions.
Where I really expect a trade to occur for the Steelers is on the defensive side of the ball. The Steelers can probably get a temporary replacement at wide receiver by poaching a practice squad or signing one of the few NFL-caliber receivers available in free agency, but they cannot upgrade their defensive inefficiencies the same way.
Instead, the Steelers need a true upgrade outside of the organization at several positions. The first one still might be cornerback, unless Murphy-Bunting becomes that dependable outside presence. The second is safety, which continues to hamper their secondary. The third is inside linebacker, as the entire depth chart has underwhelmed to start the season.
If a trade is happening, it's on the defensive side of the ball.
But that's only if a deal gets done. And depending on who you trust and what you read, you will come away with various answers on the subject.

title: Steelers WR Outlook: Who's Replacing Roman Wilson?
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers need to replace two more wide receivers in Week 6. With Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek missing the team's matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the black and gold need to add to their depth chart. So, who is joining the mix?
It's unknown how much time Wilson (finger) and Skowronek (calf) will miss, so for now, the team is taking things week-to-week with their replacements. Pittsburgh is also without Michael Pittman Jr., who is on Injured Reserve with a foot injury, leaving DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard and Kaden Wetjen on their active roster.
Which is where we should begin.
Wetjen brings plenty of excitement as a kick and punt returner, but not much as a wideout. The Iowa product and fourth-round rookie has been the team's focal point on special teams, but isn't ready to be an offensive threat.
Head coach Mike McCarthy even said Wetjen hasn't done much to prepare for a larger role within the receiving core.
"He's hasn’t gotten a lot of work as far as our primary game plan and things like that, but he's developing," McCarthy said. "He's out here every day working, so as far as how we use him so forth, we’ll let the games dictate that."
That leaves Metcalf and Bernard. The veteran and rookie will be the WR1 and WR2 for the Steelers this weekend.
Metcalf continues to be the front-runner of the receiver room, with Bernard breaking out in Week 5 with an expanded role. The second-round pick tabbed six receptions for 80 yards against the Indianapolis Colts and is now looking at even more attention after the loss of Wilson.
They won't be alone, though. The Steelers are preparing to run a lot of two-tight end sets, utilizing Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington as much as possible.
Robert Tonyan will also be involved.
Enter Brandon Smith, Brandon Johnson and Isaiah Hodgins.
The Steelers are expected to call Smith up for a second straight game off of the practice squad. The 27-year-old wideout didn't record a catch last week, but was involved in a 50-yard touchdown by Jaylen Warren. Smith and Washington were the two downfield blockers as Warren found the seam.
Right now, Smith is the team's WR3 heading into Week 6.
"It seems like at this point it's just in-house options," Rodgers said. "So, we’vegot a talented [practice] squad group of guys and guys who played football at the highest level and made plays. Excited about getting those guys in. Obviously, [Tonyan] has played a lot of football and played at a high level, so I'm sure he'll get some more opportunities. [Brandon]Smith, Brandon Johnson, maybe Isaiah [Hodgins]. We'll get some guys who haven't seen a lot of time out there and expect them to play well."
It's likely the Steelers will call up two wide receivers from their practice squad this weekend. It's unknown whether it'll be Johnson or Hodgins, with both players having playing experience throughout their careers.
Johnson has 26 catches for 335 yards and five touchdowns throughout his career. Hodgins has 19 career starts, including five last year for the New York Giants. He's recorded 70 receptions for 749 yards and eight touchdowns during his career.
If Wilson needs to be placed on Injured Reserve, Smith will likely be signed to the active roster and Hodgins or Johnson will continue to be called up as needed.
There are a lot of moving parts for the Steelers' passing game in Week 6, and nothing is expected to slow down soon. Right now, there are no signs that the team will be looking outside of the organization for options. That could change.
But heading to Tampa Bay, this is how the Steelers will handle their wide receiver room.

title: Steelers Get Good Injury News Before Bucs Game
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have some positive developments on the injury front ahead of their Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .
On their penultimate injury report of the week, running back Rico Dowdle (toe) was listed as a full participant, which is the first time that's been the case since he suffered his injury in Week 2 vs. the New England Patriots.
Furthermore, defensive tackle Keeanu Benton (ankle) and cornerback Jalen Ramsey (wrist) were both limited participants after registering as non-participants on the first injury report this week.
After missing three games in a row, Dowdle is finally on the precipice of a return for Pittsburgh.
He dislocated his toe twice against the Patriots, first in the second quarter and then in the third quarter in what was a 20-3 loss for the Steelers.
While speaking with reporters last week, the 28-year-old laid out how the entire process played out in that contest.
"The first time I did it, I came to the sideline and I was like, "I think my toe broke,'" Dowdle said. "So I went to the tent and it was dislocated and they popped it back in, did the X-rays. Nothing was broken or whatever, but once they popped it back in, I felt good, so I'm like, 'I wanna go back in the game and play.' Dr. [James] Bradley was like, 'No, we're playing on turf, think I'm gonna be done,' because when you get it, you hurt the plate at the bottom or whatever. So I ended up talking him into going back in, and he was like, 'If it pop out again, you've gotta be done,' and it popped out again, so I had to be done."
Following the team's Week 5 victory over the Indianapolis Colts, head coach Mike McCarthy stated that Dowdle was close to playing in that game .
Now, all the stars are aligning for him to be back on the field against the Bucs, even if it's not 100 percent official that he'll be active just yet.
Jaylen Warren will remain the feature back given that he has posted 491 yards in the three contests Dowdle has missed, but the latter will certainly still have a noticeable role in the offense.
Ramsey broke his wrist in Week 3 vs. the Cincinnati Bengals and has not been a full practice participant since, though he's still played since suffering that injury and his status for this week's bout with Tampa Bay was never really in question.
Benton was a surprise inclusion on the first injury report this week , though it doesn't appear that he's dealing with a serious ankle injury considering he's been upgraded to a limited participant alongside Ramsey.
The game designations for both players remains to be seen when the final injury report is put out on October 16, but it certainly would appear they'll each be active against the Bucs.

title: Steelers Chances vs. Bucs Skyrocket With QB News
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers ' chances of snagging a victory in Week 6 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers just rose.
Baker Mayfield was not practicing on October 15, as noted by Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times, meaning undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels is all but guaranteed to start against the Steelers.
Baker Mayfield is NOT practicing today so we can stop speculating. Jalon Daniels will start vs the Steelers barring something unforeseen. pic.twitter.com/GXWuYv23gp
Daniels has stepped in as the starter in each of the Buccaneers' last two games while Mayfield has dealt with a dislocated thumb that he suffered in Week 3 vs. the Minnesota Vikings.
While Daniels did help guide Tampa Bay to a victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football in Week 5, he still presents a far more favorable matchup at quarterback for Pittsburgh than Mayfield would.
Up to this point, Daniels has completed 38 of his 55 passing attempts for the Buccaneers for 337 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions.
He was not sharp in his first start against the Green Bay Packers, which was a 17-14 loss for Tampa Bay, as he went 19-of-27 for 148 yards, a touchdown and two picks.
Daniels was far more efficient vs. Dallas, however, completing 19 of his 25 attempts for 185 yards, a touchdown and no interceptions.
The 23-year-old has proven to be a real weapon with his legs as well, rushing for 55 yards on eight attempts against Green Bay and 23 yards on seven attempts vs. the Cowboys.
Daniels isn't going to push the ball down the field much at all, which could work to Pittsburgh's benefit, as his current average depth of target stands at 6.2 (per Pro Football Focus ).
The Buccaneers' offensive line has been quite good in pass protection with an allowed pressure rate of 37.6 percent (per SumerSports ), however, so the Steelers also can't afford to let Daniels sit back and pick them apart in the short and intermediate areas of the field like he did against Dallas.
Daniels has shown that he can win at the NFL level, though the Steelers ’ defense is far more stout than the Cowboys’ and is better equipped to stop a Tampa Bay offense that is led by him.
The Buccaneers are more competitive than their 1-4 record would suggest, but Pittsburgh is simply the better team.
Sure, it's never easy to win on the road and Tampa Bay has some form of momentum. At the same time, the Steelers ' defense really shouldn't have many issues getting the better of Daniels while also finding some level of success on offense against a Buccaneers defense that's been really strong thus far.
If Pittsburgh really is a playoff contender in the AFC moving forward, it has to come away with wins in situations like this.

title: Aaron Rodgers Leaks Steelers WR Plan
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have decisions to make at wide receiver. With Roman Wilson out with a finger injury and Michael Pittman Jr. on Injured Reserve with a foot injury, the team has lost two starters. Ben Skowronek (calf) is set to miss Week 6, and Pittsburgh needs to figure out how to add to their depth chart.
People are talking about outside options in Brian Thomas Jr. and Tyreek Hill. The idea of a reunion with JuJu Smith-Schuster has interested some fans, and ESPN has even named five trade candidates the Steelers may be interested in.
But Aaron Rodgers has revealed their realistic plan, at least for Week 6. Speaking with media about the team's upcoming game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Rodgers was asked about the outlook at wideout, and gave love to the three players who may be filling in.
"It seems like at this point it's just in-house options," Rodgers said. "So, we’vegot a talented [practice] squad group of guys and guys who played football at the highest level and madeplays.Excited about getting those guys in. Obviously, [Tonyan] has played a lot of football and played at a high level, so I'm sure he'll get some more opportunities. [Brandon]Smith, Brandon Johnson, maybe Isaiah [Hodgins]. We'll get some guys who haven't seen a lot of time out there and expect them to play well."
Brandon Smith was impressive all summer. He caught the first pass during team drills during training camp, and immediately became the camp darling for the black and gold.
If not for an injury, he had a real chance of making the 53-man roster, and keeping him on the practice squad felt natural. He continued to make plays throughout training camp, and was expected to be the team's first call-up when needing wide receiver help this season.
At 27 years old, he's yet to record an in-game stat at the NFL level, but he'll need to with the Steelers over the next few weeks as he operates as WR3.
Brandon Johnson and Isaiah Hodgins have NFL experience. Johnson has 26 catches for 335 yards and five touchdowns throughout his career. He has one catch for nine yards with the Steelers in 2024.
Hodgins has 70 receptions for 749 yards and eight touchdowns. He's started 19 games during his NFL career, including five last year for the New York Giants.
Expect plenty of 12-personnel for Pittsburgh this weekend, trying to utilize Pat Freiermuth, Darnell Washington and Robert Tonyan more to make up for the loss of Wilson, Pittman Jr. and Skowronek.
But when it comes to who's going to play wide receiver for the Steelers these next few weeks, Rodgers has already told us.

title: Steelers Gamble on Rookie DT Paying Off
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers gambled in the sixth round of the 2026 NFL Draft. How else could you describe the decision to take defensive lineman Gabriel Rubio out of Notre Dame?
The thing about gambling, though, is that sometimes it pays off. The Steelers are learning that firsthand with Rubio.
With injuries necessitating the rookie defensive tackle's NFL debut. Rubio went out there are did exactly what was asked of him. It was a small sample size in his first NFL action, but so far the gamble on Rubio is providing an impressive return.
Rubio is a massive human being. Walking by him in the locker room is a task, because he simply takes up a ton of space. Listed at 6'5" and 321 pounds on the team's official website, he's every bit of it in person.
Having the physical gifts is one thing, but you have to match that with drive, energy, technique and a desire to get better. Rubio possesses all of that.
The 23-year-old played in just 14 defensive snaps in Week 5, but he made each one count. For starters, he recorded three assisted tackles over those 14 plays, which is already impressive.
Even with the acknowledgment that he was in the game primarily in running situations, Rubio was an active player along the line of scrimmage. He displayed a never-ending motor after the snap, allowing him to shed blocks and continue toward the ball carrier.
That's what stuck out the most to me. He was taking on solid offensive linemen, but he was able to win the point of contact and get off the blocks in enough time to be the first one or close to the ball carrier. It's a credit to his ability to utilize his lower-body strength and large frame to his advantage. He doesn't have the fastest hands, yet, but his power and agility makes up for it, even at the NFL level.
Imagine where he will be as his technical abilities improve.
One play in particular highlighted Rubio's best traits. The Colts came out in 12 personnel, which they had been running out of frequently in Week 5. This time, however, it was a play-action passing play. Rubio was engaged with the left guard at the snap, fighting for ground. The play eventually turned into a pass to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor in the flat.
Rubio kept his head up the entire time, keeping a close eye on the quarterback. As soon as he noticed the pass, Rubio smartly disengaged with the guard, tried to get his hand up to bat the ball down, and when that failed, he took off toward the ball. Steelers linebacker Payton Wilson was the first man on the ball carrier, but Rubio was second. Despite being roughly 10 to 15 yards away from the ball when Taylor caught it, he closed in and helped end the play.
The Steelers might be ready to make some changes on defense, much like they did on offense after their Week 2 loss. Perhaps it's a linebacker trade , or perhaps it's an addition to the secondary.
But what will remain is the depth up front, which has become the strongest piece of the Steelers' defense. Rubio is a key cog in the machine. As second-year lineman Derrick Harmon recovers, Rubio will continue to get a hat on game day. If he keeps playing like this, whether it's 14 or 41 snaps, he will prove his long-term value to the franchise.
For a sixth-round flyer, that's pretty impressive. Rubio might not be an All-Pro in the future, but he gives the Steelers another legitimate defensive lineman to consider in their plans for the rest of 2026 and beyond.

title: Seahawks Defensive Dominance vs. Broncos Shouldn't Be Overlooked
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are disappointed after their 17-14 loss against the Denver Broncos in Week 6, but it shouldn't take away from the dominant defensive performance they put together, especially in the second half.
While the Seahawks surrendered a pair of touchdown drives in the second quarter, they managed to hold the team scoreless throughout the second half. The field goal they gave up in overtime to end the game was largely fueled by Sam Darnold's interception , which gave Denver great field position.
Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald praised the defense after the game.
"I am really, really proud of our guys," Macdonald said postgame.
"Really, just the resolve. I think they executed a really high level for what we were asking them to do today. It's a really good offense, especially in the second half. Their offense, they did a great job. They played together, and our coaches did a great job of finding some solutions there after those two drives. So, it was great second half by those guys."
The Seahawks allowed just 168 total yards against the Broncos. Bo Nix threw for just 94 yards, while the rushing game managed only 74. For additional context, the Broncos gained just 32 yards in their final 29 plays, which is usually the ingredient for a victory. Unfortunately, the offense was not able to muster enough points to help them out.
The defense has always been the backbone of the Seahawks, and this season has proven that it will remain the same. The defense will only continue to play at a high level as offenses get more injured throughout the season and rely more on the ground game, which Seattle looks to feast upon.
The defense is why the Seahawks shouldn't worry too much about their record at this point in the season. While they already have as many losses as they did during the 2025 regular season, their defense has the tools to win a lot more games down the line.
The Seahawks are back in action in Week 7 when they take on Patrick Mahomes, Kenneth Walker III, and the Kansas City Chiefs. Kickoff is scheduled for 5:20 pm ET inside Lumen Field for Sunday Night Football.

title: 2 Reasons Why Seahawks Should Bench Sam Darnold (And 1 Reason Why They Aren't)
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are frustrated after a 17-14 loss against the Denver Broncos , where Sam Darnold threw two interceptions late in the game that ultimately cost them the victory.
Darnold has thrown seven interceptions in four games this season, which doesn't include his Week 1 drive, during which he suffered a glute injury that held him out for Week 2 against the Arizona Cardinals. Ultimately, Darnold's struggles have prompted some to call for a quarterback change, but head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed that he wouldn't be going to Drew Lock.
Here's a look at why Macdonald and the Seahawks coaching staff could be making a mistake, but also why they are sticking to their guns:
One could make the argument that the Seahawks could be 6-0 at this point in the season. The team is 3-3, with all of their losses coming by three points or less. In games like that, the smallest margins make the biggest difference, and that could be the case with Darnold's interceptions.
In each of his starts, Darnold has vowed to clean up the turnovers, but that has not happened yet. The team is losing its grasp on its spot in the standings, and a quarterback change could be what the team needs to wake the offense up.
It would be one thing if the Seahawks had an unproven backup behind Darnold who would spark something unknown. However, Lock is the quarterback the Seahawks would turn to if they did decide to move on from Darnold.
Lock proved in the first two weeks that he is capable of leading this team to victory, pulling off a comeback in Week 1, and looking like a starter in Week 2. The team ultimately has decided to keep Darnold under center, but they have a strong backup option if they were to make a change.
Ultimately, the Seahawks have struggled a lot , but Darnold is not the only reason. The offensive line struggled against the Broncos, and the run game has yet to come into its own. While Darnold is shouldering a lot of blame for the team's losses, it is far from the only thing keeping Seattle from winning these games.
Darnold has a higher ceiling than Lock, and that is ultimately why the team is keeping him in that position. The Seahawks may get desperate later on in the year if their spot in the playoffs becomes compromised, but for now, Darnold is their best option to win football games.
He just needs to take care of the football, which he has proven to do before. During the playoffs last season, Darnold never gave the ball up to the opposing team, which fueled their Super Bowl run. If he can find that energy and apply it to the 2026 season, the Seahawks could have a similar result.

title: Seahawks Get Good, Bad News Regarding Injuries
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are fresh off of a 17-14 loss to the Denver Broncos where they could have benefitted from having some of their offensive depth healthy for the game.
The team has dealt with some injuries in the first half of the season, but a few players could be nearing a return in the coming games. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald spoke with "Brock and Salk" on Seattle Sports 710 AM and provided some clarity on players' availability.
Seattle Seahawks rookie running back Jadarian Price has missed the last three games due to a chest injury, but there is reason to believe he is going to be able to come back soon because he was placed on injured reserve.
Price has to miss a minimum of four games, which means he is out for the team's Week 7 contest against the Kansas City Chiefs. The team can, however, open his 21-day window to return from injured reserve very soon. There's a good chance that Price could be available for the team's Week 8 contest on Monday Night Football against the Chicago Bears on November 2.
Bradford, the team's starting right guard, is also on injured reserve, but Week 6 marked the fourth game of his absence. This means he is eligible to return from injured reserve and move back to the 53-man roster in time for the team to take on the Chiefs. Given that the Seahawks surrendered five sacks against the Broncos, having Bradford back in the lineup will be a big boost for the team.
The Seahawks activated Charbonnet on October 1, which means he has 21 days to join the 53-man roster, giving him until October 22, next Thursday. This means he will likely be on the roster at some point ahead of the Chiefs game, but it also doesn't mean he'll be ready to go.
The team has to put him on the active roster because if they do not, he will be out for the rest of the season. Seattle could move him to the roster but keep him inactive until he is ready to come back, which could be the direction the team ends up going in.
Macdonald did not have a clear update on his status, which means not much has changed, and it didn't sound very optimistic for him to return.
Arroyo left the team's Week 6 contest with a shoulder injury, but he is continuing to get some imaging and testing done to determine how long he will be out. It's not great news for the Seahawks, who don't have a ton of tight end depth on the roster. Arroyo's status is up in the air when the team plays the Chiefs in their next game on Sunday Night Football in Week 7.

title: Seahawks Won't Bench Sam Darnold After Loss to Broncos
full_text:
Through six games, Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold isn’t writing a great sequel to his Super Bowl-winning campaign from last season.
Darnold threw two back-breaking interceptions in the fourth quarter and overtime of the Seahawks’ loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday night, giving him seven picks in essentially four games played. However, head coach Mike Macdonald is standing by his quarterback.
Macdonald was asked about potentially making a quarterback change on his weekly radio appearance with Seattle Sports’ Brock Huard and Mike Salk, and he quickly said it wouldn’t be happening.
Later, Macdonald addressed reporters and doubled down on sticking with Darnold moving forward.
Are the #Seahawks in any way considering making a change at QB? "No." HC Mike Macdonald assesses his team's quarterback situation after Seattle's week 6 loss vs the Broncos on w/ @BrockHuard & @TheMikeSalk pic.twitter.com/GCyCSGUgPe
“I think we have a lot of faith in Sam,” Macdonald said. “Sam’s played great football for us. He’s done a lot of great things this year. We’ve obviously turned the ball over way more than we want to. I feel like there’s things on our end that can help him play better football, and I think he’s definitely part of the solution rather than the opposite.”
Macdonald said there’s a “sense of urgency” to improve in multiple areas, and especially on offense. The coaching staff is optimistic it can find solutions to the issues and help Darnold succeed.
“We just won a world championship with him. We believe in the guy; we see him every day, we see what he does, we see the plays that he’s been able to make, we see the actual talent. All those things. That’s where my mind is.”
Drew Lock essentially made three starts for the Seahawks when Darnold suffered a glute injury on the first drive of the season against the New England Patriots. Lock completed 72.9 of his 48 pass attempts for 422 yards, four touchdowns and zero interceptions.
Seattle is 1-3 since Darnold returned, largely because his interceptions have come at critical junctions in the game when Seattle has an opportunity to win the game. It’s hard not to look at the two sample sizes and wonder if the offense would perform better with Lock under center.
Macdonald, while acknowledging that Lock is a potential starting-caliber backup, shot down the idea that it’s as simple as a quarterback issue.
“I don’t think that’s doing the whole thing justice; there’s definitely more to the equation … I understand the question, but I think there’s more to it than just who’s playing quarterback,” Macdonald said.
Darnold will try to prevent the Seahawks from falling to 3-4 when they face the Kansas City Chiefs at 5:20 p.m. on Sunday, Oct. 25, at Lumen Field.

title: Should Seahawks Bench Sam Darnold? Seattle Legend Says Yes
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are losers of three of their last four games, including a 17-14 overtime loss at the hands of the Denver Broncos in Week 6.
The Seahawks had a chance to win, much like their other two losses, but two costly Sam Darnold interceptions in the fourth quarter and overtime led to the loss. With Darnold throwing seven interceptions in his last four games, it begs the question whether the team would be better with someone else, including backup Drew Lock.
Bruce Irvin, who won a Super Bowl with the Seahawks in 2013, wants Lock in at quarterback over Darnold.
There is a timeline in which the Seahawks could be 6-0, which would be their greatest start in franchise history. Still, they have lost three of their last four games by a combined eight points, which should be frustrating for a defense that is performing at a very high level. The Seahawks gave up just 168 total yards of offense against the Broncos, yet they were still unable to pull out a win. If the Seahawks had more consistent quarterback play, these losses would turn into wins.
After Darnold suffered an injury during the team's season opener against the New England Patriots, Lock stepped in and did what he needed to do. In his first game with the Seahawks, he completed 16 of 22 passes for 187 yards and a touchdown. Most importantly, he did not throw an interception.
The following week against the Arizona Cardinals, he also played extremely well, completing 19 of 26 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns while also not turning the ball over.
Seattle doesn't need a wow factor at the quarterback position. Last year was full evidence of that. They just need someone who can keep the ball in Seattle's hands and kill the clock. With the running game not as consistent as it was last season, the importance of the quarterback not turning the ball over becomes that much more crucial.
Unfortunately for the Seahawks, they haven't gotten that level of play from Darnold this season, but they have gotten it from Lock.
I believe when the Seahawks play the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football in Week 7, Darnold will be under center. It's hard to bench a Super Bowl-winning quarterback just a handful of games into the following season. Darnold has the ability to clean up this mess, but after several consistent weeks of the same mistakes being made, it does beg the question of whether his job is fully safe or not.

title: Hanich Panic Meter: The Super Bowl Hangover Is Real and Its Bad
full_text:
Thursday Night Football was a chance for the Seattle Seahawks to rebound from their disastrous play through the previous three weeks and get it together. While facing the Denver Broncos on the road is a tough setting, there is a tougher opponent than themselves as the Seahawks lose 17-14 in overtime.
​This game didn’t just show that Seattle didn’t get out of their recent sloppy play ; they are living in it. There is no denying it; the Seahawks are officially in a Super Bowl hangover and, perhaps, some tough decisions might have to be made.
​Head coach Mike Macdonald made a lot of promises through the last few weeks. Between being more in sync on offense, playing with more intensity, being smart in decision-making and avoiding turnovers, the only promise made was about turnovers, up until two crucial interceptions thrown by quarterback Sam Darnold.
​Seattle’s Dark Side Defense was bullied in the Broncos’ second and third drive of the game. They couldn’t get off the field on third downs and the defensive line was getting dominated. Offensively, there was too much pressure allowed from the offensive line and they barely got any push at the line of scrimmage. When Velus Jones Jr. had solid runs, the Seahawks went away from him and went back to Emanuel Wilson and George Holani .
​This Seahawks team is too inconsistent with their decisions. They are prone to staying with the same excuses and the same players that make mistakes. The Seahawks have now lost three of the last four games due to turnovers , and the team is implying that changes will be made, but never do.
​Oftentimes, it is okay to admit that changes can save a team. The Seahawks are not out of contention, but the more certain decisions remain that will cost the team, the more difficult it will be for them to even get back into the playoffs rather than contend for a repeat.
​There are many factors that indicate how Seattle turns a 3-3 team back into a contender. The Seahawks have to improve their offensive line after allowing five sacks. Right tackle Abraham Lucas and right guard Grey Zabel have regressed significantly and need to be reconditioned. The Seahawks could make an immediate trade for a reliable starting center.
​The Seahawks’ defense needs more impact at the line of scrimmage. Outside of Leonard Williams and Byron Murphy II, there wasn’t a lot of push. They were dominated at times against the Broncos’ offensive line. Seattle could make a trade for a much more impactful edge rusher.
​Ultimately, the biggest change might have to be at the quarterback position. Even if it is temporarily, Darnold needs to sit. He is literally throwing away the Seahawks’ chances to win games . Seven interceptions in the last four games are cause for the Seahawks to make a change. He has thrown 27 interceptions in the 21 games (not counting the first series played in Week 1 versus the New England Patriots) in his time as a Seahawk.
​Even if he isn’t the answer, veteran Drew Lock needs a chance to show he can not give the ball away for the Seahawks. Darnold proved he was a capable quarterback last season because he either helped the team overcome some of his mistakes or he prevented turnovers altogether. Now, Darnold has become a liability. Although his team will never admit it, they know his turnovers are dooming the team.
​Darnold is showing that he doesn’t deserve a wealthy contract extension, but he doesn’t deserve to be the franchise quarterback. It doesn’t help that an inexperienced offensive coordinator Brian Fleury is trying to lead and coach the offense. The Seahawks won’t likely switch to Lock or another quarterback via trade, but they should.

title: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold Calls Turnovers 'BS', Vows to Improve
full_text:
Another multi-interception performance by Sam Darnold stood out in the Seattle Seahawks’ primetime 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday, particularly because of when they occurred.
Darnold’s two picks came in the fourth quarter and overtime, and both were on drives where the Seahawks had a chance to take the lead. As they have all season, the Seattle defense silenced the Broncos, but the turnovers sank them.
“No way to sugarcoat it; that one sucked,” Darnold told reporters after the game . “I can’t turn the ball over. That’s obviously at the forefront of my mind, but there’s just a lot we can do better … We’ve just got to be better all-around, and that starts with me.”
Darnold now has seven touchdowns and seven interceptions in essentially four games played. He only threw two passes in Week 1 before suffering his glute injury that held him out the rest of the game and the following two.
Turnovers have held back an already-struggling offense that seldom generates a run game and can’t consistently score. If it doesn’t get cleaned up, the Seahawks won’t remotely rival their excellence in 2025.
“It wasn’t a performance that was good enough to win the game — by our team,” Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said. “But our quarterback leads the team, and I bet you Sam will be the first one to tell you that, but that’s just what it is.”
There are no two ways around it: Darnold and the offense lost the Seahawks the game. Following their second-quarter touchdown drives of 74 and 79 yards, the Broncos punted on seven straight drives outside of at the end of the first and second halves. They kneeled out the clock on those possessions.
Macdonald said Darnold owned the loss. Darnold was asked why it was important he do that for the team.
“I just think it’s BS for me to keep turning the ball over, and it’s not fair to our defense, not fair to our special teams group, not fair really to the entire team,” Darnold added. “So, I’ve got to be better that way.”
Seattle outgained Denver 353-168, but was doomed by Darnold’s untimely interceptions. The Broncos totaled just 25 yards of offense in the second half and only needed eight yards on their lone overtime possession to kick the game-winning field goal.
Darnold struggled most of the game, but the Seahawks made it 14-11 with 5:41 left in the game after an 11-play, 67-yard touchdown drive. The Seattle defense forced another three-and-out, setting the offense up with a prime opportunity to score a go-ahead touchdown.
On the fifth play of the Seahawks’ next drive, Darnold threw a bad interception to Broncos cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine. But the defense still held up with another three-and-out stop.
KRIS ABRAMS-DRAINE PICKS OFF SAM DARNOLD 🤯 #TNFonPrime pic.twitter.com/Ss0BoN4EYo
After forcing overtime and receiving the ball, Darnold sunk the Seahawks by giving the Broncos the ball on Seattle’s 43-yard line. It was another pick, this time into triple coverage. Denver won it four plays later.
“I think he’s trying to throw a hole shot in cover two, and we’ll look at what they were playing and how they made the play. But we have to take care of the ball,” Macdonald said. “Sam knows that; he told the team that. Gotta take care of the ball.”
The Seahawks, now sitting at 3-3 after losing three of their last four games, have a mini bye week before returning home to face the Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) at 5:20 p.m. on Sunday, Oct. 25, at Lumen Field.

title: 3 Observations as Sam Darnold, Seahawks Lose vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are losers of consecutive games for the first time in nearly two years after falling to the Denver Broncos 17-14 in an overtime matchup on Thursday Night Football.
The Seahawks trailed 14-3 for most of the game, but a touchdown from running back George Holani, a two-point conversion from Rashid Shaheed, and a field goal from Jason Myers in the final seconds of the game tied it up and sent it to overtime.
Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold threw two interceptions, including one in overtime that set the Broncos up in field goal range, leading to a Will Lutz 53-yard field goal to finish the game. Here's a look at the three observations from the game.
Darnold continues to struggle with taking care of the football. A pair of key interceptions during the game ultimately cost the Seahawks a victory. The Seahawks are 3-3, but they could easily be 6-0 if Darnold wasn't out here throwing interceptions.
The first one came late in the fourth quarter, inside the two-minute warning, when Seattle could have gone on a game-winning touchdown drive. The pick from Kris Abrams-Drain would have solidified the win for the Broncos, but they could not get a first down. That led to Seattle receiving the ball once more with little time left.
While Darnold was able to get the Seahawks into field goal range, all of that went into the trash bin when he threw another pick to Ja'Quan McMillian in overtime.
Simply put, this game was lost because Darnold was not taking care of the football. In a game where the Seahawks outgained the Broncos 353-168, they should have win, but they don't get the tally in the win column.
For three and a half quarters, the Seahawks' offense looked lifeless, and it wasn't just Darnold contributing to that. The offensive line put Darnold in uncomfortable situations throughout the evening. The team was unable to generate much rhythm on offense, and it starts in the trenches.
The Seahawks' offensive line has been up and down over the years, but last year they found some success, which ultimately made a massive difference. The offensive line plays such an important role on the team that if it is not performing at a championship level, this team is not a contender.
If there's any solace in tonight's loss, it's that the defense continues to play at an elite level. While they surrendered a pair of touchdown drives in the second quarter, most teams win football games when they only allow 17 points.
That wasn't the case tonight for the Seahawks, but they put the team in a position to win. Unfortunately, the offense didn't have their back, but there were some strong defensive plays all night long, even without any turnovers.
This team remains a defensive juggernaut and it can be a contender with this unit, but they may need to pick up even more of the slack if the Seahawks want to return to their winning ways.

title: 4 Winners & 2 Losers From Seahawks Frustrating OT Loss vs. Broncos
full_text:
The uniform matchup between the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos on Thursday Night Football was easily the best of the season thus far. Both teams wore their throwbacks, reminding old-school fans of their time as AFC West rivals. Seattle was in that division from 1977-2001 and sported the royal blue jerseys from that era Thursday, while the Broncos had their orange crush look.
The game itself was a throwback as well, with both defenses playing lights out. The Broncos had a 14-3 lead at the half, but the Seahawks fought back, scoring 11 in the fourth quarter to send the game to overtime.
Once in the extra period, the Seahawks had the ball first but an interception from Sam Darnold set the Broncos up for the win. With this one in the books, let's see who stood out as winners and losers in the Week 6 loss.
A fumble in the first half from Rashid Shaheed cost Seattle points, but he was able to make up for it after that. Not only did he haul in a 42-yard reception to give the offense a spark in the second half, but he also made a beautiful catch on a two-point conversion in the fourth quarter to make it a 14-11 game.
Shaheed then set the offense up to tie the game when he had a 31-yard punt return with less than a minute to play. He also had a key reception on their final drive in regulation, picking up 10 yards on third-and-six.
Sam Darnold struggled in this game as the Denver defense had his number. While we knew the Broncos would make things difficult, Darnold was rattled by the pass rush and didn't do a good job avoiding pressure throughout the night.
The @Broncos defense get back-to-back sacks to close out the opening drive SEAvsDEN on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NRDh4ZbGVA
Darnold made several plays in the final quarter, but also had a late interception that could have cost them the game in regulation. He then threw another in overtime, which gave the Broncos the ball on the edge of field-goal range. Those picks will be a hot topic, especially since it was a problem for Darnold coming into the game.
Nick Emmanwori is healthy again. The second-year safety had ankle surgery in July and missed their Week1 win over the Patriots. He returned in Week 2 and eased his way back in over the next couple of weeks. On Thursday, he looked like the chess piece we remember from 2025.
Emmanwori was lined up all over the defense, playing safety, slot, and linebacker. He was even used as a pass rusher on multiple snaps, including a key third-down play in the fourth quarter. On that play, Emmanwori sacked Bo Nix, forcing the Broncos to punt following a three-and-out immediately after the Seahawks cut the lead to three.
While some of the sacks in this one were due to Darnold being unable to escape pressure, the fact remains that he was under pressure all night. It was hard to pinpoint any single offensive lineman as the one who struggled most, because the pressure was coming from everywhere. This was the second week in a row where Darnold was sacked at least five times and it's become a major issue.
The Seahawks finally got into the end zone more than halfway through the fourth quarter, and it was George Holani who scored the touchdown. What was most impressive was that he had consecutive impressive runs, beginning with a 13-yarder which included the offensive line helping to push him closer to the end zone.
George Holani gets in the end zone for the @Seahawks SEAvsDEN on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MzSqMm3DVs
He was finally taken down at the one-yard line and scored on the next play. This time, he avoided a tackle in the backfield and got into the end zone, which allowed the Seahawks to cut the lead to 14-11. Of course, the turnover by Darnold on the following drive doomed them, but Holani deserves credit for giving them a chance.
Throughout the night, the Seattle offense was sleepwalking. That wasn't the case with Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who was once again their best weapon. JSN had 134 yards on 12 receptions, which wasn't enough to salvage the win, but was a reminder that he's one of the most dominant wide receivers in the NFL.

title: Elijah Arroyo Injury Update: Seahawks Tight End Leaves Late In Second Quarter
full_text:
It was about as bad a first half as you could have for the Seattle Seahawks, and it just got worse. With time running down towards the end of the first half, on a play where the Seahawks lost a fumble as well, they also may have lost Elijah Arroyo. Going down to dive on the ball, his arm was caught in a scrum and has gotten injured.
He was seen being led into the locker room with team staff holding his forearm, indicating an injury in that area. Not clearly related to the knee injury he had last season that placed him on IR late in the season, but its significance is to be determined. With the score 14-3 and Seattle trying to salvage some points before the half, nothing is going the way of the Seahawks tonight.
A few minutes later, he was declared by the Seahawks to be doubtful to return with a shoulder injury. All things considered, I can only assume he's not coming back today. Seattle has much bigger issues than their second string (at best) tight end, of course, but he remains a playmaker of note even if the team hasn't been able to unlock his abilities and potential yet.
The Seahawks actually had four tight ends active for this game anyway, five if you count Brady Russell, so I can't say there will be a massive impact from this. Arroyo is a complete afterthought in this offense for the time being. If anything, adding better blockers like Eric Saubert and Nick Kallerup to the mix might be more beneficial to this current situation.
Seattle needs to find a way to get into better situations on 2nd and 3rd down so they can sustain drives and give Darnold easier throws to convert. Arroyo, in theory, could help with that, but clearly the team hasn't figured that part out yet. And with the distinct possibility that he misses extended time given how quickly he was declared doubtful, that may not change.
Arroyo came into tonight's game having been targetted on only two passes this year, one a 17-yarder from Drew Lock and the other intercepted by the trailing defender. He's seen less than 30% of the total snaps. Eric Saubert has actually been on the field more than Arroyo, and despite his player profile has made more of an impact as a pass catcher. Onward.

title: The Most Impressive Part About the 49ers’ 5-0 Start
full_text:
Seeing the San Francisco 49ers open up the season with five straight wins is nothing short of impressive.
Now, they were expected to be a good team this season, but anytime you start off the year 5-0, especially notching a win over the Seattle Seahawks , who whooped the 49ers the last two times, it deserves applause.
It’s not just the wins that are awesome to see; it’s how the 49ers are doing. Brock Purdy is playing very sharp, along with Mike Evans , and the 49ers’ defense under Raheem Morris has been lights-out.
However, it’s not the most impressive part of their 5-0 start.
They haven’t needed to rely on Christian McCaffrey. Last year, the 49ers were McCaffrey or bust. They might as well have renamed themselves the San Francisco McCaffreys at that point.
That’s how heavy and insane his usage was, but it was also incredible, even if he wasn’t efficient. Without McCaffrey, it’s unlikely the 49ers make it to the playoffs.
Deviating from a player who’s been the star of the offense is risky and easier said than done, but the 49ers knew they couldn’t replicate his workload in 2026. Not even close to it.
During the offseason, Kyle Shanahan pointed out that the 49ers need to help him out. He’s said that before in previous offseasons, so it was tough to fully take stock of his words.
However, unlike in previous offseasons, McCaffrey wasn’t coming off unreal usage. He’s also not the same player he was in 2023 when he won the Offensive Player of the Year award.
That played a role in the running game’s ineffectiveness last year. Shanahan knows that, which led them to draft Kaelon Black. The rookie has done a solid job of filling in for McCaffrey in spurts.
But Black isn’t the only one helping McCaffrey out. Purdy is doing his part as well. Shanahan is dialing up more passing plays than in previous years.
Their passing game has been more responsible for how great their offense is clicking than the running game. They’re relying more on Purdy and his receivers than on McCaffrey.
It's a surprising yet magnificent sight to see. The best part of it all is that it preserves McCaffrey for when the 49ers need to use him heavily late in the season.
Shanahan surely has that card ready to use when the need arises. Until then, their offense is operating soundly with their newfound identity.

title: One 49ers Player is an Afterthought Despite Impressive Debut
full_text:
With injuries thinning out their wide receiver depth , the San Francisco 49ers have needed their young players to step up.
One player who did that well in Week 3 against the Arizona Cardinals was Jordan Watkins. He caught two explosive passes for 60 yards in his season debut.
He was also blocking amazingly well. That game raised Watkins' stock, and it should've earned him more playing time with the 49ers dealing with injuries.
However, Watkins has been a ghost despite his impressive debut. He hasn't registered a single catch, and that's because he isn't being targeted. Watkins is an afterthought in the 49ers' offense, but if you ask Kyle Shanahan, he doesn't think so.
“He's just gotten more opportunities since his injuries and keep doing what he's doing," Shanahan said. "Guys just run routes and sometimes the ball goes to them, sometimes it doesn't. His opportunity percentages go up with the guys that have been hurt. He was backing up Deebo last week and Mike at times. We had Cooks doing the same. But, when guys go out, you get more opportunities.”
Shanahan is correct that the ball sometimes goes to a receiver and sometimes it doesn't. The thing is, he's the head coach and the offensive play caller.
If he wants Watkins involved, it will happen. One way he can help Watkins be featured more is by having him run more routes. Against the Seattle Seahawks, Watkins only ran eight routes.
Meanwhile, Brandin Cooks, who only just arrived less than a few weeks ago, ran 12. It's clear that Watkins isn't a player that Shanahan wants to use.
In hindsight, maybe Watkins' involvement against the Cardinals was for Shanahan to see how he would respond after he approached Shanahan about playing more.
It's not like he failed that test. Otherwise, Shanahan wouldn't have spoken so highly of him. Even now, Shanahan still speaks highly of Watkins.
"We've been really happy with how he's played in these games. I think he's earned a lot of respect in these three games and with us it doesn't have to do with the stats. I know he's had two catches and stuff in his first game, and those are two really good plays, but because he hasn't had any in the other two games doesn't really mean much to us."
It seems like the only way Watkins will see opportunities with the ball again is if the 49ers are desperate at wide receiver. You'd think that would be the case now with Deebo Samuel out .
But that doesn't appear to be the case. I wouldn't bank on much involvement as a pass catcher from Watkins anytime soon, if at all, this season.

title: Why 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan is Surprised About Brock Purdy and Mike Evans' Connection
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers’ quarterback-wide receiver partnership of Brock Purdy and Mike Evans has taken the NFL by storm.
Five games into the season, FOX Sports reports Purdy has completed 24 of 34 passes targeting Evans this season for 406 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions.
Purdy has a 149.9 passer rating when targeting Evans , the highest among the 55 QB-receiver duos with at least 25 attempts this season.
This prompted a question to the 49ers' head coach, Kyle Shanahan, about whether he's surprised by that instant success. He gave an interesting response.
“Yeah, a little bit. I mean, yes and no," he told reporters on Thursday .
"Mike has been so obviously that good to anybody who watches him and especially to me watching him over the years. He’s always been right there as the best and some people can match with him, but he’s just such a first-ballot Hall of Famer.
"To get him here, just things that we weren’t used to doing as much not having a guy like him. I remember always telling Brock and stuff like, ‘Hey, there’s times you’re just going to sit there and wait and Mike will get it done. You don’t need to progress even if your feet tell you to. If the coverage doesn’t go there, you just wait and give him time because he’ll come down with it.’
"I remember saying to him a ton like, ‘This can be really important that you two have a lot of one-on-one. You guys do that stuff a lot because that’s just about you guys talking to each other.’
"Each one’s going to be different. It’s not like coach talk and telling you, ‘Hey, it’s going to be at this yard line or this hitch.’ It’s stuff you guys have just got to get used to each other.
"I remember going up to Brock in the middle of Australia. I was like, ‘Hey, all that stuff I asked you to work with Mike, are you guys there yet? Are you good?’ I did that jokingly because I knew Mike hadn’t had any reps in like two weeks and Brock got all stressed. He’s like, ‘Well, I haven’t got to yet.’ And I was like, ‘I’m just joking, dude.’ I was like, like, ‘We’ve ran out of time. We’ll see how it goes this week.’
"That fade they threw in Australia that they scored on, I think we had done that full speed once live and that’s just a different drop and different stuff that we hadn’t done.
"So those guys didn’t get a ton of reps out of it, but it just shows how natural Mike is, how natural Brock is, and that it seems like they’ve been working on that stuff for a long time.”

title: 49ers Coach Sounds Off on Mykel Williams' Debut
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers' former first-round pick Mykel Williams made his 2026 debut after tearing his ACL to end his rookie season. Williams only played 36% of the defensive snaps with 23 snaps overall. Head coach Kyle Shanahan noted that while Williams did not flash, he did show them what they wanted to see fresh off the injury.
"Yeah, that was our goal to get him around that area," Shanahan said of playing Williams just 23 snaps. "I thought he did a real good job. It was a real good first game back. He didn't have any bad plays.”
Williams had two tackles and added one pressure, according to PFF.
"He had two good plays of sniffing out a screen twice,” added Shanahan. “I thought he had a real good first step for him coming back."
The question now is how much more will the team put on Williams' plate in Week 6? They did not use him much in his versatile role sliding inside on pass-rushing downs. He played on early downs and then would come off the field for sub-package football.
In 2025, the 49ers aligned Williams along the interior defensive line for 54 snaps. That was a 14% rate. In Week 5, he did not have any snaps along the interior. This is where he had his best work as a pass rusher, so the thought is that the 49ers will start to get him mixed in more often.
The next question is how much this means for the 49ers' edge rusher room. They are expected to get Nick Bosa back in the next week or two as well. Williams should be closer to a full-time player in the next two weeks.
So, the 49ers will have two starters locked in. Rookie third-round pick Romello Height has been taking on a bigger role with those two sidelined. It has been a lot to ask of him, but if he can shift into the third edge rusher and just rush on passing downs, he could become more valuable thanks to the experience he gained.
San Francisco also has Keion White, who can serve as a solid fourth option in a rotation. On one hand, this is all in theory, and none of it has come together.  On the other hand, there is a chance this room can become a strength by Week 10.

title: Why 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan has Struggled vs. Commanders HC Dan Quinn
full_text:
After their defeat to the New England Patriots in Super Bowl LI, the careers of then Atlanta Falcons offensive coordinator Kyle Shanahan and head coach Dan Quinn have gone in rather different directions.
Now in his tenth season as the head coach of the San Francisco 49ers, Shanahan has led his team to two NFC West titles, four NFC championship games and two Super Bowl appearances.
But for Quinn, the defensive-minded coach has had to go through the NFL coaching cycle. He was fired as Falcons head coach midway through the 2020 regular season. His Atlanta squad started out 0-5 and now 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris was named the interim head coach after Quinn was let go.
Quinn found his next role quickly, spending the next three seasons as the defensive coordinator for the Dallas Cowboys and being voted the Assistant Coach of the Year in 2021. Prior to Shanahan and the 49ers taking on the Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl LVIII, Quinn was named head coach of the Washington Commanders.
“I’m so pumped for Dan, I’m so pumped for Washington,” Shanahan said at Super Bowl LVIII Opening Night. “Dan’s a hell of a coach, they got a hell of a one… Dan taught me so much in Atlanta, I’m very grateful for how much he’s helped my career…”
Shanahan’s tenure alongside Quinn in Atlanta lasted just two years but it catapulted his coaching career following their Super Bowl run and directing Matt Ryan to a Most Valuable Player award in 2016.
The Week 6 matchup between Washington and San Francisco will be the fifth time that the two will square off since their split and the first since Quinn has been the head coach of the Commanders.
Here is a recap of the prior four games:
2019 Week 15, Falcons 29-22 win vs. San Francisco
Quinn’s lone win came in their first-ever meeting. Already eliminated from playoff contention, the Falcons put up 19 points in the fourth quarter and outscored the 49ers by ten to steal a win.
The Atlanta defense forced four fumbles but only two were recovered. George Kittle had 13 catches on 17 targets for 134 yards.
Despite the loss, the 49ers still clinched a playoff spot after the Los Angeles Rams loss to the Cowboys. Julio Jones’ 5-yard goal-line touchdown to give Atlanta a one-point lead with two seconds left has been forgotten thanks to Dre Greenlaw’s goal-line stop of Jacob Hollister in Week 17.
2021 NFC Wild Card, 49ers 23-17 win vs. Dallas
Shanahan got his revenge, ending Quinn and his seventh-ranked defense in the 2021 NFC Wild Card. Deebo Samuel was in the midst of the best four-game stretch of his career, accounting for 110 yards on 13 touches. Samuel’s 26-yard touchdown run following a K’Waun Williams interception of Dak Prescott proved to be the game-winner.
On offense, Jimmy Garoppolo finished with 172 passing yards, but Shanahan ultimately took the ball out of his hands with the running game finishing with 169 yards on 38 attempts.
A late comeback from Dallas was not enough as time ran out on the final possession of the game, similar to Jayden Daniels this past week for Washington in overtime.
2022 NFC Divisional, 49ers 19-12 win vs. Dallas
The two met again in the playoff for a second straight year, and again it was Shanahan coming out on top. With Brock Purdy now at quarterback, San Francisco didn’t find the end zone until the first play of the fourth quarter, which was a 2-yard run by Christian McCaffrey.
Quinn’s defense generated two sacks, but San Francisco’s two interceptions off Prescott flipped things as one resulted in a Robbie Gould field goal and one ended a Dallas drive that reached the red zone.
2023 Week 5, 49ers 42-10 win vs. Dallas
Shanahan’s best performance against his former fellow coach came in a Sunday night thumping.
Purdy threw for four touchdowns, finding Kittle for three of them. McCaffrey was bottled up on the ground, averaging just 2.7 yards on 19 carries. He did rush for a touchdown, as did his backup, Jordan Mason, who finished with 69 yards on 10 carries.
The result put the 49ers at 5-0, tied with the Eagles for the best record in the NFC.
In the four games against Quinn, Shanahan and his offense is averaging 26.5 points and 346.7 yards per game. While a majority of this came against a Dallas defense that boasted Trevon Diggs, Micah Parsons and DeMarcus Lawrence, Shanahan has shown that no matter the defensive playmakers that Quinn has at his disposal, he can still move the ball and find the end zone.
Quinn, alongside defensive coordinator and playcaller Daronte Jones, has yet to find their footing so far in 2026, ranking 23rd in total defense (350.4 yds/g) throughout the first five weeks of the regular season.
Shanahan has the 49ers offense ranked ninth in total offense (365 yds/g), but as the team is down multiple wide receivers heading into Monday night’s showdown, we’ll have to see if the 49ers head coach can find similar success against the man he shared two seasons with on the sideline.

title: All Eyes Are Now on This 49ers WR Returning From Injury
full_text:
It's Week 5 and the San Francisco 49ers have many injuries on offense.
Deebo Samuel hurt his hamstring in Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks. Jake Tonges will miss the whole season because of a torn MCL he picked up in Week 1. Demarcus Robinson's ankle sprain in Week 2 means he will miss up to 6 games, maybe more.
Rookie De'Zhaun Stribling suffered a left ankle deltoid ligament sprain/rupture and will be back at the end of November/early December.
They desperately need bodies. Regardless of how severe these injuries are, the 49ers are still 5-0 for the season. All things considered, it's very impressive, but it doesn't change the fact that they are relying too much on their older veterans.
Christian Kirk's return should be intriguing. The 49ers have opened the practice window after battling a calf injury.
Kirk arrived in free agency on an incredibly cheap deal considering his career stats, but it couldn't have been a worse start to the San Francisco life after picking up his injury on the very first day of training camp.
"Just felt like I kind of got over that hump and feeling like myself again," Kirk said to 49erswebzone . "Body starting to respond to just the training and the recovery and whatnot.
"And so, just wanted to communicate that to them, and tell them that I was ready to go, and get back out there.
"So, excited to get out there. It's obviously been a while, and just ready to attack this week."
Kirk has yet to play a snap or be integrated into Kyle Shanahan's offense, but he believes his experience will help him adapt quickly.
"I think it's like riding a bike," Kirk said. "I've been doing it for a while, and so, for me, it's just getting back out there, getting integrated with the guys. Obviously, it's been hard not being out there, but been really cool to watch day in and day out how this team comes to work every single day, and for it to be able to carry over on Sundays.
"I'm just excited, like I said, to get in the mix, and hopefully, provide some other production to help us win some more games."
Kirk will need to step up and help ease the pressure on San Francisco's remaining receiving options. Although his return date remains uncertain, don't rush him because his importance to the 49ers is growing as injuries leave the team dangerously thin at wide receiver.

title: 49ers Coach Explains Significant Schematic Shift Under Raheem Morris
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers made a pretty dramatic change from Robert Saleh as the team's defensive coordinator to Raheem Morris. While the shift is from one current NFL head coach to a former NFL head coach, head coach Kyle Shanahan admitted that the change goes much deeper than that. So far, it has led to immense success.
The 49ers did not just change from Saleh to Morris; they went from a 4-3 defense with a cover-3 principle to a 3-4 look with more versatile schemes on the back end.
Shanahan admitted that from Saleh, who was in San Francisco from 2017-2020, to DeMeco Ryans, Steve Wilks, Nick Sorensen, and then back to Saleh last year, the scheme has remained relatively the same. Morris is the first real change from that dynamic.
“It has to do with different schemes,” admitted Shanahan. “When you play our true three-deep, four under that we played for nine years with true zone drops instead of match drops and our type of two shells and stuff, you get used to who is supposed to stop plays.”
Kyle Shanahan explains the differences in the 49ers scheme from the previous coordinators to Raheem Morris and why it's making the DBs naturally more aggressive. pic.twitter.com/Dt45MGRpKu
Shanahan noted that when teams play the 49ers, they expect a specific type of defense, and they come in with a game plan. He noted that with Morris, teams do not have that same comfort, which is making him much more valuable.
Notable differences include playing base defense more. They use a third linebacker almost twice as often as they did with Saleh last season.
They have also moved Deommodore Lenoir into the slot more often to play dime with an extra cornerback rather than a safety. Lenoir had nine snaps in the slot with Saleh. He has 20 snaps in the slot through five weeks.
Beyond that, they have already played more dime in 2026 than they did in all of 2025. The 49ers have also seen their blitz rate improve. They blitzed 18% of the time last year, and now they send an extra rusher on 24% of their snaps. Some of that is because they utilize five-man fronts more than Saleh did.
The 49ers went through major injury issues with both coordinators. Still, right now the 49ers defense looks like it could be taking another step as they continue to grow in this defense. The decision Shanahan made to switch things up is paying off in a big way.

title: 49ers Have Bigger Problem Than Pass Rush at Deadline
full_text:
As the San Francisco 49ers get closer to the trade deadline , there are going to be many suggestions for the team to add a pass rusher. However, as the days get closer to the deadline, it is becoming clearer that the run defense is the area San Francisco must pay attention to.
The 49ers edge rusher room entered the year thin. However, they just got Mykel Williams back, and they are expected to see Nick Bosa in the lineup any week. In the time that those two were out, they were able to get rookie Romello Height some experience. With Keion White in the mix, they could be set here.
The issue is run defense, particularly along the interior. Osa Odighizuwa and Gracen Halton lead the 49ers in snaps on the interior. They are both much better as pass rushers than run defenders. Odighizuwa has a 66 pass rush grade and 32 run defense grade, per PFF. Halton is at 72 in pass rush grade and 53 in run defense.
Whether the grades are entirely accurate, they do represent the difference in play. The two interior linemen who were supposed to be run defenders were C.J. West and Alfred Collins. Those two are on the IR.
So far, the 49ers have not had to pay for this. They have been able to gain leads, and teams have to shift away from the run.
That is why they rank 4th in run defense according to EPA/play but 24th in success rate. On a down-by-down basis, the team is giving up yards. However, it is not costing them overall because teams cannot lean on it, and they are not allowing big plays, thanks to Fred Warner and the back end.
Still, they rank 24th in success rate despite not facing a rushing attack in the top 15 so far this season. That includes the Rams, who have improved, but trailed against San Francisco and veered away from the running game.
Miami, Seattle, Denver, and Arizona have all had problems in their run game for one reason or another. At some point, the team is going to face a team that is able to move the ball and stick to running the ball against the 49ers. Until then, the 49ers will try to find a solution on the front line.

title: 49ers Have New Reason to Pass on WR Trade
full_text:
One of the positions that is most tied to the San Francisco 49ers in trade talks is wide receiver. The team has been linked to aging options, rentals, and long-term options. However, while the room looks thin right now, it might not be a position the team needs to address.
The  49ers just opened the 21-day practice window for wide receiver Christian Kirk. Kirk has been on the PUP since the start of training camp, but when he is healthy, he is still a reliable wideout. The team is just a couple of weeks away from activating him.
Demarcus Robinson suffered an ankle injury in Week 2. He is expected to have his practice window opened in the next week or two. So, Kirk could be back by Week 7, and Robinson as soon as Week 8.
Deebo Samuel is out now, but is only expected to miss a couple of weeks. A return before Week 10 is likely. Lastly, the expected return date for De’Zhaun Stribling is around Week 12.
By the time the 49ers leave the Thanksgiving weekend of football, they might have a healthy wide receiver room. That is still a ways away, but the team is sitting at 5-0. They are not planning to lose, but they do realize that even if they did lose a few games, they would get to Week 12 with a record that has them firmly in the mix.
If they went 3-3 over the next six games while their wide receiver corps is banged up, they will be 8-3 and will be getting healthy at the right time. Considering the 5-0 start, 3-3 sounds like a worst-case scenario for this team.
As things stand, the room looks questionable at best. However, if they are sitting at 8-3 or better and have Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, De’Zhaun Stribling, Demarcus Robinson, and Christian Kirk, it will look like one of the best rooms in the NFL.
Staying patient, letting each receiver come back on their timeline, and having the room at full strength for the playoffs is the 49ers' top priority. With all of the risks for re-injury, it would not be out of the question for the 49ers to trade for a wide receiver.
At the same time, if the 49ers stay firm and lean on their depth at receiver it could be better than they realize.

title: 49ers WR Mike Evans Misses Week 6 Practice With New Injury
full_text:
49ers star wide receiver Mike Evans is being held out of the first Week 6 practice with a new injury. Along with his rib fracture, Kyle Shanahan revealed that Evans is out with an Achilles injury.
Shanahan said Evans was dealing with soreness and that there isn't any significant concern about it. However, anytime you hear Achilles being associated with a player, it's difficult not to worry.
Evans is coming off a big-time performance with big-time usage against the Seahawks. He's four days removed from the game. Yet he's still feeling soreness in his Achilles.
It's smart of the 49ers to hold out on Evans, which they'd probably do anyway since he has a rib injury. But now that he has an Achilles issue, it's something to keep a close eye on.
I'd guess the 49ers will keep Evans out of practice on Friday as well, then let him on the field on Saturday in a limited capacity.
That said, if Evans continues to feel soreness in his Achilles in a few days, they shouldn't play him against the Commanders on Monday night. It would be reckless of them to allow him to play.
An Achilles injury is no joke. I'm sure Evans will think he's good to go, but this is a case of protecting the player for himself. It doesn't matter if the 49ers are thin at wide receiver.
There's never a desperate enough scenario in a regular-season game for a player to tough out an Achilles issue. Saturday will be the biggest indicator of where he's at with it.
Evans wasn't the only player to be held out of Thursday's practice. Five other players were missing due to injury.
All five were the usual suspects: Nick Bosa (calf), James Thompson Jr. (ankle), Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Marques Sigle (ankle), and Garrett Wallow (hamstring).
On Monday, Shanahan insinuated that Bosa might play against the Commanders , but that doesn't seem likely anymore given his comments when he was asked about today.
It's safe to say that all of the players who were out of practice today, minus Evans, will not be active in Week 6. All eyes will and should be on Evans' status throughout the week.
If the 49ers have any doubt about his Achilles, they must hold him out no matter what.
