title: Former Super Bowl Champion Believes Jalon Daniels Is Bucs' Best Option at QB
full_text:
Baker Mayfield has had a rough start to the 2026 season.
Not only did Mayfield fail to lead his team to a single victory in each of his four starts this year, but his individual performance has predominantly been defined by turnovers, poor accuracy and a lack of poise in the pocket. To make matters worse, Mayfield suffered a brutal dislocation of his right thumb in the final moments of his team's home loss to the Cleveland Browns a few weeks ago, forcing him to the sidelines for an undetermined period of time.
Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, who surprisingly beat out veteran free agent signing Jake Browning for the backup QB job in training camp, has been tasked with holding down the fort after Mayfield's injury. And that's exactly what he's done.
After a narrow defeat at the hands of the Green Bay Packers in his first NFL game, Daniels showed out in Dallas on Thursday Night Football in Week 2, leading his team to an impressive and improbable victory against one of the most prolific offenses in the NFL.
Meanwhile, although he's been very supportive of Daniels, Mayfield has been dead set on returning to the lineup as soon as possible. In fact, he recently resumed throwing in hopes of fast-tracking his path back onto the field.
But would that really be good for the team?
At least one member of the Buccaneers Super Bowl winning team in 2020 doesn't think so.
On a recent episode of his podcast hosted with Jarvis Landry, 4th and South, Fournette had quite a hot take about the Bucs' current quarterback situation.
"I think, me personally, Jalon Daniels is the perfect fit for the Bucs right now," Fournette said. "They're winning! When Baker was back there, they weren't winning nothing. So I think it was a blessing and a curse. I'm not wishing nobody gets hurt, but at the same time, he's giving them more opportunity to win."
Fournette believes that Daniels is the team's best option to win right now.
"And I'm not saying Jalon's decision-making is better than Baker," he said. "To me it's even, because Baker throws picks, he fumbles, he does a lot. But at the end of the day, what can you do for me now? They're winning. I say keep Daniels in until we figure it out. Yes, Baker's got $100 million contract, but damn that, we want to win, coach."
Lenny wants Jalon Daniels to KEEP the QB job in Tampa 😳 Jarvis isn’t buying it 👀 Jalon Daniels might be the winning fit... #4thAndSouth #GoBucs #NFL pic.twitter.com/eysRVLdDFm
Fournette is certainly entitled to his opinion. That being said, as good as Daniels looked last week against the Cowboys and as bad as Mayfield looked in the first month of the season, the Buccaneers are going to be at their best for a longer period of time with Mayfield under center.
Not only that, but there isn't a chance that the Buccaneers would even consider relegating a healthy Mayfield to the bench because of the massive contract they awarded him just over a month ago.
The Buccaneers believe in Mayfield. And with every positive performance they get out of Daniels, their belief in him will continue to increase as well. But this is Mayfield's team, and the Bucs are prepared to sink or swim with him as the captain of their ship.

title: 3 Most Dangerous Steelers Players Buccaneers Will Face
full_text:
Even though they're only 5 games into the regular season, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers have already entered 'must-win' territory. As would be the case for any team that opened the season with 4 consecutive losses.
The Bucs do have some positive momentum, though, as they're coming off an impressive victory in Dallas over the Cowboys last Thursday night. Not only did undrafted rookie QB Jalon Daniels impress in his second NFL game, but the Bucs managed to contain the Cowboys' most dangerous weapons, holding each of Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens well below their expected output and allowing the Bucs to secure a much needed victory on the road.
If the Buccaneers hope to kickstart a winning streak, they'll need to do the same against the Steelers at home and limit the damage from Pittsburgh's most dangerous players. Let's take a closer look at who those players are and how the Bucs could achieve that:
There's little doubt about which player Todd Bowles' defense should be most concerned about on Sunday.
Jaylen Warren has always had explosive ability, but he was mostly used as a change of pace back under Mike Tomlin. Now that he's finally been given the keys to the backfield, Warren has taken that opportunity and run with it... literally.
Warren currently ranks third in the NFL in total yards from scrimmage with 640 and he's undoubtedly established himself as the team's most dynamic offensive weapon. Not only is Warren averaging an impressive 5.7 yards per carry running the football, but he's also been the team's greatest weapon as he leads the team in both receptions (19) and receiving yards (230).
Warren appears to be gaining confidence as he continues to earn more touches. He had arguably his best game as a pro last week vs. Indianapolis, where he exploded for 188 yards and 1 TD.
Despite having a relatively quiet 2025 season (at least by his standards) T.J. Watt has wasted no time reminding everyone why he remains one of the NFL's truly elite edge defenders. Although his 4.5 sacks are tied for the sixth most in the league, Watt is impacting the game in other ways this year, too.
According to PFF, Watt has been the best run defender among all edge rushers so far this year with an outstanding 92.1 run defense grade. Watt has been an extremely well-rounded player in 2026, producing 13 tackles, 6 TFLs and 7 QB hits to go along with 1 forced fumble and 1 fumble recovery.  Watt also has an interception this year, which he returned 35 yards for a TD to help seal a Steelers' victory against the Falcons back in Week 1.
The point is that T.J. Watt is still a game wrecker, and the Buccaneers will need to account for his presence at all times. If not? Watt could single-handedly turn the tide in his team's favor.
Some people may roll their eyes when they see Aaron Rodgers listed as one of the Steelers' most dangerous players, but the truth is, he's still got what it takes to lead his team to victories.
Rodgers has quietly played some pretty good football over the past few weeks, as the 42-year-old has now thrown three TD passes in each of his last three games. Rodgers is currently fifth in the league with 11 TD passes this year and 11th in total passing yards with 1,234.
Although Rodgers is very much immobile at this point of his career, he's still got more than enough arm talent to make every throw on the field. He also processes the game at an elite level, which is a big reason why he's been able to find so much success this season despite a really underwhelming group of pass catchers to work with.
If the Bucs aren't strategic with the looks they give Rodgers, both in coverage and pressure packages , he will make them pay.

title: If Buccaneers Can’t Sack Aaron Rodgers, They Have a Major Problem
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' pass rush has been struggling to get off the ground this season.
The defense stands at only six sacks through five games this season, with two coming from inside linebackers Alex Anzalone and Josiah Trotter and three coming from backup pass rushers David Walker and Anthony Nelson. While it's good that young players like Walker and Trotter are showcasing their abilities and proving that they are bright prospects for the team, many did not expect them to be the leading men in this unit.
Two players who have yet to notch a stat are starters Yaya Diaby and Rueben Bain Jr., both players whom many Bucs fans were excited about this season. This isn't fully their fault, as Bain Jr. has missed a couple of games due to injury and Diaby has had a couple of nagging ailments of his own.
However, the results to this point are certainly not what Bucs fans had in mind when they thought of the revamped pass rush the team made throughout the course of this offseason, and the players present are too good to be in the situation that they are in.
Along with Diaby and Bain Jr., veteran pass rusher Al-Quadin Muhammad has yet to step in as well, which is surprising considering he had 11 sacks in a rotational role with the Detroit Lions last season.
The quarterback they are going to try to take down? Aaron Rodgers, one of the best to do it in the NFL and someone who knows how to deal with pressure when faced with it.
However, Rodgers has actually been mortal against the Bucs, posting a 3-3 record through six career games with ten touchdowns to a matching ten interceptions.
If the Buccaneers are able to force Rodgers to make some mistakes and we see players like Diaby, Bain Jr., and Muhammad rise to the occasion, we could see the Bucs come away with the upset win during Week 6.
But if the pass rush continues to be lackluster and players like Walker, Nelson and the inside linebackers are the only ones who can keep the pass rush alive, it could be a very long day for the team.

title: Buccaneers' Todd Bowles Rules Out 2 Players vs. Steelers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are set to face off against the Pittsburgh Steelers in a game that could arguably make or break their season this early in the year. A win gets the Bucs to 2-4 and keeps them hanging on in the NFC South, but a loss drops them to 1-5 and puts them even further down the NFL ladder.
Tampa Bay will be mostly healthy when they face the Steelers, but there are two big players who won't be playing, according to head coach Todd Bowles. Thankfully for Tampa Bay, it's two players that the team wasn't expecting to rely on anyway this Sunday.
There are only two players out against the Steelers on Sunday, and it's two players that were assumed to be out anyway.
Bowles said Friday that quarterback Baker Mayfield and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. will be out on Sunday. Both players have been dealing with long-term injuries and were not expected to play on Sunday regardless.
Todd Bowles says that only Baker Mayfield and Antoine Winfield are OUT. Sean Tucker will be a game-time decision, he says. pic.twitter.com/BcipWIMqSm
Mayfield dislocated his thumb against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3 and has been out since. He's been pushing to play against the Steelers since the Bucs beat the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football, but he isn't quite ready to return to football action this weekend. Expect him to start ramping up to play next week when the Bucs face off against the Panthers.
Winfield fractured his ribs against the Green Bay Packers, and he was expected to be out for 2-4 weeks. This is the second week he'll be out, but he was working on the side with a trainer on Friday — that could be an encouraging sign for future games.
Running back Sean Tucker and Ayden Garnes were both working with trainers on Wednesday, but both have been participating on Thursday and Friday — Bowles said Tucker would be a game-time decision. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison and linebacker SirVocea Dennis both missed last week's game against the Cowboys, but both are expected to be available against the Steelers.
The Bucs will face the Steelers at 1 p.m. on Oct. 18 at Raymond James Stadium.

title: Buccaneers' Biggest Advantage Over Steelers Could Be the Difference in Week 6
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are coming off their first win of the 2026 season. After stumbling out of the gate winless through their first four games, though, this isn't exactly an achievement that should be celebrated, but rather something they are hoping will translate into some momentum as they prepare to host the 3-2 Pittsburgh Steelers at Raymond James Stadium this Sunday.
Despite the Bucs' struggles this season and the fact that they're still without their starting quarterback Baker Mayfield, the Steelers are still only slightly favored to win this football game.
There is no doubt that the Buccaneers possess more talent on paper than your standard 1-4 team, and Tampa Bay absolutely has a chance to take down the Steelers at home.
If the Bucs are going to reel off a second consecutive victory this weekend, there's a strong chance it will be in large because of one distinct advantage they have over the Steelers.
Heading into this season, many expected the Buccaneers' cornerback room to be the team's weakest position group. So far? They've been the best.
Despite coming off a down year in 2025, fifth-year outside CB Zyon McCollum has been one of the most impressive shutdown corners in the entire league. Despite having to match up against some of the best WRs in the league, including Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Justin Jefferson, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, McCollum has thrived so far this year, using the size, speed and instincts that earned him the three-year, $48 million contract he signed prior to last season to completely stifle some of the league's most talented wideouts.
So far this season, McCollum has had 62 matchups against 'top receivers' and allowed just a single reception. He also has four passes defended and an incredible 39.6 passer rating when targeted in coverage.
Zyon McCollum has been lockdown 🆚 top receivers in 2026 🔒 62 matchups. 7 targets. 1 reception for 18 yards. 4 passes defensed. 39.6 passer rating when targeted. pic.twitter.com/sRDcRCxlqZ
Jacob Parrish, meanwhile, has made a seamless transition from the slot, where he excelled as a rookie, to the outside. Listed at just 5'10", there was plenty of doubt regarding whether or not Parrish could hold up on the outside, but so far, he's looked the part. Parrish is a feisty pest of a CB and his elite agility and movement skills have allowed him to irritate opposing WRs who are much bigger.
On the other side, the Pittsburgh Steelers' wide receiver room has been a complete disaster so far this year.
As a group, the Steelers are dead last in the NFL in terms of separation against man coverage. Michael Pittman Jr., the team's primary free-agent acquisition in the offseason, is currently on the injured reserve.
Meanwhile, D.K. Metcalf — who the team is paying over $30 million per season — has looked like a sunk cost. Through five games this year, Metcalf is averaging fewer than four receptions and just 45 yards per contest. He has one receiving TD this season.
The #Steelers can't have DK Metcalf continuing to have the season he's having so far. In the game yesterday he had the following stat line: 28 routes, 4 targets, 3 catches and 12 yards. He had a Rec EPA of -0.8 His YACOE was -7 Average AY/Tgt was 3.3 These numbers aren't good…
With no Antoine Winfield Jr. on the back end of the defense, the Buccaneers will need other players to step up to ensure they can limit the Steelers' passing attack on Sunday, just like the Steelers will need players like Germie Bernard to step up at the receiver position due to injury.
Either way, it's impossible to deny that the Buccaneers should have a strong advantage when it comes to how their cornerbacks match up against the Steelers' wide receivers on Sunday. As long as the Bucs' young corners continue to play how they have been, Pittsburgh could have a real challenge generating any sort of production through the air.
If that happens? It would also be a real challenge for them to win this football game against a Buccaneers team that needs to start racking up some wins.

title: 3 Questions Facing Buccaneers Against Steelers in Week 6: Will Tampa Bay Stop This Crucial Steelers Player?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a tough task on Sunday. They're looking to move to 1-4, but they'll try and do it against a stout 3-2 Pittsburgh Steelers team heading into Tampa Bay.
The Bucs got their first win of the year against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 5, but now, they'll have another test. Here are three questions we have for head coach Todd Bowles' squad as Sunday rolls around:
It's rare that one player leads a team in both rushing and receiving, but Jaylin Warren is a rare player. Warren has 410 yards and one touchdown on the ground, but he also has 230 yards and a touchdown receiving, too.
At +0.131 EPA/play, Warren is the sixth-best running back in the NFL by that metric, and he's slated to do some serious damage on Sunday. The Bucs have to know where he is at all times and be able to contain him on the ground and through the air, and Bowles knows very well how good Warren is.
“I mean, he's been playing outstanding at running, blocking and pass receiving. You really don't see [all of that] from one guy," Bowles said. "He's doing everything. He's a very good pass protector. He's an outstanding runner, and he can catch the ball very well, and he makes you miss. [If] you miss a tackle, a guy like that, if you don't wrap up, he's going to take it to the house. So, he's been playing great football.”
Bucky Irving went off for 165 yards against the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday night. He probably won't do that again (probably) — but how well will he and the Bucs do?
The Steelers give up 103.4 rushing yards per game on average. They rank 13th there and 17th in the NFL in yards per rush (4.0), so they're a decent run-stopping unit. Tampa Bay had a great game in Week 5 to inflate the average, but they're fifth in the NFL in yards per rush (4.9) and they're seventh in rush yards per game (133.0).
If Tampa Bay is going to win this game against the Steelers, they'll simply have to get the ground game rolling. Irving instills a lot of confidence that this will happen, but it remains to be seen until game day comes around.
Aaron Rodgers, so far this season, has a sack rate of 6.97%, the 11th-most-sacked quarterback in the NFL. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers can't really get to the quarterback at all — the entire defense has a sack rate of 3.49%, which is good for 30th in the league.
Rodgers is largely immobile at his age, but the Bucs haven't been able to generate a pass rush at all. It will be Rodgers' instinct to get rid of the ball quickly, which will make it harder for Tampa Bay to bring him down. That obviously includes the edge rushers, but interior pass rushers like Calijah Kancey could have a day against Rodgers — if the middle collapses, Rodgers has nowhere to go.
Tampa Bay has been trying to figure out its pass rush for years now. Rodgers is a prime candidate to do so, but can players like Kancey, Yaya Diaby and Rueben Bain Jr. get home on Sunday?

title: Todd Bowles May Have Revealed The Buccaneers’ Next Breakout Star
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers expected a lot out of their rookie class in 2026. They really focused on defense and drafted an edge rusher in the first round, bringing in Rueben Bain Jr. from Miami, and they also selected a linebacker in the second round by picking Missouri's Josiah Trotter.
Some of those picks, like Bain, haven't yet panned out the way the Bucs have hoped. Others, like Trotter, have looked really strong so far this season — but there's one defensive rookie who may have impressed more than any Bucs draft pick.
Head coach Todd Bowles spoke to media on Wednesday, and he revealed which Bucs player he thinks has been one of the best players on the team so far — and it's one of Tampa Bay's drafted rookies.
Bowles said that nickel cornerback Keionte Scott, whom the Bucs drafted in the fourth round in April out of Miami, has been one of his best players so far in 2026, and he commended his ability to tackle and his work ethic throughout the week.
“[Scott has] been one of our best players this year. I mean, he doesn't say much. He's been very solid with his fundamentalist technique, and he tackles way more than he weighs. He tackles almost like a linebacker. He's a very tough kid, wants to be good, wants to be great, extremely tough, puts in the work during the week. That's what you really like about him. He really studies and gets it down for Sunday, and he executes well.”
Scott has played well at the nickel position so far. The Bucs defense puts up −0.179 EPA with him on the field and +0.011 with him off, showing that the team is more effective when he is playing. So far this season, he has 24 solo tackles (one tackle for loss) and two passes defended.
"I think first is the want-to," Scott said. "That's something you can just tell right away about a back, if he wants to stick his head in the fan... I'm one of those guys that's proud to have that in my toolbox, have that in my game — I just wanna get in there."
Scott will continue to get snaps at nickel as the defense starts to gel. He'll have a big test on Sunday when the Bucs face off against the Steelers in Raymond James Stadium at 1 p.m.

title: Buccaneers Thursday Practice All But Confirms Starting Quarterback vs. Steelers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers play the Pittsburgh Steelers in just three days. Every game for the Bucs is important from here on out, as the team is 1-4 and needs to start stacking wins if it has any hope of making the playoffs.
Head coach Todd Bowles said after the team's win against the Dallas Cowboys last Thursday that undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, who is filling in for starter Baker Mayfield as he recovers from a dislocated thumb, was preparing to start again against the Steelers.
But Mayfield was reportedly pushing to play, per NFL insider James Palmer, and the Buccaneers tested his grip ability by watching him throw on Wednesday afternoon.
Coach Baker Mayfield could return to player Baker Mayfield next week against the Steelers. I'm told Mayfield is pushing to play but it's 10 days out and it's too early for the Bucs to know medically if he can go. The stitches were taken out Monday and it's a matter of his thumb…
The Buccaneers conducted practice on Thursday, though, and that practice virtually confirmed Mayfield's status against the Steelers this Sunday.
Mayfield once again did not practice on Thursday, with Jalon Daniels taking the brunt of the first-team reps. It's unknown how Mayfield's throwing session went, but the team doesn't seem to want him back at practice just yet.
With that, Daniels is set for his third NFL start. Daniels comes into the game having thrown for 337 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions — he's also run for 87 yards. The undrafted rookie hasn't played perfectly, but he's impressed with his ability to run the offense competently, and he's gone a long way to prove the Bucs made the right decision to have him as QB2.
A likely target for Mayfield's return will be in Week 7. The Buccaneers play the Carolina Panthers in their first divisional game, and Mayfield will be beyond the three-week minimum that Bowles previously revealed after he was injured against the Minnesota Vikings.
For now, though, the Bucs remain Daniels' team to lead heading into Week 6. The Bucs will face off against the Steelers at 1 p.m. on Oct. 18 in Raymond James Stadium and will look to continue what would be the start of a long and grueling turnaround in 2026.

title: Have the Buccaneers Found Their Offensive Identity for the 2026 Season?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got their first win of the season against the Dallas Cowboys. It was a back-and-forth game where the defense was able to do enough to help get the win, but a bigger storyline coming out of the game is the offense.
It feels like for the first time this season, the Bucs offense was in sync and able to find its footing. This was mainly due to the work of Zac Robinson, which limited what Jalon Daniels needed to do for this offense and the great running ability of back Bucky Irving.
Irving really has come back to form this season, posting 21 carries for 165 yards and a rushing touchdown against Dallas as well as two catches for ten yards and a touchdown as well. Irving already has 77 carries for 406 rushing yards and two touchdowns this season, only 182 yards away from his total last year in 2025, playing in half as many games to this point.
I believe that the Bucs' offensive identity in 2026 will literally run through Bucky Irving, something that shouldn't be too surprising when we look at Zac Robinson's history as offensive coordinator in Atlanta.
Robinson ran both Bijan Robinson and Tyler Allgeier wild in 2024 and 2025, with both backs combined having 441 carries for 2100 rushing yards and 17 rushing touchdowns as well as 74 receptions for 519 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown in 2024. In 2025, it was 430 carries for 1992 rushing yards and 15 rushing touchdowns along with 93 receptions for 916 receiving yards and four receiving touchdowns.
I think that the team does need to see more usage from Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker going forward, but it's very clear that Robinson plans to use Irving in some type of Bijan role going forward with this team.
There are pros and cons to this type of identity, as many expected players like Baker Mayfield, Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin Jr. to lead the way for this offense this season. However, the positive is that it could help Mayfield button up some of the offensive struggles he had before his injury this season and limit turnovers overall.
Time will tell if this formula will work for Tampa Bay in the long run, but it seems like we've had a glimpse into what Robinson wants to do going forward.

title: Buccaneers Wednesday Practice Updates: Is Baker Mayfield Back?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are set to face off against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday as they try to move to 2-4 on the year and turn around what is already a season on the brink.
When they do so, they're set to have undrafted free agent rookie Jalon Daniels under center for the third game in a row. Starting quarterback Baker Mayfield, whom the team signed to a three-year, $165 million extension this offseason, dislocated his thumb against the Minnesota Vikings and has been out for the last two games.
Mayfield has been trying to work his way back sooner rather than later. But did he return to practice on Wednesday to test out his thumb ahead of the Steelers matchup Sunday? We have the latest update on Mayfield and more from Wednesday's practice:
Mayfield did not return to practice on Wednesday. He appears to still be recovering from his dislocated thumb — the stitches in his thumb have reportedly been taken out, but he still needs to find the strength to grip the football, and he may not be there yet.
In other injury news, both running back Sean Tucker and cornerback Ayden Garnes were working off to the side with a trainer on Wednesday.
Tucker had just seven snaps against the Cowboys, and Garnes had just one snap on defense along with special teams duties. A Tucker injury would limit Tampa Bay's variety in the backfield, but a Garnes injury would not be too bad in the grand scheme of things — he was active to fill in for cornerback Benjamin Morrison, and he has been inactive for the rest of the year otherwise.
Morrison was back to practice after missing two games with a quad injury. So was linebacker SirVocea Dennis, who has been out with an ankle injury since Week 4. Both players provide valuable depth on the defense and are key special teams players, so that should help Tampa Bay in Week 5 if they're able to play.
The Bucs play the Steelers on Oct. 18 at 1 p.m. at Raymond James Stadium.

title: Titans vs. Colts Expert Game Picks: Tennessee Projected to Fall to an AFC South Rival For Second Straight Week
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans will look to pick up their first win of the 2026 NFL season on Sunday, as head coach Robert Saleh's group will travel to Lucas Oil Stadium to face the 2-3 Indianapolis Colts.
Tennessee is coming off an embarrassing 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans in Week 5, while Indianapolis fell on the road 34-22 to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Both teams will be eyeing major bounce-back victories, and with it being a division game, the stakes are a little higher than usual.
With all that said, let's take a look at what the experts think about Sunday's AFC South battle between the Titans and the Colts.
Words from the author Tyler Sullivan: You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket."
Words from the author Mike Florio: The Colts can’t afford to lose at home to a team that can’t do much on either side of the ball.
Jeremy Bergman: Colts 24, Titans 19 Brooke Cersosimo: Colts 32, Titans 23 Gennaro Filice: Titans 14, Colts 13 Bobby Kownack: Colts 24, Titans 20 Dan Parr: Colts 27, Titans 20
Words from author Gennaro Filice: Admittedly, Tennessee has played like the most beatable team in the entire league, particularly on offense, where the Titans rank dead last in points and yards by comfortable margins. But Saleh’s D at least has some bite, especially up front. Jeffery Simmons is an absolute force of nature, and while John Franklin-Myers has yet to validate his $63 million deal as a pass rusher, he remains quite effective against the run. Is it that hard to imagine the Titans containing Jonathan Taylor, getting just enough offense from Cam Ward and eking out a low-wattage win?
Matt Bowen: Colts Mike Clay: Colts Jeremy Fowler: Colts Dan Graziano: Titans Kalyn Kahler: Colts Pamela Maldonado: Colts Eric Moody: Colts Ben Solak: Colts Lindsey Thiry: Colts Seth Wickersham: Colts
At 0-5 and showing barely any life last week, the experts aren't giving the Titans much of a chance to pull off the upset. However, Tennessee has been competitive in a few games they've played this season, so the upset can't be ruled out.
If the Titans lose and fall to 0-6, the panic in Nashville will be at an all-time high . Tennessee hasn't won a game since December 2025, and at this point, it's hard to argue that the last three years haven't been the worst in franchise history.
Dharya Sharma is a sportswriter from Nebraska who has been covering the Tennessee Titans through his website, SharmSports, since 2023. He is also an NFL and NBA writer for The Sporting News and had a previous stop with Sportsnaut. Follow him on X @SharmSports

title: Titans OC Brian Daboll Spoke on Thursday: What Stood Out
full_text:
Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll touched on a lot of interesting topics during his Thursday press conference.
It was the media’s first opportunity to question the offensive signal caller since the team’s disastrous outing against the Texans last Sunday.
It’s clear that he isn’t the type of coach who’s going to elaborate on a lot of things publicly, but he still touched on a handful of interesting topics and gave us some insight into what he’s seeing out of his unit going into Week 6.
Daboll was asked what he thinks the key is to getting the run game going and how much he thinks that could help this offense going forward.
“I’d say early down production is important (to getting this offense going) . Whether it’s the run game or the pass game.… Executing on early downs, keeping third downs to manageable situations, or skipping some of those third downs (entirely ), but being able to effectively do everything is what we’re striving for.”
The former Giants head coach also touched on the polarizing topic of running the ball out of shotgun and whether he has concerns about how much that can limit the run game.
“I think you can call any run you need to out of shotgun. Now, there are certain elements that go with the shotgun run game, whether that’s an RPO or you’re just blocking force... But I think there’s a balance. Under center usage is good if you’re effective with it, and the same thing with shotgun.”
ESPN’s Turron Davenport followed up with a question about QB Cam Ward’s usage under center, or lack thereof, noting that approximately 85 percent of his snaps have come from shotgun. Daboll addressed why that’s the case and if he’d like to balance that out a little more.
“If you look at the first three quarters (of last week’s game) , on early downs it was pretty balanced relative to that (85 percent mark) . But if we think that’s the best thing to do for him, we’ll certainly do that.”
Davenport later asked the Titans offensive play caller how confident he was that Ward’s confidence won’t be shattered by the bad results piling up early in his career.
“I have a lot of confidence in the young man. It has not been easy, you know, the start of his career… I have a lot of belief in him, in the things that he can do, and how he approaches it every week. We got to keep our head down. We got to keep grinding. But we need to do better in a number of areas to give ourselves a chance on game day. We go out here, we practice well, but situational football is big for us to improve on third down and red zone… but he’s a strong mind with a good family, and that’s what you’re looking for with these young guys.”
Daboll then discussed what he tells a rookie receiver like Carnell Tate about adapting to the ebbs and flows of an NFL season after he followed up his 145-yard performance in Baltimore with just one catch in Week 5.
“We talk a lot, and I’ve coached receivers for a long time in the league. And I’d say the receiver position is one where you have to have really good mental toughness. Because you can control getting open, but you can’t control getting the ball. Maybe the read takes you (the QB) to a different spot. So, staying locked in whether it’s 10 (targets) , whether it’s five, whether it’s two — you make the plays when they come your way.”
Daboll then addressed how Tate is handling that adjustment to the pro game.
“Great. He’s such a mature young man. Outside of football, all the stuff that the young man has been through in his life, he’s got a great perspective on life and the game for such a young player. He’s done a nice job for us.
Lastly, Daboll provided a non-answer when asked about the infamous clip of LT Dan Moore Jr. blocking nobody while Ward gets blitzed by a free rusher, and whether Moore did the right thing on that play.
at least this isn’t your starting LT pic.twitter.com/83MNndNHSf
“Look, we need to do a better job all the way around. But in terms of the execution of that particular corner blitz, I’m not going to get into the scheme of all of those guys, but we can do a better job of that.”
Daboll’s return to the OC chair, along with his pairing with Ward, had a lot of fans excited about the possibility of their quarterback having a similar breakout as the one Bills QB Josh Allen had while working with Daboll early in his career.
To say that hasn’t been the case would be an understatement. The Titans are currently 0-5, their offense ranks 31st in passing offense (164.8 YPG), and 27th in rushing offense (82.6 YPG), all while having scored just 58 points through five games.
One of the major concerns many Titans fans routinely talked about when the team hired Daboll was their fear of this being another short-term hire due to head coaching interest elsewhere.
Unfortunately, that may have been wishful thinking, because with results like that , he may be out at the end of the year anyway, but not the way everyone initially feared.

title: How Former Titan Ryan Fitzpatrick Believes Benching Cam Ward Would Benefit his Growth
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans are staring at a potential 0-6 start, the franchise's worst start since 2009.
Discourse among Titans fans and members of the media about QB Cam Ward appears to be at an all-time high. Former Tennessee Titans QB and longtime journeyman Ryan Fitzpatrick commented on Ward's play on his weekly podcast, Fitz & Whit , co-hosted with his former teammate Andrew Whitworth.
"I think the best thing for his development is to put him on the bench," Fitzpatrick said. "I think he should be benched for the next few games. I really do."
Drafted in the seventh round of the 2005 NFL Draft out of Harvard, Fitzpatrick had an unconventional career. He spent 17 years in the NFL playing for nine different teams, including the Titans, where he made 11 appearances in the 2013 season.
"Guess what? I've been in this situation plenty," Fitzpatrick said. "It's gonna provide him a different perspective; he's gonna be able to take a step back, he's gonna get to see someone else operate the offense."
The former NFL veteran believes Ward could benefit from watching backup QB Mitchell Trubisky take over as starter.
Now on his fourth team, Trubisky is a 10-year veteran that was brought in to backup Ward. Trubisky spent a season in 2021 with offensive coordinator Brian Daboll in Buffalo, where he backed up the Bills' franchise QB Josh Allen.
"Give him a week or two, where he doesn't have to feel the weight of the world on his shoulders," Fitzpatrick said.
Fitzpatrick made a list of the three major flaws in Ward's game in his eyes: fixing the uneasy footwork, correcting the deep ball and using his legs to extend plays.
Sloppy footwork has led to inaccuracy, which has been a problem for Ward all season. According to PFF , Ward ranks in the bottom five of qualified passers in average distance of target and long-distance attempts.
"All those fundamentals and those things he's struggling with right now, really hone in on your craft in practice (sitting behind Trubisky)," Fitzpatrick said. "Work on those things in practice."
Fitzpatrick recalled getting benched when he played for the Texans in 2014 for Ryan Mallett for two games. In his return for an injured Mallett, Fitzpatrick threw for six touchdowns and zero interceptions in a 45-21 rout over Tennessee.
That time to sit behind Mallett was valuable for Fitzpatrick because he felt that it allowed him to focus on getting back to the fundamentals.
"Multiple times I've been sitting at 0-5, we were 0-8 together in 2008 (in Cincinnati)," Fitzpatrick said. "In 2019 with Miami, I was 0-7, and I was benched during that little 0-7 thing and came back."
Fitzpatrick mentioned that he was a fan of Ward's game, praising him for his arm strength and ability to read the field. Nonetheless, Fitzpatrick believes benching Ward in favor of Trubisky would bring positive change for Ward's future in the NFL.
Trubisky last made a start in December 2023 as a member of the Pittsburgh Steelers, and Ward has never been benched as a pro.

title: Titans' Cam Ward Officially Hits Rock Bottom After Disastrous Start to Year 2
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans were looking for second-year quarterback Cam Ward to take a major leap in 2026, but the exact opposite has happened over the first month of the season.
Ward has been incredibly underwhelming so far this year. The Miami product has completed 63.2% of his passes for 896 passing yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions, and hasn't led Tennessee's offense to consistent production.
Though he hasn't been given the best support from his coaches and teammates at times, Ward's struggles are mostly on him . As a result, the 2025 No. 1 overall pick officially hit rock bottom in the latest power rankings of NFL quarterbacks.
Sports Illustrated's Matt Verderame released his power rankings of the NFL starting quarterbacks through five weeks, and Ward finished last. Ward was No. 25 in Verderame's preseason rankings, but fell seven spots after his lackluster start.
"The stats don’t do justice to how much Ward has struggled in Tennessee. Last week, he threw for only 70 yards over the first three quarters in a 26–3 loss to the Texans. He has yet to throw for 250 yards in a game. It’s been a disaster, and one that must have the Titans thinking about drafting his replacement in April," Verderame wrote.
Ward is still a developing signal-caller who could end up being the Titans' long-term solution at the most pivotal position in the sport. However, he's been awful this season and hasn't lived up to his top-pick status at all.
With Tennessee at 0-5 and on the road against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday , the next few weeks will be critical for Ward. If he can at least show growth and put the Titans in a position to be in competitive games, Ward will build a stronger argument to be the No. 1 quarterback in Nashville in 2027.
However, if the 24-year-old continues to turn the ball over and be a detriment to Tennessee's chances of winning, head coach Robert Saleh may begin thinking of playing Mitch Trubisky to provide his team with a possible spark. That scenario would also prompt uncomfortable conversations about Ward's future with the Titans just a year and a half after he was the first overall selection.

title: Robert Saleh Speaks on Poor Run Game, Announces Tony Pollard as Inactive for Wednesday Practice
full_text:
On Wednesday, head coach Robert Saleh announced to the media that starting RB Tony Pollard was inactive in practice with an undisclosed injury.
Pollard has time to return to practice and trend toward playing against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Last week against Houston, the Titans were held to a season-low 57 rushing yards with Pollard receiving all but three carries out of the backfield en route to a 26-3 blowout loss .
"You go to the Jets game and last game will be two games in the second half where it got a little out of hand," Saleh said. "Your run game will look like shit."
Saleh spoke candidly about the offense being withheld from running the ball consistently due to trailing in the second half, specifically against the Jets and Texans. In both of those games, the Titans were trying to come back from being down by two scores, limiting the chance to run the ball.
"Offensively, let's get a two-score lead, and then see what our run game looks like when we get to close out a game," Saleh said. "That would be freaking awesome."
Situational football is a factor in how many times an offense can run the ball. However, the truth is the Titans have a middle-of-the-road run game.
Tennessee runs the ball nearly 40% of offensive snaps for an average of 3.8 yards per rush, which ranks 17th in the NFL .
Pollard has 68 of 91 rushing attempts from the Titans, excluding QB Cam Ward, which is nearly a staggering 75% of the carries. According to PFF , Pollard's four yards per carry ranks him 23rd of 44 qualified runners despite having the 20th most carries.
If Pollard is inactive against the Colts, Daboll will have to turn to backup RB Tyjae Spears, who has primarily served as the blocking back. Spears has been a steady receiving back for Ward; he has the third most receptions on the team with 14 for 68 yards.
There's no denying the Titans offense needs change. An increase in opportunities for Spears may benefit a stagnate offense, especially against a Colts defense that allows the fifth most rushing yards per game .
Through five games, Spears has only 17 carries for 65 yards. He has the Titans only rush for more than 20 yards all season.

title: The 2 Matchups Titans Have to Win to Beat Colts in Week 6: Can Carnell Tate Bounceback?
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans travel to Indianapolis on Sunday for an AFC South showdown with the Colts.
Both teams are coming off double-digit losses in Week 5. The Colts’ defense is looking to bounce back after getting shredded by QB Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers offense.
As for the Titans, they’re just looking for any sign of improvement after an all-around beatdown by the Texans that saw them total just 187 yards of offense. Tennessee desperately needs to get in the win column this week solely to keep the panic meter from increasing more than it already has.
So, with that said, let’s take a look at which two matchups the Titans must win if they plan on flying back to Nashville with their first win of the season.
The Colts’ cornerback is in the midst of the lowest-graded season of his career, per Pro Football Focus . After not having an overall grade of less than 70 in any prior season, Gardner currently has a grade of 59.6 through five games. Even more intriguing is the fact that opposing quarterbacks have a passer rating of 120.6 when targeting the Cincinnati product, while opposing receivers are averaging more than 21 yards per reception when targeted against him.
This is an area QB Cam Ward and rookie WR Carnell Tate can try to exploit as the game unfolds. This offense desperately needs to start hitting big plays, and with Gardner showing a rare vulnerability of late, this may be the opportunity to take advantage.
Tate is coming off a one-catch, six-yard outing last Sunday and is looking to get back to the dominant performance he had in Baltimore the week prior. If Tate can consistently win this matchup (and any other he faces), Tennessee will have a chance.
If Tate is held in check once again, then that means the entire passing attack will likely be limited. And if that’s the case, it could be another long afternoon for the Titans offense.
As always, when it comes to Taylor, the Titans will have their hands full whenever he’s in the backfield. The Colts’ star RB currently ranks in the top 10 in carries (101), rushing yards (398), and rushing touchdowns (six).
This week, he gets to see an old friend he knows well: Jeffery Simmons. The Titans’ star defensive tackle is currently playing like one of the best defensive players in football regardless of position. His grade of 81.0 is the sixth-highest at his position, and even that feels low for someone as dominant as he’s been.
But in order to stop someone like Taylor, they’ll need a complete team effort from the entire group upfront. Fellow DL John Franklin Myers, Jermaine Johnson, and Jacob Martin have to join Simmons in being disciplined in the run game. You can’t press when playing someone with Taylor’s skill set. That’s how he takes advantage of you. Tennessee has to remain patient and make the plays that are there to be made.
They don’t have to make every stop, but it’s critical for their chances that they try to make the Colts one-dimensional on Sunday by limiting this ground game as much as possible.
Accomplishing that should give them a realistic shot at leaving Indianapolis with their first win of the season.

title: Titans Snap Count Analysis: Tyjae Spears Provides in Pass Game, Mitchell Trubisky is Overdue Playtime
full_text:
Sunday's blowout 26-3 home loss to the Houston Texans keeps the Tennessee Titans winless.
Tennessee is now one of three teams without a victory through five weeks. The Texans dominated Tennessee, and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers stunned the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football.
This loss marks seven consecutive losses for the Titans; their last win came against the Kansas City Chiefs without QB Patrick Mahomes in December.
Now, it's time to take a deeper look at the snap count, performances and decision-making by the Robert Saleh-led coaching staff against Houston.
In the previous two weeks, I have listed RB Tyjae Spears as a loser due to his firm role behind starter RB Tony Pollard.
However, Spears served as a reliable security blanket for QB Cam Ward in the pass game, earning him a spot as a winner. In addition to playing a season-high with 34 snaps, Spears led Tennessee in receptions with nine on nine targets for 28 yards.
Although Spears gave up a fumble on an awkward exchange from Ward, his overall performance was positive against Houston, especially because he's been relegated to pass blocking over the previous weeks.
Tennessee should look to utilize Spears as a pass catcher out of the backfield to help an underperforming Ward make easy reads.
We're at the point in the season where benching Ward should be a real option for the Titans coaching staff.
Ward had another underwhelming performance, completing 23 of 36 passes, nine of which were check-down passes to Spears, for a total of 170 yards passing. Furthermore, Ward absorbed four sacks and turned the ball over twice with one interception and a bobbled handoff to Spears.
Ward has the worst record for any quarterback in NFL history in their first 22 starts.
QB Mitchell Trubisky is yet to take a snap this season for the Titans. The former second overall pick in the 2017 NFL Draft has a winning record as a starter , going 31-26 across a decade-long career.
Once the Texans took a 19-3 in the third quarter, the game felt essentially over due to Tennessee's inept offense.
In the fourth quarter, I thought there would be a chance Trubisky would get some reps. Instead, the Ward-led Titans turned the ball over on downs twice.
Unless Ward improves, expect to see Trubisky get play time soon.
For the third week in a row , RB Nick Singleton is a loser after not playing a single offensive snap against the Texans.
The rookie has only made 14 offensive snaps in three games this season. So far this season, Singleton has played primarily on special teams with 21 appearances.
Unexpectedly, the Titans handed the ball off to second-year pro RB Kalel Mullings over Singleton. In his one carry, Mullings earned a three-yard gain, only his fourth career touch. gs
Singleton's role in the offense continues to be a mystery.
Returning to the loser list is LB Cedric Gray; the Titans' leading tackler last season is yet to record more than 30 snaps in a game this season.
Against Houston, Gray has held to only 28 snaps, according to PFF . Despite the low snap count, Gray racked up six tackles and half a sack alongside DT John Franklin-Myers.
Gray has consistently played about half the snaps of rookie LB Anthony Hill Jr. and LB Cody Barton.
While Hill Jr. has emerged as one of Tennessee's best defensive players, Barton and Gray are nearly identical statistically. Barton has 26 total tackles and one pass deflection; Gray has 22 total tackles and half a sack in one less game.
It appears Gray's inactivity in Week 1 from a concussion has set him back in the depth chart in favor of Barton.

title: Cam Ward Beats David Carr, Tim Couch and Other Busts for Worst Record in First 22 Starts in NFL History
full_text:
After Sunday's 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans , QB Cam Ward has the fewest wins across 22 starts of any NFL quarterback to begin their career.
In Ward's rookie campaign, he led the Titans to a 3-14 record. The last time Ward guided Tennessee to a win was in December against the Kansas City Chiefs without QB Patrick Mahomes, since the Titans have lost seven straight with Ward at the helm, including a 0-5 start, to begin the 2026 season.
In Sunday's blowout loss to Houston, Titans fans poured boos over the field and held up signs showing their frustrations .
Although football is the ultimate team sport, in recent years, a quarterback's win-loss record has become just as much a position stat as ERA is to pitchers in baseball. Whether or not the blame should fall on the shoulders of the 24-year-old quarterback, the numbers contextualize how medicore Ward's career has been.
Let's take a look at the short list of losing NFL quarterbacks who have started their careers with more wins than Ward.
Former University of Kentucky great, QB Tim Couch, like Ward, was drafted number one in the 1999 NFL Draft to the newly expanded Cleveland Browns.
In 1996, the Browns moved to Baltimore, becoming the Baltimore Ravens. After three years of no football in northern Ohio, the Cleveland Browns were reinstated as an expansion franchise.
Couch made his first career start in Week 2 against the newly rebranded Tennessee Titans; the Browns lost 9-26. Cleveland would only win two games in Couch's rough rookie season, one less than Ward's rookie campaign.
In his sophomore season, Couch led the Browns to a 2-1 start before going on a four-game losing streak. A broken thumb sidelined Couch for missing the remainder of the season.
In 2001, Couch made his 22nd start and lost, going 4-18 in that stretch, earning one more than Ward to begin his career.
Unfortunately, Coach would retire at the age of 26 due to major injuries. He finished his career with the Browns, going 22-37 as a starter, throwing 67 interceptions to 64 touchdowns.
Today, Couch is remembered as the beginning of the Browns' carousel of quarterbacks .
Drafted sixth overall by the Cincinnati Bengals, QB David Klingler was a standout at the University of Houston. The Bengals selected Klingler to be the successor to franchise legend QB Boomer Esaison.
After a rocky start of 4-7, Cincinnati benched Esaison in favor of Klingler. The rookie struggled, losing his first three starts before finally earning his first and only win as a rookie.
The Bengals traded Esaison to the New York Jets, and Klingler was named the full-time starter, but he continued to underperform. In his first 22 starts, he only earned four wins, which is one more win than Ward.
Klingler was benched for good in 1994 after going 0-7 to start the season. Over the next three seasons, Klingler only appeared in five games as a backup.
He finished his career with a 4-20 record, throwing 22 interceptions and 16 touchdowns.
The Houston Texans selected QB David Carr first overall in the 2002 NFL Draft. The Texans were given the first pick because they were an expansion team, bringing football back to Houston since the Oilers left in 1996 for Tennessee.
Similar to Ward, Carr was named the day-one starter as the number one pick. In his NFL debut, Carr steered the newly formed Texans to a 19-10 victory over in-state opponent the Dallas Cowboys.
Carr ended his rookie season with a 4-12 record, earning one more win than Ward despite finishing the season without a touchdown over the final six games. In 2003, Carr made his 22nd start in his sophomore season and lost, finishing with a 6-16 record in that span.
Carr continued to quarterback the Texans for the next several seasons with little success. He made his final start in 2007 as a member of the Carolina Panthers before spending four years as a backup.
In 2012, Carr retired a Super Bowl champion as a backup for Eli Manning. Carr finished his career with a 23-56 record as a starter, throwing 71 interceptions to 65 touchdowns as a pro.
Carr holds an NFL record for the most sacks taken in a single season with 76 , which came in his rookie season.
Coming out of Washington State, QB Ryan Leaf was considered worthy of the first overall pick in the 1998 NFL Draft over Hall of Famer Peyton Manning. Ultimately, the Colts chose Manning, and Leaf was selected second to the San Diego Chargers.
In 1998, Leaf was a Week 1 starter, like Ward. He won his first two starts over the Bills and Titans before getting benched in Week 10 due to a sour performance against the Broncos.
Leaf would appear in one more game in Week 15 as a backup; he finished his rookie season 3-9 as a starter.
Over the next two seasons, Leaf would only make nine more starts before flaming out with the Dallas Cowboys in 2001. Although Leaf was one start shy of 22 career starts, he still earned one more win than Ward.
Across his three seasons as a pro, Leaf went 4-17 as a starter and had a horrendous 14-36 touchdown-to-interception ratio. He was out of the NFL by the age of 25.
Today, Leaf is widely regarded as one of the biggest busts in recent NFL history.

title: Grading Every Titans Position Group After Week 5 Loss vs. Texans
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans produced another lifeless effort on Sunday, falling 26-3 to the Houston Texans in a lopsided battle between two winless teams.
Even the most optimistic Titans fan can’t help but feel dejected after a performance like that . Things started badly, and they only got worse as the game progressed.
This Titans team is simply broken in many ways, and until things get fixed, you’re going to continue seeing the type of poor grades you’re about to sees
QB Cam Ward struggled mightily in this one, completing just 23 of his 36 passes for 170 yards and one interception.
The second-year quarterback continues to be erratic with his ball placement. Ward has a knack for making catches harder than they have to be, which leads to drops or missed opportunities after the catch.
Another area where he continues to struggle is his ability to process what he’s seeing both pre- and post-snap. His inability to diagnose the moving puzzle often gets him in trouble and/or prevents him from hitting the big plays that are there to be made.
All of these issues showed up early and often in what was arguably Ward’s worst outing of the season. But considering the performance of the offensive line (we’ll touch on that later), I’ll at least spare him from the F.
Things got off to a rocky start and never get much better. RB Tyjae Spears fumbled in the first quarter and failed to record a single rushing yard, while RB Tony Pollard averaged less than four yards per carry.
It was a putrid afternoon all around, and the inability to get anything going on the ground was a big reason why.
The receiver group of Carnell Tate, Wan’Dale Robinson, Elic Ayomanor, Calvin Ridley, and Chimere Dike combined for just 137 yards on 13 catches.
There were a couple of big plays left on the table, most notably a couple of missed opportunities to Tate that failed to connect because of poor execution and/or penalties. But aside from that, it was a rather lifeless performance by the entire passing attack.
Where do we even begin with this one?
I would say this was an absolutely atrocious performance by the offensive line, but that would somehow be downplaying how bad it really was. The offensive line allowed a combined 20 pressures, three sacks, and two hits on the day.
LT Dan Moore was the biggest culprit, allowing eight of those pressures for an absurd pressure rate of 19.5 percent.
Watching this play in slow-motion with this music is *chefs kiss* pic.twitter.com/OvC0NYFbzI
It was a long afternoon for the group upfront, and the point total on the scoreboard directly reflects that.
It was another largely irrelevant day for a group that hasn’t contributed much. The group of Gunnar Helm, Daniel Bellinger, and Kylen Granson combined for just five yards.
The latter of whom had the opportunity for a big play early in the game, but he was unable to reel in the pass, and it became another missed opportunity for a team that’s had more than its fair share.
It was a rather mediocre outing for a group that has actually played well for most of the year. The group combined for eight pressures and six run stops. DT Jeffery Simmons led the way with three pressures, while DL Jordan Elliott topped the group with two run stops.
But for the Titans to win, they need their defensive line to be a dominant front, and that just wasn’t the case here.
Cody Barton, Cedric Gray, and Anthony Hill Jr. had a solid game for the most part. The three of them were credited with 17 combined tackles, multiple pressures, and half a sack (Gray).
They also helped play a key role in holding the Texans’ ground game to under three yards per carry.
The Titans’ secondary entered the game very thin on the backend, and it only got worse. S Amani Hooker was ruled out with a concussion, while S Kevin Winston Jr. left early with a quadriceps injury, and their absence was felt throughout the contest.
The Texans’ group of pass catchers combined for 261 yards and one touchdown on 26 catches.

title: Postgame Quotes That Matter From Robert Saleh After Titans' Lifeless Week 5 Loss to Texans
full_text:
Another Sunday means another Tennessee Titans loss. This time, head coach Robert Saleh's group fell to the Houston Texans 26-3 at home, dropping to 0-5 in the 2026 season.
Not much went right for Tennessee against Houston. The offense managed just 187 total yards and didn't find the end zone, while the defense allowed Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud to get too comfortable in the pocket, leading to an efficient outing for the 2023 No. 2 overall pick.
The Titans are arguably the worst team in the NFL and have shown no improvement from last season's 3-14 performance. Saleh spoke to the media after his team's latest embarrassing loss, and it's clear that he is running out of answers.
Though he isn't the sole reason for Sunday's loss to the Texans, quarterback Cam Ward still didn't play very well . The 2025 No. 1 overall pick completed 23 of 36 passes for 170 yards and threw an interception.
After another uninspiring performance from his young signal-caller, Saleh was asked about the possibility of benching Ward for veteran Mitchell Trubisky, and the Titans head coach made it known that Ward is still Tennessee's No. 1 quarterback.
"Cam's our starting quarterback," Saleh said. "We're going to give him every opportunity to be successful this year, and we're going to continue working with him, grinding with him and trying to help him get better."
Ward was also asked why he should remain the Titans' QB1, and the Miami product said he is more than capable of handling the responsibilities of being an NFL starting quarterback.
"I just think my process, what I'm willing to sacrifice every week to get to the player that I want to be," Ward said on remaining as the Titans starting quarterback. "Also the player that the team needs and the organization needs to win games. I love the criticism and everything that comes with the quarterback territory. It's the best position in the world. Stuff goes the right way, you take all the credit. Stuff goes the wrong way, you take all the blame."
He hasn't lived up to expectations so far this year, but it is still too early to bench Ward. Tennessee must give Ward an ample sample size before making a decision on whether he is the answer at the most pivotal position in the sport.
Despite a 0-5 start to his tenure as head coach, Saleh isn't losing any confidence. The defensive-minded coach stated that he will turn the Titans around and bring the franchise back into the sun as a winning organization.
"We are going to flip this thing, and eventually this organization is going to have its day in the sun," Saleh said.
Tennessee has won six games since the start of the 2024 season, and hasn't tallied a victory since Week 16 of the 2025 season. There may not be a franchise in a darker place than the Titans right now, and we'll see whether Saleh can turn the tide and be the coach who brings winning football back to Nashville.
The most impactful quote from Saleh's press conference was his message to his guys about the next 12 games. Saleh said that the final 12 games of the year will decide who will stick around in Tennessee and be a part of the franchise turnaround.
"The next 12 games will determine which of you will be here when we turn this thing around."
The Titans were one of the most active franchises in the league on the player acquisition front this past offseason. So far, none of those additions have paid off and made major contributions. We could see another roster turnover period for Tennessee as soon as next spring.
A road contest against the 2-3 Indianapolis Colts is next for the Titans. A loss would drop Tennessee to 0-6 for the first time since 2009, and could officially kickstart draft talk.

title: Commanders Have One of NFL's Best Turnover Margins — So Why Just One Win?
full_text:
One of Washington's top defensive priorities this offseason was to carry a mindset into the season that lived and died off of takeaways. Five weeks in, the team has produced seven takeaways in a season where they've turned the ball over only twice. That's a +5 turnover differential for the Commanders, tied for second-best in the NFL, even though the team has only won once this season. This is unusual, as teams in the top five in that category tend to be better positioned to win. Washington got that lone win by turning three takeaways into 20 points in a 33-31 win, despite Seattle heavily outgaining the Commanders. That game should serve as an example moving forward of what happens when they take advantage of opponents' mistakes. Against Indianapolis, however, Washington forced two turnovers but managed just three points off those opportunities in a 30-13 loss. At the opposite end of the spectrum sits the Giants game and the way it ended after Washington found a way to squander a 14-point fourth-quarter lead and one of their young quarterback's best statistical games. In the end, the defense delivered the football when the team needed it, but the offense and coaching staff couldn't get out of their own way long enough to finish the job. The Commanders enter Week 6 ranked 30th in scoring defense, allowing 29.8 points per game. Washington is 25th against the pass, allowing 242.5 yards per game. The team's offense averages 23 points per game, good enough to rank 17th in the league. Monday, Washington faces the 49ers, who average 30.8 points per game but only have a +2 turnover differential and a 5-0 record. That's the difference between these two teams. Washington has done a good job taking the ball away, but when you're allowing nearly 30 points per game and failing to consistently capitalize on those extra possessions, even one of the NFL's best turnover margins isn't going to save you. title: Jayden Daniels Identifies What Washington Was Missing Against the Giants’ Blitz — Commanders Daily
full_text:
The Washington Commanders had more go wrong late in Sunday's 27-27 tie with the New York Giants than the final 12 seconds everyone has spent the week talking about . That ending deserves the criticism it has gotten, but Washington's offense was already having trouble before it reached the Giants' 24-yard line with 55 seconds left. New York had started bringing more pressure, and Jayden Daniels admitted Thursday that he didn't always get the Commanders into the right answer. “We just gotta learn from it,” Daniels said when asked about Washington's fourth-quarter passing game. “You know, they were bringing a lot of zero pressure. I gotta be able to get different checks to the guys and, you know, ultimately just be, play in the quarterback position, make sure we're in the right position to be able to get the ball out to its perimeters, to the skill guys, so they can make plays and hopefully break a couple tackles and make some things happen.” At first glance, four sacks against the blitz is going will put most of the attention on the offensive line. The problem is that some of these pressure looks sent more rushers than Washington had available blockers, which means the answer had to be something other than asking the line to hold up longer.
According to Next Gen Stats , New York blitzed Daniels on 62.2% of his dropbacks, the Giants' highest rate in a game this season. Daniels still completed 11-of-18 passes for 131 yards against the blitz and added a 38-yard touchdown run, so this wasn't something that wrecked Washington's offense every time New York tried it. The fourth quarter and overtime were much different. Fourteen of the Giants' 24 blitzes came during that stretch , pushing their blitz rate to approximately 74%. New York also used Cover 0 on 10 of Daniels' dropbacks, including the final three plays of regulation, and sacked him three times. Cover 0 leaves the defense without a deep safety, which can create opportunities for the offense if the quarterback has time to find them. When the Giants sent more players than Washington kept in protection, however, someone was going to come free no matter how well the offensive line handled everyone else. That's when the quarterback needs somewhere else to go with the ball. “If you're bringing more, then you need to have answers that may not even be part of the play,” Quinn said Thursday. “Okay, now there's eight players up. This is where we can go. This is the next option. And that's always a part of it.” Quinn didn't explain what those specific answers are, which isn't something Washington would want to give San Francisco anyway. It could mean changing the protection, adjusting a receiver's route, or getting the ball outside before the extra defender gets to Daniels.
This is where the responsibility starts spreading beyond the offensive line. Offensive coordinator David Blough and the rest of the staff have to give Daniels options he can get to when the defense changes the numbers; Daniels has to recognize the pressure and communicate the check, and everyone else has to understand what changes with it. That doesn't sound overly complicated, but one player missing the adjustment can ruin the entire play. “You know, sit down with Blough, and offensively his offensive staff, myself, have some answers for it knowing that, you know, teams are gonna try to get the ball out of my hand, heat us up, right, and everything like that,” Daniels said. “So just have an answer from him and, you know, preparing for it.” Of course, none of this clears the offensive line. Daniels was still sacked four times against the blitz, and there were plays when the protection could have been better. It just means blaming those sacks entirely on the players up front would ignore what Daniels and Quinn both said Thursday. There are two ways to look at how Washington handled the pressure against New York. Daniels completed more than 60% of his passes against the blitz and made the Giants pay with his legs, but New York also had enough late success to keep bringing it throughout the fourth quarter and overtime. The Giants found something that worked when they needed it most. San Francisco will see the same film, and the 49ers won't have to blitz on nearly three-quarters of Washington's late-game dropbacks to find out if the Commanders fixed anything. A few pressure looks in the right situations should be enough to test Daniels' checks and whether the rest of the offense is on the same page. Considering how the Giants ended Sunday's game, Washington should expect that test to come.

title: Commanders' Next Three Games Could Put Daron Payne on the Trade Block
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is less than a month away, looming like a ticking timer counting down to the moment when middle-of-the-road teams are forced to pick a lane.
The Washington Commanders already look to be slipping down the path of the future seller following their tough start to the regular season, having slumped out to a disappointing 1-3-1 record with the help of injuries to most of their featured offensive staples and some glaringly poor late-game choices . It's time for Commanders executives to evaluate who's worth paying while key contributors waste away in an unworthy situation, and someone like Daron Payne will continue seeing his name come up in mock trades over the weeks to come.
The longest-tenured non- Tress Way Commander has remained one of the more dependable defensive players over a near-decade of fluctuating circumstances, and he's generally made good on backing up the four-year, $90 million contract he signed in early 2023.
Just last week, the defensive tackle notched his first sack of the season on the New York Giants' Jameis Winston, yet another instance of the stability he's helped provide during Daronte Jones' maiden voyage as his defensive coordinator.
Daron Payne Week 5 vs. Giants: 3 TKL | 1 TFL | 1 SACK | 1 FF Season highs in snaps (59) and pass rushes (41), with 4 pressures and his first sack of the year, a 13-yarder on 3rd & 10. Had another one wiped out by a holding call earlier on that drive. Overtime, two minutes… https://t.co/Hc9sfraism
Amidst the final year of his contract, though, he seems like a fitting name to dangle in front of teams looking for help along the defensive interior. If Washington decides the season is slipping away, Payne's expiring deal makes him one of the more logical veterans to shop while he still carries trade value, something ESPN's Jeremy Fowler noted this week.
Offensive linemen are rarely swapped in a league where otherwise unappreciated blockers will always be highly valued, and the Commanders probably learned their lesson in trading for veteran cornerbacks midseason following the Marshon Lattimore experience .
A fringe wide receiver isn't quite as necessary as, say, a voracious pass-rusher or a go-to tight end would be to the Commanders' present operation, but that hasn't stopped a few fans and analysts from putting together some intriguing package ideas. Brian Thomas Jr., an old friend of Jayden Daniels who's currently watching his promising career start to spiral on the Jacksonville Jaguars, will remain a name to watch as a buy-low reclamation project following Marvin Harrison Jr.'s own surprise deal last weekend.
Another Brian Thomas Jr. trade idea: Commanders get: Brian Thomas Jr. Jaguars get: Daron Payne 2027 3rd round pick Commanders reunite BTJ with Jayden Daniels. Jags shore up the trenches with a talented DT on an expiring deal, plus another pick. Who says no?
As if the Commanders' one win through five matchups, a Week 3 upset victory over the defending champion Seattle Seahawks , wasn't enough to sink them into the NFC's dirt, they're in for a tough ride in looking ahead through the games scheduled between now and the deadline.
The undefeated 49ers are favored to make quick work of the uncoordinated Commanders on Monday Night Football in Week 6, and that isn't even Washington's only brush-up with the dominant NFC West; a date with the Los Angeles Rams awaits the underdogs in Week 9. The hurting Philadelphia Eagles, sandwiched between those uphill battles, hover as a wounded animal looking for an easy victory over the same team they'd already bested in this fall's season opener .
Barring another vintage Daniels fourth-quarter comeback or some rapid-fire turnarounds within Washington's coaching quarters, there's a real chance that this squad will limp into the deadline without a win in their previous five outings, assuming all of those playoff-hopefuls dispose of the hangers-on. Should the Commanders be as unimpressive as the fan base fears, add a potential shift in in-season focus to the reasons to trade Payne while they still have a chance to yield a semi-meaningful return.

title: Commanders Rookie Power Rankings: Is Washington Getting Enough From This Class?
full_text:

There’s a lot more to like about Sonny Styles than there was three games ago, which has made it hard to keep Williams ahead of him. The rookie earned NFC Defensive Player of the Week honors against Seattle after having five tackles, an interception, a forced fumble, and two passes defensed; he added eight tackles against Indianapolis and 13 against the Giants . In five games, Styles has 33 tackles, a sack, an interception, a forced fumble, and three passes defensed in 308 defensive snaps. Washington has continued asking him to handle the green dot when needed, and his PFF overall grade has gone from 50.8 in our last edition to 71.6, putting him 15th among 72 qualifying linebackers. His 75.1 coverage grade ranks sixth, though his run defense still needs some work, with a 59.7 grade and seven missed tackles. Plus, NFL.com’s Gennaro Filice put him first among defensive rookies , writing, "At this point, I’m not sure what Styles can’t do."
Washington is using Antonio Williams a lot more than it was when the season started, although he hasn’t been getting the yards he had in the first two games. The injuries at receiver have given him more playing time, with his snap share going from 37% in the opener to 69% against Indianapolis and 68% against the Giants; he’s added just 67 receiving yards over those last three games. Through five games, Williams has 15 catches for 155 yards and a touchdown, with PFF giving him a 72.8 overall grade, 34th among 86 qualifying receivers, and no drops.
It feels better to have Drew Stevens out there than it did when he was making just 60% of his field goals, because he hasn’t missed one since our last rankings. He’s made two in each of the last three games, including a 57-yarder against Seattle that set Washington’s rookie record, bringing him to 9-of-11 for the season. The extra points are still a problem, though, with one blocked in Philadelphia and misses against Seattle and the Giants leaving him at 8-of-11 (72.7%).
Matt Gulbin’s situation has changed quite a bit since we were trying to judge him on four offensive snaps. Washington needed someone to take Cosmi’s place at right guard in London, so the backup center got the start and played all 64 offensive snaps before going back to the bench when Cosmi returned against the Giants. In 72 offensive snaps, Gulbin has a 63.2 PFF overall grade, with a 62.7 pass-blocking grade and 60.9 in run blocking, allowing two pressures, including a sack and a quarterback hit, with no penalties.
We’ve finally gotten to see Athan Kaliakmanis in a regular-season game, although it came under some difficult circumstances, with Daniels already out and Mariota hurting his knee in London. Washington had to turn to the rookie for 54 offensive snaps, which gave us some good throws and some mistakes , with PFF crediting him with two big-time throws and two turnover-worthy plays. Against Indianapolis, he completed 15-of-33 passes for 186 yards, a touchdown, and an interception; Daniels’ return leaves Kaliakmanis fifth after getting his first game out of the way.
Joshua Josephs drew our attention during the preseason because he was finding ways to get after quarterbacks, but he hasn’t done much of that through five games. Washington has gradually given him more time, with his defensive snaps going from 15 against Seattle to 18 against Indianapolis and 20 against the Giants; he’s now played 73 snaps, with six solo tackles and three defensive stops. PFF rates him 49.0 overall, with a 73.7 run-defense grade and 55.8 as a pass rusher, where he’s had just one quarterback hurry on 27 pass-rush snaps.
We still don’t know much more about Tanoa Togiai than we did when he made the team as an undrafted rookie. Washington has kept him on the active roster, but he hasn’t played an offensive snap in five games and was inactive against the Giants.
It's hard to gauge if waiving RB Kaytron Allen was a good idea. Washington hoped he would clear waivers so they could bring him back to the practice squad; Miami had other plans after seeing him rush for 85 yards and a touchdown in the preseason. In four games for Washington, the rookie had 12 rushes for 41 yards in 25 snaps and added 29 snaps on special teams.
